HAMLET: What a piece of work is a man! how noble in reason!
HAMLET: how infinite in faculty! in form and moving how
HAMLET: express and admirable! in action how like an angel!
HAMLET: in apprehension how like a god! the beauty of the
HAMLET: world! the paragon of animals! And yet, to me,
HAMLET: what is this quintessence of dust? man delights not
HAMLET: me: no, nor woman neither, though by your smiling
HAMLET: you seem to say so.
ROSENCRANTZ: My lord, there was no such stuff in my thoughts.
HAMLET: Why did you laugh then, when I said 'man delights not me'?
ROSENCRANTZ: To think, my lord, if you delight not in man, what
ROSENCRANTZ: lenten entertainment the players shall receive from
ROSENCRANTZ: you: we coted them on the way, and hither are they
ROSENCRANTZ: coming, to offer you service.
HAMLET: He that plays the king shall be welcome, his majesty
HAMLET: shall have tribute of me, the adventurous knight
HAMLET: shall use his foil and target, the lover shall not
HAMLET: sigh gratis, the humourous man shall end his part
HAMLET: in peace, the clown shall make those laugh whose
HAMLET: lungs are tickled o' the sere, and the lady shall
HAMLET: say her mind freely, or the blank verse shall halt
HAMLET: for't. What players are they?
ROSENCRANTZ: Even those you were wont to take delight in, the
ROSENCRANTZ: tragedians of the city.
HAMLET: How chances it they travel? their residence, both
HAMLET: in reputation and profit, was better both ways.
ROSENCRANTZ: I think their inhibition comes by the means of the
ROSENCRANTZ: late innovation.
HAMLET: Do they hold the same estimation they did when I was
HAMLET: in the city? are they so followed?
ROSENCRANTZ: No, indeed, are they not.
HAMLET: How comes it? do they grow rusty?
ROSENCRANTZ: Nay, their endeavour keeps in the wonted pace: but
ROSENCRANTZ: there is, sir, an aery of children, little eyases,
ROSENCRANTZ: that cry out on the top of question, and are most
ROSENCRANTZ: tyrannically clapped for't: these are now the
ROSENCRANTZ: fashion, and so berattle the common stages--so they
ROSENCRANTZ: call them--that many wearing rapiers are afraid of
ROSENCRANTZ: goose-quills and dare scarce come thither.
HAMLET: What, are they children? who maintains 'em? how are
HAMLET: they escoted? Will they pursue the quality no
HAMLET: longer than they can sing? will they not say
HAMLET: afterwards, if they should grow themselves to common
HAMLET: players--as it is most like, if their means are no
HAMLET: better--their writers do them wrong, to make them
HAMLET: exclaim against their own succession?
ROSENCRANTZ: 'Faith, there has been much to do on both sides, and
ROSENCRANTZ: the nation holds it no sin to tarre them to
ROSENCRANTZ: controversy: there was, for a while, no money bid
ROSENCRANTZ: for argument, unless the poet and the player went to
ROSENCRANTZ: cuffs in the question.
HAMLET: Is't possible?
GUILDENSTERN: O, there has been much throwing about of brains.
HAMLET: Do the boys carry it away?
ROSENCRANTZ: Ay, that they do, my lord, Hercules and his load too.
HAMLET: It is not very strange, for mine uncle is king of
HAMLET: Denmark, and those that would make mows at him while
HAMLET: my father lived, give twenty, forty, fifty, an
HAMLET: hundred ducats a-piece for his picture in little.
HAMLET: 'Sblood, there is something in this more than
HAMLET: natural, if philosophy could find it out.
NARRATOR: Flourish of trumpets within
GUILDENSTERN: There are the players.
HAMLET: Gentlemen, you are welcome to Elsinore. Your hands,
HAMLET: come then: the appurtenance of welcome is fashion
HAMLET: and ceremony: let me comply with you in this garb,
HAMLET: lest my extent to the players, which, I tell you,
HAMLET: must show fairly outward, should more appear like
HAMLET: entertainment than yours. You are welcome: but my
HAMLET: uncle-father and aunt-mother are deceived.
GUILDENSTERN: In what, my dear lord?
HAMLET: I am but mad north-north-west: when the wind is
HAMLET: southerly I know a hawk from a handsaw.
NARRATOR: Enter POLONIUS
LORD POLONIUS: Well be with you, gentlemen!
HAMLET: Hark you, Guildenstern, and you too: at each ear a
HAMLET: hearer: that great baby you see there is not yet
HAMLET: out of his swaddling-clouts.
ROSENCRANTZ: Happily he's the second time come to them, for they
ROSENCRANTZ: say an old man is twice a child.
HAMLET: I will prophesy he comes to tell me of the players,
HAMLET: mark it. You say right, sir: o' Monday morning,
HAMLET: 'twas so indeed.
LORD POLONIUS: My lord, I have news to tell you.
HAMLET: My lord, I have news to tell you.
HAMLET: When Roscius was an actor in Rome,--
LORD POLONIUS: The actors are come hither, my lord.
HAMLET: Buz, buz!
LORD POLONIUS: Upon mine honour,--
HAMLET: Then came each actor on his ass,--
LORD POLONIUS: The best actors in the world, either for tragedy,
LORD POLONIUS: comedy, history, pastoral, pastoral-comical,
LORD POLONIUS: historical-pastoral, tragical-historical, tragical-
LORD POLONIUS: comical-historical-pastoral, scene individable, or
LORD POLONIUS: poem unlimited: Seneca cannot be too heavy, nor
LORD POLONIUS: Plautus too light. For the law of writ and the
LORD POLONIUS: liberty, these are the only men.
HAMLET: O Jephthah, judge of Israel, what a treasure hadst thou!
LORD POLONIUS: What a treasure had he, my lord?
HAMLET: Why,
HAMLET: 'One fair daughter and no more,
HAMLET: The which he loved passing well.'
LORD POLONIUS: [Aside]  Still on my daughter.
HAMLET: Am I not i' the right, old Jephthah?
LORD POLONIUS: If you call me Jephthah, my lord, I have a daughter
LORD POLONIUS: that I love passing well.
HAMLET: Nay, that follows not.
LORD POLONIUS: What follows, then, my lord?
HAMLET: Why,
HAMLET: 'As by lot, God wot,'
HAMLET: and then, you know,
HAMLET: 'It came to pass, as most like it was,'--
HAMLET: the first row of the pious chanson will show you
HAMLET: more, for look, where my abridgement comes.
NARRATOR: Enter four or five Players
HAMLET: You are welcome, masters, welcome, all. I am glad
HAMLET: to see thee well. Welcome, good friends. O, my old
HAMLET: friend! thy face is valenced since I saw thee last:
HAMLET: comest thou to beard me in Denmark? What, my young
HAMLET: lady and mistress! By'r lady, your ladyship is
HAMLET: nearer to heaven than when I saw you last, by the
HAMLET: altitude of a chopine. Pray God, your voice, like
HAMLET: apiece of uncurrent gold, be not cracked within the
HAMLET: ring. Masters, you are all welcome. We'll e'en
HAMLET: to't like French falconers, fly at any thing we see:
HAMLET: we'll have a speech straight: come, give us a taste
HAMLET: of your quality, come, a passionate speech.
First Player: What speech, my lord?
HAMLET: I heard thee speak me a speech once, but it was
HAMLET: never acted, or, if it was, not above once, for the
HAMLET: play, I remember, pleased not the million, 'twas
HAMLET: caviare to the general: but it was--as I received
HAMLET: it, and others, whose judgments in such matters
HAMLET: cried in the top of mine--an excellent play, well
HAMLET: digested in the scenes, set down with as much
HAMLET: modesty as cunning. I remember, one said there
HAMLET: were no sallets in the lines to make the matter
HAMLET: savoury, nor no matter in the phrase that might
HAMLET: indict the author of affectation, but called it an
HAMLET: honest method, as wholesome as sweet, and by very
HAMLET: much more handsome than fine. One speech in it I
HAMLET: chiefly loved: 'twas Aeneas' tale to Dido, and
HAMLET: thereabout of it especially, where he speaks of
HAMLET: Priam's slaughter: if it live in your memory, begin
HAMLET: at this line: let me see, let me see--
HAMLET: 'The rugged Pyrrhus, like the Hyrcanian beast,'--
HAMLET: it is not so:--it begins with Pyrrhus:--
HAMLET: 'The rugged Pyrrhus, he whose sable arms,
HAMLET: Black as his purpose, did the night resemble
HAMLET: When he lay couched in the ominous horse,
HAMLET: Hath now this dread and black complexion smear'd
HAMLET: With heraldry more dismal, head to foot
HAMLET: Now is he total gules, horridly trick'd
HAMLET: With blood of fathers, mothers, daughters, sons,
HAMLET: Baked and impasted with the parching streets,
HAMLET: That lend a tyrannous and damned light
HAMLET: To their lord's murder: roasted in wrath and fire,
HAMLET: And thus o'er-sized with coagulate gore,
HAMLET: With eyes like carbuncles, the hellish Pyrrhus
HAMLET: Old grandsire Priam seeks.'
HAMLET: So, proceed you.
LORD POLONIUS: 'Fore God, my lord, well spoken, with good accent and
LORD POLONIUS: good discretion.
First Player: 'Anon he finds him
First Player: Striking too short at Greeks, his antique sword,
First Player: Rebellious to his arm, lies where it falls,
First Player: Repugnant to command: unequal match'd,
First Player: Pyrrhus at Priam drives, in rage strikes wide,
First Player: But with the whiff and wind of his fell sword
First Player: The unnerved father falls. Then senseless Ilium,
First Player: Seeming to feel this blow, with flaming top
First Player: Stoops to his base, and with a hideous crash
First Player: Takes prisoner Pyrrhus' ear: for, lo! his sword,
First Player: Which was declining on the milky head
First Player: Of reverend Priam, seem'd i' the air to stick:
First Player: So, as a painted tyrant, Pyrrhus stood,
First Player: And like a neutral to his will and matter,
First Player: Did nothing.
First Player: But, as we often see, against some storm,
First Player: A silence in the heavens, the rack stand still,
First Player: The bold winds speechless and the orb below
First Player: As hush as death, anon the dreadful thunder
First Player: Doth rend the region, so, after Pyrrhus' pause,
First Player: Aroused vengeance sets him new a-work,
First Player: And never did the Cyclops' hammers fall
First Player: On Mars's armour forged for proof eterne
First Player: With less remorse than Pyrrhus' bleeding sword
First Player: Now falls on Priam.
First Player: Out, out, thou strumpet, Fortune! All you gods,
First Player: In general synod 'take away her power,
First Player: Break all the spokes and fellies from her wheel,
First Player: And bowl the round nave down the hill of heaven,
First Player: As low as to the fiends!'
LORD POLONIUS: This is too long.
HAMLET: It shall to the barber's, with your beard. Prithee,
HAMLET: say on: he's for a jig or a tale of bawdry, or he
HAMLET: sleeps: say on: come to Hecuba.
First Player: 'But who, O, who had seen the mobled queen--'
HAMLET: 'The mobled queen?'
LORD POLONIUS: That's good, 'mobled queen' is good.
First Player: 'Run barefoot up and down, threatening the flames
First Player: With bisson rheum, a clout upon that head
First Player: Where late the diadem stood, and for a robe,
First Player: About her lank and all o'er-teemed loins,
First Player: A blanket, in the alarm of fear caught up,
First Player: Who this had seen, with tongue in venom steep'd,
First Player: 'Gainst Fortune's state would treason have
First Player: pronounced:
First Player: But if the gods themselves did see her then
First Player: When she saw Pyrrhus make malicious sport
First Player: In mincing with his sword her husband's limbs,
First Player: The instant burst of clamour that she made,
First Player: Unless things mortal move them not at all,
First Player: Would have made milch the burning eyes of heaven,
First Player: And passion in the gods.'
LORD POLONIUS: Look, whether he has not turned his colour and has
LORD POLONIUS: tears in's eyes. Pray you, no more.
HAMLET: 'Tis well: I'll have thee speak out the rest soon.
HAMLET: Good my lord, will you see the players well
HAMLET: bestowed? Do you hear, let them be well used, for
HAMLET: they are the abstract and brief chronicles of the
HAMLET: time: after your death you were better have a bad
HAMLET: epitaph than their ill report while you live.
LORD POLONIUS: My lord, I will use them according to their desert.
HAMLET: God's bodykins, man, much better: use every man
HAMLET: after his desert, and who should 'scape whipping?
HAMLET: Use them after your own honour and dignity: the less
HAMLET: they deserve, the more merit is in your bounty.
HAMLET: Take them in.
LORD POLONIUS: Come, sirs.
HAMLET: Follow him, friends: we'll hear a play to-morrow.
NARRATOR: Exit POLONIUS with all the Players but the First
HAMLET: Dost thou hear me, old friend, can you play the
HAMLET: Murder of Gonzago?
First Player: Ay, my lord.
HAMLET: We'll ha't to-morrow night. You could, for a need,
HAMLET: study a speech of some dozen or sixteen lines, which
HAMLET: I would set down and insert in't, could you not?
First Player: Ay, my lord.
HAMLET: Very well. Follow that lord, and look you mock him
HAMLET: not.
NARRATOR: Exit First Player
HAMLET: My good friends, I'll leave you till night: you are
HAMLET: welcome to Elsinore.
ROSENCRANTZ: Good my lord!
HAMLET: Ay, so, God be wi' ye,
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
HAMLET: Now I am alone.
HAMLET: O, what a rogue and peasant slave am I!
HAMLET: Is it not monstrous that this player here,
HAMLET: But in a fiction, in a dream of passion,
HAMLET: Could force his soul so to his own conceit
HAMLET: That from her working all his visage wann'd,
HAMLET: Tears in his eyes, distraction in's aspect,
HAMLET: A broken voice, and his whole function suiting
HAMLET: With forms to his conceit? and all for nothing!
HAMLET: For Hecuba!
HAMLET: What's Hecuba to him, or he to Hecuba,
HAMLET: That he should weep for her? What would he do,
HAMLET: Had he the motive and the cue for passion
HAMLET: That I have? He would drown the stage with tears
HAMLET: And cleave the general ear with horrid speech,
HAMLET: Make mad the guilty and appal the free,
HAMLET: Confound the ignorant, and amaze indeed
HAMLET: The very faculties of eyes and ears. Yet I,
HAMLET: A dull and muddy-mettled rascal, peak,
HAMLET: Like John-a-dreams, unpregnant of my cause,
HAMLET: And can say nothing, no, not for a king,
HAMLET: Upon whose property and most dear life
HAMLET: A damn'd defeat was made. Am I a coward?
HAMLET: Who calls me villain? breaks my pate across?
HAMLET: Plucks off my beard, and blows it in my face?
HAMLET: Tweaks me by the nose? gives me the lie i' the throat,
HAMLET: As deep as to the lungs? who does me this?
HAMLET: Ha!
HAMLET: 'Swounds, I should take it: for it cannot be
HAMLET: But I am pigeon-liver'd and lack gall
HAMLET: To make oppression bitter, or ere this
HAMLET: I should have fatted all the region kites
HAMLET: With this slave's offal: bloody, bawdy villain!
HAMLET: Remorseless, treacherous, lecherous, kindless villain!
HAMLET: O, vengeance!
HAMLET: Why, what an ass am I! This is most brave,
HAMLET: That I, the son of a dear father murder'd,
HAMLET: Prompted to my revenge by heaven and hell,
HAMLET: Must, like a whore, unpack my heart with words,
HAMLET: And fall a-cursing, like a very drab,
HAMLET: A scullion!
HAMLET: Fie upon't! foh! About, my brain! I have heard
HAMLET: That guilty creatures sitting at a play
HAMLET: Have by the very cunning of the scene
HAMLET: Been struck so to the soul that presently
HAMLET: They have proclaim'd their malefactions,
HAMLET: For murder, though it have no tongue, will speak
HAMLET: With most miraculous organ. I'll have these players
HAMLET: Play something like the murder of my father
HAMLET: Before mine uncle: I'll observe his looks,
HAMLET: I'll tent him to the quick: if he but blench,
HAMLET: I know my course. The spirit that I have seen
HAMLET: May be the devil: and the devil hath power
HAMLET: To assume a pleasing shape, yea, and perhaps
HAMLET: Out of my weakness and my melancholy,
HAMLET: As he is very potent with such spirits,
HAMLET: Abuses me to damn me: I'll have grounds
HAMLET: More relative than this: the play 's the thing
HAMLET: Wherein I'll catch the conscience of the king.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter KING CLAUDIUS, QUEEN GERTRUDE, POLONIUS, OPHELIA, ROSENCRANTZ, and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: And can you, by no drift of circumstance,
KING CLAUDIUS: Get from him why he puts on this confusion,
KING CLAUDIUS: Grating so harshly all his days of quiet
KING CLAUDIUS: With turbulent and dangerous lunacy?
ROSENCRANTZ: He does confess he feels himself distracted,
ROSENCRANTZ: But from what cause he will by no means speak.
GUILDENSTERN: Nor do we find him forward to be sounded,
GUILDENSTERN: But, with a crafty madness, keeps aloof,
GUILDENSTERN: When we would bring him on to some confession
GUILDENSTERN: Of his true state.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Did he receive you well?
ROSENCRANTZ: Most like a gentleman.
GUILDENSTERN: But with much forcing of his disposition.
ROSENCRANTZ: Niggard of question, but, of our demands,
ROSENCRANTZ: Most free in his reply.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Did you assay him?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: To any pastime?
ROSENCRANTZ: Madam, it so fell out, that certain players
ROSENCRANTZ: We o'er-raught on the way: of these we told him,
ROSENCRANTZ: And there did seem in him a kind of joy
ROSENCRANTZ: To hear of it: they are about the court,
ROSENCRANTZ: And, as I think, they have already order
ROSENCRANTZ: This night to play before him.
LORD POLONIUS: 'Tis most true:
LORD POLONIUS: And he beseech'd me to entreat your majesties
LORD POLONIUS: To hear and see the matter.
KING CLAUDIUS: With all my heart, and it doth much content me
KING CLAUDIUS: To hear him so inclined.
KING CLAUDIUS: Good gentlemen, give him a further edge,
KING CLAUDIUS: And drive his purpose on to these delights.
ROSENCRANTZ: We shall, my lord.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: Sweet Gertrude, leave us too,
KING CLAUDIUS: For we have closely sent for Hamlet hither,
KING CLAUDIUS: That he, as 'twere by accident, may here
KING CLAUDIUS: Affront Ophelia:
KING CLAUDIUS: Her father and myself, lawful espials,
KING CLAUDIUS: Will so bestow ourselves that, seeing, unseen,
KING CLAUDIUS: We may of their encounter frankly judge,
KING CLAUDIUS: And gather by him, as he is behaved,
KING CLAUDIUS: If 't be the affliction of his love or no
KING CLAUDIUS: That thus he suffers for.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: I shall obey you.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And for your part, Ophelia, I do wish
QUEEN GERTRUDE: That your good beauties be the happy cause
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Of Hamlet's wildness: so shall I hope your virtues
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Will bring him to his wonted way again,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: To both your honours.
OPHELIA: Madam, I wish it may.
NARRATOR: Exit QUEEN GERTRUDE
LORD POLONIUS: Ophelia, walk you here. Gracious, so please you,
LORD POLONIUS: We will bestow ourselves.
NARRATOR: To OPHELIA
LORD POLONIUS: Read on this book,
LORD POLONIUS: That show of such an exercise may colour
LORD POLONIUS: Your loneliness. We are oft to blame in this,--
LORD POLONIUS: 'Tis too much proved--that with devotion's visage
LORD POLONIUS: And pious action we do sugar o'er
LORD POLONIUS: The devil himself.
KING CLAUDIUS: [Aside]          O, 'tis too true!
KING CLAUDIUS: How smart a lash that speech doth give my conscience!
KING CLAUDIUS: The harlot's cheek, beautied with plastering art,
KING CLAUDIUS: Is not more ugly to the thing that helps it
KING CLAUDIUS: Than is my deed to my most painted word:
KING CLAUDIUS: O heavy burthen!
LORD POLONIUS: I hear him coming: let's withdraw, my lord.
NARRATOR: Exeunt KING CLAUDIUS and POLONIUS
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET
HAMLET: To be, or not to be: that is the question:
HAMLET: Whether 'tis nobler in the mind to suffer
HAMLET: The slings and arrows of outrageous fortune,
HAMLET: Or to take arms against a sea of troubles,
HAMLET: And by opposing end them? To die: to sleep,
HAMLET: No more, and by a sleep to say we end
HAMLET: The heart-ache and the thousand natural shocks
HAMLET: That flesh is heir to, 'tis a consummation
HAMLET: Devoutly to be wish'd. To die, to sleep,
HAMLET: To sleep: perchance to dream: ay, there's the rub,
HAMLET: For in that sleep of death what dreams may come
HAMLET: When we have shuffled off this mortal coil,
HAMLET: Must give us pause: there's the respect
HAMLET: That makes calamity of so long life,
HAMLET: For who would bear the whips and scorns of time,
HAMLET: The oppressor's wrong, the proud man's contumely,
HAMLET: The pangs of despised love, the law's delay,
HAMLET: The insolence of office and the spurns
HAMLET: That patient merit of the unworthy takes,
HAMLET: When he himself might his quietus make
HAMLET: With a bare bodkin? who would fardels bear,
HAMLET: To grunt and sweat under a weary life,
HAMLET: But that the dread of something after death,
HAMLET: The undiscover'd country from whose bourn
HAMLET: No traveller returns, puzzles the will
HAMLET: And makes us rather bear those ills we have
HAMLET: Than fly to others that we know not of?
HAMLET: Thus conscience does make cowards of us all,
HAMLET: And thus the native hue of resolution
HAMLET: Is sicklied o'er with the pale cast of thought,
HAMLET: And enterprises of great pith and moment
HAMLET: With this regard their currents turn awry,
HAMLET: And lose the name of action.--Soft you now!
HAMLET: The fair Ophelia! Nymph, in thy orisons
HAMLET: Be all my sins remember'd.
OPHELIA: Good my lord,
OPHELIA: How does your honour for this many a day?
HAMLET: I humbly thank you, well, well, well.
OPHELIA: My lord, I have remembrances of yours,
OPHELIA: That I have longed long to re-deliver,
OPHELIA: I pray you, now receive them.
HAMLET: No, not I,
HAMLET: I never gave you aught.
OPHELIA: My honour'd lord, you know right well you did,
OPHELIA: And, with them, words of so sweet breath composed
OPHELIA: As made the things more rich: their perfume lost,
OPHELIA: Take these again, for to the noble mind
OPHELIA: Rich gifts wax poor when givers prove unkind.
OPHELIA: There, my lord.
HAMLET: Ha, ha! are you honest?
OPHELIA: My lord?
HAMLET: Are you fair?
OPHELIA: What means your lordship?
HAMLET: That if you be honest and fair, your honesty should
HAMLET: admit no discourse to your beauty.
OPHELIA: Could beauty, my lord, have better commerce than
OPHELIA: with honesty?
HAMLET: Ay, truly, for the power of beauty will sooner
HAMLET: transform honesty from what it is to a bawd than the
HAMLET: force of honesty can translate beauty into his
HAMLET: likeness: this was sometime a paradox, but now the
HAMLET: time gives it proof. I did love you once.
OPHELIA: Indeed, my lord, you made me believe so.
HAMLET: You should not have believed me, for virtue cannot
HAMLET: so inoculate our old stock but we shall relish of
HAMLET: it: I loved you not.
OPHELIA: I was the more deceived.
HAMLET: Get thee to a nunnery: why wouldst thou be a
HAMLET: breeder of sinners? I am myself indifferent honest,
HAMLET: but yet I could accuse me of such things that it
HAMLET: were better my mother had not borne me: I am very
HAMLET: proud, revengeful, ambitious, with more offences at
HAMLET: my beck than I have thoughts to put them in,
HAMLET: imagination to give them shape, or time to act them
HAMLET: in. What should such fellows as I do crawling
HAMLET: between earth and heaven? We are arrant knaves,
HAMLET: all, believe none of us. Go thy ways to a nunnery.
HAMLET: Where's your father?
OPHELIA: At home, my lord.
HAMLET: Let the doors be shut upon him, that he may play the
HAMLET: fool no where but in's own house. Farewell.
OPHELIA: O, help him, you sweet heavens!
HAMLET: If thou dost marry, I'll give thee this plague for
HAMLET: thy dowry: be thou as chaste as ice, as pure as
HAMLET: snow, thou shalt not escape calumny. Get thee to a
HAMLET: nunnery, go: farewell. Or, if thou wilt needs
HAMLET: marry, marry a fool, for wise men know well enough
HAMLET: what monsters you make of them. To a nunnery, go,
HAMLET: and quickly too. Farewell.
OPHELIA: O heavenly powers, restore him!
HAMLET: I have heard of your paintings too, well enough, God
HAMLET: has given you one face, and you make yourselves
HAMLET: another: you jig, you amble, and you lisp, and
HAMLET: nick-name God's creatures, and make your wantonness
HAMLET: your ignorance. Go to, I'll no more on't, it hath
HAMLET: made me mad. I say, we will have no more marriages:
HAMLET: those that are married already, all but one, shall
HAMLET: live, the rest shall keep as they are. To a
HAMLET: nunnery, go.
NARRATOR: Exit
OPHELIA: O, what a noble mind is here o'erthrown!
OPHELIA: The courtier's, soldier's, scholar's, eye, tongue, sword,
OPHELIA: The expectancy and rose of the fair state,
OPHELIA: The glass of fashion and the mould of form,
OPHELIA: The observed of all observers, quite, quite down!
OPHELIA: And I, of ladies most deject and wretched,
OPHELIA: That suck'd the honey of his music vows,
OPHELIA: Now see that noble and most sovereign reason,
OPHELIA: Like sweet bells jangled, out of tune and harsh,
OPHELIA: That unmatch'd form and feature of blown youth
OPHELIA: Blasted with ecstasy: O, woe is me,
OPHELIA: To have seen what I have seen, see what I see!

KING CLAUDIUS: Love! his affections do not that way tend,

KING CLAUDIUS: O'er which his melancholy sits on brood,

KING CLAUDIUS: I have in quick determination

KING CLAUDIUS: Madness in great ones must not unwatch'd go.

NARRATOR: SCENE II. A hall in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET and Players
HAMLET: Speak the speech, I pray you, as I pronounced it to
HAMLET: you, trippingly on the tongue: but if you mouth it,
HAMLET: as many of your players do, I had as lief the
HAMLET: town-crier spoke my lines. Nor do not saw the air
HAMLET: too much with your hand, thus, but use all gently,
HAMLET: for in the very torrent, tempest, and, as I may say,
HAMLET: the whirlwind of passion, you must acquire and beget
HAMLET: a temperance that may give it smoothness. O, it
HAMLET: offends me to the soul to hear a robustious
HAMLET: periwig-pated fellow tear a passion to tatters, to
HAMLET: very rags, to split the ears of the groundlings, who
HAMLET: for the most part are capable of nothing but
HAMLET: inexplicable dumbshows and noise: I would have such
HAMLET: a fellow whipped for o'erdoing Termagant, it
HAMLET: out-herods Herod: pray you, avoid it.
First Player: I warrant your honour.
HAMLET: Be not too tame neither, but let your own discretion
HAMLET: be your tutor: suit the action to the word, the
HAMLET: word to the action, with this special o'erstep not
HAMLET: the modesty of nature: for any thing so overdone is
HAMLET: from the purpose of playing, whose end, both at the
HAMLET: first and now, was and is, to hold, as 'twere, the
HAMLET: mirror up to nature, to show virtue her own feature,
HAMLET: scorn her own image, and the very age and body of
HAMLET: the time his form and pressure. Now this overdone,
HAMLET: or come tardy off, though it make the unskilful
HAMLET: laugh, cannot but make the judicious grieve, the
HAMLET: censure of the which one must in your allowance
HAMLET: o'erweigh a whole theatre of others. O, there be
HAMLET: players that I have seen play, and heard others
HAMLET: praise, and that highly, not to speak it profanely,
HAMLET: that, neither having the accent of Christians nor

HAMLET: strutted and bellowed that I have thought some of
HAMLET: nature's journeymen had made men and not made them
HAMLET: well, they imitated humanity so abominably.
First Player: I hope we have reformed that indifferently with us,
First Player: sir.
HAMLET: O, reform it altogether. And let those that play

HAMLET: for there be of them that will themselves laugh, to
HAMLET: set on some quantity of barren spectators to laugh
HAMLET: too, though, in the mean time, some necessary
HAMLET: question of the play be then to be considered:
HAMLET: that's villanous, and shows a most pitiful ambition
HAMLET: in the fool that uses it. Go, make you ready.

HAMLET: And could of men distinguish, her election

HAMLET: Even with the very comment of thy soul

HAMLET: And my imaginations are as foul

HAMLET: In censure of his seeming.

HORATIO: If he steal aught the whilst this play is playing,
HORATIO: And 'scape detecting, I will pay the theft.

HAMLET: Get you a place.
NARRATOR: Danish march. A flourish. Enter KING CLAUDIUS,  QUEEN GERTRUDE, POLONIUS, OPHELIA, ROSENCRANTZ, GUILDENSTERN, and others

HAMLET: No, nor mine now.

NARRATOR: Lying down at OPHELIA's feet

HAMLET: That's a fair thought to lie between maids' legs.

HAMLET: Nothing.

HAMLET: Who, I?
OPHELIA: Ay, my lord.

NARRATOR: Hautboys play. The dumb-show enters
NARRATOR: Enter a King and a Queen very lovingly, the Queen  embracing him, and he her. She kneels, and makes  show of protestation unto him. He takes her up,  and declines his head upon her neck: lays him down  upon a bank of flowers: she, seeing him asleep,  leaves him. Anon comes in a fellow, takes off his  crown, kisses it, and pours poison in the King's  ears, and exit. The Queen returns, finds the King  dead, and makes passionate action. The Poisoner,  with some two or three Mutes, comes in again,  seeming to lament with her. The dead body is  carried away. The Poisoner wooes the Queen with  gifts: she seems loath and unwilling awhile, but in the end accepts his love
NARRATOR: Exeunt
OPHELIA: What means this, my lord?

NARRATOR: Enter Prologue
HAMLET: We shall know by this fellow: the players cannot
HAMLET: keep counsel, they'll tell all.

NARRATOR: Exit
HAMLET: Is this a prologue, or the posy of a ring?
OPHELIA: 'Tis brief, my lord.
HAMLET: As woman's love.
NARRATOR: Enter two Players, King and Queen
Player King: Full thirty times hath Phoebus' cart gone round
Player King: Neptune's salt wash and Tellus' orbed ground,
Player King: And thirty dozen moons with borrow'd sheen
Player King: About the world have times twelve thirties been,
Player King: Since love our hearts and Hymen did our hands
Player King: Unite commutual in most sacred bands.
Player Queen: So many journeys may the sun and moon
Player Queen: Make us again count o'er ere love be done!
Player Queen: But, woe is me, you are so sick of late,
Player Queen: So far from cheer and from your former state,
Player Queen: That I distrust you. Yet, though I distrust,
Player Queen: Discomfort you, my lord, it nothing must:
Player Queen: For women's fear and love holds quantity,
Player Queen: In neither aught, or in extremity.
Player Queen: Now, what my love is, proof hath made you know,
Player Queen: And as my love is sized, my fear is so:
Player Queen: Where love is great, the littlest doubts are fear,
Player Queen: Where little fears grow great, great love grows there.
Player King: 'Faith, I must leave thee, love, and shortly too,
Player King: My operant powers their functions leave to do:
Player King: And thou shalt live in this fair world behind,
Player King: Honour'd, beloved, and haply one as kind
Player King: For husband shalt thou--
Player Queen: O, confound the rest!
Player Queen: Such love must needs be treason in my breast:
Player Queen: In second husband let me be accurst!
Player Queen: None wed the second but who kill'd the first.
HAMLET: [Aside]  Wormwood, wormwood.
Player Queen: The instances that second marriage move
Player Queen: Are base respects of thrift, but none of love:
Player Queen: A second time I kill my husband dead,
Player Queen: When second husband kisses me in bed.
Player King: I do believe you think what now you speak,
Player King: But what we do determine oft we break.
Player King: Purpose is but the slave to memory,
Player King: Of violent birth, but poor validity,
Player King: Which now, like fruit unripe, sticks on the tree,
Player King: But fall, unshaken, when they mellow be.
Player King: Most necessary 'tis that we forget
Player King: To pay ourselves what to ourselves is debt:
Player King: What to ourselves in passion we propose,
Player King: The passion ending, doth the purpose lose.
Player King: The violence of either grief or joy
Player King: Their own enactures with themselves destroy:
Player King: Where joy most revels, grief doth most lament,
Player King: Grief joys, joy grieves, on slender accident.
Player King: This world is not for aye, nor 'tis not strange
Player King: That even our loves should with our fortunes change,
Player King: For 'tis a question left us yet to prove,
Player King: Whether love lead fortune, or else fortune love.
Player King: The great man down, you mark his favourite flies,
Player King: The poor advanced makes friends of enemies.
Player King: And hitherto doth love on fortune tend,
Player King: For who not needs shall never lack a friend,
Player King: And who in want a hollow friend doth try,
Player King: Directly seasons him his enemy.
Player King: But, orderly to end where I begun,
Player King: Our wills and fates do so contrary run
Player King: That our devices still are overthrown,
Player King: Our thoughts are ours, their ends none of our own:
Player King: So think thou wilt no second husband wed,
Player King: But die thy thoughts when thy first lord is dead.
Player Queen: Nor earth to me give food, nor heaven light!
Player Queen: Sport and repose lock from me day and night!
Player Queen: To desperation turn my trust and hope!
Player Queen: An anchor's cheer in prison be my scope!
Player Queen: Each opposite that blanks the face of joy

Player Queen: Both here and hence pursue me lasting strife,
Player Queen: If, once a widow, ever I be wife!
HAMLET: If she should break it now!
Player King: 'Tis deeply sworn. Sweet, leave me here awhile,
Player King: My spirits grow dull, and fain I would beguile
Player King: The tedious day with sleep.

Player Queen: And never come mischance between us twain!

HAMLET: Madam, how like you this play?

HAMLET: O, but she'll keep her word.

HAMLET: Tis now the very witching time of night,

NARRATOR: SCENE III. A room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter KING CLAUDIUS, ROSENCRANTZ, and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: I like him not, nor stands it safe with us
KING CLAUDIUS: To let his madness range. Therefore prepare you,
KING CLAUDIUS: I your commission will forthwith dispatch,
KING CLAUDIUS: And he to England shall along with you:
KING CLAUDIUS: The terms of our estate may not endure
KING CLAUDIUS: Hazard so dangerous as doth hourly grow
KING CLAUDIUS: Out of his lunacies.
GUILDENSTERN: We will ourselves provide:
GUILDENSTERN: Most holy and religious fear it is
GUILDENSTERN: To keep those many many bodies safe
GUILDENSTERN: That live and feed upon your majesty.
ROSENCRANTZ: The single and peculiar life is bound,
ROSENCRANTZ: With all the strength and armour of the mind,
ROSENCRANTZ: To keep itself from noyance, but much more
ROSENCRANTZ: That spirit upon whose weal depend and rest
ROSENCRANTZ: The lives of many. The cease of majesty
ROSENCRANTZ: Dies not alone, but, like a gulf, doth draw
ROSENCRANTZ: What's near it with it: it is a massy wheel,
ROSENCRANTZ: Fix'd on the summit of the highest mount,
ROSENCRANTZ: To whose huge spokes ten thousand lesser things
ROSENCRANTZ: Are mortised and adjoin'd, which, when it falls,
ROSENCRANTZ: Each small annexment, petty consequence,
ROSENCRANTZ: Attends the boisterous ruin. Never alone
ROSENCRANTZ: Did the king sigh, but with a general groan.
KING CLAUDIUS: Arm you, I pray you, to this speedy voyage,
KING CLAUDIUS: For we will fetters put upon this fear,
KING CLAUDIUS: Which now goes too free-footed.
GUILDENSTERN: We will haste us.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
NARRATOR: Enter POLONIUS
LORD POLONIUS: My lord, he's going to his mother's closet:
LORD POLONIUS: Behind the arras I'll convey myself,
LORD POLONIUS: To hear the process, and warrant she'll tax him home:
LORD POLONIUS: And, as you said, and wisely was it said,
LORD POLONIUS: 'Tis meet that some more audience than a mother,
LORD POLONIUS: Since nature makes them partial, should o'erhear
LORD POLONIUS: The speech, of vantage. Fare you well, my liege:
LORD POLONIUS: I'll call upon you ere you go to bed,
LORD POLONIUS: And tell you what I know.
KING CLAUDIUS: Thanks, dear my lord.
NARRATOR: Exit POLONIUS
KING CLAUDIUS: O, my offence is rank it smells to heaven,
KING CLAUDIUS: It hath the primal eldest curse upon't,
KING CLAUDIUS: A brother's murder. Pray can I not,
KING CLAUDIUS: Though inclination be as sharp as will:
KING CLAUDIUS: My stronger guilt defeats my strong intent,
KING CLAUDIUS: And, like a man to double business bound,
KING CLAUDIUS: I stand in pause where I shall first begin,
KING CLAUDIUS: And both neglect. What if this cursed hand
KING CLAUDIUS: Were thicker than itself with brother's blood,
KING CLAUDIUS: Is there not rain enough in the sweet heavens
KING CLAUDIUS: To wash it white as snow? Whereto serves mercy
KING CLAUDIUS: But to confront the visage of offence?
KING CLAUDIUS: And what's in prayer but this two-fold force,
KING CLAUDIUS: To be forestalled ere we come to fall,
KING CLAUDIUS: Or pardon'd being down? Then I'll look up,
KING CLAUDIUS: My fault is past. But, O, what form of prayer
KING CLAUDIUS: Can serve my turn? 'Forgive me my foul murder'?
KING CLAUDIUS: That cannot be, since I am still possess'd
KING CLAUDIUS: Of those effects for which I did the murder,
KING CLAUDIUS: My crown, mine own ambition and my queen.
KING CLAUDIUS: May one be pardon'd and retain the offence?
KING CLAUDIUS: In the corrupted currents of this world
KING CLAUDIUS: Offence's gilded hand may shove by justice,
KING CLAUDIUS: And oft 'tis seen the wicked prize itself
KING CLAUDIUS: Buys out the law: but 'tis not so above,
KING CLAUDIUS: There is no shuffling, there the action lies
KING CLAUDIUS: In his true nature, and we ourselves compell'd,
KING CLAUDIUS: Even to the teeth and forehead of our faults,
KING CLAUDIUS: To give in evidence. What then? what rests?
KING CLAUDIUS: Try what repentance can: what can it not?
KING CLAUDIUS: Yet what can it when one can not repent?
KING CLAUDIUS: O wretched state! O bosom black as death!
KING CLAUDIUS: O limed soul, that, struggling to be free,
KING CLAUDIUS: Art more engaged! Help, angels! Make assay!
KING CLAUDIUS: Bow, stubborn knees, and, heart with strings of steel,
KING CLAUDIUS: Be soft as sinews of the newborn babe!
KING CLAUDIUS: All may be well.
NARRATOR: Retires and kneels
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET
HAMLET: Now might I do it pat, now he is praying,
HAMLET: And now I'll do't. And so he goes to heaven,
HAMLET: And so am I revenged. That would be scann'd:
HAMLET: A villain kills my father, and for that,
HAMLET: I, his sole son, do this same villain send
HAMLET: To heaven.
HAMLET: O, this is hire and salary, not revenge.
HAMLET: He took my father grossly, full of bread,
HAMLET: With all his crimes broad blown, as flush as May,
HAMLET: And how his audit stands who knows save heaven?
HAMLET: But in our circumstance and course of thought,
HAMLET: 'Tis heavy with him: and am I then revenged,
HAMLET: To take him in the purging of his soul,
HAMLET: When he is fit and season'd for his passage?
HAMLET: No!
HAMLET: Up, sword, and know thou a more horrid hent:
HAMLET: When he is drunk asleep, or in his rage,
HAMLET: Or in the incestuous pleasure of his bed,
HAMLET: At gaming, swearing, or about some act
HAMLET: That has no relish of salvation in't,
HAMLET: Then trip him, that his heels may kick at heaven,
HAMLET: And that his soul may be as damn'd and black
HAMLET: As hell, whereto it goes. My mother stays:
HAMLET: This physic but prolongs thy sickly days.
NARRATOR: Exit
KING CLAUDIUS: [Rising]  My words fly up, my thoughts remain below:
KING CLAUDIUS: Words without thoughts never to heaven go.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. The Queen's closet.
NARRATOR: Enter QUEEN GERTRUDE and POLONIUS
LORD POLONIUS: He will come straight. Look you lay home to him:
LORD POLONIUS: Tell him his pranks have been too broad to bear with,
LORD POLONIUS: And that your grace hath screen'd and stood between
LORD POLONIUS: Much heat and him. I'll sconce me even here.
LORD POLONIUS: Pray you, be round with him.
HAMLET: [Within]  Mother, mother, mother!
QUEEN GERTRUDE: I'll warrant you,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Fear me not: withdraw, I hear him coming.
NARRATOR: POLONIUS hides behind the arras
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET
HAMLET: Now, mother, what's the matter?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Hamlet, thou hast thy father much offended.
HAMLET: Mother, you have my father much offended.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Come, come, you answer with an idle tongue.
HAMLET: Go, go, you question with a wicked tongue.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Why, how now, Hamlet!
HAMLET: What's the matter now?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Have you forgot me?
HAMLET: No, by the rood, not so:
HAMLET: You are the queen, your husband's brother's wife,
HAMLET: And--would it were not so!--you are my mother.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Nay, then, I'll set those to you that can speak.
HAMLET: Come, come, and sit you down, you shall not budge,
HAMLET: You go not till I set you up a glass
HAMLET: Where you may see the inmost part of you.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: What wilt thou do? thou wilt not murder me?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Help, help, ho!
LORD POLONIUS: [Behind]  What, ho! help, help, help!
HAMLET: [Drawing]  How now! a rat? Dead, for a ducat, dead!
NARRATOR: Makes a pass through the arras
LORD POLONIUS: [Behind]  O, I am slain!
NARRATOR: Falls and dies
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O me, what hast thou done?
HAMLET: Nay, I know not:
HAMLET: Is it the king?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O, what a rash and bloody deed is this!
HAMLET: A bloody deed! almost as bad, good mother,
HAMLET: As kill a king, and marry with his brother.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: As kill a king!
HAMLET: Ay, lady, 'twas my word.
NARRATOR: Lifts up the array and discovers POLONIUS
HAMLET: Thou wretched, rash, intruding fool, farewell!
HAMLET: I took thee for thy better: take thy fortune,
HAMLET: Thou find'st to be too busy is some danger.
HAMLET: Leave wringing of your hands: peace! sit you down,
HAMLET: And let me wring your heart, for so I shall,
HAMLET: If it be made of penetrable stuff,
HAMLET: If damned custom have not brass'd it so
HAMLET: That it is proof and bulwark against sense.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: What have I done, that thou darest wag thy tongue
QUEEN GERTRUDE: In noise so rude against me?
HAMLET: Such an act
HAMLET: That blurs the grace and blush of modesty,
HAMLET: Calls virtue hypocrite, takes off the rose
HAMLET: From the fair forehead of an innocent love
HAMLET: And sets a blister there, makes marriage-vows
HAMLET: As false as dicers' oaths: O, such a deed
HAMLET: As from the body of contraction plucks
HAMLET: The very soul, and sweet religion makes
HAMLET: A rhapsody of words: heaven's face doth glow:
HAMLET: Yea, this solidity and compound mass,
HAMLET: With tristful visage, as against the doom,
HAMLET: Is thought-sick at the act.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Ay me, what act,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: That roars so loud, and thunders in the index?
HAMLET: Look here, upon this picture, and on this,
HAMLET: The counterfeit presentment of two brothers.
HAMLET: See, what a grace was seated on this brow,
HAMLET: Hyperion's curls, the front of Jove himself,
HAMLET: An eye like Mars, to threaten and command,
HAMLET: A station like the herald Mercury
HAMLET: New-lighted on a heaven-kissing hill,
HAMLET: A combination and a form indeed,
HAMLET: Where every god did seem to set his seal,
HAMLET: To give the world assurance of a man:
HAMLET: This was your husband. Look you now, what follows:
HAMLET: Here is your husband, like a mildew'd ear,
HAMLET: Blasting his wholesome brother. Have you eyes?
HAMLET: Could you on this fair mountain leave to feed,
HAMLET: And batten on this moor? Ha! have you eyes?
HAMLET: You cannot call it love, for at your age
HAMLET: The hey-day in the blood is tame, it's humble,
HAMLET: And waits upon the judgment: and what judgment
HAMLET: Would step from this to this? Sense, sure, you have,
HAMLET: Else could you not have motion, but sure, that sense
HAMLET: Is apoplex'd, for madness would not err,
HAMLET: Nor sense to ecstasy was ne'er so thrall'd
HAMLET: But it reserved some quantity of choice,
HAMLET: To serve in such a difference. What devil was't
HAMLET: That thus hath cozen'd you at hoodman-blind?
HAMLET: Eyes without feeling, feeling without sight,
HAMLET: Ears without hands or eyes, smelling sans all,
HAMLET: Or but a sickly part of one true sense
HAMLET: Could not so mope.
HAMLET: O shame! where is thy blush? Rebellious hell,
HAMLET: If thou canst mutine in a matron's bones,
HAMLET: To flaming youth let virtue be as wax,
HAMLET: And melt in her own fire: proclaim no shame
HAMLET: When the compulsive ardour gives the charge,
HAMLET: Since frost itself as actively doth burn
HAMLET: And reason panders will.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O Hamlet, speak no more:
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Thou turn'st mine eyes into my very soul,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And there I see such black and grained spots
QUEEN GERTRUDE: As will not leave their tinct.
HAMLET: Nay, but to live
HAMLET: In the rank sweat of an enseamed bed,
HAMLET: Stew'd in corruption, honeying and making love
HAMLET: Over the nasty sty,--
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O, speak to me no more,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: These words, like daggers, enter in mine ears,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: No more, sweet Hamlet!
HAMLET: A murderer and a villain,
HAMLET: A slave that is not twentieth part the tithe
HAMLET: Of your precedent lord, a vice of kings,
HAMLET: A cutpurse of the empire and the rule,
HAMLET: That from a shelf the precious diadem stole,
HAMLET: And put it in his pocket!
QUEEN GERTRUDE: No more!
HAMLET: A king of shreds and patches,--
NARRATOR: Enter Ghost
HAMLET: Save me, and hover o'er me with your wings,
HAMLET: You heavenly guards! What would your gracious figure?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alas, he's mad!
HAMLET: Do you not come your tardy son to chide,
HAMLET: That, lapsed in time and passion, lets go by
HAMLET: The important acting of your dread command? O, say!
Ghost: Do not forget: this visitation
Ghost: Is but to whet thy almost blunted purpose.
Ghost: But, look, amazement on thy mother sits:
Ghost: O, step between her and her fighting soul:
Ghost: Conceit in weakest bodies strongest works:
Ghost: Speak to her, Hamlet.
HAMLET: How is it with you, lady?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alas, how is't with you,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: That you do bend your eye on vacancy
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And with the incorporal air do hold discourse?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Forth at your eyes your spirits wildly peep,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And, as the sleeping soldiers in the alarm,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Your bedded hair, like life in excrements,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Starts up, and stands on end. O gentle son,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Upon the heat and flame of thy distemper
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Sprinkle cool patience. Whereon do you look?
HAMLET: On him, on him! Look you, how pale he glares!
HAMLET: His form and cause conjoin'd, preaching to stones,
HAMLET: Would make them capable. Do not look upon me,
HAMLET: Lest with this piteous action you convert
HAMLET: My stern effects: then what I have to do
HAMLET: Will want true colour, tears perchance for blood.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: To whom do you speak this?
HAMLET: Do you see nothing there?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Nothing at all, yet all that is I see.
HAMLET: Nor did you nothing hear?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: No, nothing but ourselves.
HAMLET: Why, look you there! look, how it steals away!
HAMLET: My father, in his habit as he lived!
HAMLET: Look, where he goes, even now, out at the portal!
NARRATOR: Exit Ghost
QUEEN GERTRUDE: This the very coinage of your brain:
QUEEN GERTRUDE: This bodiless creation ecstasy
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Is very cunning in.
HAMLET: Ecstasy!
HAMLET: My pulse, as yours, doth temperately keep time,
HAMLET: And makes as healthful music: it is not madness
HAMLET: That I have utter'd: bring me to the test,
HAMLET: And I the matter will re-word, which madness
HAMLET: Would gambol from. Mother, for love of grace,
HAMLET: Lay not that mattering unction to your soul,
HAMLET: That not your trespass, but my madness speaks:
HAMLET: It will but skin and film the ulcerous place,
HAMLET: Whilst rank corruption, mining all within,
HAMLET: Infects unseen. Confess yourself to heaven,
HAMLET: Repent what's past, avoid what is to come,
HAMLET: And do not spread the compost on the weeds,
HAMLET: To make them ranker. Forgive me this my virtue,
HAMLET: For in the fatness of these pursy times
HAMLET: Virtue itself of vice must pardon beg,
HAMLET: Yea, curb and woo for leave to do him good.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O Hamlet, thou hast cleft my heart in twain.
HAMLET: O, throw away the worser part of it,
HAMLET: And live the purer with the other half.
HAMLET: Good night: but go not to mine uncle's bed,
HAMLET: Assume a virtue, if you have it not.
HAMLET: That monster, custom, who all sense doth eat,
HAMLET: Of habits devil, is angel yet in this,
HAMLET: That to the use of actions fair and good
HAMLET: He likewise gives a frock or livery,
HAMLET: That aptly is put on. Refrain to-night,
HAMLET: And that shall lend a kind of easiness
HAMLET: To the next abstinence: the next more easy,
HAMLET: For use almost can change the stamp of nature,
HAMLET: And either [         ] the devil, or throw him out
HAMLET: With wondrous potency. Once more, good night:
HAMLET: And when you are desirous to be bless'd,
HAMLET: I'll blessing beg of you. For this same lord,
NARRATOR: Pointing to POLONIUS
HAMLET: I do repent: but heaven hath pleased it so,
HAMLET: To punish me with this and this with me,
HAMLET: That I must be their scourge and minister.
HAMLET: I will bestow him, and will answer well
HAMLET: The death I gave him. So, again, good night.
HAMLET: I must be cruel, only to be kind:
HAMLET: Thus bad begins and worse remains behind.
HAMLET: One word more, good lady.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: What shall I do?
HAMLET: Not this, by no means, that I bid you do:
HAMLET: Let the bloat king tempt you again to bed,
HAMLET: Pinch wanton on your cheek, call you his mouse,
HAMLET: And let him, for a pair of reechy kisses,
HAMLET: Or paddling in your neck with his damn'd fingers,
HAMLET: Make you to ravel all this matter out,
HAMLET: That I essentially am not in madness,
HAMLET: But mad in craft. 'Twere good you let him know,
HAMLET: For who, that's but a queen, fair, sober, wise,
HAMLET: Would from a paddock, from a bat, a gib,
HAMLET: Such dear concernings hide? who would do so?
HAMLET: No, in despite of sense and secrecy,
HAMLET: Unpeg the basket on the house's top.
HAMLET: Let the birds fly, and, like the famous ape,
HAMLET: To try conclusions, in the basket creep,
HAMLET: And break your own neck down.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Be thou assured, if words be made of breath,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And breath of life, I have no life to breathe
QUEEN GERTRUDE: What thou hast said to me.
HAMLET: I must to England, you know that?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alack,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: I had forgot: 'tis so concluded on.
HAMLET: There's letters seal'd: and my two schoolfellows,
HAMLET: Whom I will trust as I will adders fang'd,
HAMLET: They bear the mandate, they must sweep my way,
HAMLET: And marshal me to knavery. Let it work,
HAMLET: For 'tis the sport to have the engineer
HAMLET: Hoist with his own petard: and 't shall go hard
HAMLET: But I will delve one yard below their mines,
HAMLET: And blow them at the moon: O, 'tis most sweet,
HAMLET: When in one line two crafts directly meet.
HAMLET: This man shall set me packing:
HAMLET: I'll lug the guts into the neighbour room.
HAMLET: Mother, good night. Indeed this counsellor
HAMLET: Is now most still, most secret and most grave,
HAMLET: Who was in life a foolish prating knave.
HAMLET: Come, sir, to draw toward an end with you.
HAMLET: Good night, mother.
HAMLET: Exeunt severally, HAMLET dragging in POLONIUS
HAMLET: ACT IV
HAMLET: SCENE I. A room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter KING CLAUDIUS, QUEEN GERTRUDE, ROSENCRANTZ, and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: There's matter in these sighs, these profound heaves:
KING CLAUDIUS: You must translate: 'tis fit we understand them.
KING CLAUDIUS: Where is your son?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Bestow this place on us a little while.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Ah, my good lord, what have I seen to-night!
KING CLAUDIUS: What, Gertrude? How does Hamlet?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Mad as the sea and wind, when both contend
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Which is the mightier: in his lawless fit,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Behind the arras hearing something stir,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Whips out his rapier, cries, 'A rat, a rat!'
QUEEN GERTRUDE: And, in this brainish apprehension, kills
QUEEN GERTRUDE: The unseen good old man.
KING CLAUDIUS: O heavy deed!
KING CLAUDIUS: It had been so with us, had we been there:
KING CLAUDIUS: His liberty is full of threats to all,
KING CLAUDIUS: To you yourself, to us, to every one.
KING CLAUDIUS: Alas, how shall this bloody deed be answer'd?
KING CLAUDIUS: It will be laid to us, whose providence
KING CLAUDIUS: Should have kept short, restrain'd and out of haunt,
KING CLAUDIUS: This mad young man: but so much was our love,
KING CLAUDIUS: We would not understand what was most fit,
KING CLAUDIUS: But, like the owner of a foul disease,
KING CLAUDIUS: To keep it from divulging, let it feed
KING CLAUDIUS: Even on the pith of Life. Where is he gone?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: To draw apart the body he hath kill'd:
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O'er whom his very madness, like some ore
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Among a mineral of metals base,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Shows itself pure, he weeps for what is done.
KING CLAUDIUS: O Gertrude, come away!
KING CLAUDIUS: The sun no sooner shall the mountains touch,
KING CLAUDIUS: But we will ship him hence: and this vile deed
KING CLAUDIUS: We must, with all our majesty and skill,
KING CLAUDIUS: Both countenance and excuse. Ho, Guildenstern!
NARRATOR: Re-enter ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: Friends both, go join you with some further aid:
KING CLAUDIUS: Hamlet in madness hath Polonius slain,
KING CLAUDIUS: And from his mother's closet hath he dragg'd him:
KING CLAUDIUS: Go seek him out, speak fair, and bring the body
KING CLAUDIUS: Into the chapel. I pray you, haste in this.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: Come, Gertrude, we'll call up our wisest friends,
KING CLAUDIUS: And let them know, both what we mean to do,
KING CLAUDIUS: And what's untimely done. O, come away!
KING CLAUDIUS: My soul is full of discord and dismay.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Another room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET
HAMLET: Safely stowed.
HAMLET: ROSENCRANTZ:
HAMLET: GUILDENSTERN:
HAMLET: [Within]  Hamlet! Lord Hamlet!
HAMLET: What noise? who calls on Hamlet?
HAMLET: O, here they come.
NARRATOR: Enter ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
ROSENCRANTZ: What have you done, my lord, with the dead body?
HAMLET: Compounded it with dust, whereto 'tis kin.
ROSENCRANTZ: Tell us where 'tis, that we may take it thence
ROSENCRANTZ: And bear it to the chapel.
HAMLET: Do not believe it.
ROSENCRANTZ: Believe what?
HAMLET: That I can keep your counsel and not mine own.
HAMLET: Besides, to be demanded of a sponge! what
HAMLET: replication should be made by the son of a king?
ROSENCRANTZ: Take you me for a sponge, my lord?
HAMLET: Ay, sir, that soaks up the king's countenance, his
HAMLET: rewards, his authorities. But such officers do the
HAMLET: king best service in the end: he keeps them, like
HAMLET: an ape, in the corner of his jaw, first mouthed, to
HAMLET: be last swallowed: when he needs what you have
HAMLET: gleaned, it is but squeezing you, and, sponge, you
HAMLET: shall be dry again.
ROSENCRANTZ: I understand you not, my lord.
HAMLET: I am glad of it: a knavish speech sleeps in a
HAMLET: foolish ear.
ROSENCRANTZ: My lord, you must tell us where the body is, and go
ROSENCRANTZ: with us to the king.
HAMLET: The body is with the king, but the king is not with
HAMLET: the body. The king is a thing--
GUILDENSTERN: A thing, my lord!
HAMLET: Of nothing: bring me to him. Hide fox, and all after.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Another room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter KING CLAUDIUS, attended
KING CLAUDIUS: I have sent to seek him, and to find the body.
KING CLAUDIUS: How dangerous is it that this man goes loose!
KING CLAUDIUS: Yet must not we put the strong law on him:
KING CLAUDIUS: He's loved of the distracted multitude,
KING CLAUDIUS: Who like not in their judgment, but their eyes,
KING CLAUDIUS: And where tis so, the offender's scourge is weigh'd,
KING CLAUDIUS: But never the offence. To bear all smooth and even,
KING CLAUDIUS: This sudden sending him away must seem
KING CLAUDIUS: Deliberate pause: diseases desperate grown
KING CLAUDIUS: By desperate appliance are relieved,
KING CLAUDIUS: Or not at all.
NARRATOR: Enter ROSENCRANTZ
KING CLAUDIUS: How now! what hath befall'n?
ROSENCRANTZ: Where the dead body is bestow'd, my lord,
ROSENCRANTZ: We cannot get from him.
KING CLAUDIUS: But where is he?
ROSENCRANTZ: Without, my lord, guarded, to know your pleasure.
KING CLAUDIUS: Bring him before us.
ROSENCRANTZ: Ho, Guildenstern! bring in my lord.
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: Now, Hamlet, where's Polonius?
HAMLET: At supper.
KING CLAUDIUS: At supper! where?
HAMLET: Not where he eats, but where he is eaten: a certain
HAMLET: convocation of politic worms are e'en at him. Your
HAMLET: worm is your only emperor for diet: we fat all
HAMLET: creatures else to fat us, and we fat ourselves for
HAMLET: maggots: your fat king and your lean beggar is but
HAMLET: variable service, two dishes, but to one table:
HAMLET: that's the end.
KING CLAUDIUS: Alas, alas!
HAMLET: A man may fish with the worm that hath eat of a
HAMLET: king, and cat of the fish that hath fed of that worm.
KING CLAUDIUS: What dost you mean by this?
HAMLET: Nothing but to show you how a king may go a
HAMLET: progress through the guts of a beggar.
KING CLAUDIUS: Where is Polonius?
HAMLET: In heaven, send hither to see: if your messenger
HAMLET: find him not there, seek him i' the other place
HAMLET: yourself. But indeed, if you find him not within
HAMLET: this month, you shall nose him as you go up the
HAMLET: stairs into the lobby.
KING CLAUDIUS: Go seek him there.
NARRATOR: To some Attendants
HAMLET: He will stay till ye come.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Attendants
KING CLAUDIUS: Hamlet, this deed, for thine especial safety,--
KING CLAUDIUS: Which we do tender, as we dearly grieve
KING CLAUDIUS: For that which thou hast done,--must send thee hence
KING CLAUDIUS: With fiery quickness: therefore prepare thyself,
KING CLAUDIUS: The bark is ready, and the wind at help,
KING CLAUDIUS: The associates tend, and every thing is bent
KING CLAUDIUS: For England.
HAMLET: For England!
KING CLAUDIUS: Ay, Hamlet.
HAMLET: Good.
KING CLAUDIUS: So is it, if thou knew'st our purposes.
HAMLET: I see a cherub that sees them. But, come, for
HAMLET: England! Farewell, dear mother.
KING CLAUDIUS: Thy loving father, Hamlet.
HAMLET: My mother: father and mother is man and wife, man
HAMLET: and wife is one flesh, and so, my mother. Come, for England!
NARRATOR: Exit
KING CLAUDIUS: Follow him at foot, tempt him with speed aboard,
KING CLAUDIUS: Delay it not, I'll have him hence to-night:
KING CLAUDIUS: Away! for every thing is seal'd and done
KING CLAUDIUS: That else leans on the affair: pray you, make haste.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ROSENCRANTZ and GUILDENSTERN
KING CLAUDIUS: And, England, if my love thou hold'st at aught--
KING CLAUDIUS: As my great power thereof may give thee sense,
KING CLAUDIUS: Since yet thy cicatrice looks raw and red
KING CLAUDIUS: After the Danish sword, and thy free awe
KING CLAUDIUS: Pays homage to us--thou mayst not coldly set
KING CLAUDIUS: Our sovereign process, which imports at full,
KING CLAUDIUS: By letters congruing to that effect,
KING CLAUDIUS: The present death of Hamlet. Do it, England,
KING CLAUDIUS: For like the hectic in my blood he rages,
KING CLAUDIUS: And thou must cure me: till I know 'tis done,
KING CLAUDIUS: Howe'er my haps, my joys were ne'er begun.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. A plain in Denmark.
NARRATOR: Enter FORTINBRAS, a Captain, and Soldiers, marching
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: Go, captain, from me greet the Danish king,
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: Tell him that, by his licence, Fortinbras
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: Craves the conveyance of a promised march
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: Over his kingdom. You know the rendezvous.
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: If that his majesty would aught with us,
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: We shall express our duty in his eye,
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: And let him know so.
Captain: I will do't, my lord.
PRINCE FORTINBRAS: Go softly on.
NARRATOR: Exeunt FORTINBRAS and Soldiers
NARRATOR: Enter HAMLET, ROSENCRANTZ, GUILDENSTERN, and others
HAMLET: Good sir, whose powers are these?
Captain: They are of Norway, sir.
HAMLET: How purposed, sir, I pray you?
Captain: Against some part of Poland.
HAMLET: Who commands them, sir?
Captain: The nephews to old Norway, Fortinbras.
HAMLET: Goes it against the main of Poland, sir,
HAMLET: Or for some frontier?
Captain: Truly to speak, and with no addition,
Captain: We go to gain a little patch of ground
Captain: That hath in it no profit but the name.
Captain: To pay five ducats, five, I would not farm it,
Captain: Nor will it yield to Norway or the Pole
Captain: A ranker rate, should it be sold in fee.
HAMLET: Why, then the Polack never will defend it.
Captain: Yes, it is already garrison'd.
HAMLET: Two thousand souls and twenty thousand ducats
HAMLET: Will not debate the question of this straw:
HAMLET: This is the imposthume of much wealth and peace,
HAMLET: That inward breaks, and shows no cause without
HAMLET: Why the man dies. I humbly thank you, sir.
Captain: God be wi' you, sir.
NARRATOR: Exit
ROSENCRANTZ: Wilt please you go, my lord?
HAMLET: I'll be with you straight go a little before.
NARRATOR: Exeunt all except HAMLET
HAMLET: How all occasions do inform against me,
HAMLET: And spur my dull revenge! What is a man,
HAMLET: If his chief good and market of his time
HAMLET: Be but to sleep and feed? a beast, no more.
HAMLET: Sure, he that made us with such large discourse,
HAMLET: Looking before and after, gave us not
HAMLET: That capability and god-like reason
HAMLET: To fust in us unused. Now, whether it be
HAMLET: Bestial oblivion, or some craven scruple
HAMLET: Of thinking too precisely on the event,
HAMLET: A thought which, quarter'd, hath but one part wisdom
HAMLET: And ever three parts coward, I do not know
HAMLET: Why yet I live to say 'This thing's to do,'
HAMLET: Sith I have cause and will and strength and means
HAMLET: To do't. Examples gross as earth exhort me:
HAMLET: Witness this army of such mass and charge
HAMLET: Led by a delicate and tender prince,
HAMLET: Whose spirit with divine ambition puff'd
HAMLET: Makes mouths at the invisible event,
HAMLET: Exposing what is mortal and unsure
HAMLET: To all that fortune, death and danger dare,
HAMLET: Even for an egg-shell. Rightly to be great
HAMLET: Is not to stir without great argument,
HAMLET: But greatly to find quarrel in a straw
HAMLET: When honour's at the stake. How stand I then,
HAMLET: That have a father kill'd, a mother stain'd,
HAMLET: Excitements of my reason and my blood,
HAMLET: And let all sleep? while, to my shame, I see
HAMLET: The imminent death of twenty thousand men,
HAMLET: That, for a fantasy and trick of fame,
HAMLET: Go to their graves like beds, fight for a plot
HAMLET: Whereon the numbers cannot try the cause,
HAMLET: Which is not tomb enough and continent
HAMLET: To hide the slain? O, from this time forth,
HAMLET: My thoughts be bloody, or be nothing worth!
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE V. Elsinore. A room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter QUEEN GERTRUDE, HORATIO, and a Gentleman
QUEEN GERTRUDE: I will not speak with her.
Gentleman: She is importunate, indeed distract:
Gentleman: Her mood will needs be pitied.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: What would she have?
Gentleman: She speaks much of her father, says she hears
Gentleman: There's tricks i' the world, and hems, and beats her heart,
Gentleman: Spurns enviously at straws, speaks things in doubt,
Gentleman: That carry but half sense: her speech is nothing,
Gentleman: Yet the unshaped use of it doth move
Gentleman: The hearers to collection, they aim at it,
Gentleman: And botch the words up fit to their own thoughts,
Gentleman: Which, as her winks, and nods, and gestures
Gentleman: yield them,
Gentleman: Indeed would make one think there might be thought,
Gentleman: Though nothing sure, yet much unhappily.
HORATIO: 'Twere good she were spoken with, for she may strew
HORATIO: Dangerous conjectures in ill-breeding minds.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Let her come in.
NARRATOR: Exit HORATIO
QUEEN GERTRUDE: To my sick soul, as sin's true nature is,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Each toy seems prologue to some great amiss:
QUEEN GERTRUDE: So full of artless jealousy is guilt,
QUEEN GERTRUDE: It spills itself in fearing to be spilt.
NARRATOR: Re-enter HORATIO, with OPHELIA
OPHELIA: Where is the beauteous majesty of Denmark?
QUEEN GERTRUDE: How now, Ophelia!
OPHELIA: [Sings]
OPHELIA: How should I your true love know
OPHELIA: From another one?
OPHELIA: By his cockle hat and staff,
OPHELIA: And his sandal shoon.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alas, sweet lady, what imports this song?
OPHELIA: Say you? nay, pray you, mark.
NARRATOR: Sings
OPHELIA: He is dead and gone, lady,
OPHELIA: He is dead and gone,
OPHELIA: At his head a grass-green turf,
OPHELIA: At his heels a stone.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Nay, but, Ophelia,--
OPHELIA: Pray you, mark.
NARRATOR: Sings
OPHELIA: White his shroud as the mountain snow,--
NARRATOR: Enter KING CLAUDIUS
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alas, look here, my lord.
OPHELIA: [Sings]
OPHELIA: Larded with sweet flowers
OPHELIA: Which bewept to the grave did go
OPHELIA: With true-love showers.
KING CLAUDIUS: How do you, pretty lady?
OPHELIA: Well, God 'ild you! They say the owl was a baker's
OPHELIA: daughter. Lord, we know what we are, but know not
OPHELIA: what we may be. God be at your table!
KING CLAUDIUS: Conceit upon her father.
OPHELIA: Pray you, let's have no words of this, but when they
OPHELIA: ask you what it means, say you this:
NARRATOR: Sings
OPHELIA: To-morrow is Saint Valentine's day,
OPHELIA: All in the morning betime,
OPHELIA: And I a maid at your window,
OPHELIA: To be your Valentine.
OPHELIA: Then up he rose, and donn'd his clothes,
OPHELIA: And dupp'd the chamber-door,
OPHELIA: Let in the maid, that out a maid
OPHELIA: Never departed more.
KING CLAUDIUS: Pretty Ophelia!
OPHELIA: Indeed, la, without an oath, I'll make an end on't:
NARRATOR: Sings
OPHELIA: By Gis and by Saint Charity,
OPHELIA: Alack, and fie for shame!
OPHELIA: Young men will do't, if they come to't,
OPHELIA: By cock, they are to blame.
OPHELIA: Quoth she, before you tumbled me,
OPHELIA: You promised me to wed.
OPHELIA: So would I ha' done, by yonder sun,
OPHELIA: An thou hadst not come to my bed.
KING CLAUDIUS: How long hath she been thus?
OPHELIA: I hope all will be well. We must be patient: but I
OPHELIA: cannot choose but weep, to think they should lay him
OPHELIA: i' the cold ground. My brother shall know of it:
OPHELIA: and so I thank you for your good counsel. Come, my
OPHELIA: coach! Good night, ladies, good night, sweet ladies,
OPHELIA: good night, good night.
NARRATOR: Exit
KING CLAUDIUS: Follow her close, give her good watch,
KING CLAUDIUS: I pray you.
NARRATOR: Exit HORATIO
KING CLAUDIUS: O, this is the poison of deep grief, it springs
KING CLAUDIUS: All from her father's death. O Gertrude, Gertrude,
KING CLAUDIUS: When sorrows come, they come not single spies
KING CLAUDIUS: But in battalions. First, her father slain:
KING CLAUDIUS: Next, your son gone, and he most violent author
KING CLAUDIUS: Of his own just remove: the people muddied,
KING CLAUDIUS: Thick and unwholesome in their thoughts and whispers,
KING CLAUDIUS: For good Polonius' death, and we have done but greenly,
KING CLAUDIUS: In hugger-mugger to inter him: poor Ophelia
KING CLAUDIUS: Divided from herself and her fair judgment,
KING CLAUDIUS: Without the which we are pictures, or mere beasts:
KING CLAUDIUS: Last, and as much containing as all these,
KING CLAUDIUS: Her brother is in secret come from France,
KING CLAUDIUS: Feeds on his wonder, keeps himself in clouds,
KING CLAUDIUS: And wants not buzzers to infect his ear
KING CLAUDIUS: With pestilent speeches of his father's death,
KING CLAUDIUS: Wherein necessity, of matter beggar'd,
KING CLAUDIUS: Will nothing stick our person to arraign
KING CLAUDIUS: In ear and ear. O my dear Gertrude, this,
KING CLAUDIUS: Like to a murdering-piece, in many places
KING CLAUDIUS: Gives me superfluous death.
NARRATOR: A noise within
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Alack, what noise is this?
KING CLAUDIUS: Where are my Switzers? Let them guard the door.
NARRATOR: Enter another Gentleman
KING CLAUDIUS: What is the matter?
Gentleman: Save yourself, my lord:
Gentleman: The ocean, overpeering of his list,
Gentleman: Eats not the flats with more impetuous haste
Gentleman: Than young Laertes, in a riotous head,
Gentleman: O'erbears your officers. The rabble call him lord,
Gentleman: And, as the world were now but to begin,
Gentleman: Antiquity forgot, custom not known,
Gentleman: The ratifiers and props of every word,
Gentleman: They cry 'Choose we: Laertes shall be king:'
Gentleman: Caps, hands, and tongues, applaud it to the clouds:
Gentleman: 'Laertes shall be king, Laertes king!'
QUEEN GERTRUDE: How cheerfully on the false trail they cry!
QUEEN GERTRUDE: O, this is counter, you false Danish dogs!
KING CLAUDIUS: The doors are broke.
NARRATOR: Noise within
NARRATOR: Enter LAERTES, armed, Danes following
LAERTES: Where is this king? Sirs, stand you all without.
Danes: No, let's come in.
LAERTES: I pray you, give me leave.
Danes: We will, we will.
NARRATOR: They retire without the door
LAERTES: I thank you: keep the door. O thou vile king,
LAERTES: Give me my father!
QUEEN GERTRUDE: Calmly, good Laertes.
LAERTES: That drop of blood that's calm proclaims me bastard,
LAERTES: Cries cuckold to my father, brands the harlot
LAERTES: Even here, between the chaste unsmirched brow
LAERTES: Of my true mother.
KING CLAUDIUS: What is the cause, Laertes,
KING CLAUDIUS: That thy rebellion looks so giant-like?
KING CLAUDIUS: Let him go, Gertrude, do not fear our person:
KING CLAUDIUS: There's such divinity doth hedge a king,
KING CLAUDIUS: That treason can but peep to what it would,
KING CLAUDIUS: Acts little of his will. Tell me, Laertes,
KING CLAUDIUS: Why thou art thus incensed. Let him go, Gertrude.
KING CLAUDIUS: Speak, man.
LAERTES: Where is my father?
KING CLAUDIUS: Dead.
QUEEN GERTRUDE: But not by him.
KING CLAUDIUS: Let him demand his fill.
LAERTES: How came he dead? I'll not be juggled with:
LAERTES: To hell, allegiance! vows, to the blackest devil!
LAERTES: Conscience and grace, to the profoundest pit!
LAERTES: I dare damnation. To this point I stand,
LAERTES: That both the worlds I give to negligence,
LAERTES: Let come what comes, only I'll be revenged
LAERTES: Most thoroughly for my father.
KING CLAUDIUS: Who shall stay you?
LAERTES: My will, not all the world:
LAERTES: And for my means, I'll husband them so well,
LAERTES: They shall go far with little.
KING CLAUDIUS: Good Laertes,
KING CLAUDIUS: If you desire to know the certainty
KING CLAUDIUS: Of your dear father's death, is't writ in your revenge,
KING CLAUDIUS: That, swoopstake, you will draw both friend and foe,
KING CLAUDIUS: Winner and loser?
LAERTES: None but his enemies.
KING CLAUDIUS: Will you know them then?
LAERTES: To his good friends thus wide I'll ope my arms,
LAERTES: And like the kind life-rendering pelican,
LAERTES: Repast them with my blood.
KING CLAUDIUS: Why, now you speak
KING CLAUDIUS: Like a good child and a true gentleman.
KING CLAUDIUS: That I am guiltless of your father's death,
KING CLAUDIUS: And am most sensible in grief for it,
KING CLAUDIUS: It shall as level to your judgment pierce
KING CLAUDIUS: As day does to your eye.
Danes: [Within]                Let her come in.
LAERTES: How now! what noise is that?
NARRATOR: Re-enter OPHELIA
LAERTES: O heat, dry up my brains! tears seven times salt,
LAERTES: Burn out the sense and virtue of mine eye!
LAERTES: By heaven, thy madness shall be paid by weight,
LAERTES: Till our scale turn the beam. O rose of May!
LAERTES: Dear maid, kind sister, sweet Ophelia!
LAERTES: O heavens! is't possible, a young maid's wits
LAERTES: Should be as moral as an old man's life?
LAERTES: Nature is fine in love, and where 'tis fine,
LAERTES: It sends some precious instance of itself
LAERTES: After the thing it loves.
OPHELIA: [Sings]
OPHELIA: They bore him barefaced on the bier,
OPHELIA: Hey non nonny, nonny, hey nonny,
OPHELIA: And in his grave rain'd many a tear:--
OPHELIA: Fare you well, my dove!
LAERTES: Hadst thou thy wits, and didst persuade revenge,
LAERTES: It could not move thus.
OPHELIA: [Sings]
OPHELIA: You must sing a-down a-down,
OPHELIA: An you call him a-down-a.
OPHELIA: O, how the wheel becomes it! It is the false
OPHELIA: steward, that stole his master's daughter.
LAERTES: This nothing's more than matter.
OPHELIA: There's rosemary, that's for remembrance, pray,
OPHELIA: love, remember: and there is pansies. that's for thoughts.
LAERTES: A document in madness, thoughts and remembrance fitted.
OPHELIA: There's fennel for you, and columbines: there's rue
OPHELIA: for you, and here's some for me: we may call it
OPHELIA: herb-grace o' Sundays: O you must wear your rue with
OPHELIA: a difference. There's a daisy: I would give you
OPHELIA: some violets, but they withered all when my father
OPHELIA: died: they say he made a good end,--
NARRATOR: Sings
OPHELIA: For bonny sweet Robin is all my joy.
LAERTES: Thought and affliction, passion, hell itself,
LAERTES: She turns to favour and to prettiness.
OPHELIA: [Sings]
OPHELIA: And will he not come again?
OPHELIA: And will he not come again?
OPHELIA: No, no, he is dead:
OPHELIA: Go to thy death-bed:
OPHELIA: He never will come again.
OPHELIA: His beard was as white as snow,
OPHELIA: All flaxen was his poll:
OPHELIA: He is gone, he is gone,
OPHELIA: And we cast away moan:
OPHELIA: God ha' mercy on his soul!
OPHELIA: And of all Christian souls, I pray God. God be wi' ye.
NARRATOR: Exit
LAERTES: Do you see this, O God?
KING CLAUDIUS: Laertes, I must commune with your grief,
KING CLAUDIUS: Or you deny me right. Go but apart,
KING CLAUDIUS: Make choice of whom your wisest friends you will.
KING CLAUDIUS: And they shall hear and judge 'twixt you and me:
KING CLAUDIUS: If by direct or by collateral hand
KING CLAUDIUS: They find us touch'd, we will our kingdom give,
KING CLAUDIUS: Our crown, our life, and all that we can ours,
KING CLAUDIUS: To you in satisfaction, but if not,
KING CLAUDIUS: Be you content to lend your patience to us,
KING CLAUDIUS: And we shall jointly labour with your soul
KING CLAUDIUS: To give it due content.
LAERTES: Let this be so,
LAERTES: His means of death, his obscure funeral--
LAERTES: No trophy, sword, nor hatchment o'er his bones,
LAERTES: No noble rite nor formal ostentation--
LAERTES: Cry to be heard, as 'twere from heaven to earth,
LAERTES: That I must call't in question.
KING CLAUDIUS: So you shall,
KING CLAUDIUS: And where the offence is let the great axe fall.
KING CLAUDIUS: I pray you, go with me.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE VI. Another room in the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter HORATIO and a Servant
HORATIO: What are they that would speak with me?
Servant: Sailors, sir: they say they have letters for you.
HORATIO: Let them come in.
NARRATOR: Exit Servant
HORATIO: I do not know from what part of the world
HORATIO: I should be greeted, if not from Lord Hamlet.
NARRATOR: Enter Sailors
First Sailor: God bless you, sir.
HORATIO: Let him bless thee too.
First Sailor: He shall, sir, an't please him. There's a letter for
First Sailor: you, sir, it comes from the ambassador that was
First Sailor: bound for England, if your name be Horatio, as I am
First Sailor: let to know it is.
HORATIO: [Reads]  'Horatio, when thou shalt have overlooked
HORATIO: this, give these fellows some means to the king:
HORATIO: they have letters for him. Ere we were two days old
HORATIO: at sea, a pirate of very warlike appointment gave us
HORATIO: chase. Finding ourselves too slow of sail, we put on
HORATIO: a compelled valour, and in the grapple I boarded
HORATIO: them: on the instant they got clear of our ship, so

HORATIO: me like thieves of mercy: but they knew what they

HORATIO: have the letters I have sent, and repair thou to me

HORATIO: 'He that thou knowest thine, HAMLET.'

HORATIO: And do't the speedier, that you may direct me
