CARDINAL PANDULPH: If thou stand excommunicate and cursed?
KING PHILIP: Good reverend father, make my person yours,
KING PHILIP: And tell me how you would bestow yourself.
KING PHILIP: This royal hand and mine are newly knit,
KING PHILIP: And the conjunction of our inward souls
KING PHILIP: Married in league, coupled and linked together
KING PHILIP: With all religious strength of sacred vows,
KING PHILIP: The latest breath that gave the sound of words
KING PHILIP: Was deep-sworn faith, peace, amity, true love
KING PHILIP: Between our kingdoms and our royal selves,
KING PHILIP: And even before this truce, but new before,
KING PHILIP: No longer than we well could wash our hands
KING PHILIP: To clap this royal bargain up of peace,
KING PHILIP: Heaven knows, they were besmear'd and over-stain'd
KING PHILIP: With slaughter's pencil, where revenge did paint
KING PHILIP: The fearful difference of incensed kings:
KING PHILIP: And shall these hands, so lately purged of blood,
KING PHILIP: So newly join'd in love, so strong in both,
KING PHILIP: Unyoke this seizure and this kind regreet?
KING PHILIP: Play fast and loose with faith? so jest with heaven,
KING PHILIP: Make such unconstant children of ourselves,
KING PHILIP: As now again to snatch our palm from palm,
KING PHILIP: Unswear faith sworn, and on the marriage-bed
KING PHILIP: Of smiling peace to march a bloody host,
KING PHILIP: And make a riot on the gentle brow
KING PHILIP: Of true sincerity? O, holy sir,
KING PHILIP: My reverend father, let it not be so!
KING PHILIP: Out of your grace, devise, ordain, impose
KING PHILIP: Some gentle order, and then we shall be blest
KING PHILIP: To do your pleasure and continue friends.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: All form is formless, order orderless,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Save what is opposite to England's love.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Therefore to arms! be champion of our church,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Or let the church, our mother, breathe her curse,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: A mother's curse, on her revolting son.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: France, thou mayst hold a serpent by the tongue,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: A chafed lion by the mortal paw,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: A fasting tiger safer by the tooth,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Than keep in peace that hand which thou dost hold.
KING PHILIP: I may disjoin my hand, but not my faith.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: So makest thou faith an enemy to faith,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And like a civil war set'st oath to oath,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Thy tongue against thy tongue. O, let thy vow
CARDINAL PANDULPH: First made to heaven, first be to heaven perform'd,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That is, to be the champion of our church!
CARDINAL PANDULPH: What since thou sworest is sworn against thyself
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And may not be performed by thyself,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: For that which thou hast sworn to do amiss
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Is not amiss when it is truly done,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And being not done, where doing tends to ill,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The truth is then most done not doing it:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The better act of purposes mistook
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Is to mistake again, though indirect,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Yet indirection thereby grows direct,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And falsehood falsehood cures, as fire cools fire
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Within the scorched veins of one new-burn'd.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: It is religion that doth make vows kept,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: But thou hast sworn against religion,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: By what thou swear'st against the thing thou swear'st,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And makest an oath the surety for thy truth
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Against an oath: the truth thou art unsure
CARDINAL PANDULPH: To swear, swears only not to be forsworn,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Else what a mockery should it be to swear!
CARDINAL PANDULPH: But thou dost swear only to be forsworn,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And most forsworn, to keep what thou dost swear.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Therefore thy later vows against thy first
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Is in thyself rebellion to thyself,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And better conquest never canst thou make
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Than arm thy constant and thy nobler parts
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Against these giddy loose suggestions:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Upon which better part our prayers come in,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: If thou vouchsafe them. But if not, then know
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The peril of our curses light on thee
CARDINAL PANDULPH: So heavy as thou shalt not shake them off,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: But in despair die under their black weight.
AUSTRIA: Rebellion, flat rebellion!
BASTARD: Will't not be?
BASTARD: Will not a calfs-skin stop that mouth of thine?
LEWIS: Father, to arms!
BLANCH: Upon thy wedding-day?
BLANCH: Against the blood that thou hast married?
BLANCH: What, shall our feast be kept with slaughter'd men?
BLANCH: Shall braying trumpets and loud churlish drums,
BLANCH: Clamours of hell, be measures to our pomp?
BLANCH: O husband, hear me! ay, alack, how new
BLANCH: Is husband in my mouth! even for that name,
BLANCH: Which till this time my tongue did ne'er pronounce,
BLANCH: Upon my knee I beg, go not to arms
BLANCH: Against mine uncle.
CONSTANCE: O, upon my knee,
CONSTANCE: Made hard with kneeling, I do pray to thee,
CONSTANCE: Thou virtuous Dauphin, alter not the doom
CONSTANCE: Forethought by heaven!
BLANCH: Now shall I see thy love: what motive may
BLANCH: Be stronger with thee than the name of wife?
CONSTANCE: That which upholdeth him that thee upholds,
CONSTANCE: His honour: O, thine honour, Lewis, thine honour!
LEWIS: I muse your majesty doth seem so cold,
LEWIS: When such profound respects do pull you on.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: I will denounce a curse upon his head.
KING PHILIP: Thou shalt not need. England, I will fall from thee.
CONSTANCE: O fair return of banish'd majesty!
QUEEN ELINOR: O foul revolt of French inconstancy!
KING JOHN: France, thou shalt rue this hour within this hour.
BASTARD: Old Time the clock-setter, that bald sexton Time,
BASTARD: Is it as he will? well then, France shall rue.
BLANCH: The sun's o'ercast with blood: fair day, adieu!
BLANCH: Which is the side that I must go withal?
BLANCH: I am with both: each army hath a hand,
BLANCH: And in their rage, I having hold of both,
BLANCH: They swirl asunder and dismember me.
BLANCH: Husband, I cannot pray that thou mayst win,
BLANCH: Uncle, I needs must pray that thou mayst lose,
BLANCH: Father, I may not wish the fortune thine,
BLANCH: Grandam, I will not wish thy fortunes thrive:
BLANCH: Whoever wins, on that side shall I lose
BLANCH: Assured loss before the match be play'd.
LEWIS: Lady, with me, with me thy fortune lies.
BLANCH: There where my fortune lives, there my life dies.
KING JOHN: Cousin, go draw our puissance together.
NARRATOR: Exit BASTARD
KING JOHN: France, I am burn'd up with inflaming wrath,
KING JOHN: A rage whose heat hath this condition,
KING JOHN: That nothing can allay, nothing but blood,
KING JOHN: The blood, and dearest-valued blood, of France.
KING PHILIP: Thy rage sham burn thee up, and thou shalt turn
KING PHILIP: To ashes, ere our blood shall quench that fire:
KING PHILIP: Look to thyself, thou art in jeopardy.
KING JOHN: No more than he that threats. To arms let's hie!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The same. Plains near Angiers.
NARRATOR: Alarums, excursions. Enter the BASTARD, with AUSTRIA'S head
BASTARD: Now, by my life, this day grows wondrous hot,
BASTARD: Some airy devil hovers in the sky
BASTARD: And pours down mischief. Austria's head lie there,
BASTARD: While Philip breathes.
NARRATOR: Enter KING JOHN, ARTHUR, and HUBERT
KING JOHN: Hubert, keep this boy. Philip, make up:
KING JOHN: My mother is assailed in our tent,
KING JOHN: And ta'en, I fear.
BASTARD: My lord, I rescued her,
BASTARD: Her highness is in safety, fear you not:
BASTARD: But on, my liege, for very little pains
BASTARD: Will bring this labour to an happy end.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. The same.
NARRATOR: Alarums, excursions, retreat. Enter KING JOHN,  QUEEN ELINOR, ARTHUR, the BASTARD, HUBERT, and Lords
KING JOHN: [To QUEEN ELINOR]  So shall it be, your grace shall
KING JOHN: stay behind
KING JOHN: So strongly guarded.
NARRATOR: To ARTHUR
KING JOHN: Cousin, look not sad:
KING JOHN: Thy grandam loves thee, and thy uncle will
KING JOHN: As dear be to thee as thy father was.
ARTHUR: O, this will make my mother die with grief!
KING JOHN: [To the BASTARD]  Cousin, away for England!
KING JOHN: haste before:
KING JOHN: And, ere our coming, see thou shake the bags
KING JOHN: Of hoarding abbots, imprisoned angels
KING JOHN: Set at liberty: the fat ribs of peace
KING JOHN: Must by the hungry now be fed upon:
KING JOHN: Use our commission in his utmost force.
BASTARD: Bell, book, and candle shall not drive me back,
BASTARD: When gold and silver becks me to come on.
BASTARD: I leave your highness. Grandam, I will pray,
BASTARD: If ever I remember to be holy,
BASTARD: For your fair safety, so, I kiss your hand.
ELINOR: Farewell, gentle cousin.
KING JOHN: Coz, farewell.
NARRATOR: Exit the BASTARD
QUEEN ELINOR: Come hither, little kinsman, hark, a word.
KING JOHN: Come hither, Hubert. O my gentle Hubert,
KING JOHN: We owe thee much! within this wall of flesh
KING JOHN: There is a soul counts thee her creditor
KING JOHN: And with advantage means to pay thy love:
KING JOHN: And my good friend, thy voluntary oath
KING JOHN: Lives in this bosom, dearly cherished.
KING JOHN: Give me thy hand. I had a thing to say,
KING JOHN: But I will fit it with some better time.
KING JOHN: By heaven, Hubert, I am almost ashamed
KING JOHN: To say what good respect I have of thee.
HUBERT: I am much bounden to your majesty.
KING JOHN: Good friend, thou hast no cause to say so yet,
KING JOHN: But thou shalt have, and creep time ne'er so slow,
KING JOHN: Yet it shall come from me to do thee good.
KING JOHN: I had a thing to say, but let it go:
KING JOHN: The sun is in the heaven, and the proud day,
KING JOHN: Attended with the pleasures of the world,
KING JOHN: Is all too wanton and too full of gawds
KING JOHN: To give me audience: if the midnight bell
KING JOHN: Did, with his iron tongue and brazen mouth,
KING JOHN: Sound on into the drowsy race of night,
KING JOHN: If this same were a churchyard where we stand,
KING JOHN: And thou possessed with a thousand wrongs,
KING JOHN: Or if that surly spirit, melancholy,
KING JOHN: Had baked thy blood and made it heavy-thick,
KING JOHN: Which else runs tickling up and down the veins,
KING JOHN: Making that idiot, laughter, keep men's eyes
KING JOHN: And strain their cheeks to idle merriment,
KING JOHN: A passion hateful to my purposes,
KING JOHN: Or if that thou couldst see me without eyes,
KING JOHN: Hear me without thine ears, and make reply
KING JOHN: Without a tongue, using conceit alone,
KING JOHN: Without eyes, ears and harmful sound of words,
KING JOHN: Then, in despite of brooded watchful day,
KING JOHN: I would into thy bosom pour my thoughts:
KING JOHN: But, ah, I will not! yet I love thee well,
KING JOHN: And, by my troth, I think thou lovest me well.
HUBERT: So well, that what you bid me undertake,
HUBERT: Though that my death were adjunct to my act,
HUBERT: By heaven, I would do it.
KING JOHN: Do not I know thou wouldst?
KING JOHN: Good Hubert, Hubert, Hubert, throw thine eye
KING JOHN: On yon young boy: I'll tell thee what, my friend,
KING JOHN: He is a very serpent in my way,
KING JOHN: And whereso'er this foot of mine doth tread,
KING JOHN: He lies before me: dost thou understand me?
KING JOHN: Thou art his keeper.
HUBERT: And I'll keep him so,
HUBERT: That he shall not offend your majesty.
KING JOHN: Death.
HUBERT: My lord?
KING JOHN: A grave.
HUBERT: He shall not live.
KING JOHN: Enough.
KING JOHN: I could be merry now. Hubert, I love thee,
KING JOHN: Well, I'll not say what I intend for thee:
KING JOHN: Remember. Madam, fare you well:
KING JOHN: I'll send those powers o'er to your majesty.
ELINOR: My blessing go with thee!
KING JOHN: For England, cousin, go:
KING JOHN: Hubert shall be your man, attend on you
KING JOHN: With all true duty. On toward Calais, ho!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. The same. KING PHILIP'S tent.
NARRATOR: Enter KING PHILIP, LEWIS, CARDINAL PANDULPH, and Attendants
KING PHILIP: So, by a roaring tempest on the flood,
KING PHILIP: A whole armado of convicted sail
KING PHILIP: Is scatter'd and disjoin'd from fellowship.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Courage and comfort! all shall yet go well.
KING PHILIP: What can go well, when we have run so ill?
KING PHILIP: Are we not beaten? Is not Angiers lost?
KING PHILIP: Arthur ta'en prisoner? divers dear friends slain?
KING PHILIP: And bloody England into England gone,
KING PHILIP: O'erbearing interruption, spite of France?
LEWIS: What he hath won, that hath he fortified:
LEWIS: So hot a speed with such advice disposed,
LEWIS: Such temperate order in so fierce a cause,
LEWIS: Doth want example: who hath read or heard
LEWIS: Of any kindred action like to this?
KING PHILIP: Well could I bear that England had this praise,
KING PHILIP: So we could find some pattern of our shame.
NARRATOR: Enter CONSTANCE
KING PHILIP: Look, who comes here! a grave unto a soul,
KING PHILIP: Holding the eternal spirit against her will,
KING PHILIP: In the vile prison of afflicted breath.
KING PHILIP: I prithee, lady, go away with me.
CONSTANCE: Lo, now I now see the issue of your peace.
KING PHILIP: Patience, good lady! comfort, gentle Constance!
CONSTANCE: No, I defy all counsel, all redress,
CONSTANCE: But that which ends all counsel, true redress,
CONSTANCE: Death, death, O amiable lovely death!
CONSTANCE: Thou odouriferous stench! sound rottenness!
CONSTANCE: Arise forth from the couch of lasting night,
CONSTANCE: Thou hate and terror to prosperity,
CONSTANCE: And I will kiss thy detestable bones
CONSTANCE: And put my eyeballs in thy vaulty brows
CONSTANCE: And ring these fingers with thy household worms
CONSTANCE: And stop this gap of breath with fulsome dust
CONSTANCE: And be a carrion monster like thyself:
CONSTANCE: Come, grin on me, and I will think thou smilest
CONSTANCE: And buss thee as thy wife. Misery's love,
CONSTANCE: O, come to me!
KING PHILIP: O fair affliction, peace!
CONSTANCE: No, no, I will not, having breath to cry:
CONSTANCE: O, that my tongue were in the thunder's mouth!
CONSTANCE: Then with a passion would I shake the world,
CONSTANCE: And rouse from sleep that fell anatomy
CONSTANCE: Which cannot hear a lady's feeble voice,
CONSTANCE: Which scorns a modern invocation.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Lady, you utter madness, and not sorrow.
CONSTANCE: Thou art not holy to belie me so,
CONSTANCE: I am not mad: this hair I tear is mine,
CONSTANCE: My name is Constance, I was Geffrey's wife,
CONSTANCE: Young Arthur is my son, and he is lost:
CONSTANCE: I am not mad: I would to heaven I were!
CONSTANCE: For then, 'tis like I should forget myself:
CONSTANCE: O, if I could, what grief should I forget!
CONSTANCE: Preach some philosophy to make me mad,
CONSTANCE: And thou shalt be canonized, cardinal,
CONSTANCE: For being not mad but sensible of grief,
CONSTANCE: My reasonable part produces reason
CONSTANCE: How I may be deliver'd of these woes,
CONSTANCE: And teaches me to kill or hang myself:
CONSTANCE: If I were mad, I should forget my son,
CONSTANCE: Or madly think a babe of clouts were he:
CONSTANCE: I am not mad, too well, too well I feel
CONSTANCE: The different plague of each calamity.
KING PHILIP: Bind up those tresses. O, what love I note
KING PHILIP: In the fair multitude of those her hairs!
KING PHILIP: Where but by chance a silver drop hath fallen,
KING PHILIP: Even to that drop ten thousand wiry friends
KING PHILIP: Do glue themselves in sociable grief,
KING PHILIP: Like true, inseparable, faithful loves,
KING PHILIP: Sticking together in calamity.
CONSTANCE: To England, if you will.
KING PHILIP: Bind up your hairs.
CONSTANCE: Yes, that I will, and wherefore will I do it?
CONSTANCE: I tore them from their bonds and cried aloud
CONSTANCE: 'O that these hands could so redeem my son,
CONSTANCE: As they have given these hairs their liberty!'
CONSTANCE: But now I envy at their liberty,
CONSTANCE: And will again commit them to their bonds,
CONSTANCE: Because my poor child is a prisoner.
CONSTANCE: And, father cardinal, I have heard you say
CONSTANCE: That we shall see and know our friends in heaven:
CONSTANCE: If that be true, I shall see my boy again,
CONSTANCE: For since the birth of Cain, the first male child,
CONSTANCE: To him that did but yesterday suspire,
CONSTANCE: There was not such a gracious creature born.
CONSTANCE: But now will canker-sorrow eat my bud
CONSTANCE: And chase the native beauty from his cheek
CONSTANCE: And he will look as hollow as a ghost,
CONSTANCE: As dim and meagre as an ague's fit,
CONSTANCE: And so he'll die, and, rising so again,
CONSTANCE: When I shall meet him in the court of heaven
CONSTANCE: I shall not know him: therefore never, never
CONSTANCE: Must I behold my pretty Arthur more.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: You hold too heinous a respect of grief.
CONSTANCE: He talks to me that never had a son.
KING PHILIP: You are as fond of grief as of your child.
CONSTANCE: Grief fills the room up of my absent child,
CONSTANCE: Lies in his bed, walks up and down with me,
CONSTANCE: Puts on his pretty looks, repeats his words,
CONSTANCE: Remembers me of all his gracious parts,
CONSTANCE: Stuffs out his vacant garments with his form,
CONSTANCE: Then, have I reason to be fond of grief?
CONSTANCE: Fare you well: had you such a loss as I,
CONSTANCE: I could give better comfort than you do.
CONSTANCE: I will not keep this form upon my head,
CONSTANCE: When there is such disorder in my wit.
CONSTANCE: O Lord! my boy, my Arthur, my fair son!
CONSTANCE: My life, my joy, my food, my all the world!
CONSTANCE: My widow-comfort, and my sorrows' cure!
NARRATOR: Exit
KING PHILIP: I fear some outrage, and I'll follow her.
NARRATOR: Exit
LEWIS: There's nothing in this world can make me joy:
LEWIS: Life is as tedious as a twice-told tale
LEWIS: Vexing the dull ear of a drowsy man,
LEWIS: And bitter shame hath spoil'd the sweet world's taste
LEWIS: That it yields nought but shame and bitterness.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Before the curing of a strong disease,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Even in the instant of repair and health,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The fit is strongest, evils that take leave,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: On their departure most of all show evil:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: What have you lost by losing of this day?
LEWIS: All days of glory, joy and happiness.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: If you had won it, certainly you had.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: No, no, when Fortune means to men most good,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: She looks upon them with a threatening eye.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: 'Tis strange to think how much King John hath lost
CARDINAL PANDULPH: In this which he accounts so clearly won:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Are not you grieved that Arthur is his prisoner?
LEWIS: As heartily as he is glad he hath him.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Your mind is all as youthful as your blood.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Now hear me speak with a prophetic spirit,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: For even the breath of what I mean to speak
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Shall blow each dust, each straw, each little rub,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Out of the path which shall directly lead
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Thy foot to England's throne, and therefore mark.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: John hath seized Arthur, and it cannot be
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That, whiles warm life plays in that infant's veins,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The misplaced John should entertain an hour,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: One minute, nay, one quiet breath of rest.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: A sceptre snatch'd with an unruly hand
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Must be as boisterously maintain'd as gain'd,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And he that stands upon a slippery place
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Makes nice of no vile hold to stay him up:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That John may stand, then Arthur needs must fall,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: So be it, for it cannot be but so.
LEWIS: But what shall I gain by young Arthur's fall?
CARDINAL PANDULPH: You, in the right of Lady Blanch your wife,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: May then make all the claim that Arthur did.
LEWIS: And lose it, life and all, as Arthur did.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: How green you are and fresh in this old world!
CARDINAL PANDULPH: John lays you plots, the times conspire with you,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: For he that steeps his safety in true blood
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Shall find but bloody safety and untrue.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: This act so evilly born shall cool the hearts
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Of all his people and freeze up their zeal,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That none so small advantage shall step forth
CARDINAL PANDULPH: To cheque his reign, but they will cherish it,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: No natural exhalation in the sky,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: No scope of nature, no distemper'd day,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: No common wind, no customed event,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: But they will pluck away his natural cause
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And call them meteors, prodigies and signs,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Abortives, presages and tongues of heaven,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Plainly denouncing vengeance upon John.
LEWIS: May be he will not touch young Arthur's life,
LEWIS: But hold himself safe in his prisonment.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: O, sir, when he shall hear of your approach,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: If that young Arthur be not gone already,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Even at that news he dies, and then the hearts
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Of all his people shall revolt from him
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And kiss the lips of unacquainted change
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And pick strong matter of revolt and wrath
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Out of the bloody fingers' ends of John.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Methinks I see this hurly all on foot:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And, O, what better matter breeds for you
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Than I have named! The bastard Faulconbridge
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Is now in England, ransacking the church,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Offending charity: if but a dozen French
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Were there in arms, they would be as a call
CARDINAL PANDULPH: To train ten thousand English to their side,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Or as a little snow, tumbled about,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Anon becomes a mountain. O noble Dauphin,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Go with me to the king: 'tis wonderful
CARDINAL PANDULPH: What may be wrought out of their discontent,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Now that their souls are topful of offence.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: For England go: I will whet on the king.
LEWIS: Strong reasons make strong actions: let us go:
LEWIS: If you say ay, the king will not say no.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT IV
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A room in a castle.
NARRATOR: Enter HUBERT and Executioners
HUBERT: Heat me these irons hot, and look thou stand
HUBERT: Within the arras: when I strike my foot
HUBERT: Upon the bosom of the ground, rush forth,
HUBERT: And bind the boy which you shall find with me
HUBERT: Fast to the chair: be heedful: hence, and watch.
First Executioner: I hope your warrant will bear out the deed.
HUBERT: Uncleanly scruples! fear not you: look to't.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Executioners
HUBERT: Young lad, come forth, I have to say with you.
NARRATOR: Enter ARTHUR
ARTHUR: Good morrow, Hubert.
HUBERT: Good morrow, little prince.
ARTHUR: As little prince, having so great a title
ARTHUR: To be more prince, as may be. You are sad.
HUBERT: Indeed, I have been merrier.
ARTHUR: Mercy on me!
ARTHUR: Methinks no body should be sad but I:
ARTHUR: Yet, I remember, when I was in France,
ARTHUR: Young gentlemen would be as sad as night,
ARTHUR: Only for wantonness. By my christendom,
ARTHUR: So I were out of prison and kept sheep,
ARTHUR: I should be as merry as the day is long,
ARTHUR: And so I would be here, but that I doubt
ARTHUR: My uncle practises more harm to me:
ARTHUR: He is afraid of me and I of him:
ARTHUR: Is it my fault that I was Geffrey's son?
ARTHUR: No, indeed, is't not, and I would to heaven
ARTHUR: I were your son, so you would love me, Hubert.
HUBERT: [Aside]  If I talk to him, with his innocent prate
HUBERT: He will awake my mercy which lies dead:
HUBERT: Therefore I will be sudden and dispatch.
ARTHUR: Are you sick, Hubert? you look pale to-day:
ARTHUR: In sooth, I would you were a little sick,
ARTHUR: That I might sit all night and watch with you:
ARTHUR: I warrant I love you more than you do me.
HUBERT: [Aside]  His words do take possession of my bosom.
HUBERT: Read here, young Arthur.
NARRATOR: Showing a paper
NARRATOR: Aside
HUBERT: How now, foolish rheum!
HUBERT: Turning dispiteous torture out of door!
HUBERT: I must be brief, lest resolution drop
HUBERT: Out at mine eyes in tender womanish tears.
HUBERT: Can you not read it? Is it not fair writ?
ARTHUR: Too fairly, Hubert, for so foul effect:
ARTHUR: Must you with hot irons burn out both mine eyes?
HUBERT: Young boy, I must.
ARTHUR: And will you?
HUBERT: And I will.
ARTHUR: Have you the heart? When your head did but ache,
ARTHUR: I knit my handercher about your brows,
ARTHUR: The best I had, a princess wrought it me,
ARTHUR: And I did never ask it you again,
ARTHUR: And with my hand at midnight held your head,
ARTHUR: And like the watchful minutes to the hour,
ARTHUR: Still and anon cheer'd up the heavy time,
ARTHUR: Saying, 'What lack you?' and 'Where lies your grief?'
ARTHUR: Or 'What good love may I perform for you?'
ARTHUR: Many a poor man's son would have lien still
ARTHUR: And ne'er have spoke a loving word to you,
ARTHUR: But you at your sick service had a prince.
ARTHUR: Nay, you may think my love was crafty love
ARTHUR: And call it cunning: do, an if you will:
ARTHUR: If heaven be pleased that you must use me ill,
ARTHUR: Why then you must. Will you put out mine eyes?
ARTHUR: These eyes that never did nor never shall
ARTHUR: So much as frown on you.
HUBERT: I have sworn to do it,
HUBERT: And with hot irons must I burn them out.
ARTHUR: Ah, none but in this iron age would do it!
ARTHUR: The iron of itself, though heat red-hot,
ARTHUR: Approaching near these eyes, would drink my tears
ARTHUR: And quench his fiery indignation
ARTHUR: Even in the matter of mine innocence,
ARTHUR: Nay, after that, consume away in rust
ARTHUR: But for containing fire to harm mine eye.
ARTHUR: Are you more stubborn-hard than hammer'd iron?
ARTHUR: An if an angel should have come to me
ARTHUR: And told me Hubert should put out mine eyes,
ARTHUR: I would not have believed him,--no tongue but Hubert's.
HUBERT: Come forth.
NARRATOR: Stamps
NARRATOR: Re-enter Executioners, with a cord, irons,  and c
HUBERT: Do as I bid you do.
ARTHUR: O, save me, Hubert, save me! my eyes are out
ARTHUR: Even with the fierce looks of these bloody men.
HUBERT: Give me the iron, I say, and bind him here.
ARTHUR: Alas, what need you be so boisterous-rough?
ARTHUR: I will not struggle, I will stand stone-still.
ARTHUR: For heaven sake, Hubert, let me not be bound!
ARTHUR: Nay, hear me, Hubert, drive these men away,
ARTHUR: And I will sit as quiet as a lamb,
ARTHUR: I will not stir, nor wince, nor speak a word,
ARTHUR: Nor look upon the iron angerly:
ARTHUR: Thrust but these men away, and I'll forgive you,
ARTHUR: Whatever torment you do put me to.
HUBERT: Go, stand within, let me alone with him.
First Executioner: I am best pleased to be from such a deed.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Executioners
ARTHUR: Alas, I then have chid away my friend!
ARTHUR: He hath a stern look, but a gentle heart:
ARTHUR: Let him come back, that his compassion may
ARTHUR: Give life to yours.
HUBERT: Come, boy, prepare yourself.
ARTHUR: Is there no remedy?
HUBERT: None, but to lose your eyes.
ARTHUR: O heaven, that there were but a mote in yours,
ARTHUR: A grain, a dust, a gnat, a wandering hair,
ARTHUR: Any annoyance in that precious sense!
ARTHUR: Then feeling what small things are boisterous there,
ARTHUR: Your vile intent must needs seem horrible.
HUBERT: Is this your promise? go to, hold your tongue.
ARTHUR: Hubert, the utterance of a brace of tongues
ARTHUR: Must needs want pleading for a pair of eyes:
ARTHUR: Let me not hold my tongue, let me not, Hubert,
ARTHUR: Or, Hubert, if you will, cut out my tongue,
ARTHUR: So I may keep mine eyes: O, spare mine eyes.
ARTHUR: Though to no use but still to look on you!
ARTHUR: Lo, by my truth, the instrument is cold
ARTHUR: And would not harm me.
HUBERT: I can heat it, boy.
ARTHUR: No, in good sooth: the fire is dead with grief,
ARTHUR: Being create for comfort, to be used
ARTHUR: In undeserved extremes: see else yourself,
ARTHUR: There is no malice in this burning coal,
ARTHUR: The breath of heaven has blown his spirit out
ARTHUR: And strew'd repentent ashes on his head.
HUBERT: But with my breath I can revive it, boy.
ARTHUR: An if you do, you will but make it blush
ARTHUR: And glow with shame of your proceedings, Hubert:
ARTHUR: Nay, it perchance will sparkle in your eyes,
ARTHUR: And like a dog that is compell'd to fight,
ARTHUR: Snatch at his master that doth tarre him on.
ARTHUR: All things that you should use to do me wrong
ARTHUR: Deny their office: only you do lack
ARTHUR: That mercy which fierce fire and iron extends,
ARTHUR: Creatures of note for mercy-lacking uses.
HUBERT: Well, see to live, I will not touch thine eye
HUBERT: For all the treasure that thine uncle owes:
HUBERT: Yet am I sworn and I did purpose, boy,
HUBERT: With this same very iron to burn them out.
ARTHUR: O, now you look like Hubert! all this while
ARTHUR: You were disguised.
HUBERT: Peace, no more. Adieu.
HUBERT: Your uncle must not know but you are dead,
HUBERT: I'll fill these dogged spies with false reports:
HUBERT: And, pretty child, sleep doubtless and secure,
HUBERT: That Hubert, for the wealth of all the world,
HUBERT: Will not offend thee.
ARTHUR: O heaven! I thank you, Hubert.
HUBERT: Silence, no more: go closely in with me:
HUBERT: Much danger do I undergo for thee.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. KING JOHN'S palace.
NARRATOR: Enter KING JOHN, PEMBROKE, SALISBURY, and other Lords
KING JOHN: Here once again we sit, once again crown'd,
KING JOHN: And looked upon, I hope, with cheerful eyes.
PEMBROKE: This 'once again,' but that your highness pleased,
PEMBROKE: Was once superfluous: you were crown'd before,
PEMBROKE: And that high royalty was ne'er pluck'd off,
PEMBROKE: The faiths of men ne'er stained with revolt,
PEMBROKE: Fresh expectation troubled not the land
PEMBROKE: With any long'd-for change or better state.
SALISBURY: Therefore, to be possess'd with double pomp,
SALISBURY: To guard a title that was rich before,
SALISBURY: To gild refined gold, to paint the lily,
SALISBURY: To throw a perfume on the violet,
SALISBURY: To smooth the ice, or add another hue
SALISBURY: Unto the rainbow, or with taper-light
SALISBURY: To seek the beauteous eye of heaven to garnish,
SALISBURY: Is wasteful and ridiculous excess.
PEMBROKE: But that your royal pleasure must be done,
PEMBROKE: This act is as an ancient tale new told,
PEMBROKE: And in the last repeating troublesome,
PEMBROKE: Being urged at a time unseasonable.
SALISBURY: In this the antique and well noted face
SALISBURY: Of plain old form is much disfigured,
SALISBURY: And, like a shifted wind unto a sail,
SALISBURY: It makes the course of thoughts to fetch about,
SALISBURY: Startles and frights consideration,
SALISBURY: Makes sound opinion sick and truth suspected,
SALISBURY: For putting on so new a fashion'd robe.
PEMBROKE: When workmen strive to do better than well,
PEMBROKE: They do confound their skill in covetousness,
PEMBROKE: And oftentimes excusing of a fault
PEMBROKE: Doth make the fault the worse by the excuse,
PEMBROKE: As patches set upon a little breach
PEMBROKE: Discredit more in hiding of the fault
PEMBROKE: Than did the fault before it was so patch'd.
SALISBURY: To this effect, before you were new crown'd,
SALISBURY: We breathed our counsel: but it pleased your highness
SALISBURY: To overbear it, and we are all well pleased,
SALISBURY: Since all and every part of what we would
SALISBURY: Doth make a stand at what your highness will.
KING JOHN: Some reasons of this double coronation
KING JOHN: I have possess'd you with and think them strong,
KING JOHN: And more, more strong, then lesser is my fear,
KING JOHN: I shall indue you with: meantime but ask
KING JOHN: What you would have reform'd that is not well,
KING JOHN: And well shall you perceive how willingly
KING JOHN: I will both hear and grant you your requests.
PEMBROKE: Then I, as one that am the tongue of these,
PEMBROKE: To sound the purpose of all their hearts,
PEMBROKE: Both for myself and them, but, chief of all,
PEMBROKE: Your safety, for the which myself and them
PEMBROKE: Bend their best studies, heartily request
PEMBROKE: The enfranchisement of Arthur, whose restraint
PEMBROKE: Doth move the murmuring lips of discontent
PEMBROKE: To break into this dangerous argument,--
PEMBROKE: If what in rest you have in right you hold,
PEMBROKE: Why then your fears, which, as they say, attend
PEMBROKE: The steps of wrong, should move you to mew up
PEMBROKE: Your tender kinsman and to choke his days
PEMBROKE: With barbarous ignorance and deny his youth
PEMBROKE: The rich advantage of good exercise?
PEMBROKE: That the time's enemies may not have this
PEMBROKE: To grace occasions, let it be our suit
PEMBROKE: That you have bid us ask his liberty,
PEMBROKE: Which for our goods we do no further ask
PEMBROKE: Than whereupon our weal, on you depending,
PEMBROKE: Counts it your weal he have his liberty.
NARRATOR: Enter HUBERT
KING JOHN: Let it be so: I do commit his youth
KING JOHN: To your direction. Hubert, what news with you?
NARRATOR: Taking him apart
PEMBROKE: This is the man should do the bloody deed,
PEMBROKE: He show'd his warrant to a friend of mine:
PEMBROKE: The image of a wicked heinous fault
PEMBROKE: Lives in his eye, that close aspect of his
PEMBROKE: Does show the mood of a much troubled breast,
PEMBROKE: And I do fearfully believe 'tis done,
PEMBROKE: What we so fear'd he had a charge to do.
SALISBURY: The colour of the king doth come and go
SALISBURY: Between his purpose and his conscience,
SALISBURY: Like heralds 'twixt two dreadful battles set:
SALISBURY: His passion is so ripe, it needs must break.
PEMBROKE: And when it breaks, I fear will issue thence
PEMBROKE: The foul corruption of a sweet child's death.
KING JOHN: We cannot hold mortality's strong hand:
KING JOHN: Good lords, although my will to give is living,
KING JOHN: The suit which you demand is gone and dead:
KING JOHN: He tells us Arthur is deceased to-night.
SALISBURY: Indeed we fear'd his sickness was past cure.
PEMBROKE: Indeed we heard how near his death he was
PEMBROKE: Before the child himself felt he was sick:
PEMBROKE: This must be answer'd either here or hence.
KING JOHN: Why do you bend such solemn brows on me?
KING JOHN: Think you I bear the shears of destiny?
KING JOHN: Have I commandment on the pulse of life?
SALISBURY: It is apparent foul play, and 'tis shame
SALISBURY: That greatness should so grossly offer it:
SALISBURY: So thrive it in your game! and so, farewell.
PEMBROKE: Stay yet, Lord Salisbury, I'll go with thee,
PEMBROKE: And find the inheritance of this poor child,
PEMBROKE: His little kingdom of a forced grave.
PEMBROKE: That blood which owed the breadth of all this isle,
PEMBROKE: Three foot of it doth hold: bad world the while!
PEMBROKE: This must not be thus borne: this will break out
PEMBROKE: To all our sorrows, and ere long I doubt.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Lords
KING JOHN: They burn in indignation. I repent:
KING JOHN: There is no sure foundation set on blood,
KING JOHN: No certain life achieved by others' death.
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
KING JOHN: A fearful eye thou hast: where is that blood
KING JOHN: That I have seen inhabit in those cheeks?
KING JOHN: So foul a sky clears not without a storm:
KING JOHN: Pour down thy weather: how goes all in France?
Messenger: From France to England. Never such a power
Messenger: For any foreign preparation
Messenger: Was levied in the body of a land.
Messenger: The copy of your speed is learn'd by them,
Messenger: For when you should be told they do prepare,
Messenger: The tidings come that they are all arrived.
KING JOHN: O, where hath our intelligence been drunk?
KING JOHN: Where hath it slept? Where is my mother's care,
KING JOHN: That such an army could be drawn in France,
KING JOHN: And she not hear of it?
Messenger: My liege, her ear
Messenger: Is stopp'd with dust, the first of April died
Messenger: Your noble mother: and, as I hear, my lord,
Messenger: The Lady Constance in a frenzy died
Messenger: Three days before: but this from rumour's tongue
Messenger: I idly heard, if true or false I know not.
KING JOHN: Withhold thy speed, dreadful occasion!
KING JOHN: O, make a league with me, till I have pleased
KING JOHN: My discontented peers! What! mother dead!
KING JOHN: How wildly then walks my estate in France!
KING JOHN: Under whose conduct came those powers of France
KING JOHN: That thou for truth givest out are landed here?
Messenger: Under the Dauphin.
KING JOHN: Thou hast made me giddy
KING JOHN: With these ill tidings.
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD and PETER of Pomfret
KING JOHN: Now, what says the world
KING JOHN: To your proceedings? do not seek to stuff
KING JOHN: My head with more ill news, for it is full.
BASTARD: But if you be afeard to hear the worst,
BASTARD: Then let the worst unheard fall on your bead.
KING JOHN: Bear with me cousin, for I was amazed
KING JOHN: Under the tide: but now I breathe again
KING JOHN: Aloft the flood, and can give audience
KING JOHN: To any tongue, speak it of what it will.
BASTARD: How I have sped among the clergymen,
BASTARD: The sums I have collected shall express.
BASTARD: But as I travell'd hither through the land,
BASTARD: I find the people strangely fantasied,
BASTARD: Possess'd with rumours, full of idle dreams,
BASTARD: Not knowing what they fear, but full of fear:
BASTARD: And here a prophet, that I brought with me
BASTARD: From forth the streets of Pomfret, whom I found
BASTARD: With many hundreds treading on his heels,
BASTARD: To whom he sung, in rude harsh-sounding rhymes,
BASTARD: That, ere the next Ascension-day at noon,
BASTARD: Your highness should deliver up your crown.
KING JOHN: Thou idle dreamer, wherefore didst thou so?
PETER: Foreknowing that the truth will fall out so.
KING JOHN: Hubert, away with him, imprison him,
KING JOHN: And on that day at noon whereon he says
KING JOHN: I shall yield up my crown, let him be hang'd.
KING JOHN: Deliver him to safety, and return,
KING JOHN: For I must use thee.
NARRATOR: Exeunt HUBERT with PETER
KING JOHN: O my gentle cousin,
KING JOHN: Hear'st thou the news abroad, who are arrived?
BASTARD: The French, my lord, men's mouths are full of it:
BASTARD: Besides, I met Lord Bigot and Lord Salisbury,
BASTARD: With eyes as red as new-enkindled fire,
BASTARD: And others more, going to seek the grave
BASTARD: Of Arthur, who they say is kill'd to-night
BASTARD: On your suggestion.
KING JOHN: Gentle kinsman, go,
KING JOHN: And thrust thyself into their companies:
KING JOHN: I have a way to win their loves again,
KING JOHN: Bring them before me.
BASTARD: I will seek them out.
KING JOHN: Nay, but make haste, the better foot before.
KING JOHN: O, let me have no subject enemies,
KING JOHN: When adverse foreigners affright my towns
KING JOHN: With dreadful pomp of stout invasion!
KING JOHN: Be Mercury, set feathers to thy heels,
KING JOHN: And fly like thought from them to me again.
BASTARD: The spirit of the time shall teach me speed.
NARRATOR: Exit
KING JOHN: Spoke like a sprightful noble gentleman.
KING JOHN: Go after him, for he perhaps shall need
KING JOHN: Some messenger betwixt me and the peers,
KING JOHN: And be thou he.
Messenger: With all my heart, my liege.
NARRATOR: Exit
KING JOHN: My mother dead!
NARRATOR: Re-enter HUBERT
HUBERT: My lord, they say five moons were seen to-night,
HUBERT: Four fixed, and the fifth did whirl about
HUBERT: The other four in wondrous motion.
KING JOHN: Five moons!
HUBERT: Old men and beldams in the streets
HUBERT: Do prophesy upon it dangerously:
HUBERT: Young Arthur's death is common in their mouths:
HUBERT: And when they talk of him, they shake their heads
HUBERT: And whisper one another in the ear,
HUBERT: And he that speaks doth gripe the hearer's wrist,
HUBERT: Whilst he that hears makes fearful action,
HUBERT: With wrinkled brows, with nods, with rolling eyes.
HUBERT: I saw a smith stand with his hammer, thus,
HUBERT: The whilst his iron did on the anvil cool,
HUBERT: With open mouth swallowing a tailor's news,
HUBERT: Who, with his shears and measure in his hand,
HUBERT: Standing on slippers, which his nimble haste
HUBERT: Had falsely thrust upon contrary feet,
HUBERT: Told of a many thousand warlike French
HUBERT: That were embattailed and rank'd in Kent:
HUBERT: Another lean unwash'd artificer
HUBERT: Cuts off his tale and talks of Arthur's death.
KING JOHN: Why seek'st thou to possess me with these fears?
KING JOHN: Why urgest thou so oft young Arthur's death?
KING JOHN: Thy hand hath murder'd him: I had a mighty cause
KING JOHN: To wish him dead, but thou hadst none to kill him.
HUBERT: No had, my lord! why, did you not provoke me?
KING JOHN: It is the curse of kings to be attended
KING JOHN: By slaves that take their humours for a warrant
KING JOHN: To break within the bloody house of life,
KING JOHN: And on the winking of authority
KING JOHN: To understand a law, to know the meaning
KING JOHN: Of dangerous majesty, when perchance it frowns
KING JOHN: More upon humour than advised respect.
HUBERT: Here is your hand and seal for what I did.
KING JOHN: O, when the last account 'twixt heaven and earth
KING JOHN: Is to be made, then shall this hand and seal
KING JOHN: Witness against us to damnation!
KING JOHN: How oft the sight of means to do ill deeds
KING JOHN: Make deeds ill done! Hadst not thou been by,
KING JOHN: A fellow by the hand of nature mark'd,
KING JOHN: Quoted and sign'd to do a deed of shame,
KING JOHN: This murder had not come into my mind:
KING JOHN: But taking note of thy abhorr'd aspect,
KING JOHN: Finding thee fit for bloody villany,
KING JOHN: Apt, liable to be employ'd in danger,
KING JOHN: I faintly broke with thee of Arthur's death,
KING JOHN: And thou, to be endeared to a king,
KING JOHN: Made it no conscience to destroy a prince.
HUBERT: My lord--
KING JOHN: Hadst thou but shook thy head or made a pause
KING JOHN: When I spake darkly what I purposed,
KING JOHN: Or turn'd an eye of doubt upon my face,
KING JOHN: As bid me tell my tale in express words,
KING JOHN: Deep shame had struck me dumb, made me break off,
KING JOHN: And those thy fears might have wrought fears in me:
KING JOHN: But thou didst understand me by my signs
KING JOHN: And didst in signs again parley with sin,
KING JOHN: Yea, without stop, didst let thy heart consent,
KING JOHN: And consequently thy rude hand to act
KING JOHN: The deed, which both our tongues held vile to name.
KING JOHN: Out of my sight, and never see me more!
KING JOHN: My nobles leave me, and my state is braved,
KING JOHN: Even at my gates, with ranks of foreign powers:
KING JOHN: Nay, in the body of this fleshly land,
KING JOHN: This kingdom, this confine of blood and breath,
KING JOHN: Hostility and civil tumult reigns
KING JOHN: Between my conscience and my cousin's death.
HUBERT: Arm you against your other enemies,
HUBERT: I'll make a peace between your soul and you.
HUBERT: Young Arthur is alive: this hand of mine
HUBERT: Is yet a maiden and an innocent hand,
HUBERT: Not painted with the crimson spots of blood.
HUBERT: Within this bosom never enter'd yet
HUBERT: The dreadful motion of a murderous thought,
HUBERT: And you have slander'd nature in my form,
HUBERT: Which, howsoever rude exteriorly,
HUBERT: Is yet the cover of a fairer mind
HUBERT: Than to be butcher of an innocent child.
KING JOHN: Doth Arthur live? O, haste thee to the peers,
KING JOHN: Throw this report on their incensed rage,
KING JOHN: And make them tame to their obedience!
KING JOHN: Forgive the comment that my passion made
KING JOHN: Upon thy feature, for my rage was blind,
KING JOHN: And foul imaginary eyes of blood
KING JOHN: Presented thee more hideous than thou art.
KING JOHN: O, answer not, but to my closet bring
KING JOHN: The angry lords with all expedient haste.
KING JOHN: I conjure thee but slowly, run more fast.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Before the castle.
NARRATOR: Enter ARTHUR, on the walls
ARTHUR: The wall is high, and yet will I leap down:
ARTHUR: Good ground, be pitiful and hurt me not!
ARTHUR: There's few or none do know me: if they did,
ARTHUR: This ship-boy's semblance hath disguised me quite.
ARTHUR: I am afraid, and yet I'll venture it.
ARTHUR: If I get down, and do not break my limbs,
ARTHUR: I'll find a thousand shifts to get away:
ARTHUR: As good to die and go, as die and stay.
NARRATOR: Leaps down
ARTHUR: O me! my uncle's spirit is in these stones:
ARTHUR: Heaven take my soul, and England keep my bones!
NARRATOR: Dies
NARRATOR: Enter PEMBROKE, SALISBURY, and BIGOT
SALISBURY: Lords, I will meet him at Saint Edmundsbury:
SALISBURY: It is our safety, and we must embrace
SALISBURY: This gentle offer of the perilous time.
PEMBROKE: Who brought that letter from the cardinal?
SALISBURY: The Count Melun, a noble lord of France,
SALISBURY: Whose private with me of the Dauphin's love
SALISBURY: Is much more general than these lines import.
BIGOT: To-morrow morning let us meet him then.
SALISBURY: Or rather then set forward, for 'twill be
SALISBURY: Two long days' journey, lords, or ere we meet.
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD
BASTARD: Once more to-day well met, distemper'd lords!
BASTARD: The king by me requests your presence straight.
SALISBURY: The king hath dispossess'd himself of us:
SALISBURY: We will not line his thin bestained cloak
SALISBURY: With our pure honours, nor attend the foot
SALISBURY: That leaves the print of blood where'er it walks.
SALISBURY: Return and tell him so: we know the worst.
BASTARD: Whate'er you think, good words, I think, were best.
SALISBURY: Our griefs, and not our manners, reason now.
BASTARD: But there is little reason in your grief,
BASTARD: Therefore 'twere reason you had manners now.
PEMBROKE: Sir, sir, impatience hath his privilege.
BASTARD: 'Tis true, to hurt his master, no man else.
SALISBURY: This is the prison. What is he lies here?
NARRATOR: Seeing ARTHUR
PEMBROKE: O death, made proud with pure and princely beauty!
PEMBROKE: The earth had not a hole to hide this deed.
SALISBURY: Murder, as hating what himself hath done,
SALISBURY: Doth lay it open to urge on revenge.
BIGOT: Or, when he doom'd this beauty to a grave,
BIGOT: Found it too precious-princely for a grave.
SALISBURY: Sir Richard, what think you? have you beheld,
SALISBURY: Or have you read or heard? or could you think?
SALISBURY: Or do you almost think, although you see,
SALISBURY: That you do see? could thought, without this object,
SALISBURY: Form such another? This is the very top,
SALISBURY: The height, the crest, or crest unto the crest,
SALISBURY: Of murder's arms: this is the bloodiest shame,
SALISBURY: The wildest savagery, the vilest stroke,
SALISBURY: That ever wall-eyed wrath or staring rage
SALISBURY: Presented to the tears of soft remorse.
PEMBROKE: All murders past do stand excused in this:
PEMBROKE: And this, so sole and so unmatchable,
PEMBROKE: Shall give a holiness, a purity,
PEMBROKE: To the yet unbegotten sin of times,
PEMBROKE: And prove a deadly bloodshed but a jest,
PEMBROKE: Exampled by this heinous spectacle.
BASTARD: It is a damned and a bloody work,
BASTARD: The graceless action of a heavy hand,
BASTARD: If that it be the work of any hand.
SALISBURY: If that it be the work of any hand!
SALISBURY: We had a kind of light what would ensue:
SALISBURY: It is the shameful work of Hubert's hand,
SALISBURY: The practise and the purpose of the king:
SALISBURY: From whose obedience I forbid my soul,
SALISBURY: Kneeling before this ruin of sweet life,
SALISBURY: And breathing to his breathless excellence
SALISBURY: The incense of a vow, a holy vow,
SALISBURY: Never to taste the pleasures of the world,
SALISBURY: Never to be infected with delight,
SALISBURY: Nor conversant with ease and idleness,
SALISBURY: Till I have set a glory to this hand,
SALISBURY: By giving it the worship of revenge.
BIGOT: Our souls religiously confirm thy words.
NARRATOR: Enter HUBERT
HUBERT: Lords, I am hot with haste in seeking you:
HUBERT: Arthur doth live, the king hath sent for you.
SALISBURY: O, he is old and blushes not at death.
SALISBURY: Avaunt, thou hateful villain, get thee gone!
HUBERT: I am no villain.
SALISBURY: Must I rob the law?
NARRATOR: Drawing his sword
BASTARD: Your sword is bright, sir, put it up again.
SALISBURY: Not till I sheathe it in a murderer's skin.
HUBERT: Stand back, Lord Salisbury, stand back, I say,
HUBERT: By heaven, I think my sword's as sharp as yours:
HUBERT: I would not have you, lord, forget yourself,
HUBERT: Nor tempt the danger of my true defence,
HUBERT: Lest I, by marking of your rage, forget
HUBERT: Your worth, your greatness and nobility.
BIGOT: Out, dunghill! darest thou brave a nobleman?
HUBERT: Not for my life: but yet I dare defend
HUBERT: My innocent life against an emperor.
SALISBURY: Thou art a murderer.
HUBERT: Do not prove me so,
HUBERT: Yet I am none: whose tongue soe'er speaks false,
HUBERT: Not truly speaks, who speaks not truly, lies.
PEMBROKE: Cut him to pieces.
BASTARD: Keep the peace, I say.
SALISBURY: Stand by, or I shall gall you, Faulconbridge.
BASTARD: Thou wert better gall the devil, Salisbury:
BASTARD: If thou but frown on me, or stir thy foot,
BASTARD: Or teach thy hasty spleen to do me shame,
BASTARD: I'll strike thee dead. Put up thy sword betime,
BASTARD: Or I'll so maul you and your toasting-iron,
BASTARD: That you shall think the devil is come from hell.
BIGOT: What wilt thou do, renowned Faulconbridge?
BIGOT: Second a villain and a murderer?
HUBERT: Lord Bigot, I am none.
BIGOT: Who kill'd this prince?
HUBERT: 'Tis not an hour since I left him well:
HUBERT: I honour'd him, I loved him, and will weep
HUBERT: My date of life out for his sweet life's loss.
SALISBURY: Trust not those cunning waters of his eyes,
SALISBURY: For villany is not without such rheum,
SALISBURY: And he, long traded in it, makes it seem
SALISBURY: Like rivers of remorse and innocency.
SALISBURY: Away with me, all you whose souls abhor
SALISBURY: The uncleanly savours of a slaughter-house,
SALISBURY: For I am stifled with this smell of sin.
BIGOT: Away toward Bury, to the Dauphin there!
PEMBROKE: There tell the king he may inquire us out.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Lords
BASTARD: Here's a good world! Knew you of this fair work?
BASTARD: Beyond the infinite and boundless reach
BASTARD: Of mercy, if thou didst this deed of death,
BASTARD: Art thou damn'd, Hubert.
HUBERT: Do but hear me, sir.
BASTARD: Ha! I'll tell thee what,
BASTARD: Thou'rt damn'd as black--nay, nothing is so black,
BASTARD: Thou art more deep damn'd than Prince Lucifer:
BASTARD: There is not yet so ugly a fiend of hell
BASTARD: As thou shalt be, if thou didst kill this child.
HUBERT: Upon my soul--
BASTARD: If thou didst but consent
BASTARD: To this most cruel act, do but despair,
BASTARD: And if thou want'st a cord, the smallest thread
BASTARD: That ever spider twisted from her womb
BASTARD: Will serve to strangle thee, a rush will be a beam
BASTARD: To hang thee on, or wouldst thou drown thyself,
BASTARD: Put but a little water in a spoon,
BASTARD: And it shall be as all the ocean,
BASTARD: Enough to stifle such a villain up.
BASTARD: I do suspect thee very grievously.
HUBERT: If I in act, consent, or sin of thought,
HUBERT: Be guilty of the stealing that sweet breath
HUBERT: Which was embounded in this beauteous clay,
HUBERT: Let hell want pains enough to torture me.
HUBERT: I left him well.
BASTARD: Go, bear him in thine arms.
BASTARD: I am amazed, methinks, and lose my way
BASTARD: Among the thorns and dangers of this world.
BASTARD: How easy dost thou take all England up!
BASTARD: From forth this morsel of dead royalty,
BASTARD: The life, the right and truth of all this realm
BASTARD: Is fled to heaven, and England now is left
BASTARD: To tug and scamble and to part by the teeth
BASTARD: The unowed interest of proud-swelling state.
BASTARD: Now for the bare-pick'd bone of majesty
BASTARD: Doth dogged war bristle his angry crest
BASTARD: And snarleth in the gentle eyes of peace:
BASTARD: Now powers from home and discontents at home
BASTARD: Meet in one line, and vast confusion waits,
BASTARD: As doth a raven on a sick-fall'n beast,
BASTARD: The imminent decay of wrested pomp.
BASTARD: Now happy he whose cloak and cincture can
BASTARD: Hold out this tempest. Bear away that child
BASTARD: And follow me with speed: I'll to the king:
BASTARD: A thousand businesses are brief in hand,
BASTARD: And heaven itself doth frown upon the land.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT V
NARRATOR: SCENE I. KING JOHN'S palace.
NARRATOR: Enter KING JOHN, CARDINAL PANDULPH, and Attendants
KING JOHN: Thus have I yielded up into your hand
KING JOHN: The circle of my glory.
NARRATOR: Giving the crown
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Take again
CARDINAL PANDULPH: From this my hand, as holding of the pope
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Your sovereign greatness and authority.
KING JOHN: Now keep your holy word: go meet the French,
KING JOHN: And from his holiness use all your power
KING JOHN: To stop their marches 'fore we are inflamed.
KING JOHN: Our discontented counties do revolt,
KING JOHN: Our people quarrel with obedience,
KING JOHN: Swearing allegiance and the love of soul
KING JOHN: To stranger blood, to foreign royalty.
KING JOHN: This inundation of mistemper'd humour
KING JOHN: Rests by you only to be qualified:
KING JOHN: Then pause not, for the present time's so sick,
KING JOHN: That present medicine must be minister'd,
KING JOHN: Or overthrow incurable ensues.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: It was my breath that blew this tempest up,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Upon your stubborn usage of the pope,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: But since you are a gentle convertite,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: My tongue shall hush again this storm of war
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And make fair weather in your blustering land.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: On this Ascension-day, remember well,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Upon your oath of service to the pope,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Go I to make the French lay down their arms.
NARRATOR: Exit
KING JOHN: Is this Ascension-day? Did not the prophet
KING JOHN: Say that before Ascension-day at noon
KING JOHN: My crown I should give off? Even so I have:
KING JOHN: I did suppose it should be on constraint:
KING JOHN: But, heaven be thank'd, it is but voluntary.
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD
BASTARD: All Kent hath yielded, nothing there holds out
BASTARD: But Dover castle: London hath received,
BASTARD: Like a kind host, the Dauphin and his powers:
BASTARD: Your nobles will not hear you, but are gone
BASTARD: To offer service to your enemy,
BASTARD: And wild amazement hurries up and down
BASTARD: The little number of your doubtful friends.
KING JOHN: Would not my lords return to me again,
KING JOHN: After they heard young Arthur was alive?
BASTARD: They found him dead and cast into the streets,
BASTARD: An empty casket, where the jewel of life
BASTARD: By some damn'd hand was robb'd and ta'en away.
KING JOHN: That villain Hubert told me he did live.
BASTARD: So, on my soul, he did, for aught he knew.
BASTARD: But wherefore do you droop? why look you sad?
BASTARD: Be great in act, as you have been in thought,
BASTARD: Let not the world see fear and sad distrust
BASTARD: Govern the motion of a kingly eye:
BASTARD: Be stirring as the time, be fire with fire,
BASTARD: Threaten the threatener and outface the brow
BASTARD: Of bragging horror: so shall inferior eyes,
BASTARD: That borrow their behaviors from the great,
BASTARD: Grow great by your example and put on
BASTARD: The dauntless spirit of resolution.
BASTARD: Away, and glister like the god of war,
BASTARD: When he intendeth to become the field:
BASTARD: Show boldness and aspiring confidence.
BASTARD: What, shall they seek the lion in his den,
BASTARD: And fright him there? and make him tremble there?
BASTARD: O, let it not be said: forage, and run
BASTARD: To meet displeasure farther from the doors,
BASTARD: And grapple with him ere he comes so nigh.
KING JOHN: The legate of the pope hath been with me,
KING JOHN: And I have made a happy peace with him,
KING JOHN: And he hath promised to dismiss the powers
KING JOHN: Led by the Dauphin.
BASTARD: O inglorious league!
BASTARD: Shall we, upon the footing of our land,
BASTARD: Send fair-play orders and make compromise,
BASTARD: Insinuation, parley and base truce
BASTARD: To arms invasive? shall a beardless boy,
BASTARD: A cocker'd silken wanton, brave our fields,
BASTARD: And flesh his spirit in a warlike soil,
BASTARD: Mocking the air with colours idly spread,
BASTARD: And find no cheque? Let us, my liege, to arms:
BASTARD: Perchance the cardinal cannot make your peace,
BASTARD: Or if he do, let it at least be said
BASTARD: They saw we had a purpose of defence.
KING JOHN: Have thou the ordering of this present time.
BASTARD: Away, then, with good courage! yet, I know,
BASTARD: Our party may well meet a prouder foe.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. LEWIS's camp at St. Edmundsbury.
NARRATOR: Enter, in arms, LEWIS, SALISBURY, MELUN, PEMBROKE, BIGOT, and Soldiers
LEWIS: My Lord Melun, let this be copied out,
LEWIS: And keep it safe for our remembrance:
LEWIS: Return the precedent to these lords again,
LEWIS: That, having our fair order written down,
LEWIS: Both they and we, perusing o'er these notes,
LEWIS: May know wherefore we took the sacrament
LEWIS: And keep our faiths firm and inviolable.
SALISBURY: Upon our sides it never shall be broken.
SALISBURY: And, noble Dauphin, albeit we swear
SALISBURY: A voluntary zeal and an unurged faith
SALISBURY: To your proceedings, yet believe me, prince,
SALISBURY: I am not glad that such a sore of time
SALISBURY: Should seek a plaster by contemn'd revolt,
SALISBURY: And heal the inveterate canker of one wound
SALISBURY: By making many. O, it grieves my soul,
SALISBURY: That I must draw this metal from my side
SALISBURY: To be a widow-maker! O, and there
SALISBURY: Where honourable rescue and defence
SALISBURY: Cries out upon the name of Salisbury!
SALISBURY: But such is the infection of the time,
SALISBURY: That, for the health and physic of our right,
SALISBURY: We cannot deal but with the very hand
SALISBURY: Of stern injustice and confused wrong.
SALISBURY: And is't not pity, O my grieved friends,
SALISBURY: That we, the sons and children of this isle,
SALISBURY: Were born to see so sad an hour as this,
SALISBURY: Wherein we step after a stranger march
SALISBURY: Upon her gentle bosom, and fill up
SALISBURY: Her enemies' ranks,--I must withdraw and weep
SALISBURY: Upon the spot of this enforced cause,--
SALISBURY: To grace the gentry of a land remote,
SALISBURY: And follow unacquainted colours here?
SALISBURY: What, here? O nation, that thou couldst remove!
SALISBURY: That Neptune's arms, who clippeth thee about,
SALISBURY: Would bear thee from the knowledge of thyself,
SALISBURY: And grapple thee unto a pagan shore,
SALISBURY: Where these two Christian armies might combine
SALISBURY: The blood of malice in a vein of league,
SALISBURY: And not to spend it so unneighbourly!
LEWIS: A noble temper dost thou show in this,
LEWIS: And great affections wrestling in thy bosom
LEWIS: Doth make an earthquake of nobility.
LEWIS: O, what a noble combat hast thou fought
LEWIS: Between compulsion and a brave respect!
LEWIS: Let me wipe off this honourable dew,
LEWIS: That silverly doth progress on thy cheeks:
LEWIS: My heart hath melted at a lady's tears,
LEWIS: Being an ordinary inundation,
LEWIS: But this effusion of such manly drops,
LEWIS: This shower, blown up by tempest of the soul,
LEWIS: Startles mine eyes, and makes me more amazed
LEWIS: Than had I seen the vaulty top of heaven
LEWIS: Figured quite o'er with burning meteors.
LEWIS: Lift up thy brow, renowned Salisbury,
LEWIS: And with a great heart heave away the storm:
LEWIS: Commend these waters to those baby eyes
LEWIS: That never saw the giant world enraged,
LEWIS: Nor met with fortune other than at feasts,
LEWIS: Full of warm blood, of mirth, of gossiping.
LEWIS: Come, come, for thou shalt thrust thy hand as deep
LEWIS: Into the purse of rich prosperity
LEWIS: As Lewis himself: so, nobles, shall you all,
LEWIS: That knit your sinews to the strength of mine.
LEWIS: And even there, methinks, an angel spake:
NARRATOR: Enter CARDINAL PANDULPH
LEWIS: Look, where the holy legate comes apace,
LEWIS: To give us warrant from the hand of heaven
LEWIS: And on our actions set the name of right
LEWIS: With holy breath.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Hail, noble prince of France!
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The next is this, King John hath reconciled
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Himself to Rome, his spirit is come in,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That so stood out against the holy church,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The great metropolis and see of Rome:
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Therefore thy threatening colours now wind up,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And tame the savage spirit of wild war,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: That like a lion foster'd up at hand,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: It may lie gently at the foot of peace,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And be no further harmful than in show.
LEWIS: Your grace shall pardon me, I will not back:
LEWIS: I am too high-born to be propertied,
LEWIS: To be a secondary at control,
LEWIS: Or useful serving-man and instrument,
LEWIS: To any sovereign state throughout the world.
LEWIS: Your breath first kindled the dead coal of wars
LEWIS: Between this chastised kingdom and myself,
LEWIS: And brought in matter that should feed this fire,
LEWIS: And now 'tis far too huge to be blown out
LEWIS: With that same weak wind which enkindled it.
LEWIS: You taught me how to know the face of right,
LEWIS: Acquainted me with interest to this land,
LEWIS: Yea, thrust this enterprise into my heart,
LEWIS: And come ye now to tell me John hath made
LEWIS: His peace with Rome? What is that peace to me?
LEWIS: I, by the honour of my marriage-bed,
LEWIS: After young Arthur, claim this land for mine,
LEWIS: And, now it is half-conquer'd, must I back
LEWIS: Because that John hath made his peace with Rome?
LEWIS: Am I Rome's slave? What penny hath Rome borne,
LEWIS: What men provided, what munition sent,
LEWIS: To underprop this action? Is't not I
LEWIS: That undergo this charge? who else but I,
LEWIS: And such as to my claim are liable,
LEWIS: Sweat in this business and maintain this war?
LEWIS: Have I not heard these islanders shout out
LEWIS: 'Vive le roi!' as I have bank'd their towns?
LEWIS: Have I not here the best cards for the game,
LEWIS: To win this easy match play'd for a crown?
LEWIS: And shall I now give o'er the yielded set?
LEWIS: No, no, on my soul, it never shall be said.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: You look but on the outside of this work.
LEWIS: Outside or inside, I will not return
LEWIS: Till my attempt so much be glorified
LEWIS: As to my ample hope was promised
LEWIS: Before I drew this gallant head of war,
LEWIS: And cull'd these fiery spirits from the world,
LEWIS: To outlook conquest and to win renown
LEWIS: Even in the jaws of danger and of death.
NARRATOR: Trumpet sounds
LEWIS: What lusty trumpet thus doth summon us?
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD, attended
BASTARD: According to the fair play of the world,
BASTARD: Let me have audience, I am sent to speak:
BASTARD: My holy lord of Milan, from the king
BASTARD: I come, to learn how you have dealt for him,
BASTARD: And, as you answer, I do know the scope
BASTARD: And warrant limited unto my tongue.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: The Dauphin is too wilful-opposite,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: And will not temporize with my entreaties,
CARDINAL PANDULPH: He flatly says he'll not lay down his arms.
BASTARD: By all the blood that ever fury breathed,
BASTARD: The youth says well. Now hear our English king,
BASTARD: For thus his royalty doth speak in me.
BASTARD: He is prepared, and reason too he should:
BASTARD: This apish and unmannerly approach,
BASTARD: This harness'd masque and unadvised revel,
BASTARD: This unhair'd sauciness and boyish troops,
BASTARD: The king doth smile at, and is well prepared
BASTARD: To whip this dwarfish war, these pigmy arms,
BASTARD: From out the circle of his territories.
BASTARD: That hand which had the strength, even at your door,
BASTARD: To cudgel you and make you take the hatch,
BASTARD: To dive like buckets in concealed wells,
BASTARD: To crouch in litter of your stable planks,
BASTARD: To lie like pawns lock'd up in chests and trunks,
BASTARD: To hug with swine, to seek sweet safety out
BASTARD: In vaults and prisons, and to thrill and shake
BASTARD: Even at the crying of your nation's crow,
BASTARD: Thinking his voice an armed Englishman,
BASTARD: Shall that victorious hand be feebled here,
BASTARD: That in your chambers gave you chastisement?
BASTARD: No: know the gallant monarch is in arms
BASTARD: And like an eagle o'er his aery towers,
BASTARD: To souse annoyance that comes near his nest.
BASTARD: And you degenerate, you ingrate revolts,
BASTARD: You bloody Neroes, ripping up the womb
BASTARD: Of your dear mother England, blush for shame,
BASTARD: For your own ladies and pale-visaged maids
BASTARD: Like Amazons come tripping after drums,
BASTARD: Their thimbles into armed gauntlets change,
BASTARD: Their needles to lances, and their gentle hearts
BASTARD: To fierce and bloody inclination.
LEWIS: There end thy brave, and turn thy face in peace,
LEWIS: We grant thou canst outscold us: fare thee well,
LEWIS: We hold our time too precious to be spent
LEWIS: With such a brabbler.
CARDINAL PANDULPH: Give me leave to speak.
BASTARD: No, I will speak.
LEWIS: We will attend to neither.
LEWIS: Strike up the drums, and let the tongue of war
LEWIS: Plead for our interest and our being here.
BASTARD: Indeed your drums, being beaten, will cry out,
BASTARD: And so shall you, being beaten: do but start
BASTARD: An echo with the clamour of thy drum,
BASTARD: And even at hand a drum is ready braced
BASTARD: That shall reverberate all as loud as thine,
BASTARD: Sound but another, and another shall
BASTARD: As loud as thine rattle the welkin's ear
BASTARD: And mock the deep-mouth'd thunder: for at hand,
BASTARD: Not trusting to this halting legate here,
BASTARD: Whom he hath used rather for sport than need
BASTARD: Is warlike John, and in his forehead sits
BASTARD: A bare-ribb'd death, whose office is this day
BASTARD: To feast upon whole thousands of the French.
LEWIS: Strike up our drums, to find this danger out.
BASTARD: And thou shalt find it, Dauphin, do not doubt.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. The field of battle.
NARRATOR: Alarums. Enter KING JOHN and HUBERT
KING JOHN: How goes the day with us? O, tell me, Hubert.
HUBERT: Badly, I fear. How fares your majesty?
KING JOHN: This fever, that hath troubled me so long,
KING JOHN: Lies heavy on me, O, my heart is sick!
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
Messenger: My lord, your valiant kinsman, Faulconbridge,
Messenger: Desires your majesty to leave the field
Messenger: And send him word by me which way you go.
KING JOHN: Tell him, toward Swinstead, to the abbey there.
Messenger: Be of good comfort, for the great supply
Messenger: That was expected by the Dauphin here,
Messenger: Are wreck'd three nights ago on Goodwin Sands.
Messenger: This news was brought to Richard but even now:
Messenger: The French fight coldly, and retire themselves.
KING JOHN: Ay me! this tyrant fever burns me up,
KING JOHN: And will not let me welcome this good news.
KING JOHN: Set on toward Swinstead: to my litter straight,
KING JOHN: Weakness possesseth me, and I am faint.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Another part of the field.
NARRATOR: Enter SALISBURY, PEMBROKE, and BIGOT
SALISBURY: I did not think the king so stored with friends.
PEMBROKE: Up once again, put spirit in the French:
PEMBROKE: If they miscarry, we miscarry too.
SALISBURY: That misbegotten devil, Faulconbridge,
SALISBURY: In spite of spite, alone upholds the day.
PEMBROKE: They say King John sore sick hath left the field.
NARRATOR: Enter MELUN, wounded
MELUN: Lead me to the revolts of England here.
SALISBURY: When we were happy we had other names.
PEMBROKE: It is the Count Melun.
SALISBURY: Wounded to death.
MELUN: Fly, noble English, you are bought and sold,
MELUN: Unthread the rude eye of rebellion
MELUN: And welcome home again discarded faith.
MELUN: Seek out King John and fall before his feet,
MELUN: For if the French be lords of this loud day,
MELUN: He means to recompense the pains you take
MELUN: By cutting off your heads: thus hath he sworn
MELUN: And I with him, and many moe with me,
MELUN: Upon the altar at Saint Edmundsbury,
MELUN: Even on that altar where we swore to you
MELUN: Dear amity and everlasting love.
SALISBURY: May this be possible? may this be true?
MELUN: Have I not hideous death within my view,
MELUN: Retaining but a quantity of life,
MELUN: Which bleeds away, even as a form of wax
MELUN: Resolveth from his figure 'gainst the fire?
MELUN: What in the world should make me now deceive,
MELUN: Since I must lose the use of all deceit?
MELUN: Why should I then be false, since it is true
MELUN: That I must die here and live hence by truth?
MELUN: I say again, if Lewis do win the day,
MELUN: He is forsworn, if e'er those eyes of yours
MELUN: Behold another day break in the east:
MELUN: But even this night, whose black contagious breath
MELUN: Already smokes about the burning crest
MELUN: Of the old, feeble and day-wearied sun,
MELUN: Even this ill night, your breathing shall expire,
MELUN: Paying the fine of rated treachery
MELUN: Even with a treacherous fine of all your lives,
MELUN: If Lewis by your assistance win the day.
MELUN: Commend me to one Hubert with your king:
MELUN: The love of him, and this respect besides,
MELUN: For that my grandsire was an Englishman,
MELUN: Awakes my conscience to confess all this.
MELUN: In lieu whereof, I pray you, bear me hence
MELUN: From forth the noise and rumour of the field,
MELUN: Where I may think the remnant of my thoughts
MELUN: In peace, and part this body and my soul
MELUN: With contemplation and devout desires.
SALISBURY: We do believe thee: and beshrew my soul
SALISBURY: But I do love the favour and the form
SALISBURY: Of this most fair occasion, by the which
SALISBURY: We will untread the steps of damned flight,
SALISBURY: And like a bated and retired flood,
SALISBURY: Leaving our rankness and irregular course,
SALISBURY: Stoop low within those bounds we have o'erlook'd
SALISBURY: And cabby run on in obedience
SALISBURY: Even to our ocean, to our great King John.
SALISBURY: My arm shall give thee help to bear thee hence,
SALISBURY: For I do see the cruel pangs of death
SALISBURY: Right in thine eye. Away, my friends! New flight,
SALISBURY: And happy newness, that intends old right.
NARRATOR: Exeunt, leading off MELUN
NARRATOR: SCENE V. The French camp.
NARRATOR: Enter LEWIS and his train
LEWIS: The sun of heaven methought was loath to set,
LEWIS: But stay'd and made the western welkin blush,
LEWIS: When English measure backward their own ground
LEWIS: In faint retire. O, bravely came we off,
LEWIS: When with a volley of our needless shot,
LEWIS: After such bloody toil, we bid good night,
LEWIS: And wound our tattering colours clearly up,
LEWIS: Last in the field, and almost lords of it!
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
Messenger: Where is my prince, the Dauphin?
LEWIS: Here: what news?
Messenger: The Count Melun is slain, the English lords
Messenger: By his persuasion are again fall'n off,
Messenger: And your supply, which you have wish'd so long,
Messenger: Are cast away and sunk on Goodwin Sands.
LEWIS: Ah, foul shrewd news! beshrew thy very heart!
LEWIS: I did not think to be so sad to-night
LEWIS: As this hath made me. Who was he that said
LEWIS: King John did fly an hour or two before
LEWIS: The stumbling night did part our weary powers?
Messenger: Whoever spoke it, it is true, my lord.
LEWIS: Well, keep good quarter and good care to-night:
LEWIS: The day shall not be up so soon as I,
LEWIS: To try the fair adventure of to-morrow.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE VI. An open place in the neighbourhood of Swinstead Abbey.
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD and HUBERT, severally
HUBERT: Who's there? speak, ho! speak quickly, or I shoot.
BASTARD: A friend. What art thou?
HUBERT: Of the part of England.
BASTARD: Whither dost thou go?
HUBERT: What's that to thee? why may not I demand
HUBERT: Of thine affairs, as well as thou of mine?
BASTARD: Hubert, I think?
HUBERT: Thou hast a perfect thought:
HUBERT: I will upon all hazards well believe
HUBERT: Thou art my friend, that know'st my tongue so well.
HUBERT: Who art thou?
BASTARD: Who thou wilt: and if thou please,
BASTARD: Thou mayst befriend me so much as to think
BASTARD: I come one way of the Plantagenets.
HUBERT: Unkind remembrance! thou and eyeless night
HUBERT: Have done me shame: brave soldier, pardon me,
HUBERT: That any accent breaking from thy tongue
HUBERT: Should 'scape the true acquaintance of mine ear.
BASTARD: Come, come, sans compliment, what news abroad?
HUBERT: Why, here walk I in the black brow of night,
HUBERT: To find you out.
BASTARD: Brief, then, and what's the news?
HUBERT: O, my sweet sir, news fitting to the night,
HUBERT: Black, fearful, comfortless and horrible.
BASTARD: Show me the very wound of this ill news:
BASTARD: I am no woman, I'll not swoon at it.
HUBERT: The king, I fear, is poison'd by a monk:
HUBERT: I left him almost speechless, and broke out
HUBERT: To acquaint you with this evil, that you might
HUBERT: The better arm you to the sudden time,
HUBERT: Than if you had at leisure known of this.
BASTARD: How did he take it? who did taste to him?
HUBERT: A monk, I tell you, a resolved villain,
HUBERT: Whose bowels suddenly burst out: the king
HUBERT: Yet speaks and peradventure may recover.
BASTARD: Who didst thou leave to tend his majesty?
HUBERT: Why, know you not? the lords are all come back,
HUBERT: And brought Prince Henry in their company,
HUBERT: At whose request the king hath pardon'd them,
HUBERT: And they are all about his majesty.
BASTARD: Withhold thine indignation, mighty heaven,
BASTARD: And tempt us not to bear above our power!
BASTARD: I'll tell tree, Hubert, half my power this night,
BASTARD: Passing these flats, are taken by the tide,
BASTARD: These Lincoln Washes have devoured them,
BASTARD: Myself, well mounted, hardly have escaped.
BASTARD: Away before: conduct me to the king,
BASTARD: I doubt he will be dead or ere I come.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE VII. The orchard in Swinstead Abbey.
NARRATOR: Enter PRINCE HENRY, SALISBURY, and BIGOT
PRINCE HENRY: It is too late: the life of all his blood
PRINCE HENRY: Is touch'd corruptibly, and his pure brain,
PRINCE HENRY: Which some suppose the soul's frail dwelling-house,
PRINCE HENRY: Doth by the idle comments that it makes
PRINCE HENRY: Foretell the ending of mortality.
NARRATOR: Enter PEMBROKE
PEMBROKE: His highness yet doth speak, and holds belief
PEMBROKE: That, being brought into the open air,
PEMBROKE: It would allay the burning quality
PEMBROKE: Of that fell poison which assaileth him.
PRINCE HENRY: Let him be brought into the orchard here.
PRINCE HENRY: Doth he still rage?
NARRATOR: Exit BIGOT
PEMBROKE: He is more patient
PEMBROKE: Than when you left him, even now he sung.
PRINCE HENRY: O vanity of sickness! fierce extremes
PRINCE HENRY: In their continuance will not feel themselves.
PRINCE HENRY: Death, having prey'd upon the outward parts,
PRINCE HENRY: Leaves them invisible, and his siege is now
PRINCE HENRY: Against the mind, the which he pricks and wounds
PRINCE HENRY: With many legions of strange fantasies,
PRINCE HENRY: Whi ch, in their throng and press to that last hold,
PRINCE HENRY: Confound themselves. 'Tis strange that death
PRINCE HENRY: should sing.
PRINCE HENRY: I am the cygnet to this pale faint swan,
PRINCE HENRY: Who chants a doleful hymn to his own death,
PRINCE HENRY: And from the organ-pipe of frailty sings
PRINCE HENRY: His soul and body to their lasting rest.
SALISBURY: Be of good comfort, prince, for you are born
SALISBURY: To set a form upon that indigest
SALISBURY: Which he hath left so shapeless and so rude.
NARRATOR: Enter Attendants, and BIGOT, carrying KING JOHN in a chair
KING JOHN: Ay, marry, now my soul hath elbow-room,
KING JOHN: It would not out at windows nor at doors.
KING JOHN: There is so hot a summer in my bosom,
KING JOHN: That all my bowels crumble up to dust:
KING JOHN: I am a scribbled form, drawn with a pen
KING JOHN: Upon a parchment, and against this fire
KING JOHN: Do I shrink up.
PRINCE HENRY: How fares your majesty?
KING JOHN: Poison'd,--ill fare--dead, forsook, cast off:
KING JOHN: And none of you will bid the winter come
KING JOHN: To thrust his icy fingers in my maw,
KING JOHN: Nor let my kingdom's rivers take their course
KING JOHN: Through my burn'd bosom, nor entreat the north
KING JOHN: To make his bleak winds kiss my parched lips
KING JOHN: And comfort me with cold. I do not ask you much,
KING JOHN: I beg cold comfort, and you are so strait
KING JOHN: And so ingrateful, you deny me that.
PRINCE HENRY: O that there were some virtue in my tears,
PRINCE HENRY: That might relieve you!
KING JOHN: The salt in them is hot.
KING JOHN: Within me is a hell, and there the poison
KING JOHN: Is as a fiend confined to tyrannize
KING JOHN: On unreprievable condemned blood.
NARRATOR: Enter the BASTARD
BASTARD: O, I am scalded with my violent motion,
BASTARD: And spleen of speed to see your majesty!
KING JOHN: O cousin, thou art come to set mine eye:
KING JOHN: The tackle of my heart is crack'd and burn'd,
KING JOHN: And all the shrouds wherewith my life should sail
KING JOHN: Are turned to one thread, one little hair:
KING JOHN: My heart hath one poor string to stay it by,
KING JOHN: Which holds but till thy news be uttered,
KING JOHN: And then all this thou seest is but a clod
KING JOHN: And module of confounded royalty.
BASTARD: The Dauphin is preparing hitherward,
BASTARD: Where heaven He knows how we shall answer him,
BASTARD: For in a night the best part of my power,
BASTARD: As I upon advantage did remove,
BASTARD: Were in the Washes all unwarily
BASTARD: Devoured by the unexpected flood.
NARRATOR: KING JOHN dies
SALISBURY: You breathe these dead news in as dead an ear.
SALISBURY: My liege! my lord! but now a king, now thus.
PRINCE HENRY: Even so must I run on, and even so stop.
PRINCE HENRY: What surety of the world, what hope, what stay,
PRINCE HENRY: When this was now a king, and now is clay?
BASTARD: Art thou gone so? I do but stay behind
BASTARD: To do the office for thee of revenge,
BASTARD: And then my soul shall wait on thee to heaven,
BASTARD: As it on earth hath been thy servant still.
BASTARD: Now, now, you stars that move in your right spheres,
BASTARD: Where be your powers? show now your mended faiths,
BASTARD: And instantly return with me again,
BASTARD: To push destruction and perpetual shame
BASTARD: Out of the weak door of our fainting land.
BASTARD: Straight let us seek, or straight we shall be sought,
BASTARD: The Dauphin rages at our very heels.
SALISBURY: It seems you know not, then, so much as we:
SALISBURY: The Cardinal Pandulph is within at rest,
SALISBURY: Who half an hour since came from the Dauphin,
SALISBURY: And brings from him such offers of our peace
SALISBURY: As we with honour and respect may take,
SALISBURY: With purpose presently to leave this war.
BASTARD: He will the rather do it when he sees
BASTARD: Ourselves well sinewed to our defence.
SALISBURY: Nay, it is in a manner done already,
SALISBURY: For many carriages he hath dispatch'd
