FERDINAND: How fares your majesty?
PRINCESS: Boyet, prepare, I will away tonight.
FERDINAND: Madam, not so, I do beseech you, stay.
PRINCESS: Prepare, I say. I thank you, gracious lords,
PRINCESS: For all your fair endeavors, and entreat,
PRINCESS: Out of a new-sad soul, that you vouchsafe
PRINCESS: In your rich wisdom to excuse or hide
PRINCESS: The liberal opposition of our spirits,
PRINCESS: If over-boldly we have borne ourselves
PRINCESS: In the converse of breath: your gentleness
PRINCESS: Was guilty of it. Farewell worthy lord!
PRINCESS: A heavy heart bears not a nimble tongue:
PRINCESS: Excuse me so, coming too short of thanks
PRINCESS: For my great suit so easily obtain'd.
FERDINAND: The extreme parts of time extremely forms
FERDINAND: All causes to the purpose of his speed,
FERDINAND: And often at his very loose decides
FERDINAND: That which long process could not arbitrate:
FERDINAND: And though the mourning brow of progeny
FERDINAND: Forbid the smiling courtesy of love
FERDINAND: The holy suit which fain it would convince,
FERDINAND: Yet, since love's argument was first on foot,
FERDINAND: Let not the cloud of sorrow justle it
FERDINAND: From what it purposed, since, to wail friends lost
FERDINAND: Is not by much so wholesome-profitable
FERDINAND: As to rejoice at friends but newly found.
PRINCESS: I understand you not: my griefs are double.
BIRON: Honest plain words best pierce the ear of grief,
BIRON: And by these badges understand the king.
BIRON: For your fair sakes have we neglected time,
BIRON: Play'd foul play with our oaths: your beauty, ladies,
BIRON: Hath much deform'd us, fashioning our humours
BIRON: Even to the opposed end of our intents:
BIRON: And what in us hath seem'd ridiculous,--
BIRON: As love is full of unbefitting strains,
BIRON: All wanton as a child, skipping and vain,
BIRON: Form'd by the eye and therefore, like the eye,
BIRON: Full of strange shapes, of habits and of forms,
BIRON: Varying in subjects as the eye doth roll
BIRON: To every varied object in his glance:
BIRON: Which parti-coated presence of loose love
BIRON: Put on by us, if, in your heavenly eyes,
BIRON: Have misbecomed our oaths and gravities,
BIRON: Those heavenly eyes, that look into these faults,
BIRON: Suggested us to make. Therefore, ladies,
BIRON: Our love being yours, the error that love makes
BIRON: Is likewise yours: we to ourselves prove false,
BIRON: By being once false for ever to be true
BIRON: To those that make us both,--fair ladies, you:
BIRON: And even that falsehood, in itself a sin,
BIRON: Thus purifies itself and turns to grace.
PRINCESS: We have received your letters full of love,
PRINCESS: Your favours, the ambassadors of love,
PRINCESS: And, in our maiden council, rated them
PRINCESS: At courtship, pleasant jest and courtesy,
PRINCESS: As bombast and as lining to the time:
PRINCESS: But more devout than this in our respects
PRINCESS: Have we not been, and therefore met your loves
PRINCESS: In their own fashion, like a merriment.
DUMAIN: Our letters, madam, show'd much more than jest.
LONGAVILLE: So did our looks.
ROSALINE: We did not quote them so.
FERDINAND: Now, at the latest minute of the hour,
FERDINAND: Grant us your loves.
PRINCESS: A time, methinks, too short
PRINCESS: To make a world-without-end bargain in.
PRINCESS: No, no, my lord, your grace is perjured much,
PRINCESS: Full of dear guiltiness, and therefore this:
PRINCESS: If for my love, as there is no such cause,
PRINCESS: You will do aught, this shall you do for me:
PRINCESS: Your oath I will not trust, but go with speed
PRINCESS: To some forlorn and naked hermitage,
PRINCESS: Remote from all the pleasures of the world,
PRINCESS: There stay until the twelve celestial signs
PRINCESS: Have brought about the annual reckoning.
PRINCESS: If this austere insociable life
PRINCESS: Change not your offer made in heat of blood,
PRINCESS: If frosts and fasts, hard lodging and thin weeds
PRINCESS: Nip not the gaudy blossoms of your love,
PRINCESS: But that it bear this trial and last love,
PRINCESS: Then, at the expiration of the year,
PRINCESS: Come challenge me, challenge me by these deserts,
PRINCESS: And, by this virgin palm now kissing thine
PRINCESS: I will be thine, and till that instant shut
PRINCESS: My woeful self up in a mourning house,
PRINCESS: Raining the tears of lamentation
PRINCESS: For the remembrance of my father's death.
PRINCESS: If this thou do deny, let our hands part,
PRINCESS: Neither entitled in the other's heart.
FERDINAND: If this, or more than this, I would deny,
FERDINAND: To flatter up these powers of mine with rest,
FERDINAND: The sudden hand of death close up mine eye!
FERDINAND: Hence ever then my heart is in thy breast.
DUMAIN: But what to me, my love? but what to me? A wife?
KATHARINE: A beard, fair health, and honesty,
KATHARINE: With three-fold love I wish you all these three.
DUMAIN: O, shall I say, I thank you, gentle wife?
KATHARINE: Not so, my lord, a twelvemonth and a day
KATHARINE: I'll mark no words that smooth-faced wooers say:
KATHARINE: Come when the king doth to my lady come,
KATHARINE: Then, if I have much love, I'll give you some.
DUMAIN: I'll serve thee true and faithfully till then.
KATHARINE: Yet swear not, lest ye be forsworn again.
LONGAVILLE: What says Maria?
MARIA: At the twelvemonth's end
MARIA: I'll change my black gown for a faithful friend.
LONGAVILLE: I'll stay with patience, but the time is long.
MARIA: The liker you, few taller are so young.
BIRON: Studies my lady? mistress, look on me,
BIRON: Behold the window of my heart, mine eye,
BIRON: What humble suit attends thy answer there:
BIRON: Impose some service on me for thy love.
ROSALINE: Oft have I heard of you, my Lord Biron,
ROSALINE: Before I saw you, and the world's large tongue
ROSALINE: Proclaims you for a man replete with mocks,
ROSALINE: Full of comparisons and wounding flouts,
ROSALINE: Which you on all estates will execute
ROSALINE: That lie within the mercy of your wit.
ROSALINE: To weed this wormwood from your fruitful brain,
ROSALINE: And therewithal to win me, if you please,
ROSALINE: Without the which I am not to be won,
ROSALINE: You shall this twelvemonth term from day to day
ROSALINE: Visit the speechless sick and still converse
ROSALINE: With groaning wretches, and your task shall be,
ROSALINE: With all the fierce endeavor of your wit
ROSALINE: To enforce the pained impotent to smile.
BIRON: To move wild laughter in the throat of death?
BIRON: It cannot be, it is impossible:
BIRON: Mirth cannot move a soul in agony.
ROSALINE: Why, that's the way to choke a gibing spirit,
ROSALINE: Whose influence is begot of that loose grace
ROSALINE: Which shallow laughing hearers give to fools:
ROSALINE: A jest's prosperity lies in the ear
ROSALINE: Of him that hears it, never in the tongue
ROSALINE: Of him that makes it: then, if sickly ears,
ROSALINE: Deaf'd with the clamours of their own dear groans,
ROSALINE: Will hear your idle scorns, continue then,
ROSALINE: And I will have you and that fault withal,
ROSALINE: But if they will not, throw away that spirit,
ROSALINE: And I shall find you empty of that fault,
ROSALINE: Right joyful of your reformation.
BIRON: A twelvemonth! well, befall what will befall,
BIRON: I'll jest a twelvemonth in an hospital.
PRINCESS: [To FERDINAND]  Ay, sweet my lord, and so I take my leave.
FERDINAND: No, madam, we will bring you on your way.
BIRON: Our wooing doth not end like an old play,
BIRON: Jack hath not Jill: these ladies' courtesy
BIRON: Might well have made our sport a comedy.
FERDINAND: Come, sir, it wants a twelvemonth and a day,
FERDINAND: And then 'twill end.
BIRON: That's too long for a play.
NARRATOR: Re-enter DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
BIRON: DON
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Sweet majesty, vouchsafe me,--
PRINCESS: Was not that Hector?
DUMAIN: The worthy knight of Troy.
DUMAIN: DON
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: I will kiss thy royal finger, and take leave. I am
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: a votary, I have vowed to Jaquenetta to hold the
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: plough for her sweet love three years. But, most
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: esteemed greatness, will you hear the dialogue that
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: the two learned men have compiled in praise of the
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: owl and the cuckoo? It should have followed in the
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: end of our show.
FERDINAND: Call them forth quickly, we will do so.
FERDINAND: DON
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Holla! approach.
NARRATOR: Re-enter HOLOFERNES, SIR NATHANIEL, MOTH, COSTARD, and others
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: This side is Hiems, Winter, this Ver, the Spring,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: the one maintained by the owl, the other by the
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: cuckoo. Ver, begin.
NARRATOR: THE SONG
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: SPRING.
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When daisies pied and violets blue
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And lady-smocks all silver-white
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And cuckoo-buds of yellow hue
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Do paint the meadows with delight,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: The cuckoo then, on every tree,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Mocks married men, for thus sings he, 	Cuckoo,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Cuckoo, cuckoo: O word of fear,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Unpleasing to a married ear!
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When shepherds pipe on oaten straws
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And merry larks are ploughmen's clocks,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When turtles tread, and rooks, and daws,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And maidens bleach their summer smocks
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: The cuckoo then, on every tree,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Mocks married men, for thus sings he, 	Cuckoo,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Cuckoo, cuckoo: O word of fear,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Unpleasing to a married ear!
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: WINTER.
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When icicles hang by the wall
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And Dick the shepherd blows his nail
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And Tom bears logs into the hall
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And milk comes frozen home in pail,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When blood is nipp'd and ways be foul,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Then nightly sings the staring owl, 	Tu-whit,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Tu-who, a merry note,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: While greasy Joan doth keel the pot.
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When all aloud the wind doth blow
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And coughing drowns the parson's saw
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And birds sit brooding in the snow
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: And Marian's nose looks red and raw,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: When roasted crabs hiss in the bowl,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Then nightly sings the staring owl, 	Tu-whit,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Tu-who, a merry note,
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: While greasy Joan doth keel the pot.
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: DON
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: The words of Mercury are harsh after the songs of
ADRIANO DE ARMADO: Apollo. You that way: we this way.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
''' PLAY: Measure for measure '''
NARRATOR: ACT I
NARRATOR: SCENE I. An apartment in the DUKE'S palace.
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO, ESCALUS, Lords and Attendants
DUKE VINCENTIO: Escalus.
ESCALUS: My lord.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of government the properties to unfold,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Would seem in me to affect speech and discourse,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Since I am put to know that your own science
DUKE VINCENTIO: Exceeds, in that, the lists of all advice
DUKE VINCENTIO: My strength can give you: then no more remains,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But that to your sufficiency as your Worth is able,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And let them work. The nature of our people,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Our city's institutions, and the terms
DUKE VINCENTIO: For common justice, you're as pregnant in
DUKE VINCENTIO: As art and practise hath enriched any
DUKE VINCENTIO: That we remember. There is our commission,
DUKE VINCENTIO: From which we would not have you warp. Call hither,
DUKE VINCENTIO: I say, bid come before us Angelo.
NARRATOR: Exit an Attendant
DUKE VINCENTIO: What figure of us think you he will bear?
DUKE VINCENTIO: For you must know, we have with special soul
DUKE VINCENTIO: Elected him our absence to supply,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Lent him our terror, dress'd him with our love,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And given his deputation all the organs
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of our own power: what think you of it?
ESCALUS: If any in Vienna be of worth
ESCALUS: To undergo such ample grace and honour,
ESCALUS: It is Lord Angelo.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Look where he comes.
NARRATOR: Enter ANGELO
ANGELO: Always obedient to your grace's will,
ANGELO: I come to know your pleasure.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Angelo,
DUKE VINCENTIO: There is a kind of character in thy life,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That to the observer doth thy history
DUKE VINCENTIO: Fully unfold. Thyself and thy belongings
DUKE VINCENTIO: Are not thine own so proper as to waste
DUKE VINCENTIO: Thyself upon thy virtues, they on thee.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Heaven doth with us as we with torches do,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Not light them for themselves, for if our virtues
DUKE VINCENTIO: Did not go forth of us, 'twere all alike
DUKE VINCENTIO: As if we had them not. Spirits are not finely touch'd
DUKE VINCENTIO: But to fine issues, nor Nature never lends
DUKE VINCENTIO: The smallest scruple of her excellence
DUKE VINCENTIO: But, like a thrifty goddess, she determines
DUKE VINCENTIO: Herself the glory of a creditor,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Both thanks and use. But I do bend my speech
DUKE VINCENTIO: To one that can my part in him advertise,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hold therefore, Angelo:--
DUKE VINCENTIO: In our remove be thou at full ourself,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Mortality and mercy in Vienna
DUKE VINCENTIO: Live in thy tongue and heart: old Escalus,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Though first in question, is thy secondary.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Take thy commission.
ANGELO: Now, good my lord,
ANGELO: Let there be some more test made of my metal,
ANGELO: Before so noble and so great a figure
ANGELO: Be stamp'd upon it.
DUKE VINCENTIO: No more evasion:
DUKE VINCENTIO: We have with a leaven'd and prepared choice
DUKE VINCENTIO: Proceeded to you, therefore take your honours.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Our haste from hence is of so quick condition
DUKE VINCENTIO: That it prefers itself and leaves unquestion'd
DUKE VINCENTIO: Matters of needful value. We shall write to you,
DUKE VINCENTIO: As time and our concernings shall importune,
DUKE VINCENTIO: How it goes with us, and do look to know
DUKE VINCENTIO: What doth befall you here. So, fare you well,
DUKE VINCENTIO: To the hopeful execution do I leave you
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of your commissions.
ANGELO: Yet give leave, my lord,
ANGELO: That we may bring you something on the way.
DUKE VINCENTIO: My haste may not admit it,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Nor need you, on mine honour, have to do
DUKE VINCENTIO: With any scruple, your scope is as mine own
DUKE VINCENTIO: So to enforce or qualify the laws
DUKE VINCENTIO: As to your soul seems good. Give me your hand:
DUKE VINCENTIO: I'll privily away. I love the people,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But do not like to stage me to their eyes:
DUKE VINCENTIO: Through it do well, I do not relish well
DUKE VINCENTIO: Their loud applause and Aves vehement,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Nor do I think the man of safe discretion
DUKE VINCENTIO: That does affect it. Once more, fare you well.
ANGELO: The heavens give safety to your purposes!
ESCALUS: Lead forth and bring you back in happiness!
DUKE: I thank you. Fare you well.
NARRATOR: Exit
ESCALUS: I shall desire you, sir, to give me leave
ESCALUS: To have free speech with you, and it concerns me
ESCALUS: To look into the bottom of my place:
ESCALUS: A power I have, but of what strength and nature
ESCALUS: I am not yet instructed.
ANGELO: 'Tis so with me. Let us withdraw together,
ANGELO: And we may soon our satisfaction have
ANGELO: Touching that point.
ESCALUS: I'll wait upon your honour.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. A Street.
NARRATOR: Enter LUCIO and two Gentlemen
LUCIO: If the duke with the other dukes come not to
LUCIO: composition with the King of Hungary, why then all
LUCIO: the dukes fall upon the king.
First Gentleman: Heaven grant us its peace, but not the King of
First Gentleman: Hungary's!
Second Gentleman: Amen.
LUCIO: Thou concludest like the sanctimonious pirate, that
LUCIO: went to sea with the Ten Commandments, but scraped
LUCIO: one out of the table.
Second Gentleman: 'Thou shalt not steal'?
LUCIO: Ay, that he razed.
First Gentleman: Why, 'twas a commandment to command the captain and
First Gentleman: all the rest from their functions: they put forth
First Gentleman: to steal. There's not a soldier of us all, that, in
First Gentleman: the thanksgiving before meat, do relish the petition
First Gentleman: well that prays for peace.
Second Gentleman: I never heard any soldier dislike it.
LUCIO: I believe thee, for I think thou never wast where
LUCIO: grace was said.
Second Gentleman: No? a dozen times at least.
First Gentleman: What, in metre?
LUCIO: In any proportion or in any language.
First Gentleman: I think, or in any religion.
LUCIO: Ay, why not? Grace is grace, despite of all
LUCIO: controversy: as, for example, thou thyself art a
LUCIO: wicked villain, despite of all grace.
First Gentleman: Well, there went but a pair of shears between us.
LUCIO: I grant, as there may between the lists and the
LUCIO: velvet. Thou art the list.
First Gentleman: And thou the velvet: thou art good velvet, thou'rt
First Gentleman: a three-piled piece, I warrant thee: I had as lief
First Gentleman: be a list of an English kersey as be piled, as thou
First Gentleman: art piled, for a French velvet. Do I speak
First Gentleman: feelingly now?
LUCIO: I think thou dost, and, indeed, with most painful
LUCIO: feeling of thy speech: I will, out of thine own
LUCIO: confession, learn to begin thy health, but, whilst I
LUCIO: live, forget to drink after thee.
First Gentleman: I think I have done myself wrong, have I not?
Second Gentleman: Yes, that thou hast, whether thou art tainted or free.
LUCIO: Behold, behold. where Madam Mitigation comes! I
LUCIO: have purchased as many diseases under her roof as come to--
Second Gentleman: To what, I pray?
LUCIO: Judge.
Second Gentleman: To three thousand dolours a year.
First Gentleman: Ay, and more.
LUCIO: A French crown more.
First Gentleman: Thou art always figuring diseases in me, but thou
First Gentleman: art full of error, I am sound.
LUCIO: Nay, not as one would say, healthy, but so sound as
LUCIO: things that are hollow: thy bones are hollow,
LUCIO: impiety has made a feast of thee.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS OVERDONE
First Gentleman: How now! which of your hips has the most profound sciatica?
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Well, well, there's one yonder arrested and carried
MISTRESS OVERDONE: to prison was worth five thousand of you all.
Second Gentleman: Who's that, I pray thee?
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Marry, sir, that's Claudio, Signior Claudio.
First Gentleman: Claudio to prison? 'tis not so.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Nay, but I know 'tis so: I saw him arrested, saw
MISTRESS OVERDONE: him carried away, and, which is more, within these
MISTRESS OVERDONE: three days his head to be chopped off.
LUCIO: But, after all this fooling, I would not have it so.
LUCIO: Art thou sure of this?
MISTRESS OVERDONE: I am too sure of it: and it is for getting Madam
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Julietta with child.
LUCIO: Believe me, this may be: he promised to meet me two
LUCIO: hours since, and he was ever precise in
LUCIO: promise-keeping.
Second Gentleman: Besides, you know, it draws something near to the
Second Gentleman: speech we had to such a purpose.
First Gentleman: But, most of all, agreeing with the proclamation.
LUCIO: Away! let's go learn the truth of it.
NARRATOR: Exeunt LUCIO and Gentlemen
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Thus, what with the war, what with the sweat, what
MISTRESS OVERDONE: with the gallows and what with poverty, I am
MISTRESS OVERDONE: custom-shrunk.
NARRATOR: Enter POMPEY
MISTRESS OVERDONE: How now! what's the news with you?
POMPEY: Yonder man is carried to prison.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Well, what has he done?
POMPEY: A woman.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: But what's his offence?
POMPEY: Groping for trouts in a peculiar river.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: What, is there a maid with child by him?
POMPEY: No, but there's a woman with maid by him. You have
POMPEY: not heard of the proclamation, have you?
MISTRESS OVERDONE: What proclamation, man?
POMPEY: All houses in the suburbs of Vienna must be plucked down.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: And what shall become of those in the city?
POMPEY: They shall stand for seed: they had gone down too,
POMPEY: but that a wise burgher put in for them.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: But shall all our houses of resort in the suburbs be
MISTRESS OVERDONE: pulled down?
POMPEY: To the ground, mistress.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Why, here's a change indeed in the commonwealth!
MISTRESS OVERDONE: What shall become of me?
POMPEY: Come, fear you not: good counsellors lack no
POMPEY: clients: though you change your place, you need not
POMPEY: change your trade, I'll be your tapster still.
POMPEY: Courage! there will be pity taken on you: you that
POMPEY: have worn your eyes almost out in the service, you
POMPEY: will be considered.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: What's to do here, Thomas tapster? let's withdraw.
POMPEY: Here comes Signior Claudio, led by the provost to
POMPEY: prison, and there's Madam Juliet.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: Enter Provost, CLAUDIO, JULIET, and Officers
CLAUDIO: Fellow, why dost thou show me thus to the world?
CLAUDIO: Bear me to prison, where I am committed.
Provost: I do it not in evil disposition,
Provost: But from Lord Angelo by special charge.
CLAUDIO: Thus can the demigod Authority
CLAUDIO: Make us pay down for our offence by weight
CLAUDIO: The words of heaven, on whom it will, it will,
CLAUDIO: On whom it will not, so, yet still 'tis just.
NARRATOR: Re-enter LUCIO and two Gentlemen
LUCIO: Why, how now, Claudio! whence comes this restraint?
CLAUDIO: From too much liberty, my Lucio, liberty:
CLAUDIO: As surfeit is the father of much fast,
CLAUDIO: So every scope by the immoderate use
CLAUDIO: Turns to restraint. Our natures do pursue,
CLAUDIO: Like rats that ravin down their proper bane,
CLAUDIO: A thirsty evil, and when we drink we die.
LUCIO: If could speak so wisely under an arrest, I would
LUCIO: send for certain of my creditors: and yet, to say
LUCIO: the truth, I had as lief have the foppery of freedom
LUCIO: as the morality of imprisonment. What's thy
LUCIO: offence, Claudio?
CLAUDIO: What but to speak of would offend again.
LUCIO: What, is't murder?
CLAUDIO: No.
LUCIO: Lechery?
CLAUDIO: Call it so.
Provost: Away, sir! you must go.
CLAUDIO: One word, good friend. Lucio, a word with you.
LUCIO: A hundred, if they'll do you any good.
LUCIO: Is lechery so look'd after?
CLAUDIO: Thus stands it with me: upon a true contract
CLAUDIO: I got possession of Julietta's bed:
CLAUDIO: You know the lady, she is fast my wife,
CLAUDIO: Save that we do the denunciation lack
CLAUDIO: Of outward order: this we came not to,
CLAUDIO: Only for propagation of a dower
CLAUDIO: Remaining in the coffer of her friends,
CLAUDIO: From whom we thought it meet to hide our love
CLAUDIO: Till time had made them for us. But it chances
CLAUDIO: The stealth of our most mutual entertainment
CLAUDIO: With character too gross is writ on Juliet.
LUCIO: With child, perhaps?
CLAUDIO: Unhappily, even so.
CLAUDIO: And the new deputy now for the duke--
CLAUDIO: Whether it be the fault and glimpse of newness,
CLAUDIO: Or whether that the body public be
CLAUDIO: A horse whereon the governor doth ride,
CLAUDIO: Who, newly in the seat, that it may know
CLAUDIO: He can command, lets it straight feel the spur,
CLAUDIO: Whether the tyranny be in his place,
CLAUDIO: Or in his emmence that fills it up,
CLAUDIO: I stagger in:--but this new governor
CLAUDIO: Awakes me all the enrolled penalties
CLAUDIO: Which have, like unscour'd armour, hung by the wall
CLAUDIO: So long that nineteen zodiacs have gone round
CLAUDIO: And none of them been worn, and, for a name,
CLAUDIO: Now puts the drowsy and neglected act
CLAUDIO: Freshly on me: 'tis surely for a name.
LUCIO: I warrant it is: and thy head stands so tickle on
LUCIO: thy shoulders that a milkmaid, if she be in love,
LUCIO: may sigh it off. Send after the duke and appeal to
LUCIO: him.
CLAUDIO: I have done so, but he's not to be found.
CLAUDIO: I prithee, Lucio, do me this kind service:
CLAUDIO: This day my sister should the cloister enter
CLAUDIO: And there receive her approbation:
CLAUDIO: Acquaint her with the danger of my state:
CLAUDIO: Implore her, in my voice, that she make friends
CLAUDIO: To the strict deputy, bid herself assay him:
CLAUDIO: I have great hope in that, for in her youth
CLAUDIO: There is a prone and speechless dialect,
CLAUDIO: Such as move men, beside, she hath prosperous art
CLAUDIO: When she will play with reason and discourse,
CLAUDIO: And well she can persuade.
LUCIO: I pray she may, as well for the encouragement of the
LUCIO: like, which else would stand under grievous
LUCIO: imposition, as for the enjoying of thy life, who I
LUCIO: would be sorry should be thus foolishly lost at a
LUCIO: game of tick-tack. I'll to her.
CLAUDIO: I thank you, good friend Lucio.
LUCIO: Within two hours.
CLAUDIO: Come, officer, away!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A monastery.
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO and FRIAR THOMAS
DUKE VINCENTIO: No, holy father, throw away that thought,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Believe not that the dribbling dart of love
DUKE VINCENTIO: Can pierce a complete bosom. Why I desire thee
DUKE VINCENTIO: To give me secret harbour, hath a purpose
DUKE VINCENTIO: More grave and wrinkled than the aims and ends
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of burning youth.
FRIAR THOMAS: May your grace speak of it?
DUKE VINCENTIO: My holy sir, none better knows than you
DUKE VINCENTIO: How I have ever loved the life removed
DUKE VINCENTIO: And held in idle price to haunt assemblies
DUKE VINCENTIO: Where youth, and cost, and witless bravery keeps.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I have deliver'd to Lord Angelo,
DUKE VINCENTIO: A man of stricture and firm abstinence,
DUKE VINCENTIO: My absolute power and place here in Vienna,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And he supposes me travell'd to Poland,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For so I have strew'd it in the common ear,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And so it is received. Now, pious sir,
DUKE VINCENTIO: You will demand of me why I do this?
FRIAR THOMAS: Gladly, my lord.
DUKE VINCENTIO: We have strict statutes and most biting laws.
DUKE VINCENTIO: The needful bits and curbs to headstrong weeds,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Which for this nineteen years we have let slip,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Even like an o'ergrown lion in a cave,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That goes not out to prey. Now, as fond fathers,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Having bound up the threatening twigs of birch,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Only to stick it in their children's sight
DUKE VINCENTIO: For terror, not to use, in time the rod
DUKE VINCENTIO: Becomes more mock'd than fear'd, so our decrees,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Dead to infliction, to themselves are dead,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And liberty plucks justice by the nose,
DUKE VINCENTIO: The baby beats the nurse, and quite athwart
DUKE VINCENTIO: Goes all decorum.
FRIAR THOMAS: It rested in your grace
FRIAR THOMAS: To unloose this tied-up justice when you pleased:
FRIAR THOMAS: And it in you more dreadful would have seem'd
FRIAR THOMAS: Than in Lord Angelo.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I do fear, too dreadful:
DUKE VINCENTIO: Sith 'twas my fault to give the people scope,
DUKE VINCENTIO: 'Twould be my tyranny to strike and gall them
DUKE VINCENTIO: For what I bid them do: for we bid this be done,
DUKE VINCENTIO: When evil deeds have their permissive pass
DUKE VINCENTIO: And not the punishment. Therefore indeed, my father,
DUKE VINCENTIO: I have on Angelo imposed the office,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Who may, in the ambush of my name, strike home,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And yet my nature never in the fight
DUKE VINCENTIO: To do in slander. And to behold his sway,
DUKE VINCENTIO: I will, as 'twere a brother of your order,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Visit both prince and people: therefore, I prithee,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Supply me with the habit and instruct me
DUKE VINCENTIO: How I may formally in person bear me
DUKE VINCENTIO: Like a true friar. More reasons for this action
DUKE VINCENTIO: At our more leisure shall I render you,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Only, this one: Lord Angelo is precise,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Stands at a guard with envy, scarce confesses
DUKE VINCENTIO: That his blood flows, or that his appetite
DUKE VINCENTIO: Is more to bread than stone: hence shall we see,
DUKE VINCENTIO: If power change purpose, what our seemers be.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. A nunnery.
NARRATOR: Enter ISABELLA and FRANCISCA
ISABELLA: And have you nuns no farther privileges?
FRANCISCA: Are not these large enough?
ISABELLA: Yes, truly, I speak not as desiring more,
ISABELLA: But rather wishing a more strict restraint
ISABELLA: Upon the sisterhood, the votarists of Saint Clare.
LUCIO: [Within]  Ho! Peace be in this place!
ISABELLA: Who's that which calls?
FRANCISCA: It is a man's voice. Gentle Isabella,
FRANCISCA: Turn you the key, and know his business of him,
FRANCISCA: You may, I may not, you are yet unsworn.
FRANCISCA: When you have vow'd, you must not speak with men
FRANCISCA: But in the presence of the prioress:
FRANCISCA: Then, if you speak, you must not show your face,
FRANCISCA: Or, if you show your face, you must not speak.
FRANCISCA: He calls again, I pray you, answer him.
NARRATOR: Exit
ISABELLA: Peace and prosperity! Who is't that calls
NARRATOR: Enter LUCIO
LUCIO: Hail, virgin, if you be, as those cheek-roses
LUCIO: Proclaim you are no less! Can you so stead me
LUCIO: As bring me to the sight of Isabella,
LUCIO: A novice of this place and the fair sister
LUCIO: To her unhappy brother Claudio?
ISABELLA: Why 'her unhappy brother'? let me ask,
ISABELLA: The rather for I now must make you know
ISABELLA: I am that Isabella and his sister.
LUCIO: Gentle and fair, your brother kindly greets you:
LUCIO: Not to be weary with you, he's in prison.
ISABELLA: Woe me! for what?
LUCIO: For that which, if myself might be his judge,
LUCIO: He should receive his punishment in thanks:
LUCIO: He hath got his friend with child.
ISABELLA: Sir, make me not your story.
LUCIO: It is true.
LUCIO: I would not--though 'tis my familiar sin
LUCIO: With maids to seem the lapwing and to jest,
LUCIO: Tongue far from heart--play with all virgins so:
LUCIO: I hold you as a thing ensky'd and sainted.
LUCIO: By your renouncement an immortal spirit,
LUCIO: And to be talk'd with in sincerity,
LUCIO: As with a saint.
ISABELLA: You do blaspheme the good in mocking me.
LUCIO: Do not believe it. Fewness and truth, 'tis thus:
LUCIO: Your brother and his lover have embraced:
LUCIO: As those that feed grow full, as blossoming time
LUCIO: That from the seedness the bare fallow brings
LUCIO: To teeming foison, even so her plenteous womb
LUCIO: Expresseth his full tilth and husbandry.
ISABELLA: Some one with child by him? My cousin Juliet?
LUCIO: Is she your cousin?
ISABELLA: Adoptedly, as school-maids change their names
ISABELLA: By vain though apt affection.
LUCIO: She it is.
ISABELLA: O, let him marry her.
LUCIO: This is the point.
LUCIO: The duke is very strangely gone from hence,
LUCIO: Bore many gentlemen, myself being one,
LUCIO: In hand and hope of action: but we do learn
LUCIO: By those that know the very nerves of state,
LUCIO: His givings-out were of an infinite distance
LUCIO: From his true-meant design. Upon his place,
LUCIO: And with full line of his authority,
LUCIO: Governs Lord Angelo, a man whose blood
LUCIO: Is very snow-broth, one who never feels
LUCIO: The wanton stings and motions of the sense,
LUCIO: But doth rebate and blunt his natural edge
LUCIO: With profits of the mind, study and fast.
LUCIO: He--to give fear to use and liberty,
LUCIO: Which have for long run by the hideous law,
LUCIO: As mice by lions--hath pick'd out an act,
LUCIO: Under whose heavy sense your brother's life
LUCIO: Falls into forfeit: he arrests him on it,
LUCIO: And follows close the rigour of the statute,
LUCIO: To make him an example. All hope is gone,
LUCIO: Unless you have the grace by your fair prayer
LUCIO: To soften Angelo: and that's my pith of business
LUCIO: 'Twixt you and your poor brother.
ISABELLA: Doth he so seek his life?
LUCIO: Has censured him
LUCIO: Already, and, as I hear, the provost hath
LUCIO: A warrant for his execution.
ISABELLA: Alas! what poor ability's in me
ISABELLA: To do him good?
LUCIO: Assay the power you have.
ISABELLA: My power? Alas, I doubt--
LUCIO: Our doubts are traitors
LUCIO: And make us lose the good we oft might win
LUCIO: By fearing to attempt. Go to Lord Angelo,
LUCIO: And let him learn to know, when maidens sue,
LUCIO: Men give like gods, but when they weep and kneel,
LUCIO: All their petitions are as freely theirs
LUCIO: As they themselves would owe them.
ISABELLA: I'll see what I can do.
LUCIO: But speedily.
ISABELLA: I will about it straight,
ISABELLA: No longer staying but to give the mother
ISABELLA: Notice of my affair. I humbly thank you:
ISABELLA: Commend me to my brother: soon at night
ISABELLA: I'll send him certain word of my success.
LUCIO: I take my leave of you.
ISABELLA: Good sir, adieu.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT II
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A hall In ANGELO's house.
NARRATOR: Enter ANGELO, ESCALUS, and a Justice, Provost, Officers, and other Attendants, behind
ANGELO: We must not make a scarecrow of the law,
ANGELO: Setting it up to fear the birds of prey,
ANGELO: And let it keep one shape, till custom make it
ANGELO: Their perch and not their terror.
ESCALUS: Ay, but yet
ESCALUS: Let us be keen, and rather cut a little,
ESCALUS: Than fall, and bruise to death. Alas, this gentleman
ESCALUS: Whom I would save, had a most noble father!
ESCALUS: Let but your honour know,
ESCALUS: Whom I believe to be most strait in virtue,
ESCALUS: That, in the working of your own affections,
ESCALUS: Had time cohered with place or place with wishing,
ESCALUS: Or that the resolute acting of your blood
ESCALUS: Could have attain'd the effect of your own purpose,
ESCALUS: Whether you had not sometime in your life
ESCALUS: Err'd in this point which now you censure him,
ESCALUS: And pull'd the law upon you.
ANGELO: 'Tis one thing to be tempted, Escalus,
ANGELO: Another thing to fall. I not deny,
ANGELO: The jury, passing on the prisoner's life,
ANGELO: May in the sworn twelve have a thief or two
ANGELO: Guiltier than him they try. What's open made to justice,
ANGELO: That justice seizes: what know the laws
ANGELO: That thieves do pass on thieves? 'Tis very pregnant,
ANGELO: The jewel that we find, we stoop and take't
ANGELO: Because we see it, but what we do not see
ANGELO: We tread upon, and never think of it.
ANGELO: You may not so extenuate his offence
ANGELO: For I have had such faults, but rather tell me,
ANGELO: When I, that censure him, do so offend,
ANGELO: Let mine own judgment pattern out my death,
ANGELO: And nothing come in partial. Sir, he must die.
ESCALUS: Be it as your wisdom will.
ANGELO: Where is the provost?
Provost: Here, if it like your honour.
ANGELO: See that Claudio
ANGELO: Be executed by nine to-morrow morning:
ANGELO: Bring him his confessor, let him be prepared,
ANGELO: For that's the utmost of his pilgrimage.
NARRATOR: Exit Provost
ESCALUS: [Aside]  Well, heaven forgive him! and forgive us all!
ESCALUS: Some rise by sin, and some by virtue fall:
ESCALUS: Some run from brakes of ice, and answer none:
ESCALUS: And some condemned for a fault alone.
NARRATOR: Enter ELBOW, and Officers with FROTH and POMPEY

ELBOW: a commonweal that do nothing but use their abuses in
ELBOW: common houses, I know no law: bring them away.

ELBOW: If it Please your honour, I am the poor duke's
ELBOW: constable, and my name is Elbow: I do lean upon
ELBOW: justice, sir, and do bring in here before your good
ELBOW: honour two notorious benefactors.
ANGELO: Benefactors? Well, what benefactors are they? are
ANGELO: they not malefactors?
ELBOW: If it? please your honour, I know not well what they

ELBOW: of, and void of all profanation in the world that
ELBOW: good Christians ought to have.
ESCALUS: This comes off well, here's a wise officer.
ANGELO: Go to: what quality are they of? Elbow is your
ANGELO: name? why dost thou not speak, Elbow?
POMPEY: He cannot, sir, he's out at elbow.

ELBOW: He, sir! a tapster, sir, parcel-bawd, one that
ELBOW: serves a bad woman, whose house, sir, was, as they
ELBOW: say, plucked down in the suburbs, and now she
ELBOW: professes a hot-house, which, I think, is a very ill house too.
ESCALUS: How know you that?
ELBOW: My wife, sir, whom I detest before heaven and your honour,--
ESCALUS: How? thy wife?
ELBOW: Ay, sir, whom, I thank heaven, is an honest woman,--

ELBOW: I say, sir, I will detest myself also, as well as
ELBOW: she, that this house, if it be not a bawd's house,
ELBOW: it is pity of her life, for it is a naughty house.
ESCALUS: How dost thou know that, constable?
ELBOW: Marry, sir, by my wife, who, if she had been a woman
ELBOW: cardinally given, might have been accused in
ELBOW: fornication, adultery, and all uncleanliness there.
ESCALUS: By the woman's means?
ELBOW: Ay, sir, by Mistress Overdone's means: but as she
ELBOW: spit in his face, so she defied him.
POMPEY: Sir, if it please your honour, this is not so.
ELBOW: Prove it before these varlets here, thou honourable
ELBOW: man, prove it.
ESCALUS: Do you hear how he misplaces?
POMPEY: Sir, she came in great with child, and longing,

POMPEY: sir, we had but two in the house, which at that very

POMPEY: good dishes,--
ESCALUS: Go to, go to: no matter for the dish, sir.
POMPEY: No, indeed, sir, not of a pin, you are therein in
POMPEY: the right: but to the point. As I say, this
POMPEY: Mistress Elbow, being, as I say, with child, and
POMPEY: being great-bellied, and longing, as I said, for
POMPEY: prunes, and having but two in the dish, as I said,
POMPEY: Master Froth here, this very man, having eaten the
POMPEY: rest, as I said, and, as I say, paying for them very

POMPEY: not give you three-pence again.
FROTH: No, indeed.
POMPEY: Very well: you being then, if you be remembered,
POMPEY: cracking the stones of the foresaid prunes,--
FROTH: Ay, so I did indeed.
POMPEY: Why, very well, I telling you then, if you be
POMPEY: remembered, that such a one and such a one were past

POMPEY: good diet, as I told you,--
FROTH: All this is true.
POMPEY: Why, very well, then,--

POMPEY: Sir, your honour cannot come to that yet.

POMPEY: Sir, but you shall come to it, by your honour's
POMPEY: leave. And, I beseech you, look into Master Froth

FROTH: All-hallond eve.
POMPEY: Why, very well, I hope here be truths. He, sir,

FROTH: I have so, because it is an open room and good for winter.
POMPEY: Why, very well, then, I hope here be truths.
ANGELO: This will last out a night in Russia,

ANGELO: And leave you to the hearing of the cause,
ANGELO: Hoping you'll find good cause to whip them all.

POMPEY: Once, sir? there was nothing done to her once.

POMPEY: I beseech your honour, ask me.

POMPEY: Nay, I beseech you, mark it well.

ESCALUS: Come you hither to me, Master tapster. What's your
ESCALUS: name, Master tapster?
POMPEY: Pompey.
ESCALUS: What else?
POMPEY: Bum, sir.
ESCALUS: Troth, and your bum is the greatest thing about you,

POMPEY: I thank your worship for your good counsel:
NARRATOR: Aside
POMPEY: but I shall follow it as the flesh and fortune shall
POMPEY: better determine.
POMPEY: Whip me? No, no, let carman whip his jade:
POMPEY: The valiant heart is not whipt out of his trade.

ESCALUS: Come hither to me, Master Elbow, come hither, Master

ELBOW: And a half, sir.

ESCALUS: To my house. Fare you well.
NARRATOR: Exit ELBOW
ESCALUS: What's o'clock, think you?

ESCALUS: It grieves me for the death of Claudio,

ESCALUS: Mercy is not itself, that oft looks so,
