Provost: What shall be done, sir, with the groaning Juliet?
Provost: She's very near her hour.
ANGELO: Dispose of her
ANGELO: To some more fitter place, and that with speed.
NARRATOR: Re-enter Servant
Servant: Here is the sister of the man condemn'd
Servant: Desires access to you.
ANGELO: Hath he a sister?
Provost: Ay, my good lord, a very virtuous maid,
Provost: And to be shortly of a sisterhood,
Provost: If not already.
ANGELO: Well, let her be admitted.
NARRATOR: Exit Servant
ANGELO: See you the fornicatress be removed:
ANGELO: Let have needful, but not lavish, means,
ANGELO: There shall be order for't.
NARRATOR: Enter ISABELLA and LUCIO
Provost: God save your honour!
ANGELO: Stay a little while.
NARRATOR: To ISABELLA
ANGELO: You're welcome: what's your will?
ISABELLA: I am a woeful suitor to your honour,
ISABELLA: Please but your honour hear me.
ANGELO: Well, what's your suit?
ISABELLA: There is a vice that most I do abhor,
ISABELLA: And most desire should meet the blow of justice,
ISABELLA: For which I would not plead, but that I must,
ISABELLA: For which I must not plead, but that I am
ISABELLA: At war 'twixt will and will not.
ANGELO: Well, the matter?
ISABELLA: I have a brother is condemn'd to die:
ISABELLA: I do beseech you, let it be his fault,
ISABELLA: And not my brother.
Provost: [Aside]  Heaven give thee moving graces!
ANGELO: Condemn the fault and not the actor of it?
ANGELO: Why, every fault's condemn'd ere it be done:
ANGELO: Mine were the very cipher of a function,
ANGELO: To fine the faults whose fine stands in record,
ANGELO: And let go by the actor.
ISABELLA: O just but severe law!
ISABELLA: I had a brother, then. Heaven keep your honour!
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  Give't not o'er so: to him
LUCIO: again, entreat him,
LUCIO: Kneel down before him, hang upon his gown:
LUCIO: You are too cold, if you should need a pin,
LUCIO: You could not with more tame a tongue desire it:
LUCIO: To him, I say!
ISABELLA: Must he needs die?
ANGELO: Maiden, no remedy.
ISABELLA: Yes, I do think that you might pardon him,
ISABELLA: And neither heaven nor man grieve at the mercy.
ANGELO: I will not do't.
ISABELLA: But can you, if you would?
ANGELO: Look, what I will not, that I cannot do.
ISABELLA: But might you do't, and do the world no wrong,
ISABELLA: If so your heart were touch'd with that remorse
ISABELLA: A s mine is to him?
ANGELO: He's sentenced, 'tis too late.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  You are too cold.
ISABELLA: Too late? why, no, I, that do speak a word.
ISABELLA: May call it back again. Well, believe this,
ISABELLA: No ceremony that to great ones 'longs,
ISABELLA: Not the king's crown, nor the deputed sword,
ISABELLA: The marshal's truncheon, nor the judge's robe,
ISABELLA: Become them with one half so good a grace
ISABELLA: As mercy does.
ISABELLA: If he had been as you and you as he,
ISABELLA: You would have slipt like him, but he, like you,
ISABELLA: Would not have been so stern.
ANGELO: Pray you, be gone.
ISABELLA: I would to heaven I had your potency,
ISABELLA: And you were Isabel! should it then be thus?
ISABELLA: No, I would tell what 'twere to be a judge,
ISABELLA: And what a prisoner.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]
LUCIO: Ay, touch him, there's the vein.
ANGELO: Your brother is a forfeit of the law,
ANGELO: And you but waste your words.
ISABELLA: Alas, alas!
ISABELLA: Why, all the souls that were were forfeit once,
ISABELLA: And He that might the vantage best have took
ISABELLA: Found out the remedy. How would you be,
ISABELLA: If He, which is the top of judgment, should
ISABELLA: But judge you as you are? O, think on that,
ISABELLA: And mercy then will breathe within your lips,
ISABELLA: Like man new made.
ANGELO: Be you content, fair maid,
ANGELO: It is the law, not I condemn your brother:
ANGELO: Were he my kinsman, brother, or my son,
ANGELO: It should be thus with him: he must die tomorrow.
ISABELLA: To-morrow! O, that's sudden! Spare him, spare him!
ISABELLA: He's not prepared for death. Even for our kitchens
ISABELLA: We kill the fowl of season: shall we serve heaven
ISABELLA: With less respect than we do minister
ISABELLA: To our gross selves? Good, good my lord, bethink you,
ISABELLA: Who is it that hath died for this offence?
ISABELLA: There's many have committed it.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]           Ay, well said.
ANGELO: The law hath not been dead, though it hath slept:
ANGELO: Those many had not dared to do that evil,
ANGELO: If the first that did the edict infringe
ANGELO: Had answer'd for his deed: now 'tis awake
ANGELO: Takes note of what is done, and, like a prophet,
ANGELO: Looks in a glass, that shows what future evils,
ANGELO: Either new, or by remissness new-conceived,
ANGELO: And so in progress to be hatch'd and born,
ANGELO: Are now to have no successive degrees,
ANGELO: But, ere they live, to end.
ISABELLA: Yet show some pity.
ANGELO: I show it most of all when I show justice,
ANGELO: For then I pity those I do not know,
ANGELO: Which a dismiss'd offence would after gall,
ANGELO: And do him right that, answering one foul wrong,
ANGELO: Lives not to act another. Be satisfied,
ANGELO: Your brother dies to-morrow, be content.
ISABELLA: So you must be the first that gives this sentence,
ISABELLA: And he, that suffer's. O, it is excellent
ISABELLA: To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous
ISABELLA: To use it like a giant.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]   That's well said.
ISABELLA: Could great men thunder
ISABELLA: As Jove himself does, Jove would ne'er be quiet,
ISABELLA: For every pelting, petty officer
ISABELLA: Would use his heaven for thunder,
ISABELLA: Nothing but thunder! Merciful Heaven,
ISABELLA: Thou rather with thy sharp and sulphurous bolt
ISABELLA: Split'st the unwedgeable and gnarled oak
ISABELLA: Than the soft myrtle: but man, proud man,
ISABELLA: Drest in a little brief authority,
ISABELLA: Most ignorant of what he's most assured,
ISABELLA: His glassy essence, like an angry ape,
ISABELLA: Plays such fantastic tricks before high heaven
ISABELLA: As make the angels weep, who, with our spleens,
ISABELLA: Would all themselves laugh mortal.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  O, to him, to him, wench! he
LUCIO: will relent,
LUCIO: He's coming, I perceive 't.
Provost: [Aside]  Pray heaven she win him!
ISABELLA: We cannot weigh our brother with ourself:
ISABELLA: Great men may jest with saints, 'tis wit in them,
ISABELLA: But in the less foul profanation.
LUCIO: Thou'rt i' the right, girl, more o, that.
ISABELLA: That in the captain's but a choleric word,
ISABELLA: Which in the soldier is flat blasphemy.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  Art avised o' that? more on 't.
ANGELO: Why do you put these sayings upon me?
ISABELLA: Because authority, though it err like others,
ISABELLA: Hath yet a kind of medicine in itself,
ISABELLA: That skins the vice o' the top. Go to your bosom,
ISABELLA: Knock there, and ask your heart what it doth know
ISABELLA: That's like my brother's fault: if it confess
ISABELLA: A natural guiltiness such as is his,
ISABELLA: Let it not sound a thought upon your tongue
ISABELLA: Against my brother's life.
ANGELO: [Aside]                  She speaks, and 'tis
ANGELO: Such sense, that my sense breeds with it. Fare you well.
ISABELLA: Gentle my lord, turn back.
ANGELO: I will bethink me: come again tomorrow.
ISABELLA: Hark how I'll bribe you: good my lord, turn back.
ANGELO: How! bribe me?
ISABELLA: Ay, with such gifts that heaven shall share with you.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  You had marr'd all else.
ISABELLA: Not with fond shekels of the tested gold,
ISABELLA: Or stones whose rates are either rich or poor
ISABELLA: As fancy values them, but with true prayers
ISABELLA: That shall be up at heaven and enter there
ISABELLA: Ere sun-rise, prayers from preserved souls,
ISABELLA: From fasting maids whose minds are dedicate
ISABELLA: To nothing temporal.
ANGELO: Well, come to me to-morrow.
LUCIO: [Aside to ISABELLA]  Go to, 'tis well, away!
ISABELLA: Heaven keep your honour safe!
ANGELO: [Aside]	Amen:
ANGELO: For I am that way going to temptation,
ANGELO: Where prayers cross.
ISABELLA: At what hour to-morrow
ISABELLA: Shall I attend your lordship?
ANGELO: At any time 'fore noon.
ISABELLA: 'Save your honour!
NARRATOR: Exeunt ISABELLA, LUCIO, and Provost
ANGELO: From thee, even from thy virtue!
ANGELO: What's this, what's this? Is this her fault or mine?
ANGELO: The tempter or the tempted, who sins most?
ANGELO: Ha!
ANGELO: Not she: nor doth she tempt: but it is I
ANGELO: That, lying by the violet in the sun,
ANGELO: Do as the carrion does, not as the flower,
ANGELO: Corrupt with virtuous season. Can it be
ANGELO: That modesty may more betray our sense
ANGELO: Than woman's lightness? Having waste ground enough,
ANGELO: Shall we desire to raze the sanctuary
ANGELO: And pitch our evils there? O, fie, fie, fie!
ANGELO: What dost thou, or what art thou, Angelo?
ANGELO: Dost thou desire her foully for those things
ANGELO: That make her good? O, let her brother live!
ANGELO: Thieves for their robbery have authority
ANGELO: When judges steal themselves. What, do I love her,
ANGELO: That I desire to hear her speak again,
ANGELO: And feast upon her eyes? What is't I dream on?
ANGELO: O cunning enemy, that, to catch a saint,
ANGELO: With saints dost bait thy hook! Most dangerous
ANGELO: Is that temptation that doth goad us on
ANGELO: To sin in loving virtue: never could the strumpet,
ANGELO: With all her double vigour, art and nature,
ANGELO: Once stir my temper, but this virtuous maid
ANGELO: Subdues me quite. Even till now,
ANGELO: When men were fond, I smiled and wonder'd how.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A room in a prison.
NARRATOR: Enter, severally, DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as a friar, and Provost
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hail to you, provost! so I think you are.
Provost: I am the provost. What's your will, good friar?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Bound by my charity and my blest order,
DUKE VINCENTIO: I come to visit the afflicted spirits
DUKE VINCENTIO: Here in the prison. Do me the common right
DUKE VINCENTIO: To let me see them and to make me know
DUKE VINCENTIO: The nature of their crimes, that I may minister
DUKE VINCENTIO: To them accordingly.
Provost: I would do more than that, if more were needful.
NARRATOR: Enter JULIET
Provost: Look, here comes one: a gentlewoman of mine,
Provost: Who, falling in the flaws of her own youth,
Provost: Hath blister'd her report: she is with child,
Provost: And he that got it, sentenced, a young man
Provost: More fit to do another such offence
Provost: Than die for this.
DUKE VINCENTIO: When must he die?
Provost: As I do think, to-morrow.
Provost: I have provided for you: stay awhile,
NARRATOR: To JULIET
Provost: And you shall be conducted.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Repent you, fair one, of the sin you carry?
JULIET: I do, and bear the shame most patiently.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I'll teach you how you shall arraign your conscience,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And try your penitence, if it be sound,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Or hollowly put on.
JULIET: I'll gladly learn.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Love you the man that wrong'd you?
JULIET: Yes, as I love the woman that wrong'd him.
DUKE VINCENTIO: So then it seems your most offenceful act
DUKE VINCENTIO: Was mutually committed?
JULIET: Mutually.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Then was your sin of heavier kind than his.
JULIET: I do confess it, and repent it, father.
DUKE VINCENTIO: 'Tis meet so, daughter: but lest you do repent,
DUKE VINCENTIO: As that the sin hath brought you to this shame,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Which sorrow is always towards ourselves, not heaven,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Showing we would not spare heaven as we love it,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But as we stand in fear,--
JULIET: I do repent me, as it is an evil,
JULIET: And take the shame with joy.
DUKE VINCENTIO: There rest.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Your partner, as I hear, must die to-morrow,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And I am going with instruction to him.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Grace go with you, Benedicite!
NARRATOR: Exit
JULIET: Must die to-morrow! O injurious love,
JULIET: That respites me a life, whose very comfort
JULIET: Is still a dying horror!
Provost: 'Tis pity of him.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. A room in ANGELO's house.
NARRATOR: Enter ANGELO
ANGELO: When I would pray and think, I think and pray
ANGELO: To several subjects. Heaven hath my empty words,
ANGELO: Whilst my invention, hearing not my tongue,
ANGELO: Anchors on Isabel: Heaven in my mouth,
ANGELO: As if I did but only chew his name,
ANGELO: And in my heart the strong and swelling evil
ANGELO: Of my conception. The state, whereon I studied
ANGELO: Is like a good thing, being often read,
ANGELO: Grown fear'd and tedious, yea, my gravity,
ANGELO: Wherein--let no man hear me--I take pride,
ANGELO: Could I with boot change for an idle plume,
ANGELO: Which the air beats for vain. O place, O form,
ANGELO: How often dost thou with thy case, thy habit,
ANGELO: Wrench awe from fools and tie the wiser souls
ANGELO: To thy false seeming! Blood, thou art blood:
ANGELO: Let's write good angel on the devil's horn:
ANGELO: 'Tis not the devil's crest.
NARRATOR: Enter a Servant
ANGELO: How now! who's there?
Servant: One Isabel, a sister, desires access to you.
ANGELO: Teach her the way.
NARRATOR: Exit Servant
ANGELO: O heavens!
ANGELO: Why does my blood thus muster to my heart,
ANGELO: Making both it unable for itself,
ANGELO: And dispossessing all my other parts
ANGELO: Of necessary fitness?
ANGELO: So play the foolish throngs with one that swoons,
ANGELO: Come all to help him, and so stop the air
ANGELO: By which he should revive: and even so
ANGELO: The general, subject to a well-wish'd king,
ANGELO: Quit their own part, and in obsequious fondness
ANGELO: Crowd to his presence, where their untaught love
ANGELO: Must needs appear offence.
NARRATOR: Enter ISABELLA
ANGELO: How now, fair maid?
ISABELLA: I am come to know your pleasure.
ANGELO: That you might know it, would much better please me
ANGELO: Than to demand what 'tis. Your brother cannot live.
ISABELLA: Even so. Heaven keep your honour!
ANGELO: Yet may he live awhile, and, it may be,
ANGELO: As long as you or I yet he must die.
ISABELLA: Under your sentence?
ANGELO: Yea.
ISABELLA: When, I beseech you? that in his reprieve,
ISABELLA: Longer or shorter, he may be so fitted
ISABELLA: That his soul sicken not.
ANGELO: Ha! fie, these filthy vices! It were as good
ANGELO: To pardon him that hath from nature stolen
ANGELO: A man already made, as to remit
ANGELO: Their saucy sweetness that do coin heaven's image
ANGELO: In stamps that are forbid: 'tis all as easy
ANGELO: Falsely to take away a life true made
ANGELO: As to put metal in restrained means
ANGELO: To make a false one.
ISABELLA: 'Tis set down so in heaven, but not in earth.
ANGELO: Say you so? then I shall pose you quickly.
ANGELO: Which had you rather, that the most just law
ANGELO: Now took your brother's life, or, to redeem him,
ANGELO: Give up your body to such sweet uncleanness
ANGELO: As she that he hath stain'd?
ISABELLA: Sir, believe this,
ISABELLA: I had rather give my body than my soul.
ANGELO: I talk not of your soul: our compell'd sins
ANGELO: Stand more for number than for accompt.
ISABELLA: How say you?
ANGELO: Nay, I'll not warrant that, for I can speak
ANGELO: Against the thing I say. Answer to this:
ANGELO: I, now the voice of the recorded law,
ANGELO: Pronounce a sentence on your brother's life:
ANGELO: Might there not be a charity in sin
ANGELO: To save this brother's life?
ISABELLA: Please you to do't,
ISABELLA: I'll take it as a peril to my soul,
ISABELLA: It is no sin at all, but charity.
ANGELO: Pleased you to do't at peril of your soul,
ANGELO: Were equal poise of sin and charity.
ISABELLA: That I do beg his life, if it be sin,
ISABELLA: Heaven let me bear it! you granting of my suit,
ISABELLA: If that be sin, I'll make it my morn prayer
ISABELLA: To have it added to the faults of mine,
ISABELLA: And nothing of your answer.
ANGELO: Nay, but hear me.
ANGELO: Your sense pursues not mine: either you are ignorant,
ANGELO: Or seem so craftily, and that's not good.
ISABELLA: Let me be ignorant, and in nothing good,
ISABELLA: But graciously to know I am no better.
ANGELO: Thus wisdom wishes to appear most bright
ANGELO: When it doth tax itself, as these black masks
ANGELO: Proclaim an enshield beauty ten times louder
ANGELO: Than beauty could, display'd. But mark me,
ANGELO: To be received plain, I'll speak more gross:
ANGELO: Your brother is to die.
ISABELLA: So.
ANGELO: And his offence is so, as it appears,
ANGELO: Accountant to the law upon that pain.
ISABELLA: True.
ANGELO: Admit no other way to save his life,--
ANGELO: As I subscribe not that, nor any other,
ANGELO: But in the loss of question,--that you, his sister,
ANGELO: Finding yourself desired of such a person,
ANGELO: Whose credit with the judge, or own great place,
ANGELO: Could fetch your brother from the manacles
ANGELO: Of the all-building law, and that there were
ANGELO: No earthly mean to save him, but that either
ANGELO: You must lay down the treasures of your body
ANGELO: To this supposed, or else to let him suffer,
ANGELO: What would you do?
ISABELLA: As much for my poor brother as myself:
ISABELLA: That is, were I under the terms of death,
ISABELLA: The impression of keen whips I'ld wear as rubies,
ISABELLA: And strip myself to death, as to a bed
ISABELLA: That longing have been sick for, ere I'ld yield
ISABELLA: My body up to shame.
ANGELO: Then must your brother die.
ISABELLA: And 'twere the cheaper way:
ISABELLA: Better it were a brother died at once,
ISABELLA: Than that a sister, by redeeming him,
ISABELLA: Should die for ever.
ANGELO: Were not you then as cruel as the sentence
ANGELO: That you have slander'd so?
ISABELLA: Ignomy in ransom and free pardon
ISABELLA: Are of two houses: lawful mercy
ISABELLA: Is nothing kin to foul redemption.
ANGELO: You seem'd of late to make the law a tyrant,
ANGELO: And rather proved the sliding of your brother
ANGELO: A merriment than a vice.
ISABELLA: O, pardon me, my lord, it oft falls out,
ISABELLA: To have what we would have, we speak not what we mean:
ISABELLA: I something do excuse the thing I hate,
ISABELLA: For his advantage that I dearly love.
ANGELO: We are all frail.
ISABELLA: Else let my brother die,
ISABELLA: If not a feodary, but only he
ISABELLA: Owe and succeed thy weakness.
ANGELO: Nay, women are frail too.
ISABELLA: Ay, as the glasses where they view themselves,
ISABELLA: Which are as easy broke as they make forms.
ISABELLA: Women! Help Heaven! men their creation mar
ISABELLA: In profiting by them. Nay, call us ten times frail,
ISABELLA: For we are soft as our complexions are,
ISABELLA: And credulous to false prints.
ANGELO: I think it well:
ANGELO: And from this testimony of your own sex,--
ANGELO: Since I suppose we are made to be no stronger
ANGELO: Than faults may shake our frames,--let me be bold,
ANGELO: I do arrest your words. Be that you are,
ANGELO: That is, a woman, if you be more, you're none,
ANGELO: If you be one, as you are well express'd
ANGELO: By all external warrants, show it now,
ANGELO: By putting on the destined livery.
ISABELLA: I have no tongue but one: gentle my lord,
ISABELLA: Let me entreat you speak the former language.
ANGELO: Plainly conceive, I love you.
ISABELLA: My brother did love Juliet,
ISABELLA: And you tell me that he shall die for it.
ANGELO: He shall not, Isabel, if you give me love.
ISABELLA: I know your virtue hath a licence in't,
ISABELLA: Which seems a little fouler than it is,
ISABELLA: To pluck on others.
ANGELO: Believe me, on mine honour,
ANGELO: My words express my purpose.
ISABELLA: Ha! little honour to be much believed,
ISABELLA: And most pernicious purpose! Seeming, seeming!
ISABELLA: I will proclaim thee, Angelo, look for't:
ISABELLA: Sign me a present pardon for my brother,
ISABELLA: Or with an outstretch'd throat I'll tell the world aloud
ISABELLA: What man thou art.
ANGELO: Who will believe thee, Isabel?
ANGELO: My unsoil'd name, the austereness of my life,
ANGELO: My vouch against you, and my place i' the state,
ANGELO: Will so your accusation overweigh,
ANGELO: That you shall stifle in your own report
ANGELO: And smell of calumny. I have begun,
ANGELO: And now I give my sensual race the rein:
ANGELO: Fit thy consent to my sharp appetite,
ANGELO: Lay by all nicety and prolixious blushes,
ANGELO: That banish what they sue for, redeem thy brother
ANGELO: By yielding up thy body to my will,
ANGELO: Or else he must not only die the death,
ANGELO: But thy unkindness shall his death draw out
ANGELO: To lingering sufferance. Answer me to-morrow,
ANGELO: Or, by the affection that now guides me most,
ANGELO: I'll prove a tyrant to him. As for you,
ANGELO: Say what you can, my false o'erweighs your true.
NARRATOR: Exit
ISABELLA: To whom should I complain? Did I tell this,
ISABELLA: Who would believe me? O perilous mouths,
ISABELLA: That bear in them one and the self-same tongue,
ISABELLA: Either of condemnation or approof,
ISABELLA: Bidding the law make court'sy to their will:
ISABELLA: Hooking both right and wrong to the appetite,
ISABELLA: To follow as it draws! I'll to my brother:
ISABELLA: Though he hath fallen by prompture of the blood,
ISABELLA: Yet hath he in him such a mind of honour.
ISABELLA: That, had he twenty heads to tender down
ISABELLA: On twenty bloody blocks, he'ld yield them up,
ISABELLA: Before his sister should her body stoop
ISABELLA: To such abhorr'd pollution.
ISABELLA: Then, Isabel, live chaste, and, brother, die:
ISABELLA: More than our brother is our chastity.
ISABELLA: I'll tell him yet of Angelo's request,
ISABELLA: And fit his mind to death, for his soul's rest.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A room in the prison.
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as before, CLAUDIO, and Provost
DUKE VINCENTIO: So then you hope of pardon from Lord Angelo?
CLAUDIO: The miserable have no other medicine
CLAUDIO: But only hope:
CLAUDIO: I've hope to live, and am prepared to die.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Be absolute for death, either death or life
DUKE VINCENTIO: Shall thereby be the sweeter. Reason thus with life:
DUKE VINCENTIO: If I do lose thee, I do lose a thing
DUKE VINCENTIO: That none but fools would keep: a breath thou art,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Servile to all the skyey influences,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That dost this habitation, where thou keep'st,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hourly afflict: merely, thou art death's fool,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For him thou labour'st by thy flight to shun
DUKE VINCENTIO: And yet runn'st toward him still. Thou art not noble,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For all the accommodations that thou bear'st
DUKE VINCENTIO: Are nursed by baseness. Thou'rt by no means valiant,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For thou dost fear the soft and tender fork
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of a poor worm. Thy best of rest is sleep,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And that thou oft provokest, yet grossly fear'st
DUKE VINCENTIO: Thy death, which is no more. Thou art not thyself,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For thou exist'st on many a thousand grains
DUKE VINCENTIO: That issue out of dust. Happy thou art not,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For what thou hast not, still thou strivest to get,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And what thou hast, forget'st. Thou art not certain,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For thy complexion shifts to strange effects,
DUKE VINCENTIO: After the moon. If thou art rich, thou'rt poor,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For, like an ass whose back with ingots bows,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Thou bear's thy heavy riches but a journey,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And death unloads thee. Friend hast thou none,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For thine own bowels, which do call thee sire,
DUKE VINCENTIO: The mere effusion of thy proper loins,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Do curse the gout, serpigo, and the rheum,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For ending thee no sooner. Thou hast nor youth nor age,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But, as it were, an after-dinner's sleep,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Dreaming on both, for all thy blessed youth
DUKE VINCENTIO: Becomes as aged, and doth beg the alms
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of palsied eld, and when thou art old and rich,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Thou hast neither heat, affection, limb, nor beauty,
DUKE VINCENTIO: To make thy riches pleasant. What's yet in this
DUKE VINCENTIO: That bears the name of life? Yet in this life
DUKE VINCENTIO: Lie hid moe thousand deaths: yet death we fear,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That makes these odds all even.
CLAUDIO: I humbly thank you.
CLAUDIO: To sue to live, I find I seek to die,
CLAUDIO: And, seeking death, find life: let it come on.
ISABELLA: [Within]  What, ho! Peace here, grace and good company!
Provost: Who's there? come in: the wish deserves a welcome.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Dear sir, ere long I'll visit you again.
CLAUDIO: Most holy sir, I thank you.
NARRATOR: Enter ISABELLA
ISABELLA: My business is a word or two with Claudio.
Provost: And very welcome. Look, signior, here's your sister.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Provost, a word with you.
Provost: As many as you please.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Bring me to hear them speak, where I may be concealed.
NARRATOR: Exeunt DUKE VINCENTIO and Provost
CLAUDIO: Now, sister, what's the comfort?
ISABELLA: Why,
ISABELLA: As all comforts are, most good, most good indeed.
ISABELLA: Lord Angelo, having affairs to heaven,
ISABELLA: Intends you for his swift ambassador,
ISABELLA: Where you shall be an everlasting leiger:
ISABELLA: Therefore your best appointment make with speed,
ISABELLA: To-morrow you set on.
CLAUDIO: Is there no remedy?
ISABELLA: None, but such remedy as, to save a head,
ISABELLA: To cleave a heart in twain.
CLAUDIO: But is there any?
ISABELLA: Yes, brother, you may live:
ISABELLA: There is a devilish mercy in the judge,
ISABELLA: If you'll implore it, that will free your life,
ISABELLA: But fetter you till death.
CLAUDIO: Perpetual durance?
ISABELLA: Ay, just, perpetual durance, a restraint,
ISABELLA: Though all the world's vastidity you had,
ISABELLA: To a determined scope.
CLAUDIO: But in what nature?
ISABELLA: In such a one as, you consenting to't,
ISABELLA: Would bark your honour from that trunk you bear,
ISABELLA: And leave you naked.
CLAUDIO: Let me know the point.
ISABELLA: O, I do fear thee, Claudio, and I quake,
ISABELLA: Lest thou a feverous life shouldst entertain,
ISABELLA: And six or seven winters more respect
ISABELLA: Than a perpetual honour. Darest thou die?
ISABELLA: The sense of death is most in apprehension,
ISABELLA: And the poor beetle, that we tread upon,
ISABELLA: In corporal sufferance finds a pang as great
ISABELLA: As when a giant dies.
CLAUDIO: Why give you me this shame?
CLAUDIO: Think you I can a resolution fetch
CLAUDIO: From flowery tenderness? If I must die,
CLAUDIO: I will encounter darkness as a bride,
CLAUDIO: And hug it in mine arms.
ISABELLA: There spake my brother, there my father's grave
ISABELLA: Did utter forth a voice. Yes, thou must die:
ISABELLA: Thou art too noble to conserve a life
ISABELLA: In base appliances. This outward-sainted deputy,
ISABELLA: Whose settled visage and deliberate word
ISABELLA: Nips youth i' the head and follies doth emmew
ISABELLA: As falcon doth the fowl, is yet a devil
ISABELLA: His filth within being cast, he would appear
ISABELLA: A pond as deep as hell.
CLAUDIO: The prenzie Angelo!
ISABELLA: O, 'tis the cunning livery of hell,
ISABELLA: The damned'st body to invest and cover
ISABELLA: In prenzie guards! Dost thou think, Claudio?
ISABELLA: If I would yield him my virginity,
ISABELLA: Thou mightst be freed.
CLAUDIO: O heavens! it cannot be.
ISABELLA: Yes, he would give't thee, from this rank offence,
ISABELLA: So to offend him still. This night's the time
ISABELLA: That I should do what I abhor to name,
ISABELLA: Or else thou diest to-morrow.
CLAUDIO: Thou shalt not do't.
ISABELLA: O, were it but my life,
ISABELLA: I'ld throw it down for your deliverance
ISABELLA: As frankly as a pin.
CLAUDIO: Thanks, dear Isabel.
ISABELLA: Be ready, Claudio, for your death tomorrow.
CLAUDIO: Yes. Has he affections in him,
CLAUDIO: That thus can make him bite the law by the nose,
CLAUDIO: When he would force it? Sure, it is no sin,
CLAUDIO: Or of the deadly seven, it is the least.
ISABELLA: Which is the least?
CLAUDIO: If it were damnable, he being so wise,
CLAUDIO: Why would he for the momentary trick
CLAUDIO: Be perdurably fined? O Isabel!
ISABELLA: What says my brother?
CLAUDIO: Death is a fearful thing.
ISABELLA: And shamed life a hateful.
CLAUDIO: Ay, but to die, and go we know not where,
CLAUDIO: To lie in cold obstruction and to rot,
CLAUDIO: This sensible warm motion to become
CLAUDIO: A kneaded clod, and the delighted spirit
CLAUDIO: To bathe in fiery floods, or to reside
CLAUDIO: In thrilling region of thick-ribbed ice,
CLAUDIO: To be imprison'd in the viewless winds,
CLAUDIO: And blown with restless violence round about
CLAUDIO: The pendent world, or to be worse than worst
CLAUDIO: Of those that lawless and incertain thought
CLAUDIO: Imagine howling: 'tis too horrible!
CLAUDIO: The weariest and most loathed worldly life
CLAUDIO: That age, ache, penury and imprisonment
CLAUDIO: Can lay on nature is a paradise
CLAUDIO: To what we fear of death.
ISABELLA: Alas, alas!
CLAUDIO: Sweet sister, let me live:
CLAUDIO: What sin you do to save a brother's life,
CLAUDIO: Nature dispenses with the deed so far
CLAUDIO: That it becomes a virtue.
ISABELLA: O you beast!
ISABELLA: O faithless coward! O dishonest wretch!
ISABELLA: Wilt thou be made a man out of my vice?
ISABELLA: Is't not a kind of incest, to take life
ISABELLA: From thine own sister's shame? What should I think?
ISABELLA: Heaven shield my mother play'd my father fair!
ISABELLA: For such a warped slip of wilderness
ISABELLA: Ne'er issued from his blood. Take my defiance!
ISABELLA: Die, perish! Might but my bending down
ISABELLA: Reprieve thee from thy fate, it should proceed:
ISABELLA: I'll pray a thousand prayers for thy death,
ISABELLA: No word to save thee.
CLAUDIO: Nay, hear me, Isabel.
ISABELLA: O, fie, fie, fie!
ISABELLA: Thy sin's not accidental, but a trade.
ISABELLA: Mercy to thee would prove itself a bawd:
ISABELLA: 'Tis best thou diest quickly.
CLAUDIO: O hear me, Isabella!
NARRATOR: Re-enter DUKE VINCENTIO
DUKE VINCENTIO: Vouchsafe a word, young sister, but one word.
ISABELLA: What is your will?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Might you dispense with your leisure, I would by and
DUKE VINCENTIO: by have some speech with you: the satisfaction I
DUKE VINCENTIO: would require is likewise your own benefit.
ISABELLA: I have no superfluous leisure, my stay must be
ISABELLA: stolen out of other affairs, but I will attend you awhile.
NARRATOR: Walks apart
DUKE VINCENTIO: Son, I have overheard what hath passed between you
DUKE VINCENTIO: and your sister. Angelo had never the purpose to
DUKE VINCENTIO: corrupt her, only he hath made an essay of her
DUKE VINCENTIO: virtue to practise his judgment with the disposition
DUKE VINCENTIO: of natures: she, having the truth of honour in her,
DUKE VINCENTIO: hath made him that gracious denial which he is most
DUKE VINCENTIO: glad to receive. I am confessor to Angelo, and I
DUKE VINCENTIO: know this to be true, therefore prepare yourself to
DUKE VINCENTIO: death: do not satisfy your resolution with hopes
DUKE VINCENTIO: that are fallible: tomorrow you must die, go to
DUKE VINCENTIO: your knees and make ready.
CLAUDIO: Let me ask my sister pardon. I am so out of love
CLAUDIO: with life that I will sue to be rid of it.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hold you there: farewell.
NARRATOR: Exit CLAUDIO
DUKE VINCENTIO: Provost, a word with you!
NARRATOR: Re-enter Provost
Provost: What's your will, father
DUKE VINCENTIO: That now you are come, you will be gone. Leave me
DUKE VINCENTIO: awhile with the maid: my mind promises with my
DUKE VINCENTIO: habit no loss shall touch her by my company.
Provost: In good time.
NARRATOR: Exit Provost. ISABELLA comes forward
DUKE VINCENTIO: The hand that hath made you fair hath made you good:
DUKE VINCENTIO: the goodness that is cheap in beauty makes beauty
DUKE VINCENTIO: brief in goodness, but grace, being the soul of
DUKE VINCENTIO: your complexion, shall keep the body of it ever
DUKE VINCENTIO: fair. The assault that Angelo hath made to you,
DUKE VINCENTIO: fortune hath conveyed to my understanding, and, but
DUKE VINCENTIO: that frailty hath examples for his falling, I should
DUKE VINCENTIO: wonder at Angelo. How will you do to content this
DUKE VINCENTIO: substitute, and to save your brother?
ISABELLA: I am now going to resolve him: I had rather my
ISABELLA: brother die by the law than my son should be
ISABELLA: unlawfully born. But, O, how much is the good duke
ISABELLA: deceived in Angelo! If ever he return and I can
ISABELLA: speak to him, I will open my lips in vain, or
ISABELLA: discover his government.
DUKE VINCENTIO: That shall not be much amiss: Yet, as the matter
DUKE VINCENTIO: now stands, he will avoid your accusation, he made
DUKE VINCENTIO: trial of you only. Therefore fasten your ear on my
DUKE VINCENTIO: advisings: to the love I have in doing good a
DUKE VINCENTIO: remedy presents itself. I do make myself believe
DUKE VINCENTIO: that you may most uprighteously do a poor wronged
DUKE VINCENTIO: lady a merited benefit, redeem your brother from
DUKE VINCENTIO: the angry law, do no stain to your own gracious
DUKE VINCENTIO: person, and much please the absent duke, if
DUKE VINCENTIO: peradventure he shall ever return to have hearing of
DUKE VINCENTIO: this business.
ISABELLA: Let me hear you speak farther. I have spirit to do
ISABELLA: anything that appears not foul in the truth of my spirit.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Virtue is bold, and goodness never fearful. Have
DUKE VINCENTIO: you not heard speak of Mariana, the sister of
DUKE VINCENTIO: Frederick the great soldier who miscarried at sea?
ISABELLA: I have heard of the lady, and good words went with her name.
DUKE VINCENTIO: She should this Angelo have married, was affianced
DUKE VINCENTIO: to her by oath, and the nuptial appointed: between
DUKE VINCENTIO: which time of the contract and limit of the
DUKE VINCENTIO: solemnity, her brother Frederick was wrecked at sea,
DUKE VINCENTIO: having in that perished vessel the dowry of his
DUKE VINCENTIO: sister. But mark how heavily this befell to the
DUKE VINCENTIO: poor gentlewoman: there she lost a noble and
DUKE VINCENTIO: renowned brother, in his love toward her ever most
DUKE VINCENTIO: kind and natural, with him, the portion and sinew of
DUKE VINCENTIO: her fortune, her marriage-dowry, with both, her
DUKE VINCENTIO: combinate husband, this well-seeming Angelo.
ISABELLA: Can this be so? did Angelo so leave her?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Left her in her tears, and dried not one of them
DUKE VINCENTIO: with his comfort, swallowed his vows whole,
DUKE VINCENTIO: pretending in her discoveries of dishonour: in few,
DUKE VINCENTIO: bestowed her on her own lamentation, which she yet
DUKE VINCENTIO: wears for his sake, and he, a marble to her tears,
DUKE VINCENTIO: is washed with them, but relents not.
ISABELLA: What a merit were it in death to take this poor maid
ISABELLA: from the world! What corruption in this life, that
ISABELLA: it will let this man live! But how out of this can she avail?
DUKE VINCENTIO: It is a rupture that you may easily heal: and the
DUKE VINCENTIO: cure of it not only saves your brother, but keeps
DUKE VINCENTIO: you from dishonour in doing it.
ISABELLA: Show me how, good father.
DUKE VINCENTIO: This forenamed maid hath yet in her the continuance
DUKE VINCENTIO: of her first affection: his unjust unkindness, that
DUKE VINCENTIO: in all reason should have quenched her love, hath,
DUKE VINCENTIO: like an impediment in the current, made it more
DUKE VINCENTIO: violent and unruly. Go you to Angelo, answer his
DUKE VINCENTIO: requiring with a plausible obedience, agree with
DUKE VINCENTIO: his demands to the point, only refer yourself to
DUKE VINCENTIO: this advantage, first, that your stay with him may
DUKE VINCENTIO: not be long, that the time may have all shadow and
DUKE VINCENTIO: silence in it, and the place answer to convenience.
DUKE VINCENTIO: This being granted in course,--and now follows
DUKE VINCENTIO: all,--we shall advise this wronged maid to stead up
DUKE VINCENTIO: your appointment, go in your place, if the encounter
DUKE VINCENTIO: acknowledge itself hereafter, it may compel him to
DUKE VINCENTIO: her recompense: and here, by this, is your brother
DUKE VINCENTIO: saved, your honour untainted, the poor Mariana
DUKE VINCENTIO: advantaged, and the corrupt deputy scaled. The maid
DUKE VINCENTIO: will I frame and make fit for his attempt. If you
DUKE VINCENTIO: think well to carry this as you may, the doubleness
DUKE VINCENTIO: of the benefit defends the deceit from reproof.
DUKE VINCENTIO: What think you of it?
ISABELLA: The image of it gives me content already, and I
ISABELLA: trust it will grow to a most prosperous perfection.
DUKE VINCENTIO: It lies much in your holding up. Haste you speedily
DUKE VINCENTIO: to Angelo: if for this night he entreat you to his
DUKE VINCENTIO: bed, give him promise of satisfaction. I will
DUKE VINCENTIO: presently to Saint Luke's: there, at the moated
DUKE VINCENTIO: grange, resides this dejected Mariana. At that
DUKE VINCENTIO: place call upon me, and dispatch with Angelo, that
DUKE VINCENTIO: it may be quickly.
ISABELLA: I thank you for this comfort. Fare you well, good father.
NARRATOR: Exeunt severally
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The street before the prison.
NARRATOR: Enter, on one side, DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as before, on the other, ELBOW, and Officers with POMPEY
ELBOW: Nay, if there be no remedy for it, but that you will
ELBOW: needs buy and sell men and women like beasts, we
ELBOW: shall have all the world drink brown and white bastard.
DUKE VINCENTIO: O heavens! what stuff is here
POMPEY: 'Twas never merry world since, of two usuries, the
POMPEY: merriest was put down, and the worser allowed by
POMPEY: order of law a furred gown to keep him warm, and
POMPEY: furred with fox and lamb-skins too, to signify, that
POMPEY: craft, being richer than innocency, stands for the facing.
ELBOW: Come your way, sir. 'Bless you, good father friar.
DUKE VINCENTIO: And you, good brother father. What offence hath
DUKE VINCENTIO: this man made you, sir?
ELBOW: Marry, sir, he hath offended the law: and, sir, we
ELBOW: take him to be a thief too, sir, for we have found
ELBOW: upon him, sir, a strange picklock, which we have
ELBOW: sent to the deputy.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Fie, sirrah! a bawd, a wicked bawd!
DUKE VINCENTIO: The evil that thou causest to be done,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That is thy means to live. Do thou but think
DUKE VINCENTIO: What 'tis to cram a maw or clothe a back
DUKE VINCENTIO: From such a filthy vice: say to thyself,
DUKE VINCENTIO: From their abominable and beastly touches
DUKE VINCENTIO: I drink, I eat, array myself, and live.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Canst thou believe thy living is a life,
DUKE VINCENTIO: So stinkingly depending? Go mend, go mend.
POMPEY: Indeed, it does stink in some sort, sir, but yet,
POMPEY: sir, I would prove--
DUKE VINCENTIO: Nay, if the devil have given thee proofs for sin,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Thou wilt prove his. Take him to prison, officer:
DUKE VINCENTIO: Correction and instruction must both work
DUKE VINCENTIO: Ere this rude beast will profit.
ELBOW: He must before the deputy, sir, he has given him
ELBOW: warning: the deputy cannot abide a whoremaster: if
ELBOW: he be a whoremonger, and comes before him, he were
ELBOW: as good go a mile on his errand.
DUKE VINCENTIO: That we were all, as some would seem to be,
DUKE VINCENTIO: From our faults, as faults from seeming, free!
ELBOW: His neck will come to your waist,--a cord, sir.
POMPEY: I spy comfort, I cry bail. Here's a gentleman and a
POMPEY: friend of mine.
NARRATOR: Enter LUCIO
LUCIO: How now, noble Pompey! What, at the wheels of
LUCIO: Caesar? art thou led in triumph? What, is there
LUCIO: none of Pygmalion's images, newly made woman, to be
LUCIO: had now, for putting the hand in the pocket and
LUCIO: extracting it clutch'd? What reply, ha? What
LUCIO: sayest thou to this tune, matter and method? Is't
LUCIO: not drowned i' the last rain, ha? What sayest
LUCIO: thou, Trot? Is the world as it was, man? Which is
LUCIO: the way? Is it sad, and few words? or how? The
LUCIO: trick of it?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Still thus, and thus, still worse!
LUCIO: How doth my dear morsel, thy mistress? Procures she
LUCIO: still, ha?
POMPEY: Troth, sir, she hath eaten up all her beef, and she
POMPEY: is herself in the tub.
LUCIO: Why, 'tis good, it is the right of it, it must be
LUCIO: so: ever your fresh whore and your powdered bawd:
LUCIO: an unshunned consequence, it must be so. Art going
LUCIO: to prison, Pompey?
POMPEY: Yes, faith, sir.
LUCIO: Why, 'tis not amiss, Pompey. Farewell: go, say I
LUCIO: sent thee thither. For debt, Pompey? or how?
ELBOW: For being a bawd, for being a bawd.
LUCIO: Well, then, imprison him: if imprisonment be the
LUCIO: due of a bawd, why, 'tis his right: bawd is he
LUCIO: doubtless, and of antiquity too, bawd-born.
LUCIO: Farewell, good Pompey. Commend me to the prison,
LUCIO: Pompey: you will turn good husband now, Pompey, you
LUCIO: will keep the house.
POMPEY: I hope, sir, your good worship will be my bail.
LUCIO: No, indeed, will I not, Pompey, it is not the wear.
LUCIO: I will pray, Pompey, to increase your bondage: If
LUCIO: you take it not patiently, why, your mettle is the
LUCIO: more. Adieu, trusty Pompey. 'Bless you, friar.
DUKE VINCENTIO: And you.
LUCIO: Does Bridget paint still, Pompey, ha?
ELBOW: Come your ways, sir, come.
POMPEY: You will not bail me, then, sir?
LUCIO: Then, Pompey, nor now. What news abroad, friar?
LUCIO: what news?
ELBOW: Come your ways, sir, come.
LUCIO: Go to kennel, Pompey, go.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ELBOW, POMPEY and Officers
LUCIO: What news, friar, of the duke?
DUKE VINCENTIO: I know none. Can you tell me of any?
LUCIO: Some say he is with the Emperor of Russia, other
LUCIO: some, he is in Rome: but where is he, think you?
DUKE VINCENTIO: I know not where, but wheresoever, I wish him well.
LUCIO: It was a mad fantastical trick of him to steal from
LUCIO: the state, and usurp the beggary he was never born
LUCIO: to. Lord Angelo dukes it well in his absence, he
LUCIO: puts transgression to 't.
DUKE VINCENTIO: He does well in 't.
LUCIO: A little more lenity to lechery would do no harm in
LUCIO: him: something too crabbed that way, friar.
DUKE VINCENTIO: It is too general a vice, and severity must cure it.
LUCIO: Yes, in good sooth, the vice is of a great kindred,
LUCIO: it is well allied: but it is impossible to extirp
LUCIO: it quite, friar, till eating and drinking be put
LUCIO: down. They say this Angelo was not made by man and
LUCIO: woman after this downright way of creation: is it
LUCIO: true, think you?
DUKE VINCENTIO: How should he be made, then?
LUCIO: Some report a sea-maid spawned him, some, that he
LUCIO: was begot between two stock-fishes. But it is
LUCIO: certain that when he makes water his urine is
LUCIO: congealed ice, that I know to be true: and he is a
LUCIO: motion generative, that's infallible.
DUKE VINCENTIO: You are pleasant, sir, and speak apace.
LUCIO: Why, what a ruthless thing is this in him, for the
LUCIO: rebellion of a codpiece to take away the life of a
LUCIO: man! Would the duke that is absent have done this?
LUCIO: Ere he would have hanged a man for the getting a
LUCIO: hundred bastards, he would have paid for the nursing
LUCIO: a thousand: he had some feeling of the sport: he
LUCIO: knew the service, and that instructed him to mercy.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I never heard the absent duke much detected for
DUKE VINCENTIO: women, he was not inclined that way.
LUCIO: O, sir, you are deceived.
DUKE VINCENTIO: 'Tis not possible.
LUCIO: Who, not the duke? yes, your beggar of fifty, and
LUCIO: his use was to put a ducat in her clack-dish: the
LUCIO: duke had crotchets in him. He would be drunk too,
LUCIO: that let me inform you.
DUKE VINCENTIO: You do him wrong, surely.
LUCIO: Sir, I was an inward of his. A shy fellow was the
LUCIO: duke: and I believe I know the cause of his
LUCIO: withdrawing.
DUKE VINCENTIO: What, I prithee, might be the cause?
LUCIO: No, pardon, 'tis a secret must be locked within the
LUCIO: teeth and the lips: but this I can let you
LUCIO: understand, the greater file of the subject held the
LUCIO: duke to be wise.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Wise! why, no question but he was.
LUCIO: A very superficial, ignorant, unweighing fellow.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Either this is the envy in you, folly, or mistaking:
DUKE VINCENTIO: the very stream of his life and the business he hath
DUKE VINCENTIO: helmed must upon a warranted need give him a better
DUKE VINCENTIO: proclamation. Let him be but testimonied in his own
DUKE VINCENTIO: bringings-forth, and he shall appear to the
DUKE VINCENTIO: envious a scholar, a statesman and a soldier.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Therefore you speak unskilfully: or if your
DUKE VINCENTIO: knowledge be more it is much darkened in your malice.
LUCIO: Sir, I know him, and I love him.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Love talks with better knowledge, and knowledge with
DUKE VINCENTIO: dearer love.
LUCIO: Come, sir, I know what I know.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I can hardly believe that, since you know not what
DUKE VINCENTIO: you speak. But, if ever the duke return, as our
DUKE VINCENTIO: prayers are he may, let me desire you to make your
DUKE VINCENTIO: answer before him. If it be honest you have spoke,
DUKE VINCENTIO: you have courage to maintain it: I am bound to call
DUKE VINCENTIO: upon you, and, I pray you, your name?
LUCIO: Sir, my name is Lucio, well known to the duke.
DUKE VINCENTIO: He shall know you better, sir, if I may live to
DUKE VINCENTIO: report you.
LUCIO: I fear you not.
DUKE VINCENTIO: O, you hope the duke will return no more, or you
DUKE VINCENTIO: imagine me too unhurtful an opposite. But indeed I
DUKE VINCENTIO: can do you little harm, you'll forswear this again.
LUCIO: I'll be hanged first: thou art deceived in me,
LUCIO: friar. But no more of this. Canst thou tell if
LUCIO: Claudio die to-morrow or no?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Why should he die, sir?
LUCIO: Why? For filling a bottle with a tundish. I would
LUCIO: the duke we talk of were returned again: the
LUCIO: ungenitured agent will unpeople the province with
LUCIO: continency, sparrows must not build in his
LUCIO: house-eaves, because they are lecherous. The duke
LUCIO: yet would have dark deeds darkly answered, he would
LUCIO: never bring them to light: would he were returned!
LUCIO: Marry, this Claudio is condemned for untrussing.
LUCIO: Farewell, good friar: I prithee, pray for me. The
LUCIO: duke, I say to thee again, would eat mutton on
LUCIO: Fridays. He's not past it yet, and I say to thee,
LUCIO: he would mouth with a beggar, though she smelt brown
LUCIO: bread and garlic: say that I said so. Farewell.
NARRATOR: Exit
DUKE VINCENTIO: No might nor greatness in mortality
DUKE VINCENTIO: Can censure 'scape, back-wounding calumny
DUKE VINCENTIO: The whitest virtue strikes. What king so strong
DUKE VINCENTIO: Can tie the gall up in the slanderous tongue?
DUKE VINCENTIO: But who comes here?
NARRATOR: Enter ESCALUS, Provost, and Officers with MISTRESS OVERDONE
ESCALUS: Go, away with her to prison!
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Good my lord, be good to me, your honour is accounted
MISTRESS OVERDONE: a merciful man, good my lord.
ESCALUS: Double and treble admonition, and still forfeit in
ESCALUS: the same kind! This would make mercy swear and play
ESCALUS: the tyrant.
Provost: A bawd of eleven years' continuance, may it please
Provost: your honour.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: My lord, this is one Lucio's information against me.
MISTRESS OVERDONE: Mistress Kate Keepdown was with child by him in the
MISTRESS OVERDONE: duke's time, he promised her marriage: his child
MISTRESS OVERDONE: is a year and a quarter old, come Philip and Jacob:
MISTRESS OVERDONE: I have kept it myself, and see how he goes about to abuse me!
ESCALUS: That fellow is a fellow of much licence: let him be
ESCALUS: called before us. Away with her to prison! Go to,
ESCALUS: no more words.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Officers with MISTRESS OVERDONE
ESCALUS: Provost, my brother Angelo will not be altered,
ESCALUS: Claudio must die to-morrow: let him be furnished
ESCALUS: with divines, and have all charitable preparation.
ESCALUS: if my brother wrought by my pity, it should not be
ESCALUS: so with him.
Provost: So please you, this friar hath been with him, and
Provost: advised him for the entertainment of death.
ESCALUS: Good even, good father.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Bliss and goodness on you!
ESCALUS: Of whence are you?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Not of this country, though my chance is now
DUKE VINCENTIO: To use it for my time: I am a brother
DUKE VINCENTIO: Of gracious order, late come from the See
DUKE VINCENTIO: In special business from his holiness.
ESCALUS: What news abroad i' the world?
DUKE VINCENTIO: None, but that there is so great a fever on
DUKE VINCENTIO: goodness, that the dissolution of it must cure it:
DUKE VINCENTIO: novelty is only in request, and it is as dangerous
DUKE VINCENTIO: to be aged in any kind of course, as it is virtuous
DUKE VINCENTIO: to be constant in any undertaking. There is scarce
DUKE VINCENTIO: truth enough alive to make societies secure, but
DUKE VINCENTIO: security enough to make fellowships accurst: much
DUKE VINCENTIO: upon this riddle runs the wisdom of the world. This
DUKE VINCENTIO: news is old enough, yet it is every day's news. I
DUKE VINCENTIO: pray you, sir, of what disposition was the duke?
ESCALUS: One that, above all other strifes, contended
ESCALUS: especially to know himself.
DUKE VINCENTIO: What pleasure was he given to?
ESCALUS: Rather rejoicing to see another merry, than merry at
ESCALUS: any thing which professed to make him rejoice: a
ESCALUS: gentleman of all temperance. But leave we him to
ESCALUS: his events, with a prayer they may prove prosperous,
ESCALUS: and let me desire to know how you find Claudio
ESCALUS: prepared. I am made to understand that you have
ESCALUS: lent him visitation.
DUKE VINCENTIO: He professes to have received no sinister measure
DUKE VINCENTIO: from his judge, but most willingly humbles himself
DUKE VINCENTIO: to the determination of justice: yet had he framed
DUKE VINCENTIO: to himself, by the instruction of his frailty, many
DUKE VINCENTIO: deceiving promises of life, which I by my good
DUKE VINCENTIO: leisure have discredited to him, and now is he
DUKE VINCENTIO: resolved to die.
ESCALUS: You have paid the heavens your function, and the
ESCALUS: prisoner the very debt of your calling. I have
ESCALUS: laboured for the poor gentleman to the extremest
ESCALUS: shore of my modesty: but my brother justice have I
ESCALUS: found so severe, that he hath forced me to tell him
ESCALUS: he is indeed Justice.
DUKE VINCENTIO: If his own life answer the straitness of his
DUKE VINCENTIO: proceeding, it shall become him well, wherein if he
DUKE VINCENTIO: chance to fail, he hath sentenced himself.
ESCALUS: I am going to visit the prisoner. Fare you well.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Peace be with you!
NARRATOR: Exeunt ESCALUS and Provost
DUKE VINCENTIO: He who the sword of heaven will bear
DUKE VINCENTIO: Should be as holy as severe,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Pattern in himself to know,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Grace to stand, and virtue go,
DUKE VINCENTIO: More nor less to others paying
DUKE VINCENTIO: Than by self-offences weighing.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Shame to him whose cruel striking
DUKE VINCENTIO: Kills for faults of his own liking!
DUKE VINCENTIO: Twice treble shame on Angelo,
DUKE VINCENTIO: To weed my vice and let his grow!
DUKE VINCENTIO: O, what may man within him hide,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Though angel on the outward side!
DUKE VINCENTIO: How may likeness made in crimes,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Making practise on the times,
DUKE VINCENTIO: To draw with idle spiders' strings
DUKE VINCENTIO: Most ponderous and substantial things!
DUKE VINCENTIO: Craft against vice I must apply:
DUKE VINCENTIO: With Angelo to-night shall lie
DUKE VINCENTIO: His old betrothed but despised,
DUKE VINCENTIO: So disguise shall, by the disguised,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Pay with falsehood false exacting,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And perform an old contracting.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: ACT IV
NARRATOR: SCENE I. The moated grange at ST. LUKE's.
NARRATOR: Enter MARIANA and a Boy
NARRATOR: Boy sings
DUKE VINCENTIO: Take, O, take those lips away,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That so sweetly were forsworn,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And those eyes, the break of day,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Lights that do mislead the morn:
DUKE VINCENTIO: But my kisses bring again, bring again,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Seals of love, but sealed in vain, sealed in vain.
MARIANA: Break off thy song, and haste thee quick away:
MARIANA: Here comes a man of comfort, whose advice
MARIANA: Hath often still'd my brawling discontent.
NARRATOR: Exit Boy
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as before
MARIANA: I cry you mercy, sir, and well could wish
MARIANA: You had not found me here so musical:
MARIANA: Let me excuse me, and believe me so,
MARIANA: My mirth it much displeased, but pleased my woe.
DUKE VINCENTIO: 'Tis good, though music oft hath such a charm
DUKE VINCENTIO: To make bad good, and good provoke to harm.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I pray, you, tell me, hath any body inquired
DUKE VINCENTIO: for me here to-day? much upon this time have
DUKE VINCENTIO: I promised here to meet.
MARIANA: You have not been inquired after:
MARIANA: I have sat here all day.
NARRATOR: Enter ISABELLA
DUKE VINCENTIO: I do constantly believe you. The time is come even
DUKE VINCENTIO: now. I shall crave your forbearance a little: may
DUKE VINCENTIO: be I will call upon you anon, for some advantage to yourself.
MARIANA: I am always bound to you.
NARRATOR: Exit
DUKE VINCENTIO: Very well met, and well come.
DUKE VINCENTIO: What is the news from this good deputy?
ISABELLA: He hath a garden circummured with brick,
ISABELLA: Whose western side is with a vineyard back'd,
ISABELLA: And to that vineyard is a planched gate,
ISABELLA: That makes his opening with this bigger key:
ISABELLA: This other doth command a little door
ISABELLA: Which from the vineyard to the garden leads,
ISABELLA: There have I made my promise
ISABELLA: Upon the heavy middle of the night
ISABELLA: To call upon him.
DUKE VINCENTIO: But shall you on your knowledge find this way?
ISABELLA: I have ta'en a due and wary note upon't:
ISABELLA: With whispering and most guilty diligence,
ISABELLA: In action all of precept, he did show me
ISABELLA: The way twice o'er.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Are there no other tokens
DUKE VINCENTIO: Between you 'greed concerning her observance?
ISABELLA: No, none, but only a repair i' the dark,
ISABELLA: And that I have possess'd him my most stay
ISABELLA: Can be but brief, for I have made him know
ISABELLA: I have a servant comes with me along,
ISABELLA: That stays upon me, whose persuasion is
ISABELLA: I come about my brother.
DUKE VINCENTIO: 'Tis well borne up.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I have not yet made known to Mariana
DUKE VINCENTIO: A word of this. What, ho! within! come forth!
NARRATOR: Re-enter MARIANA
DUKE VINCENTIO: I pray you, be acquainted with this maid,
DUKE VINCENTIO: She comes to do you good.
ISABELLA: I do desire the like.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Do you persuade yourself that I respect you?
MARIANA: Good friar, I know you do, and have found it.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Take, then, this your companion by the hand,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Who hath a story ready for your ear.
DUKE VINCENTIO: I shall attend your leisure: but make haste,
DUKE VINCENTIO: The vaporous night approaches.
MARIANA: Will't please you walk aside?
NARRATOR: Exeunt MARIANA and ISABELLA
DUKE VINCENTIO: O place and greatness! millions of false eyes
DUKE VINCENTIO: Are stuck upon thee: volumes of report
DUKE VINCENTIO: Run with these false and most contrarious quests
DUKE VINCENTIO: Upon thy doings: thousand escapes of wit
DUKE VINCENTIO: Make thee the father of their idle dreams
DUKE VINCENTIO: And rack thee in their fancies.
NARRATOR: Re-enter MARIANA and ISABELLA
DUKE VINCENTIO: Welcome, how agreed?
ISABELLA: She'll take the enterprise upon her, father,
ISABELLA: If you advise it.
DUKE VINCENTIO: It is not my consent,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But my entreaty too.
ISABELLA: Little have you to say
ISABELLA: When you depart from him, but, soft and low,
ISABELLA: 'Remember now my brother.'
MARIANA: Fear me not.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Nor, gentle daughter, fear you not at all.
DUKE VINCENTIO: He is your husband on a pre-contract:
DUKE VINCENTIO: To bring you thus together, 'tis no sin,
DUKE VINCENTIO: Sith that the justice of your title to him
DUKE VINCENTIO: Doth flourish the deceit. Come, let us go:
DUKE VINCENTIO: Our corn's to reap, for yet our tithe's to sow.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. A room in the prison.
NARRATOR: Enter Provost and POMPEY
Provost: Come hither, sirrah. Can you cut off a man's head?
POMPEY: If the man be a bachelor, sir, I can, but if he be a
POMPEY: married man, he's his wife's head, and I can never
POMPEY: cut off a woman's head.
Provost: Come, sir, leave me your snatches, and yield me a
Provost: direct answer. To-morrow morning are to die Claudio
Provost: and Barnardine. Here is in our prison a common
Provost: executioner, who in his office lacks a helper: if
Provost: you will take it on you to assist him, it shall
Provost: redeem you from your gyves, if not, you shall have
Provost: your full time of imprisonment and your deliverance
Provost: with an unpitied whipping, for you have been a
Provost: notorious bawd.
POMPEY: Sir, I have been an unlawful bawd time out of mind,
POMPEY: but yet I will be content to be a lawful hangman. I
POMPEY: would be glad to receive some instruction from my
POMPEY: fellow partner.
Provost: What, ho! Abhorson! Where's Abhorson, there?
NARRATOR: Enter ABHORSON
ABHORSON: Do you call, sir?
Provost: Sirrah, here's a fellow will help you to-morrow in
Provost: your execution. If you think it meet, compound with
Provost: him by the year, and let him abide here with you, if
Provost: not, use him for the present and dismiss him. He
Provost: cannot plead his estimation with you, he hath been a bawd.
ABHORSON: A bawd, sir? fie upon him! he will discredit our mystery.
Provost: Go to, sir, you weigh equally, a feather will turn
Provost: the scale.
NARRATOR: Exit
POMPEY: Pray, sir, by your good favour,--for surely, sir, a
POMPEY: good favour you have, but that you have a hanging
POMPEY: look,--do you call, sir, your occupation a mystery?
ABHORSON: Ay, sir, a mystery
POMPEY: Painting, sir, I have heard say, is a mystery, and
POMPEY: your whores, sir, being members of my occupation,
POMPEY: using painting, do prove my occupation a mystery:
POMPEY: but what mystery there should be in hanging, if I
POMPEY: should be hanged, I cannot imagine.
ABHORSON: Sir, it is a mystery.
POMPEY: Proof?
ABHORSON: Every true man's apparel fits your thief: if it be
ABHORSON: too little for your thief, your true man thinks it
ABHORSON: big enough, if it be too big for your thief, your
ABHORSON: thief thinks it little enough: so every true man's
ABHORSON: apparel fits your thief.
NARRATOR: Re-enter Provost
Provost: Are you agreed?
POMPEY: Sir, I will serve him, for I do find your hangman is
POMPEY: a more penitent trade than your bawd, he doth
POMPEY: oftener ask forgiveness.
Provost: You, sirrah, provide your block and your axe
Provost: to-morrow four o'clock.
ABHORSON: Come on, bawd, I will instruct thee in my trade, follow.
POMPEY: I do desire to learn, sir: and I hope, if you have
POMPEY: occasion to use me for your own turn, you shall find
POMPEY: me yare, for truly, sir, for your kindness I owe you
POMPEY: a good turn.
Provost: Call hither Barnardine and Claudio:
NARRATOR: Exeunt POMPEY and ABHORSON
Provost: The one has my pity, not a jot the other,
Provost: Being a murderer, though he were my brother.
NARRATOR: Enter CLAUDIO
Provost: Look, here's the warrant, Claudio, for thy death:
Provost: 'Tis now dead midnight, and by eight to-morrow
Provost: Thou must be made immortal. Where's Barnardine?
CLAUDIO: As fast lock'd up in sleep as guiltless labour
CLAUDIO: When it lies starkly in the traveller's bones:
CLAUDIO: He will not wake.
Provost: Who can do good on him?
Provost: Well, go, prepare yourself.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Provost: But, hark, what noise?
Provost: Heaven give your spirits comfort!
NARRATOR: Exit CLAUDIO
Provost: By and by.
Provost: I hope it is some pardon or reprieve
Provost: For the most gentle Claudio.
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as before
Provost: Welcome father.
DUKE VINCENTIO: The best and wholesomest spirts of the night
DUKE VINCENTIO: Envelope you, good Provost! Who call'd here of late?
Provost: None, since the curfew rung.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Not Isabel?
Provost: No.
DUKE VINCENTIO: They will, then, ere't be long.
Provost: What comfort is for Claudio?
DUKE VINCENTIO: There's some in hope.
Provost: It is a bitter deputy.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Not so, not so, his life is parallel'd
DUKE VINCENTIO: Even with the stroke and line of his great justice:
DUKE VINCENTIO: He doth with holy abstinence subdue
DUKE VINCENTIO: That in himself which he spurs on his power
DUKE VINCENTIO: To qualify in others: were he meal'd with that
DUKE VINCENTIO: Which he corrects, then were he tyrannous,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But this being so, he's just.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
DUKE VINCENTIO: Now are they come.
NARRATOR: Exit Provost
DUKE VINCENTIO: This is a gentle provost: seldom when
DUKE VINCENTIO: The steeled gaoler is the friend of men.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
DUKE VINCENTIO: How now! what noise? That spirit's possessed with haste
DUKE VINCENTIO: That wounds the unsisting postern with these strokes.
NARRATOR: Re-enter Provost
Provost: There he must stay until the officer
Provost: Arise to let him in: he is call'd up.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet,
DUKE VINCENTIO: But he must die to-morrow?
Provost: None, sir, none.
DUKE VINCENTIO: As near the dawning, provost, as it is,
DUKE VINCENTIO: You shall hear more ere morning.
Provost: Happily
Provost: You something know, yet I believe there comes
Provost: No countermand, no such example have we:
Provost: Besides, upon the very siege of justice
Provost: Lord Angelo hath to the public ear
Provost: Profess'd the contrary.
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
Provost: This is his lordship's man.
DUKE VINCENTIO: And here comes Claudio's pardon.
Messenger: [Giving a paper]
Messenger: My lord hath sent you this note, and by me this
Messenger: further charge, that you swerve not from the
Messenger: smallest article of it, neither in time, matter, or
Messenger: other circumstance. Good morrow, for, as I take it,
Messenger: it is almost day.
Provost: I shall obey him.
NARRATOR: Exit Messenger
DUKE VINCENTIO: [Aside]  This is his pardon, purchased by such sin
DUKE VINCENTIO: For which the pardoner himself is in.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hence hath offence his quick celerity,
DUKE VINCENTIO: When it is born in high authority:
DUKE VINCENTIO: When vice makes mercy, mercy's so extended,
DUKE VINCENTIO: That for the fault's love is the offender friended.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Now, sir, what news?
Provost: I told you. Lord Angelo, belike thinking me remiss
Provost: in mine office, awakens me with this unwonted
Provost: putting-on, methinks strangely, for he hath not used it before.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Pray you, let's hear.
Provost: [Reads]
Provost: 'Whatsoever you may hear to the contrary, let
Provost: Claudio be executed by four of the clock, and in the
Provost: afternoon Barnardine: for my better satisfaction,
Provost: let me have Claudio's head sent me by five. Let
Provost: this be duly performed, with a thought that more
Provost: depends on it than we must yet deliver. Thus fail
Provost: not to do your office, as you will answer it at your peril.'
Provost: What say you to this, sir?
DUKE VINCENTIO: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in the
DUKE VINCENTIO: afternoon?
Provost: A Bohemian born, but here nursed un and bred, one
Provost: that is a prisoner nine years old.
DUKE VINCENTIO: How came it that the absent duke had not either
DUKE VINCENTIO: delivered him to his liberty or executed him? I
DUKE VINCENTIO: have heard it was ever his manner to do so.
Provost: His friends still wrought reprieves for him: and,
Provost: indeed, his fact, till now in the government of Lord
Provost: Angelo, came not to an undoubtful proof.
DUKE VINCENTIO: It is now apparent?
Provost: Most manifest, and not denied by himself.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Hath he born himself penitently in prison? how
DUKE VINCENTIO: seems he to be touched?
Provost: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but
Provost: as a drunken sleep, careless, reckless, and fearless
Provost: of what's past, present, or to come, insensible of
Provost: mortality, and desperately mortal.
DUKE VINCENTIO: He wants advice.
Provost: He will hear none: he hath evermore had the liberty
Provost: of the prison, give him leave to escape hence, he
Provost: would not: drunk many times a day, if not many days
Provost: entirely drunk. We have very oft awaked him, as if
Provost: to carry him to execution, and showed him a seeming
Provost: warrant for it: it hath not moved him at all.
DUKE VINCENTIO: More of him anon. There is written in your brow,
DUKE VINCENTIO: provost, honesty and constancy: if I read it not
DUKE VINCENTIO: truly, my ancient skill beguiles me, but, in the
DUKE VINCENTIO: boldness of my cunning, I will lay myself in hazard.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Claudio, whom here you have warrant to execute, is
DUKE VINCENTIO: no greater forfeit to the law than Angelo who hath
DUKE VINCENTIO: sentenced him. To make you understand this in a
DUKE VINCENTIO: manifested effect, I crave but four days' respite,
DUKE VINCENTIO: for the which you are to do me both a present and a
DUKE VINCENTIO: dangerous courtesy.
Provost: Pray, sir, in what?
DUKE VINCENTIO: In the delaying death.
Provost: A lack, how may I do it, having the hour limited,
Provost: and an express command, under penalty, to deliver
Provost: his head in the view of Angelo? I may make my case
Provost: as Claudio's, to cross this in the smallest.
DUKE VINCENTIO: By the vow of mine order I warrant you, if my
DUKE VINCENTIO: instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine
DUKE VINCENTIO: be this morning executed, and his head born to Angelo.
Provost: Angelo hath seen them both, and will discover the favour.
DUKE VINCENTIO: O, death's a great disguiser, and you may add to it.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Shave the head, and tie the beard, and say it was
DUKE VINCENTIO: the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his
DUKE VINCENTIO: death: you know the course is common. If any thing
DUKE VINCENTIO: fall to you upon this, more than thanks and good
DUKE VINCENTIO: fortune, by the saint whom I profess, I will plead
DUKE VINCENTIO: against it with my life.
Provost: Pardon me, good father, it is against my oath.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Were you sworn to the duke, or to the deputy?
Provost: To him, and to his substitutes.
DUKE VINCENTIO: You will think you have made no offence, if the duke
DUKE VINCENTIO: avouch the justice of your dealing?
Provost: But what likelihood is in that?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see
DUKE VINCENTIO: you fearful, that neither my coat, integrity, nor
DUKE VINCENTIO: persuasion can with ease attempt you, I will go
DUKE VINCENTIO: further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the
DUKE VINCENTIO: duke: you know the character, I doubt not, and the
DUKE VINCENTIO: signet is not strange to you.
Provost: I know them both.
DUKE VINCENTIO: The contents of this is the return of the duke: you
DUKE VINCENTIO: shall anon over-read it at your pleasure, where you
DUKE VINCENTIO: shall find, within these two days he will be here.
DUKE VINCENTIO: This is a thing that Angelo knows not, for he this
DUKE VINCENTIO: very day receives letters of strange tenor,
DUKE VINCENTIO: perchance of the duke's death, perchance entering
DUKE VINCENTIO: into some monastery, but, by chance, nothing of what
DUKE VINCENTIO: is writ. Look, the unfolding star calls up the
DUKE VINCENTIO: shepherd. Put not yourself into amazement how these
DUKE VINCENTIO: things should be: all difficulties are but easy
DUKE VINCENTIO: when they are known. Call your executioner, and off
DUKE VINCENTIO: with Barnardine's head: I will give him a present
DUKE VINCENTIO: shrift and advise him for a better place. Yet you
DUKE VINCENTIO: are amazed, but this shall absolutely resolve you.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Come away, it is almost clear dawn.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Another room in the same.
NARRATOR: Enter POMPEY
POMPEY: I am as well acquainted here as I was in our house
POMPEY: of profession: one would think it were Mistress
POMPEY: Overdone's own house, for here be many of her old
POMPEY: customers. First, here's young Master Rash, he's in
POMPEY: for a commodity of brown paper and old ginger,
POMPEY: ninescore and seventeen pounds, of which he made
POMPEY: five marks, ready money: marry, then ginger was not
POMPEY: much in request, for the old women were all dead.
POMPEY: Then is there here one Master Caper, at the suit of
POMPEY: Master Three-pile the mercer, for some four suits of
POMPEY: peach-coloured satin, which now peaches him a
POMPEY: beggar. Then have we here young Dizy, and young
POMPEY: Master Deep-vow, and Master Copperspur, and Master
POMPEY: Starve-lackey the rapier and dagger man, and young
POMPEY: Drop-heir that killed lusty Pudding, and Master
POMPEY: Forthlight the tilter, and brave Master Shooty the
POMPEY: great traveller, and wild Half-can that stabbed
POMPEY: Pots, and, I think, forty more, all great doers in
POMPEY: our trade, and are now 'for the Lord's sake.'
NARRATOR: Enter ABHORSON
ABHORSON: Sirrah, bring Barnardine hither.
POMPEY: Master Barnardine! you must rise and be hanged.
POMPEY: Master Barnardine!
ABHORSON: What, ho, Barnardine!
BARNARDINE: [Within]  A pox o' your throats! Who makes that
BARNARDINE: noise there? What are you?
POMPEY: Your friends, sir, the hangman. You must be so
POMPEY: good, sir, to rise and be put to death.
BARNARDINE: [Within]  Away, you rogue, away! I am sleepy.
ABHORSON: Tell him he must awake, and that quickly too.
POMPEY: Pray, Master Barnardine, awake till you are
POMPEY: executed, and sleep afterwards.
ABHORSON: Go in to him, and fetch him out.
POMPEY: He is coming, sir, he is coming, I hear his straw rustle.
ABHORSON: Is the axe upon the block, sirrah?
POMPEY: Very ready, sir.
NARRATOR: Enter BARNARDINE
BARNARDINE: How now, Abhorson? what's the news with you?
ABHORSON: Truly, sir, I would desire you to clap into your
ABHORSON: prayers, for, look you, the warrant's come.
BARNARDINE: You rogue, I have been drinking all night, I am not
BARNARDINE: fitted for 't.
POMPEY: O, the better, sir, for he that drinks all night,
POMPEY: and is hanged betimes in the morning, may sleep the
POMPEY: sounder all the next day.
ABHORSON: Look you, sir, here comes your ghostly father: do
ABHORSON: we jest now, think you?
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE VINCENTIO disguised as before
DUKE VINCENTIO: Sir, induced by my charity, and hearing how hastily
DUKE VINCENTIO: you are to depart, I am come to advise you, comfort
DUKE VINCENTIO: you and pray with you.
BARNARDINE: Friar, not I	I have been drinking hard all night,
BARNARDINE: and I will have more time to prepare me, or they
BARNARDINE: shall beat out my brains with billets: I will not
BARNARDINE: consent to die this day, that's certain.
DUKE VINCENTIO: O, sir, you must: and therefore I beseech you
DUKE VINCENTIO: Look forward on the journey you shall go.
BARNARDINE: I swear I will not die to-day for any man's
BARNARDINE: persuasion.
DUKE VINCENTIO: But hear you.
BARNARDINE: Not a word: if you have any thing to say to me,
BARNARDINE: come to my ward, for thence will not I to-day.
NARRATOR: Exit
DUKE VINCENTIO: Unfit to live or die: O gravel heart!
DUKE VINCENTIO: After him, fellows, bring him to the block.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ABHORSON and POMPEY
NARRATOR: Re-enter Provost
Provost: Now, sir, how do you find the prisoner?
DUKE VINCENTIO: A creature unprepared, unmeet for death,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And to transport him in the mind he is
DUKE VINCENTIO: Were damnable.
Provost: Here in the prison, father,
Provost: There died this morning of a cruel fever
Provost: One Ragozine, a most notorious pirate,
Provost: A man of Claudio's years, his beard and head
Provost: Just of his colour. What if we do omit
Provost: This reprobate till he were well inclined,
Provost: And satisfy the deputy with the visage
Provost: Of Ragozine, more like to Claudio?
DUKE VINCENTIO: O, 'tis an accident that heaven provides!
DUKE VINCENTIO: Dispatch it presently, the hour draws on
DUKE VINCENTIO: Prefix'd by Angelo: see this be done,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And sent according to command, whiles I
DUKE VINCENTIO: Persuade this rude wretch willingly to die.
Provost: This shall be done, good father, presently.
Provost: But Barnardine must die this afternoon:
Provost: And how shall we continue Claudio,
Provost: To save me from the danger that might come
Provost: If he were known alive?
DUKE VINCENTIO: Let this be done.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Put them in secret holds, both Barnardine and Claudio:
DUKE VINCENTIO: Ere twice the sun hath made his journal greeting
DUKE VINCENTIO: To the under generation, you shall find
DUKE VINCENTIO: Your safety manifested.
Provost: I am your free dependant.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Quick, dispatch, and send the head to Angelo.
NARRATOR: Exit Provost
DUKE VINCENTIO: Now will I write letters to Angelo,--
DUKE VINCENTIO: The provost, he shall bear them, whose contents
DUKE VINCENTIO: Shall witness to him I am near at home,
DUKE VINCENTIO: And that, by great injunctions, I am bound
DUKE VINCENTIO: To enter publicly: him I'll desire
DUKE VINCENTIO: To meet me at the consecrated fount
DUKE VINCENTIO: A league below the city, and from thence,
DUKE VINCENTIO: By cold gradation and well-balanced form,
DUKE VINCENTIO: We shall proceed with Angelo.
NARRATOR: Re-enter Provost
Provost: Here is the head, I'll carry it myself.
DUKE VINCENTIO: Convenient is it. Make a swift return,
DUKE VINCENTIO: For I would commune with you of such things
DUKE VINCENTIO: That want no ear but yours.
Provost: I'll make all speed.
