SLENDER: I am not a-hungry, I thank you, forsooth. Go,
SLENDER: sirrah, for all you are my man, go wait upon my
SLENDER: cousin Shallow.
NARRATOR: Exit SIMPLE
SLENDER: A justice of peace sometimes may be beholding to his
SLENDER: friend for a man. I keep but three men and a boy
SLENDER: yet, till my mother be dead: but what though? Yet I
SLENDER: live like a poor gentleman born.
ANNE PAGE: I may not go in without your worship: they will not
ANNE PAGE: sit till you come.
SLENDER: I' faith, I'll eat nothing, I thank you as much as
SLENDER: though I did.
ANNE PAGE: I pray you, sir, walk in.
SLENDER: I had rather walk here, I thank you. I bruised
SLENDER: my shin th' other day with playing at sword and
SLENDER: dagger with a master of fence, three veneys for a
SLENDER: dish of stewed prunes, and, by my troth, I cannot
SLENDER: abide the smell of hot meat since. Why do your
SLENDER: dogs bark so? be there bears i' the town?
ANNE PAGE: I think there are, sir, I heard them talked of.
SLENDER: I love the sport well but I shall as soon quarrel at
SLENDER: it as any man in England. You are afraid, if you see
SLENDER: the bear loose, are you not?
ANNE PAGE: Ay, indeed, sir.
SLENDER: That's meat and drink to me, now. I have seen
SLENDER: Sackerson loose twenty times, and have taken him by
SLENDER: the chain, but, I warrant you, the women have so
SLENDER: cried and shrieked at it, that it passed: but women,
SLENDER: indeed, cannot abide 'em, they are very ill-favored
SLENDER: rough things.
NARRATOR: Re-enter PAGE
PAGE: Come, gentle Master Slender, come, we stay for you.
SLENDER: I'll eat nothing, I thank you, sir.
PAGE: By cock and pie, you shall not choose, sir! come, come.
SLENDER: Nay, pray you, lead the way.
PAGE: Come on, sir.
SLENDER: Mistress Anne, yourself shall go first.
ANNE PAGE: Not I, sir, pray you, keep on.
SLENDER: I'll rather be unmannerly than troublesome.
SLENDER: You do yourself wrong, indeed, la!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The same.
NARRATOR: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS and SIMPLE
SIR HUGH EVANS: Go your ways, and ask of Doctor Caius' house which
SIR HUGH EVANS: is the way: and there dwells one Mistress Quickly,
SIR HUGH EVANS: which is in the manner of his nurse, or his dry
SIR HUGH EVANS: nurse, or his cook, or his laundry, his washer, and
SIR HUGH EVANS: his wringer.
SIMPLE: Well, sir.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Nay, it is petter yet. Give her this letter, for it
SIR HUGH EVANS: is a 'oman that altogether's acquaintance with
SIR HUGH EVANS: Mistress Anne Page: and the letter is, to desire
SIR HUGH EVANS: and require her to solicit your master's desires to
SIR HUGH EVANS: Mistress Anne Page. I pray you, be gone: I will
SIR HUGH EVANS: make an end of my dinner, there's pippins and cheese to come.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn.
NARRATOR: Enter FALSTAFF, Host, BARDOLPH, NYM, PISTOL, and ROBIN
FALSTAFF: Mine host of the Garter!
Host: What says my bully-rook? speak scholarly and wisely.
FALSTAFF: Truly, mine host, I must turn away some of my
FALSTAFF: followers.
Host: Discard, bully Hercules, cashier: let them wag, trot, trot.
FALSTAFF: I sit at ten pounds a week.
Host: Thou'rt an emperor, Caesar, Keisar, and Pheezar. I
Host: will entertain Bardolph, he shall draw, he shall
Host: tap: said I well, bully Hector?
FALSTAFF: Do so, good mine host.
Host: I have spoke, let him follow.
NARRATOR: To BARDOLPH
Host: Let me see thee froth and lime: I am at a word, follow.
NARRATOR: Exit
FALSTAFF: Bardolph, follow him. A tapster is a good trade:
FALSTAFF: an old cloak makes a new jerkin, a withered
FALSTAFF: serving-man a fresh tapster. Go, adieu.
BARDOLPH: It is a life that I have desired: I will thrive.
PISTOL: O base Hungarian wight! wilt thou the spigot wield?
NARRATOR: Exit BARDOLPH
NYM: He was gotten in drink: is not the humour conceited?
FALSTAFF: I am glad I am so acquit of this tinderbox: his
FALSTAFF: thefts were too open, his filching was like an
FALSTAFF: unskilful singer, he kept not time.
NYM: The good humour is to steal at a minute's rest.
PISTOL: 'Convey,' the wise it call. 'Steal!' foh! a fico
PISTOL: for the phrase!
FALSTAFF: Well, sirs, I am almost out at heels.
PISTOL: Why, then, let kibes ensue.
FALSTAFF: There is no remedy, I must cony-catch, I must shift.
PISTOL: Young ravens must have food.
FALSTAFF: Which of you know Ford of this town?
PISTOL: I ken the wight: he is of substance good.
FALSTAFF: My honest lads, I will tell you what I am about.
PISTOL: Two yards, and more.
FALSTAFF: No quips now, Pistol! Indeed, I am in the waist two
FALSTAFF: yards about, but I am now about no waste, I am about
FALSTAFF: thrift. Briefly, I do mean to make love to Ford's
FALSTAFF: wife: I spy entertainment in her, she discourses,
FALSTAFF: she carves, she gives the leer of invitation: I
FALSTAFF: can construe the action of her familiar style, and
FALSTAFF: the hardest voice of her behavior, to be Englished
FALSTAFF: rightly, is, 'I am Sir John Falstaff's.'
PISTOL: He hath studied her will, and translated her will,
PISTOL: out of honesty into English.
NYM: The anchor is deep: will that humour pass?
FALSTAFF: Now, the report goes she has all the rule of her
FALSTAFF: husband's purse: he hath a legion of angels.
PISTOL: As many devils entertain, and 'To her, boy,' say I.
NYM: The humour rises, it is good: humour me the angels.
FALSTAFF: I have writ me here a letter to her: and here
FALSTAFF: another to Page's wife, who even now gave me good
FALSTAFF: eyes too, examined my parts with most judicious
FALSTAFF: oeillades, sometimes the beam of her view gilded my
FALSTAFF: foot, sometimes my portly belly.
PISTOL: Then did the sun on dunghill shine.
NYM: I thank thee for that humour.
FALSTAFF: O, she did so course o'er my exteriors with such a
FALSTAFF: greedy intention, that the appetite of her eye did
FALSTAFF: seem to scorch me up like a burning-glass! Here's
FALSTAFF: another letter to her: she bears the purse too, she
FALSTAFF: is a region in Guiana, all gold and bounty. I will
FALSTAFF: be cheater to them both, and they shall be
FALSTAFF: exchequers to me, they shall be my East and West
FALSTAFF: Indies, and I will trade to them both. Go bear thou
FALSTAFF: this letter to Mistress Page, and thou this to
FALSTAFF: Mistress Ford: we will thrive, lads, we will thrive.
PISTOL: Shall I Sir Pandarus of Troy become,
PISTOL: And by my side wear steel? then, Lucifer take all!
NYM: I will run no base humour: here, take the
NYM: humour-letter: I will keep the havior of reputation.
FALSTAFF: [To ROBIN]  Hold, sirrah, bear you these letters tightly,
FALSTAFF: Sail like my pinnace to these golden shores.
FALSTAFF: Rogues, hence, avaunt! vanish like hailstones, go,
FALSTAFF: Trudge, plod away o' the hoof, seek shelter, pack!
FALSTAFF: Falstaff will learn the humour of the age,
FALSTAFF: French thrift, you rogues, myself and skirted page.
NARRATOR: Exeunt FALSTAFF and ROBIN
PISTOL: Let vultures gripe thy guts! for gourd and fullam holds,
PISTOL: And high and low beguiles the rich and poor:
PISTOL: Tester I'll have in pouch when thou shalt lack,
PISTOL: Base Phrygian Turk!
NYM: I have operations which be humours of revenge.
PISTOL: Wilt thou revenge?
NYM: By welkin and her star!
PISTOL: With wit or steel?
NYM: With both the humours, I:
NYM: I will discuss the humour of this love to Page.
PISTOL: And I to Ford shall eke unfold
PISTOL: How Falstaff, varlet vile,
PISTOL: His dove will prove, his gold will hold,
PISTOL: And his soft couch defile.
NYM: My humour shall not cool: I will incense Page to
NYM: deal with poison, I will possess him with
NYM: yellowness, for the revolt of mine is dangerous:
NYM: that is my true humour.
PISTOL: Thou art the Mars of malecontents: I second thee, troop on.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. A room in DOCTOR CAIUS' house.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY, SIMPLE, and RUGBY
MISTRESS QUICKLY: What, John Rugby! I pray thee, go to the casement,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: and see if you can see my master, Master Doctor
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Caius, coming. If he do, i' faith, and find any
MISTRESS QUICKLY: body in the house, here will be an old abusing of
MISTRESS QUICKLY: God's patience and the king's English.
RUGBY: I'll go watch.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Go, and we'll have a posset for't soon at night, in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: faith, at the latter end of a sea-coal fire.
NARRATOR: Exit RUGBY
MISTRESS QUICKLY: An honest, willing, kind fellow, as ever servant
MISTRESS QUICKLY: shall come in house withal, and, I warrant you, no
MISTRESS QUICKLY: tell-tale nor no breed-bate: his worst fault is,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: that he is given to prayer, he is something peevish
MISTRESS QUICKLY: that way: but nobody but has his fault, but let
MISTRESS QUICKLY: that pass. Peter Simple, you say your name is?
SIMPLE: Ay, for fault of a better.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: And Master Slender's your master?
SIMPLE: Ay, forsooth.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Does he not wear a great round beard, like a
MISTRESS QUICKLY: glover's paring-knife?
SIMPLE: No, forsooth: he hath but a little wee face, with a
SIMPLE: little yellow beard, a Cain-coloured beard.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: A softly-sprighted man, is he not?
SIMPLE: Ay, forsooth: but he is as tall a man of his hands
SIMPLE: as any is between this and his head, he hath fought
SIMPLE: with a warrener.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: How say you? O, I should remember him: does he not
MISTRESS QUICKLY: hold up his head, as it were, and strut in his gait?
SIMPLE: Yes, indeed, does he.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Well, heaven send Anne Page no worse fortune! Tell
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Master Parson Evans I will do what I can for your
MISTRESS QUICKLY: master: Anne is a good girl, and I wish--
NARRATOR: Re-enter RUGBY
RUGBY: Out, alas! here comes my master.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: We shall all be shent. Run in here, good young man,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: go into this closet: he will not stay long.
NARRATOR: Shuts SIMPLE in the closet
MISTRESS QUICKLY: What, John Rugby! John! what, John, I say!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Go, John, go inquire for my master, I doubt
MISTRESS QUICKLY: he be not well, that he comes not home.
NARRATOR: Singing
MISTRESS QUICKLY: And down, down, adown-a,  and c.
NARRATOR: Enter DOCTOR CAIUS
DOCTOR CAIUS: Vat is you sing? I do not like des toys. Pray you,
DOCTOR CAIUS: go and vetch me in my closet un boitier vert, a box,
DOCTOR CAIUS: a green-a box: do intend vat I speak? a green-a box.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Ay, forsooth, I'll fetch it you.
NARRATOR: Aside
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I am glad he went not in himself: if he had found
MISTRESS QUICKLY: the young man, he would have been horn-mad.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Fe, fe, fe, fe! ma foi, il fait fort chaud. Je
DOCTOR CAIUS: m'en vais a la cour--la grande affaire.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Is it this, sir?
DOCTOR CAIUS: Oui, mette le au mon pocket: depeche, quickly. Vere
DOCTOR CAIUS: is dat knave Rugby?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: What, John Rugby! John!
RUGBY: Here, sir!
DOCTOR CAIUS: You are John Rugby, and you are Jack Rugby. Come,
DOCTOR CAIUS: take-a your rapier, and come after my heel to the court.
RUGBY: 'Tis ready, sir, here in the porch.
DOCTOR CAIUS: By my trot, I tarry too long. Od's me!
DOCTOR CAIUS: Qu'ai-j'oublie! dere is some simples in my closet,
DOCTOR CAIUS: dat I vill not for the varld I shall leave behind.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Ay me, he'll find the young man here, and be mad!
DOCTOR CAIUS: O diable, diable! vat is in my closet? Villain! larron!
NARRATOR: Pulling SIMPLE out
DOCTOR CAIUS: Rugby, my rapier!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Good master, be content.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Wherefore shall I be content-a?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: The young man is an honest man.
DOCTOR CAIUS: What shall de honest man do in my closet? dere is
DOCTOR CAIUS: no honest man dat shall come in my closet.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I beseech you, be not so phlegmatic. Hear the truth
MISTRESS QUICKLY: of it: he came of an errand to me from Parson Hugh.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Vell.
SIMPLE: Ay, forsooth, to desire her to--
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Peace, I pray you.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Peace-a your tongue. Speak-a your tale.
SIMPLE: To desire this honest gentlewoman, your maid, to
SIMPLE: speak a good word to Mistress Anne Page for my
SIMPLE: master in the way of marriage.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: This is all, indeed, la! but I'll ne'er put my
MISTRESS QUICKLY: finger in the fire, and need not.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Sir Hugh send-a you? Rugby, baille me some paper.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Tarry you a little-a while.
NARRATOR: Writes
MISTRESS QUICKLY: [Aside to SIMPLE]  I am glad he is so quiet: if he
MISTRESS QUICKLY: had been thoroughly moved, you should have heard him
MISTRESS QUICKLY: so loud and so melancholy. But notwithstanding,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: man, I'll do you your master what good I can: and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: the very yea and the no is, the French doctor, my
MISTRESS QUICKLY: master,--I may call him my master, look you, for I
MISTRESS QUICKLY: keep his house, and I wash, wring, brew, bake,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: scour, dress meat and drink, make the beds and do
MISTRESS QUICKLY: all myself,--
SIMPLE: [Aside to MISTRESS QUICKLY]  'Tis a great charge to
SIMPLE: come under one body's hand.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: [Aside to SIMPLE]  Are you avised o' that? you
MISTRESS QUICKLY: shall find it a great charge: and to be up early
MISTRESS QUICKLY: and down late, but notwithstanding,--to tell you in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: your ear, I would have no words of it,--my master
MISTRESS QUICKLY: himself is in love with Mistress Anne Page: but
MISTRESS QUICKLY: notwithstanding that, I know Anne's mind,--that's
MISTRESS QUICKLY: neither here nor there.
DOCTOR CAIUS: You jack'nape, give-a this letter to Sir Hugh, by
DOCTOR CAIUS: gar, it is a shallenge: I will cut his troat in dee
DOCTOR CAIUS: park, and I will teach a scurvy jack-a-nape priest
DOCTOR CAIUS: to meddle or make. You may be gone, it is not good
DOCTOR CAIUS: you tarry here. By gar, I will cut all his two
DOCTOR CAIUS: stones, by gar, he shall not have a stone to throw
DOCTOR CAIUS: at his dog:
NARRATOR: Exit SIMPLE
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Alas, he speaks but for his friend.
DOCTOR CAIUS: It is no matter-a ver dat: do not you tell-a me
DOCTOR CAIUS: dat I shall have Anne Page for myself? By gar, I
DOCTOR CAIUS: vill kill de Jack priest, and I have appointed mine
DOCTOR CAIUS: host of de Jarteer to measure our weapon. By gar, I
DOCTOR CAIUS: will myself have Anne Page.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Sir, the maid loves you, and all shall be well. We
MISTRESS QUICKLY: must give folks leave to prate: what, the good-jer!
DOCTOR CAIUS: Rugby, come to the court with me. By gar, if I have
DOCTOR CAIUS: not Anne Page, I shall turn your head out of my
DOCTOR CAIUS: door. Follow my heels, Rugby.
NARRATOR: Exeunt DOCTOR CAIUS and RUGBY
MISTRESS QUICKLY: You shall have An fool's-head of your own. No, I
MISTRESS QUICKLY: know Anne's mind for that: never a woman in Windsor
MISTRESS QUICKLY: knows more of Anne's mind than I do, nor can do more
MISTRESS QUICKLY: than I do with her, I thank heaven.
FENTON: [Within]  Who's within there? ho!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Who's there, I trow! Come near the house, I pray you.
NARRATOR: Enter FENTON
FENTON: How now, good woman? how dost thou?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: The better that it pleases your good worship to ask.
FENTON: What news? how does pretty Mistress Anne?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: In truth, sir, and she is pretty, and honest, and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: gentle, and one that is your friend, I can tell you
MISTRESS QUICKLY: that by the way, I praise heaven for it.
FENTON: Shall I do any good, thinkest thou? shall I not lose my suit?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Troth, sir, all is in his hands above: but
MISTRESS QUICKLY: notwithstanding, Master Fenton, I'll be sworn on a
MISTRESS QUICKLY: book, she loves you. Have not your worship a wart
MISTRESS QUICKLY: above your eye?
FENTON: Yes, marry, have I, what of that?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Well, thereby hangs a tale: good faith, it is such
MISTRESS QUICKLY: another Nan, but, I detest, an honest maid as ever
MISTRESS QUICKLY: broke bread: we had an hour's talk of that wart. I
MISTRESS QUICKLY: shall never laugh but in that maid's company! But
MISTRESS QUICKLY: indeed she is given too much to allicholy and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: musing: but for you--well, go to.
FENTON: Well, I shall see her to-day. Hold, there's money
FENTON: for thee, let me have thy voice in my behalf: if
FENTON: thou seest her before me, commend me.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Will I? i'faith, that we will, and I will tell your
MISTRESS QUICKLY: worship more of the wart the next time we have
MISTRESS QUICKLY: confidence, and of other wooers.
FENTON: Well, farewell, I am in great haste now.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Farewell to your worship.
NARRATOR: Exit FENTON
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Truly, an honest gentleman: but Anne loves him not,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: for I know Anne's mind as well as another does. Out
MISTRESS QUICKLY: upon't! what have I forgot?
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: ACT II
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Before PAGE'S house.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, with a letter
MISTRESS PAGE: What, have I scaped love-letters in the holiday-
MISTRESS PAGE: time of my beauty, and am I now a subject for them?
MISTRESS PAGE: Let me see.
NARRATOR: Reads
MISTRESS PAGE: 'Ask me no reason why I love you, for though
MISTRESS PAGE: Love use Reason for his physician, he admits him
MISTRESS PAGE: not for his counsellor. You are not young, no more
MISTRESS PAGE: am I, go to then, there's sympathy: you are merry,
MISTRESS PAGE: so am I, ha, ha! then there's more sympathy: you
MISTRESS PAGE: love sack, and so do I, would you desire better
MISTRESS PAGE: sympathy? Let it suffice thee, Mistress Page,--at
MISTRESS PAGE: the least, if the love of soldier can suffice,--
MISTRESS PAGE: that I love thee. I will not say, pity me, 'tis
MISTRESS PAGE: not a soldier-like phrase: but I say, love me. By me,
MISTRESS PAGE: Thine own true knight,
MISTRESS PAGE: By day or night,
MISTRESS PAGE: Or any kind of light,
MISTRESS PAGE: With all his might
MISTRESS PAGE: For thee to fight,    JOHN FALSTAFF'
MISTRESS PAGE: What a Herod of Jewry is this! O wicked
MISTRESS PAGE: world! One that is well-nigh worn to pieces with
MISTRESS PAGE: age to show himself a young gallant! What an
MISTRESS PAGE: unweighed behavior hath this Flemish drunkard
MISTRESS PAGE: picked--with the devil's name!--out of my
MISTRESS PAGE: conversation, that he dares in this manner assay me?
MISTRESS PAGE: Why, he hath not been thrice in my company! What
MISTRESS PAGE: should I say to him? I was then frugal of my
MISTRESS PAGE: mirth: Heaven forgive me! Why, I'll exhibit a bill
MISTRESS PAGE: in the parliament for the putting down of men. How
MISTRESS PAGE: shall I be revenged on him? for revenged I will be,
MISTRESS PAGE: as sure as his guts are made of puddings.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS FORD
MISTRESS FORD: Mistress Page! trust me, I was going to your house.
MISTRESS PAGE: And, trust me, I was coming to you. You look very
MISTRESS PAGE: ill.
MISTRESS FORD: Nay, I'll ne'er believe that, I have to show to the contrary.
MISTRESS PAGE: Faith, but you do, in my mind.
MISTRESS FORD: Well, I do then, yet I say I could show you to the
MISTRESS FORD: contrary. O Mistress Page, give me some counsel!
MISTRESS PAGE: What's the matter, woman?
MISTRESS FORD: O woman, if it were not for one trifling respect, I
MISTRESS FORD: could come to such honour!
MISTRESS PAGE: Hang the trifle, woman! take the honour. What is
MISTRESS PAGE: it? dispense with trifles, what is it?
MISTRESS FORD: If I would but go to hell for an eternal moment or so,
MISTRESS FORD: I could be knighted.
MISTRESS PAGE: What? thou liest! Sir Alice Ford! These knights
MISTRESS PAGE: will hack, and so thou shouldst not alter the
MISTRESS PAGE: article of thy gentry.
MISTRESS FORD: We burn daylight: here, read, read, perceive how I
MISTRESS FORD: might be knighted. I shall think the worse of fat
MISTRESS FORD: men, as long as I have an eye to make difference of
MISTRESS FORD: men's liking: and yet he would not swear, praised
MISTRESS FORD: women's modesty, and gave such orderly and
MISTRESS FORD: well-behaved reproof to all uncomeliness, that I
MISTRESS FORD: would have sworn his disposition would have gone to
MISTRESS FORD: the truth of his words, but they do no more adhere
MISTRESS FORD: and keep place together than the Hundredth Psalm to
MISTRESS FORD: the tune of 'Green Sleeves.' What tempest, I trow,
MISTRESS FORD: threw this whale, with so many tuns of oil in his
MISTRESS FORD: belly, ashore at Windsor? How shall I be revenged
MISTRESS FORD: on him? I think the best way were to entertain him
MISTRESS FORD: with hope, till the wicked fire of lust have melted
MISTRESS FORD: him in his own grease. Did you ever hear the like?
MISTRESS PAGE: Letter for letter, but that the name of Page and
MISTRESS PAGE: Ford differs! To thy great comfort in this mystery
MISTRESS PAGE: of ill opinions, here's the twin-brother of thy
MISTRESS PAGE: letter: but let thine inherit first, for, I
MISTRESS PAGE: protest, mine never shall. I warrant he hath a
MISTRESS PAGE: thousand of these letters, writ with blank space for
MISTRESS PAGE: different names--sure, more,--and these are of the
MISTRESS PAGE: second edition: he will print them, out of doubt,
MISTRESS PAGE: for he cares not what he puts into the press, when
MISTRESS PAGE: he would put us two. I had rather be a giantess,
MISTRESS PAGE: and lie under Mount Pelion. Well, I will find you
MISTRESS PAGE: twenty lascivious turtles ere one chaste man.
MISTRESS FORD: Why, this is the very same, the very hand, the very
MISTRESS FORD: words. What doth he think of us?
MISTRESS PAGE: Nay, I know not: it makes me almost ready to
MISTRESS PAGE: wrangle with mine own honesty. I'll entertain
MISTRESS PAGE: myself like one that I am not acquainted withal,
MISTRESS PAGE: for, sure, unless he know some strain in me, that I
MISTRESS PAGE: know not myself, he would never have boarded me in this fury.
MISTRESS FORD: 'Boarding,' call you it? I'll be sure to keep him
MISTRESS FORD: above deck.
MISTRESS PAGE: So will I	if he come under my hatches, I'll never
MISTRESS PAGE: to sea again. Let's be revenged on him: let's
MISTRESS PAGE: appoint him a meeting, give him a show of comfort in
MISTRESS PAGE: his suit and lead him on with a fine-baited delay,
MISTRESS PAGE: till he hath pawned his horses to mine host of the Garter.
MISTRESS FORD: Nay, I will consent to act any villany against him,
MISTRESS FORD: that may not sully the chariness of our honesty. O,
MISTRESS FORD: that my husband saw this letter! it would give
MISTRESS FORD: eternal food to his jealousy.
MISTRESS PAGE: Why, look where he comes, and my good man too: he's
MISTRESS PAGE: as far from jealousy as I am from giving him cause,
MISTRESS PAGE: and that I hope is an unmeasurable distance.
MISTRESS FORD: You are the happier woman.
MISTRESS PAGE: Let's consult together against this greasy knight.
MISTRESS PAGE: Come hither.
NARRATOR: They retire
NARRATOR: Enter FORD with PISTOL, and PAGE with NYM
FORD: Well, I hope it be not so.
PISTOL: Hope is a curtal dog in some affairs:
PISTOL: Sir John affects thy wife.
FORD: Why, sir, my wife is not young.
PISTOL: He wooes both high and low, both rich and poor,
PISTOL: Both young and old, one with another, Ford,
PISTOL: He loves the gallimaufry: Ford, perpend.
FORD: Love my wife!
PISTOL: With liver burning hot. Prevent, or go thou,
PISTOL: Like Sir Actaeon he, with Ringwood at thy heels:
PISTOL: O, odious is the name!
FORD: What name, sir?
PISTOL: The horn, I say. Farewell.
PISTOL: Take heed, have open eye, for thieves do foot by night:
PISTOL: Take heed, ere summer comes or cuckoo-birds do sing.
PISTOL: Away, Sir Corporal Nym!
PISTOL: Believe it, Page, he speaks sense.
NARRATOR: Exit
FORD: [Aside]  I will be patient, I will find out this.
NYM: [To PAGE]  And this is true, I like not the humour
NYM: of lying. He hath wronged me in some humours: I
NYM: should have borne the humoured letter to her, but I
NYM: have a sword and it shall bite upon my necessity.
NYM: He loves your wife, there's the short and the long.
NYM: My name is Corporal Nym, I speak and I avouch, 'tis
NYM: true: my name is Nym and Falstaff loves your wife.
NYM: Adieu. I love not the humour of bread and cheese,
NYM: and there's the humour of it. Adieu.
NARRATOR: Exit
PAGE: 'The humour of it,' quoth a'! here's a fellow
PAGE: frights English out of his wits.
FORD: I will seek out Falstaff.
PAGE: I never heard such a drawling, affecting rogue.
FORD: If I do find it: well.
PAGE: I will not believe such a Cataian, though the priest
PAGE: o' the town commended him for a true man.
FORD: 'Twas a good sensible fellow: well.
PAGE: How now, Meg!
NARRATOR: MISTRESS PAGE and MISTRESS FORD come forward
MISTRESS PAGE: Whither go you, George? Hark you.
MISTRESS FORD: How now, sweet Frank! why art thou melancholy?
FORD: I melancholy! I am not melancholy. Get you home, go.
MISTRESS FORD: Faith, thou hast some crotchets in thy head. Now,
MISTRESS FORD: will you go, Mistress Page?
MISTRESS PAGE: Have with you. You'll come to dinner, George.
NARRATOR: Aside to MISTRESS FORD
MISTRESS PAGE: Look who comes yonder: she shall be our messenger
MISTRESS PAGE: to this paltry knight.
MISTRESS FORD: [Aside to MISTRESS PAGE]  Trust me, I thought on her:
MISTRESS FORD: she'll fit it.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY
MISTRESS PAGE: You are come to see my daughter Anne?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Ay, forsooth, and, I pray, how does good Mistress Anne?
MISTRESS PAGE: Go in with us and see: we have an hour's talk with
MISTRESS PAGE: you.
NARRATOR: Exeunt MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and MISTRESS QUICKLY
PAGE: How now, Master Ford!
FORD: You heard what this knave told me, did you not?
PAGE: Yes: and you heard what the other told me?
FORD: Do you think there is truth in them?
PAGE: Hang 'em, slaves! I do not think the knight would
PAGE: offer it: but these that accuse him in his intent
PAGE: towards our wives are a yoke of his discarded men,
PAGE: very rogues, now they be out of service.
FORD: Were they his men?
PAGE: Marry, were they.
FORD: I like it never the better for that. Does he lie at
FORD: the Garter?
PAGE: Ay, marry, does he. If he should intend this voyage
PAGE: towards my wife, I would turn her loose to him, and
PAGE: what he gets more of her than sharp words, let it
PAGE: lie on my head.
FORD: I do not misdoubt my wife, but I would be loath to
FORD: turn them together. A man may be too confident: I
FORD: would have nothing lie on my head: I cannot be thus satisfied.
PAGE: Look where my ranting host of the Garter comes:
PAGE: there is either liquor in his pate or money in his
PAGE: purse when he looks so merrily.
NARRATOR: Enter Host
PAGE: How now, mine host!
Host: How now, bully-rook! thou'rt a gentleman.
Host: Cavaleiro-justice, I say!
NARRATOR: Enter SHALLOW
SHALLOW: I follow, mine host, I follow. Good even and
SHALLOW: twenty, good Master Page! Master Page, will you go
SHALLOW: with us? we have sport in hand.
Host: Tell him, cavaleiro-justice, tell him, bully-rook.
SHALLOW: Sir, there is a fray to be fought between Sir Hugh
SHALLOW: the Welsh priest and Caius the French doctor.
FORD: Good mine host o' the Garter, a word with you.
NARRATOR: Drawing him aside
Host: What sayest thou, my bully-rook?
SHALLOW: [To PAGE]  Will you go with us to behold it? My
SHALLOW: merry host hath had the measuring of their weapons,
SHALLOW: and, I think, hath appointed them contrary places,
SHALLOW: for, believe me, I hear the parson is no jester.
SHALLOW: Hark, I will tell you what our sport shall be.
NARRATOR: They converse apart
Host: Hast thou no suit against my knight, my
Host: guest-cavaleire?
FORD: None, I protest: but I'll give you a pottle of
FORD: burnt sack to give me recourse to him and tell him
FORD: my name is Brook, only for a jest.
Host: My hand, bully, thou shalt have egress and regress,
Host: --said I well?--and thy name shall be Brook. It is
Host: a merry knight. Will you go, An-heires?
SHALLOW: Have with you, mine host.
PAGE: I have heard the Frenchman hath good skill in
PAGE: his rapier.
SHALLOW: Tut, sir, I could have told you more. In these times
SHALLOW: you stand on distance, your passes, stoccadoes, and
SHALLOW: I know not what: 'tis the heart, Master Page, 'tis
SHALLOW: here, 'tis here. I have seen the time, with my long
SHALLOW: sword I would have made you four tall fellows skip like rats.
Host: Here, boys, here, here! shall we wag?
PAGE: Have with you. I would rather hear them scold than fight.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Host, SHALLOW, and PAGE
FORD: Though Page be a secure fool, an stands so firmly
FORD: on his wife's frailty, yet I cannot put off my
FORD: opinion so easily: she was in his company at Page's
FORD: house, and what they made there, I know not. Well,
FORD: I will look further into't: and I have a disguise
FORD: to sound Falstaff. If I find her honest, I lose not
FORD: my labour, if she be otherwise, 'tis labour well bestowed.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE II. A room in the Garter Inn.
NARRATOR: Enter FALSTAFF and PISTOL
FALSTAFF: I will not lend thee a penny.
PISTOL: Why, then the world's mine oyster.
PISTOL: Which I with sword will open.
FALSTAFF: Not a penny. I have been content, sir, you should
FALSTAFF: lay my countenance to pawn, I have grated upon my
FALSTAFF: good friends for three reprieves for you and your
FALSTAFF: coach-fellow Nym, or else you had looked through
FALSTAFF: the grate, like a geminy of baboons. I am damned in
FALSTAFF: hell for swearing to gentlemen my friends, you were
FALSTAFF: good soldiers and tall fellows, and when Mistress
FALSTAFF: Bridget lost the handle of her fan, I took't upon
FALSTAFF: mine honour thou hadst it not.
PISTOL: Didst not thou share? hadst thou not fifteen pence?
FALSTAFF: Reason, you rogue, reason: thinkest thou I'll
FALSTAFF: endanger my soul gratis? At a word, hang no more
FALSTAFF: about me, I am no gibbet for you. Go. A short knife
FALSTAFF: and a throng! To your manor of Pickt-hatch! Go.
FALSTAFF: You'll not bear a letter for me, you rogue! you
FALSTAFF: stand upon your honour! Why, thou unconfinable
FALSTAFF: baseness, it is as much as I can do to keep the
FALSTAFF: terms of my honour precise: I, I, I myself
FALSTAFF: sometimes, leaving the fear of God on the left hand
FALSTAFF: and hiding mine honour in my necessity, am fain to
FALSTAFF: shuffle, to hedge and to lurch, and yet you, rogue,
FALSTAFF: will ensconce your rags, your cat-a-mountain
FALSTAFF: looks, your red-lattice phrases, and your
FALSTAFF: bold-beating oaths, under the shelter of your
FALSTAFF: honour! You will not do it, you!
PISTOL: I do relent: what would thou more of man?
NARRATOR: Enter ROBIN
ROBIN: Sir, here's a woman would speak with you.
FALSTAFF: Let her approach.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Give your worship good morrow.
FALSTAFF: Good morrow, good wife.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Not so, an't please your worship.
FALSTAFF: Good maid, then.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I'll be sworn,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: As my mother was, the first hour I was born.
FALSTAFF: I do believe the swearer. What with me?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Shall I vouchsafe your worship a word or two?
FALSTAFF: Two thousand, fair woman: and I'll vouchsafe thee
FALSTAFF: the hearing.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: There is one Mistress Ford, sir:--I pray, come a
MISTRESS QUICKLY: little nearer this ways:--I myself dwell with master
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Doctor Caius,--
FALSTAFF: Well, on: Mistress Ford, you say,--
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Your worship says very true: I pray your worship,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: come a little nearer this ways.
FALSTAFF: I warrant thee, nobody hears, mine own people, mine
FALSTAFF: own people.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Are they so? God bless them and make them his servants!
FALSTAFF: Well, Mistress Ford, what of her?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Why, sir, she's a good creature. Lord Lord! your
MISTRESS QUICKLY: worship's a wanton! Well, heaven forgive you and all
MISTRESS QUICKLY: of us, I pray!
FALSTAFF: Mistress Ford, come, Mistress Ford,--
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Marry, this is the short and the long of it, you
MISTRESS QUICKLY: have brought her into such a canaries as 'tis
MISTRESS QUICKLY: wonderful. The best courtier of them all, when the
MISTRESS QUICKLY: court lay at Windsor, could never have brought her
MISTRESS QUICKLY: to such a canary. Yet there has been knights, and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: lords, and gentlemen, with their coaches, I warrant
MISTRESS QUICKLY: you, coach after coach, letter after letter, gift
MISTRESS QUICKLY: after gift, smelling so sweetly, all musk, and so
MISTRESS QUICKLY: rushling, I warrant you, in silk and gold, and in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: such alligant terms, and in such wine and sugar of
MISTRESS QUICKLY: the best and the fairest, that would have won any
MISTRESS QUICKLY: woman's heart, and, I warrant you, they could never
MISTRESS QUICKLY: get an eye-wink of her: I had myself twenty angels
MISTRESS QUICKLY: given me this morning, but I defy all angels, in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: any such sort, as they say, but in the way of
MISTRESS QUICKLY: honesty: and, I warrant you, they could never get
MISTRESS QUICKLY: her so much as sip on a cup with the proudest of
MISTRESS QUICKLY: them all: and yet there has been earls, nay, which
MISTRESS QUICKLY: is more, pensioners, but, I warrant you, all is one with her.
FALSTAFF: But what says she to me? be brief, my good
FALSTAFF: she-Mercury.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Marry, she hath received your letter, for the which
MISTRESS QUICKLY: she thanks you a thousand times, and she gives you
MISTRESS QUICKLY: to notify that her husband will be absence from his
MISTRESS QUICKLY: house between ten and eleven.
FALSTAFF: Ten and eleven?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Ay, forsooth, and then you may come and see the
MISTRESS QUICKLY: picture, she says, that you wot of: Master Ford,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: her husband, will be from home. Alas! the sweet
MISTRESS QUICKLY: woman leads an ill life with him: he's a very
MISTRESS QUICKLY: jealousy man: she leads a very frampold life with
MISTRESS QUICKLY: him, good heart.
FALSTAFF: Ten and eleven. Woman, commend me to her, I will
FALSTAFF: not fail her.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Why, you say well. But I have another messenger to
MISTRESS QUICKLY: your worship. Mistress Page hath her hearty
MISTRESS QUICKLY: commendations to you too: and let me tell you in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: your ear, she's as fartuous a civil modest wife, and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: one, I tell you, that will not miss you morning nor
MISTRESS QUICKLY: evening prayer, as any is in Windsor, whoe'er be the
MISTRESS QUICKLY: other: and she bade me tell your worship that her
MISTRESS QUICKLY: husband is seldom from home, but she hopes there
MISTRESS QUICKLY: will come a time. I never knew a woman so dote upon
MISTRESS QUICKLY: a man: surely I think you have charms, la, yes, in truth.
FALSTAFF: Not I, I assure thee: setting the attractions of my
FALSTAFF: good parts aside I have no other charms.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Blessing on your heart for't!
FALSTAFF: But, I pray thee, tell me this: has Ford's wife and
FALSTAFF: Page's wife acquainted each other how they love me?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: That were a jest indeed! they have not so little
MISTRESS QUICKLY: grace, I hope: that were a trick indeed! but
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Mistress Page would desire you to send her your
MISTRESS QUICKLY: little page, of all loves: her husband has a
MISTRESS QUICKLY: marvellous infection to the little page, and truly
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Master Page is an honest man. Never a wife in
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Windsor leads a better life than she does: do what
MISTRESS QUICKLY: she will, say what she will, take all, pay all, go
MISTRESS QUICKLY: to bed when she list, rise when she list, all is as
MISTRESS QUICKLY: she will: and truly she deserves it, for if there
MISTRESS QUICKLY: be a kind woman in Windsor, she is one. You must
MISTRESS QUICKLY: send her your page, no remedy.
FALSTAFF: Why, I will.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Nay, but do so, then: and, look you, he may come and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: go between you both, and in any case have a
MISTRESS QUICKLY: nay-word, that you may know one another's mind, and
MISTRESS QUICKLY: the boy never need to understand any thing, for
MISTRESS QUICKLY: 'tis not good that children should know any
MISTRESS QUICKLY: wickedness: old folks, you know, have discretion,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: as they say, and know the world.
FALSTAFF: Fare thee well: commend me to them both: there's
FALSTAFF: my purse, I am yet thy debtor. Boy, go along with
FALSTAFF: this woman.
NARRATOR: Exeunt MISTRESS QUICKLY and ROBIN
FALSTAFF: This news distracts me!
PISTOL: This punk is one of Cupid's carriers:
PISTOL: Clap on more sails, pursue, up with your fights:
PISTOL: Give fire: she is my prize, or ocean whelm them all!
NARRATOR: Exit
FALSTAFF: Sayest thou so, old Jack? go thy ways, I'll make
FALSTAFF: more of thy old body than I have done. Will they
FALSTAFF: yet look after thee? Wilt thou, after the expense
FALSTAFF: of so much money, be now a gainer? Good body, I
FALSTAFF: thank thee. Let them say 'tis grossly done, so it be
FALSTAFF: fairly done, no matter.
NARRATOR: Enter BARDOLPH
BARDOLPH: Sir John, there's one Master Brook below would fain
BARDOLPH: speak with you, and be acquainted with you, and hath
BARDOLPH: sent your worship a morning's draught of sack.
FALSTAFF: Brook is his name?
BARDOLPH: Ay, sir.
FALSTAFF: Call him in.
NARRATOR: Exit BARDOLPH
FALSTAFF: Such Brooks are welcome to me, that o'erflow such
FALSTAFF: liquor. Ah, ha! Mistress Ford and Mistress Page
FALSTAFF: have I encompassed you? go to, via!
NARRATOR: Re-enter BARDOLPH, with FORD disguised
FORD: Bless you, sir!
FALSTAFF: And you, sir! Would you speak with me?
FORD: I make bold to press with so little preparation upon
FORD: you.
FALSTAFF: You're welcome. What's your will? Give us leave, drawer.
NARRATOR: Exit BARDOLPH
FORD: Sir, I am a gentleman that have spent much, my name is Brook.
FALSTAFF: Good Master Brook, I desire more acquaintance of you.
FORD: Good Sir John, I sue for yours: not to charge you,
FORD: for I must let you understand I think myself in
FORD: better plight for a lender than you are: the which
FORD: hath something embolden'd me to this unseasoned
FORD: intrusion, for they say, if money go before, all
FORD: ways do lie open.
FALSTAFF: Money is a good soldier, sir, and will on.
FORD: Troth, and I have a bag of money here troubles me:
FORD: if you will help to bear it, Sir John, take all, or
FORD: half, for easing me of the carriage.
FALSTAFF: Sir, I know not how I may deserve to be your porter.
FORD: I will tell you, sir, if you will give me the hearing.
FALSTAFF: Speak, good Master Brook: I shall be glad to be
FALSTAFF: your servant.
FORD: Sir, I hear you are a scholar,--I will be brief
FORD: with you,--and you have been a man long known to me,
FORD: though I had never so good means, as desire, to make
FORD: myself acquainted with you. I shall discover a
FORD: thing to you, wherein I must very much lay open mine
FORD: own imperfection: but, good Sir John, as you have
FORD: one eye upon my follies, as you hear them unfolded,
FORD: turn another into the register of your own, that I
FORD: may pass with a reproof the easier, sith you
FORD: yourself know how easy it is to be such an offender.
FALSTAFF: Very well, sir, proceed.
FORD: There is a gentlewoman in this town, her husband's
FORD: name is Ford.
FALSTAFF: Well, sir.
FORD: I have long loved her, and, I protest to you,
FORD: bestowed much on her, followed her with a doting
FORD: observance, engrossed opportunities to meet her,
FORD: fee'd every slight occasion that could but niggardly
FORD: give me sight of her, not only bought many presents
FORD: to give her, but have given largely to many to know
FORD: what she would have given, briefly, I have pursued
FORD: her as love hath pursued me, which hath been on the
FORD: wing of all occasions. But whatsoever I have
FORD: merited, either in my mind or, in my means, meed,
FORD: I am sure, I have received none, unless experience
FORD: be a jewel that I have purchased at an infinite
FORD: rate, and that hath taught me to say this:
FORD: 'Love like a shadow flies when substance love pursues,
FORD: Pursuing that that flies, and flying what pursues.'
FALSTAFF: Have you received no promise of satisfaction at her hands?
FORD: Never.
FALSTAFF: Have you importuned her to such a purpose?
FORD: Never.
FALSTAFF: Of what quality was your love, then?
FORD: Like a fair house built on another man's ground, so
FORD: that I have lost my edifice by mistaking the place
FORD: where I erected it.
FALSTAFF: To what purpose have you unfolded this to me?
FORD: When I have told you that, I have told you all.
FORD: Some say, that though she appear honest to me, yet in
FORD: other places she enlargeth her mirth so far that
FORD: there is shrewd construction made of her. Now, Sir
FORD: John, here is the heart of my purpose: you are a
FORD: gentleman of excellent breeding, admirable
FORD: discourse, of great admittance, authentic in your
FORD: place and person, generally allowed for your many
FORD: war-like, court-like, and learned preparations.
FALSTAFF: O, sir!
FORD: Believe it, for you know it. There is money, spend
FORD: it, spend it, spend more, spend all I have, only
FORD: give me so much of your time in exchange of it, as
FORD: to lay an amiable siege to the honesty of this
FORD: Ford's wife: use your art of wooing, win her to
FORD: consent to you: if any man may, you may as soon as
FORD: any.
FALSTAFF: Would it apply well to the vehemency of your
FALSTAFF: affection, that I should win what you would enjoy?
FALSTAFF: Methinks you prescribe to yourself very preposterously.
FORD: O, understand my drift. She dwells so securely on
FORD: the excellency of her honour, that the folly of my
FORD: soul dares not present itself: she is too bright to
FORD: be looked against. Now, could I could come to her
FORD: with any detection in my hand, my desires had
FORD: instance and argument to commend themselves: I
FORD: could drive her then from the ward of her purity,
FORD: her reputation, her marriage-vow, and a thousand
FORD: other her defences, which now are too too strongly
FORD: embattled against me. What say you to't, Sir John?
FALSTAFF: Master Brook, I will first make bold with your
FALSTAFF: money, next, give me your hand, and last, as I am a
FALSTAFF: gentleman, you shall, if you will, enjoy Ford's wife.
FORD: O good sir!
FALSTAFF: I say you shall.
FORD: Want no money, Sir John, you shall want none.
FALSTAFF: Want no Mistress Ford, Master Brook, you shall want
FALSTAFF: none. I shall be with her, I may tell you, by her
FALSTAFF: own appointment, even as you came in to me, her
FALSTAFF: assistant or go-between parted from me: I say I
FALSTAFF: shall be with her between ten and eleven, for at
FALSTAFF: that time the jealous rascally knave her husband
FALSTAFF: will be forth. Come you to me at night, you shall
FALSTAFF: know how I speed.
FORD: I am blest in your acquaintance. Do you know Ford,
FORD: sir?
FALSTAFF: Hang him, poor cuckoldly knave! I know him not:
FALSTAFF: yet I wrong him to call him poor, they say the
FALSTAFF: jealous wittolly knave hath masses of money, for the
FALSTAFF: which his wife seems to me well-favored. I will
FALSTAFF: use her as the key of the cuckoldly rogue's coffer,
FALSTAFF: and there's my harvest-home.
FORD: I would you knew Ford, sir, that you might avoid him
FORD: if you saw him.
FALSTAFF: Hang him, mechanical salt-butter rogue! I will
FALSTAFF: stare him out of his wits, I will awe him with my
FALSTAFF: cudgel: it shall hang like a meteor o'er the
FALSTAFF: cuckold's horns. Master Brook, thou shalt know I
FALSTAFF: will predominate over the peasant, and thou shalt
FALSTAFF: lie with his wife. Come to me soon at night.
FALSTAFF: Ford's a knave, and I will aggravate his style,
FALSTAFF: thou, Master Brook, shalt know him for knave and
FALSTAFF: cuckold. Come to me soon at night.
NARRATOR: Exit
FORD: What a damned Epicurean rascal is this! My heart is
FORD: ready to crack with impatience. Who says this is
FORD: improvident jealousy? my wife hath sent to him, the
FORD: hour is fixed, the match is made. Would any man
FORD: have thought this? See the hell of having a false
FORD: woman! My bed shall be abused, my coffers
FORD: ransacked, my reputation gnawn at, and I shall not
FORD: only receive this villanous wrong, but stand under
FORD: the adoption of abominable terms, and by him that
FORD: does me this wrong. Terms! names! Amaimon sounds
FORD: well, Lucifer, well, Barbason, well, yet they are
FORD: devils' additions, the names of fiends: but
FORD: Cuckold! Wittol!--Cuckold! the devil himself hath
FORD: not such a name. Page is an ass, a secure ass: he
FORD: will trust his wife, he will not be jealous. I will
FORD: rather trust a Fleming with my butter, Parson Hugh
FORD: the Welshman with my cheese, an Irishman with my
FORD: aqua-vitae bottle, or a thief to walk my ambling
FORD: gelding, than my wife with herself, then she plots,
FORD: then she ruminates, then she devises, and what they
FORD: think in their hearts they may effect, they will
FORD: break their hearts but they will effect. God be
FORD: praised for my jealousy! Eleven o'clock the hour.
FORD: I will prevent this, detect my wife, be revenged on
FORD: Falstaff, and laugh at Page. I will about it,
FORD: better three hours too soon than a minute too late.
FORD: Fie, fie, fie! cuckold! cuckold! cuckold!
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A field near Windsor.
NARRATOR: Enter DOCTOR CAIUS and RUGBY
DOCTOR CAIUS: Jack Rugby!
RUGBY: Sir?
DOCTOR CAIUS: Vat is de clock, Jack?
RUGBY: 'Tis past the hour, sir, that Sir Hugh promised to meet.
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, he has save his soul, dat he is no come, he
DOCTOR CAIUS: has pray his Pible well, dat he is no come: by gar,
DOCTOR CAIUS: Jack Rugby, he is dead already, if he be come.
RUGBY: He is wise, sir, he knew your worship would kill
RUGBY: him, if he came.
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, de herring is no dead so as I vill kill him.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Take your rapier, Jack, I vill tell you how I vill kill him.
RUGBY: Alas, sir, I cannot fence.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Villany, take your rapier.
RUGBY: Forbear, here's company.
NARRATOR: Enter Host, SHALLOW, SLENDER, and PAGE
Host: Bless thee, bully doctor!
SHALLOW: Save you, Master Doctor Caius!
PAGE: Now, good master doctor!
SLENDER: Give you good morrow, sir.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Vat be all you, one, two, tree, four, come for?
Host: To see thee fight, to see thee foin, to see thee
Host: traverse, to see thee here, to see thee there, to
Host: see thee pass thy punto, thy stock, thy reverse, thy
Host: distance, thy montant. Is he dead, my Ethiopian? is
Host: he dead, my Francisco? ha, bully! What says my
Host: AEsculapius? my Galen? my heart of elder? ha! is
Host: he dead, bully stale? is he dead?
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, he is de coward Jack priest of de vorld, he
DOCTOR CAIUS: is not show his face.
Host: Thou art a Castalion-King-Urinal. Hector of Greece, my boy!
DOCTOR CAIUS: I pray you, bear vitness that me have stay six or
DOCTOR CAIUS: seven, two, tree hours for him, and he is no come.
SHALLOW: He is the wiser man, master doctor: he is a curer of
SHALLOW: souls, and you a curer of bodies, if you should
SHALLOW: fight, you go against the hair of your professions.
SHALLOW: Is it not true, Master Page?
PAGE: Master Shallow, you have yourself been a great
PAGE: fighter, though now a man of peace.
SHALLOW: Bodykins, Master Page, though I now be old and of
SHALLOW: the peace, if I see a sword out, my finger itches to
SHALLOW: make one. Though we are justices and doctors and
SHALLOW: churchmen, Master Page, we have some salt of our
SHALLOW: youth in us, we are the sons of women, Master Page.
PAGE: 'Tis true, Master Shallow.
SHALLOW: It will be found so, Master Page. Master Doctor
SHALLOW: Caius, I am come to fetch you home. I am sworn of
SHALLOW: the peace: you have showed yourself a wise
SHALLOW: physician, and Sir Hugh hath shown himself a wise
SHALLOW: and patient churchman. You must go with me, master doctor.
Host: Pardon, guest-justice. A word, Mounseur Mockwater.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Mock-vater! vat is dat?
Host: Mock-water, in our English tongue, is valour, bully.
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, den, I have as mush mock-vater as de
DOCTOR CAIUS: Englishman. Scurvy jack-dog priest! by gar, me
DOCTOR CAIUS: vill cut his ears.
Host: He will clapper-claw thee tightly, bully.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Clapper-de-claw! vat is dat?
Host: That is, he will make thee amends.
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, me do look he shall clapper-de-claw me,
DOCTOR CAIUS: for, by gar, me vill have it.
Host: And I will provoke him to't, or let him wag.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Me tank you for dat.
Host: And, moreover, bully,--but first, master guest, and
Host: Master Page, and eke Cavaleiro Slender, go you
Host: through the town to Frogmore.
NARRATOR: Aside to them
PAGE: Sir Hugh is there, is he?
Host: He is there: see what humour he is in, and I will
Host: bring the doctor about by the fields. Will it do well?
SHALLOW: We will do it.
SLENDER: Adieu, good master doctor.
NARRATOR: Exeunt PAGE, SHALLOW, and SLENDER
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, me vill kill de priest, for he speak for a
DOCTOR CAIUS: jack-an-ape to Anne Page.
Host: Let him die: sheathe thy impatience, throw cold
Host: water on thy choler: go about the fields with me
Host: through Frogmore: I will bring thee where Mistress
Host: Anne Page is, at a farm-house a-feasting, and thou
Host: shalt woo her. Cried I aim? said I well?
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, me dank you for dat: by gar, I love you,
DOCTOR CAIUS: and I shall procure-a you de good guest, de earl,
DOCTOR CAIUS: de knight, de lords, de gentlemen, my patients.
Host: For the which I will be thy adversary toward Anne
Host: Page. Said I well?
DOCTOR CAIUS: By gar, 'tis good, vell said.
Host: Let us wag, then.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Come at my heels, Jack Rugby.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A field near Frogmore.

PAGE: to breakfast: after, we'll a-birding together, I
PAGE: have a fine hawk for the bush. Shall it be so?
FORD: Any thing.
SIR HUGH EVANS: If there is one, I shall make two in the company.
DOCTOR CAIUS: If dere be one or two, I shall make-a the turd.
FORD: Pray you, go, Master Page.
SIR HUGH EVANS: I pray you now, remembrance tomorrow on the lousy
SIR HUGH EVANS: knave, mine host.
DOCTOR CAIUS: Dat is good, by gar, with all my heart!
SIR HUGH EVANS: A lousy knave, to have his gibes and his mockeries!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. A room in PAGE'S house.
NARRATOR: Enter FENTON and ANNE PAGE
FENTON: I see I cannot get thy father's love,
FENTON: Therefore no more turn me to him, sweet Nan.
ANNE PAGE: Alas, how then?
FENTON: Why, thou must be thyself.
FENTON: He doth object I am too great of birth--,
FENTON: And that, my state being gall'd with my expense,
FENTON: I seek to heal it only by his wealth:
FENTON: Besides these, other bars he lays before me,
FENTON: My riots past, my wild societies,
FENTON: And tells me 'tis a thing impossible
FENTON: I should love thee but as a property.
ANNE PAGE: May be he tells you true.
FENTON: No, heaven so speed me in my time to come!
FENTON: Albeit I will confess thy father's wealth
FENTON: Was the first motive that I woo'd thee, Anne:
FENTON: Yet, wooing thee, I found thee of more value
FENTON: Than stamps in gold or sums in sealed bags,
FENTON: And 'tis the very riches of thyself
FENTON: That now I aim at.
ANNE PAGE: Gentle Master Fenton,
ANNE PAGE: Yet seek my father's love, still seek it, sir:
ANNE PAGE: If opportunity and humblest suit
ANNE PAGE: Cannot attain it, why, then,--hark you hither!
NARRATOR: They converse apart
NARRATOR: Enter SHALLOW, SLENDER, and MISTRESS QUICKLY
SHALLOW: Break their talk, Mistress Quickly: my kinsman shall
SHALLOW: speak for himself.
SLENDER: I'll make a shaft or a bolt on't: 'slid, 'tis but
SLENDER: venturing.
SHALLOW: Be not dismayed.
SLENDER: No, she shall not dismay me: I care not for that,
SLENDER: but that I am afeard.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Hark ye, Master Slender would speak a word with you.
ANNE PAGE: I come to him.
NARRATOR: Aside
ANNE PAGE: This is my father's choice.
ANNE PAGE: O, what a world of vile ill-favor'd faults
ANNE PAGE: Looks handsome in three hundred pounds a-year!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: And how does good Master Fenton? Pray you, a word with you.
SHALLOW: She's coming, to her, coz. O boy, thou hadst a father!
SLENDER: I had a father, Mistress Anne, my uncle can tell you
SLENDER: good jests of him. Pray you, uncle, tell Mistress
SLENDER: Anne the jest, how my father stole two geese out of
SLENDER: a pen, good uncle.
SHALLOW: Mistress Anne, my cousin loves you.
SLENDER: Ay, that I do, as well as I love any woman in
SLENDER: Gloucestershire.
SHALLOW: He will maintain you like a gentlewoman.
SLENDER: Ay, that I will, come cut and long-tail, under the
SLENDER: degree of a squire.
SHALLOW: He will make you a hundred and fifty pounds jointure.
ANNE PAGE: Good Master Shallow, let him woo for himself.
SHALLOW: Marry, I thank you for it, I thank you for that good
SHALLOW: comfort. She calls you, coz: I'll leave you.
ANNE PAGE: Now, Master Slender,--
SLENDER: Now, good Mistress Anne,--
ANNE PAGE: What is your will?
SLENDER: My will! 'od's heartlings, that's a pretty jest
SLENDER: indeed! I ne'er made my will yet, I thank heaven, I
SLENDER: am not such a sickly creature, I give heaven praise.
ANNE PAGE: I mean, Master Slender, what would you with me?
SLENDER: Truly, for mine own part, I would little or nothing
SLENDER: with you. Your father and my uncle hath made
SLENDER: motions: if it be my luck, so, if not, happy man be
SLENDER: his dole! They can tell you how things go better
SLENDER: than I can: you may ask your father, here he comes.
NARRATOR: Enter PAGE and MISTRESS PAGE
PAGE: Now, Master Slender: love him, daughter Anne.
PAGE: Why, how now! what does Master Fenton here?
PAGE: You wrong me, sir, thus still to haunt my house:
PAGE: I told you, sir, my daughter is disposed of.
FENTON: Nay, Master Page, be not impatient.
MISTRESS PAGE: Good Master Fenton, come not to my child.
PAGE: She is no match for you.
FENTON: Sir, will you hear me?
PAGE: No, good Master Fenton.
PAGE: Come, Master Shallow, come, son Slender, in.
PAGE: Knowing my mind, you wrong me, Master Fenton.
NARRATOR: Exeunt PAGE, SHALLOW, and SLENDER
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Speak to Mistress Page.
FENTON: Good Mistress Page, for that I love your daughter
FENTON: In such a righteous fashion as I do,
FENTON: Perforce, against all cheques, rebukes and manners,
FENTON: I must advance the colours of my love
FENTON: And not retire: let me have your good will.
ANNE PAGE: Good mother, do not marry me to yond fool.
MISTRESS PAGE: I mean it not, I seek you a better husband.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: That's my master, master doctor.
ANNE PAGE: Alas, I had rather be set quick i' the earth
ANNE PAGE: And bowl'd to death with turnips!
MISTRESS PAGE: Come, trouble not yourself. Good Master Fenton,
MISTRESS PAGE: I will not be your friend nor enemy:
MISTRESS PAGE: My daughter will I question how she loves you,
MISTRESS PAGE: And as I find her, so am I affected.
MISTRESS PAGE: Till then farewell, sir: she must needs go in,
MISTRESS PAGE: Her father will be angry.
FENTON: Farewell, gentle mistress: farewell, Nan.
NARRATOR: Exeunt MISTRESS PAGE and ANNE PAGE
MISTRESS QUICKLY: This is my doing, now: 'Nay,' said I, 'will you cast
MISTRESS QUICKLY: away your child on a fool, and a physician? Look on
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Master Fenton:' this is my doing.
FENTON: I thank thee, and I pray thee, once to-night
FENTON: Give my sweet Nan this ring: there's for thy pains.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Now heaven send thee good fortune!
NARRATOR: Exit FENTON
MISTRESS QUICKLY: A kind heart he hath: a woman would run through
MISTRESS QUICKLY: fire and water for such a kind heart. But yet I
MISTRESS QUICKLY: would my master had Mistress Anne, or I would
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Master Slender had her, or, in sooth, I would Master
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Fenton had her, I will do what I can for them all
MISTRESS QUICKLY: three, for so I have promised, and I'll be as good
MISTRESS QUICKLY: as my word, but speciously for Master Fenton. Well,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I must of another errand to Sir John Falstaff from
MISTRESS QUICKLY: my two mistresses: what a beast am I to slack it!
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn.
NARRATOR: Enter FALSTAFF and BARDOLPH
FALSTAFF: Bardolph, I say,--
BARDOLPH: Here, sir.
FALSTAFF: Go fetch me a quart of sack, put a toast in't.
NARRATOR: Exit BARDOLPH
FALSTAFF: Have I lived to be carried in a basket, like a
FALSTAFF: barrow of butcher's offal, and to be thrown in the
FALSTAFF: Thames? Well, if I be served such another trick,
FALSTAFF: I'll have my brains ta'en out and buttered, and give
FALSTAFF: them to a dog for a new-year's gift. The rogues
FALSTAFF: slighted me into the river with as little remorse as
FALSTAFF: they would have drowned a blind bitch's puppies,
FALSTAFF: fifteen i' the litter: and you may know by my size
FALSTAFF: that I have a kind of alacrity in sinking, if the
FALSTAFF: bottom were as deep as hell, I should down. I had
FALSTAFF: been drowned, but that the shore was shelvy and
FALSTAFF: shallow,--a death that I abhor, for the water swells
FALSTAFF: a man, and what a thing should I have been when I
FALSTAFF: had been swelled! I should have been a mountain of mummy.
NARRATOR: Re-enter BARDOLPH with sack
BARDOLPH: Here's Mistress Quickly, sir, to speak with you.
FALSTAFF: Let me pour in some sack to the Thames water, for my
FALSTAFF: belly's as cold as if I had swallowed snowballs for
FALSTAFF: pills to cool the reins. Call her in.
BARDOLPH: Come in, woman!
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY
MISTRESS QUICKLY: By your leave, I cry you mercy: give your worship
MISTRESS QUICKLY: good morrow.
FALSTAFF: Take away these chalices. Go brew me a pottle of
FALSTAFF: sack finely.
BARDOLPH: With eggs, sir?
FALSTAFF: Simple of itself, I'll no pullet-sperm in my brewage.
NARRATOR: Exit BARDOLPH
FALSTAFF: How now!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Marry, sir, I come to your worship from Mistress Ford.
FALSTAFF: Mistress Ford! I have had ford enough, I was thrown
FALSTAFF: into the ford, I have my belly full of ford.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Alas the day! good heart, that was not her fault:
MISTRESS QUICKLY: she does so take on with her men, they mistook their erection.
FALSTAFF: So did I mine, to build upon a foolish woman's promise.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Well, she laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn
MISTRESS QUICKLY: your heart to see it. Her husband goes this morning
MISTRESS QUICKLY: a-birding, she desires you once more to come to her
MISTRESS QUICKLY: between eight and nine: I must carry her word
MISTRESS QUICKLY: quickly: she'll make you amends, I warrant you.
FALSTAFF: Well, I will visit her: tell her so, and bid her
FALSTAFF: think what a man is: let her consider his frailty,
FALSTAFF: and then judge of my merit.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I will tell her.
FALSTAFF: Do so. Between nine and ten, sayest thou?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Eight and nine, sir.
FALSTAFF: Well, be gone: I will not miss her.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Peace be with you, sir.
NARRATOR: Exit
FALSTAFF: I marvel I hear not of Master Brook, he sent me word
FALSTAFF: to stay within: I like his money well. O, here he comes.
NARRATOR: Enter FORD
FORD: Bless you, sir!
FALSTAFF: Now, master Brook, you come to know what hath passed
FALSTAFF: between me and Ford's wife?
FORD: That, indeed, Sir John, is my business.
FALSTAFF: Master Brook, I will not lie to you: I was at her
FALSTAFF: house the hour she appointed me.
FORD: And sped you, sir?
FALSTAFF: Very ill-favoredly, Master Brook.
FORD: How so, sir? Did she change her determination?
FALSTAFF: No, Master Brook, but the peaking Cornuto her
FALSTAFF: husband, Master Brook, dwelling in a continual
FALSTAFF: 'larum of jealousy, comes me in the instant of our
FALSTAFF: encounter, after we had embraced, kissed, protested,
FALSTAFF: and, as it were, spoke the prologue of our comedy,
FALSTAFF: and at his heels a rabble of his companions, thither
FALSTAFF: provoked and instigated by his distemper, and,
FALSTAFF: forsooth, to search his house for his wife's love.
FORD: What, while you were there?
FALSTAFF: While I was there.
FORD: And did he search for you, and could not find you?
FALSTAFF: You shall hear. As good luck would have it, comes
FALSTAFF: in one Mistress Page, gives intelligence of Ford's
FALSTAFF: approach, and, in her invention and Ford's wife's
FALSTAFF: distraction, they conveyed me into a buck-basket.
FORD: A buck-basket!
FALSTAFF: By the Lord, a buck-basket! rammed me in with foul
FALSTAFF: shirts and smocks, socks, foul stockings, greasy
FALSTAFF: napkins, that, Master Brook, there was the rankest
FALSTAFF: compound of villanous smell that ever offended nostril.
FORD: And how long lay you there?
FALSTAFF: Nay, you shall hear, Master Brook, what I have
FALSTAFF: suffered to bring this woman to evil for your good.
FALSTAFF: Being thus crammed in the basket, a couple of Ford's
FALSTAFF: knaves, his hinds, were called forth by their
FALSTAFF: mistress to carry me in the name of foul clothes to
FALSTAFF: Datchet-lane: they took me on their shoulders, met
FALSTAFF: the jealous knave their master in the door, who
FALSTAFF: asked them once or twice what they had in their
FALSTAFF: basket: I quaked for fear, lest the lunatic knave
FALSTAFF: would have searched it, but fate, ordaining he
FALSTAFF: should be a cuckold, held his hand. Well: on went he
FALSTAFF: for a search, and away went I for foul clothes. But
FALSTAFF: mark the sequel, Master Brook: I suffered the pangs
FALSTAFF: of three several deaths, first, an intolerable
FALSTAFF: fright, to be detected with a jealous rotten
FALSTAFF: bell-wether, next, to be compassed, like a good
FALSTAFF: bilbo, in the circumference of a peck, hilt to
FALSTAFF: point, heel to head, and then, to be stopped in,
FALSTAFF: like a strong distillation, with stinking clothes
FALSTAFF: that fretted in their own grease: think of that,--a
FALSTAFF: man of my kidney,--think of that,--that am as subject
FALSTAFF: to heat as butter, a man of continual dissolution
FALSTAFF: and thaw: it was a miracle to scape suffocation.
FALSTAFF: And in the height of this bath, when I was more than
FALSTAFF: half stewed in grease, like a Dutch dish, to be
FALSTAFF: thrown into the Thames, and cooled, glowing hot,
FALSTAFF: in that surge, like a horse-shoe, think of
FALSTAFF: that,--hissing hot,--think of that, Master Brook.
FORD: In good sadness, I am sorry that for my sake you
FORD: have sufferd all this. My suit then is desperate,
FORD: you'll undertake her no more?
FALSTAFF: Master Brook, I will be thrown into Etna, as I have
FALSTAFF: been into Thames, ere I will leave her thus. Her
FALSTAFF: husband is this morning gone a-birding: I have
FALSTAFF: received from her another embassy of meeting, 'twixt
FALSTAFF: eight and nine is the hour, Master Brook.
FORD: 'Tis past eight already, sir.
FALSTAFF: Is it? I will then address me to my appointment.
FALSTAFF: Come to me at your convenient leisure, and you shall
FALSTAFF: know how I speed, and the conclusion shall be
FALSTAFF: crowned with your enjoying her. Adieu. You shall
FALSTAFF: have her, Master Brook, Master Brook, you shall
FALSTAFF: cuckold Ford.
NARRATOR: Exit
FORD: Hum! ha! is this a vision? is this a dream? do I
FORD: sleep? Master Ford awake! awake, Master Ford!
FORD: there's a hole made in your best coat, Master Ford.
FORD: This 'tis to be married! this 'tis to have linen
FORD: and buck-baskets! Well, I will proclaim myself
FORD: what I am: I will now take the lecher, he is at my
FORD: house, he cannot 'scape me, 'tis impossible he
FORD: should, he cannot creep into a halfpenny purse,
FORD: nor into a pepper-box: but, lest the devil that
FORD: guides him should aid him, I will search
FORD: impossible places. Though what I am I cannot avoid,
FORD: yet to be what I would not shall not make me tame:
FORD: if I have horns to make one mad, let the proverb go
FORD: with me: I'll be horn-mad.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: ACT IV
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A street.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS QUICKLY, and WILLIAM PAGE
MISTRESS PAGE: Is he at Master Ford's already, think'st thou?
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Sure he is by this, or will be presently: but,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: truly, he is very courageous mad about his throwing
MISTRESS QUICKLY: into the water. Mistress Ford desires you to come suddenly.
MISTRESS PAGE: I'll be with her by and by, I'll but bring my young
MISTRESS PAGE: man here to school. Look, where his master comes,
MISTRESS PAGE: 'tis a playing-day, I see.
NARRATOR: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS
MISTRESS PAGE: How now, Sir Hugh! no school to-day?
SIR HUGH EVANS: No, Master Slender is let the boys leave to play.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Blessing of his heart!
MISTRESS PAGE: Sir Hugh, my husband says my son profits nothing in
MISTRESS PAGE: the world at his book. I pray you, ask him some
MISTRESS PAGE: questions in his accidence.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Come hither, William, hold up your head, come.
MISTRESS PAGE: Come on, sirrah, hold up your head, answer your
MISTRESS PAGE: master, be not afraid.
SIR HUGH EVANS: William, how many numbers is in nouns?
WILLIAM PAGE: Two.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Truly, I thought there had been one number more,
MISTRESS QUICKLY: because they say, ''Od's nouns.'
SIR HUGH EVANS: Peace your tattlings! What is 'fair,' William?
WILLIAM PAGE: Pulcher.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Polecats! there are fairer things than polecats, sure.
SIR HUGH EVANS: You are a very simplicity 'oman: I pray you peace.
SIR HUGH EVANS: What is 'lapis,' William?
WILLIAM PAGE: A stone.
SIR HUGH EVANS: And what is 'a stone,' William?
WILLIAM PAGE: A pebble.
SIR HUGH EVANS: No, it is 'lapis:' I pray you, remember in your prain.
WILLIAM PAGE: Lapis.
SIR HUGH EVANS: That is a good William. What is he, William, that
SIR HUGH EVANS: does lend articles?
WILLIAM PAGE: Articles are borrowed of the pronoun, and be thus
WILLIAM PAGE: declined, Singulariter, nominativo, hic, haec, hoc.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Nominativo, hig, hag, hog, pray you, mark:
SIR HUGH EVANS: genitivo, hujus. Well, what is your accusative case?
WILLIAM PAGE: Accusativo, hinc.
SIR HUGH EVANS: I pray you, have your remembrance, child,
SIR HUGH EVANS: accusative, hung, hang, hog.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: 'Hang-hog' is Latin for bacon, I warrant you.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Leave your prabbles, 'oman. What is the focative
SIR HUGH EVANS: case, William?
WILLIAM PAGE: O,--vocativo, O.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Remember, William, focative is caret.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: And that's a good root.
SIR HUGH EVANS: 'Oman, forbear.
MISTRESS PAGE: Peace!
SIR HUGH EVANS: What is your genitive case plural, William?
WILLIAM PAGE: Genitive case!
SIR HUGH EVANS: Ay.
WILLIAM PAGE: Genitive,--horum, harum, horum.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: Vengeance of Jenny's case! fie on her! never name
MISTRESS QUICKLY: her, child, if she be a whore.
SIR HUGH EVANS: For shame, 'oman.
MISTRESS QUICKLY: You do ill to teach the child such words: he
MISTRESS QUICKLY: teaches him to hick and to hack, which they'll do
MISTRESS QUICKLY: fast enough of themselves, and to call 'horum:' fie upon you!
SIR HUGH EVANS: 'Oman, art thou lunatics? hast thou no
SIR HUGH EVANS: understandings for thy cases and the numbers of the
SIR HUGH EVANS: genders? Thou art as foolish Christian creatures as
SIR HUGH EVANS: I would desires.
MISTRESS PAGE: Prithee, hold thy peace.
SIR HUGH EVANS: Show me now, William, some declensions of your pronouns.
WILLIAM PAGE: Forsooth, I have forgot.
SIR HUGH EVANS: It is qui, quae, quod: if you forget your 'quies,'
SIR HUGH EVANS: your 'quaes,' and your 'quods,' you must be
SIR HUGH EVANS: preeches. Go your ways, and play, go.
MISTRESS PAGE: He is a better scholar than I thought he was.
SIR HUGH EVANS: He is a good sprag memory. Farewell, Mistress Page.
MISTRESS PAGE: Adieu, good Sir Hugh.
NARRATOR: Exit SIR HUGH EVANS
MISTRESS PAGE: Get you home, boy. Come, we stay too long.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. A room in FORD'S house.
NARRATOR: Enter FALSTAFF and MISTRESS FORD
FALSTAFF: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my
FALSTAFF: sufferance. I see you are obsequious in your love,
FALSTAFF: and I profess requital to a hair's breadth, not
FALSTAFF: only, Mistress Ford, in the simple
FALSTAFF: office of love, but in all the accoutrement,
FALSTAFF: complement and ceremony of it. But are you
FALSTAFF: sure of your husband now?
MISTRESS FORD: He's a-birding, sweet Sir John.
MISTRESS PAGE: [Within]  What, ho, gossip Ford! what, ho!
MISTRESS FORD: Step into the chamber, Sir John.
NARRATOR: Exit FALSTAFF
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE
MISTRESS PAGE: How now, sweetheart! who's at home besides yourself?
MISTRESS FORD: Why, none but mine own people.
MISTRESS PAGE: Indeed!
MISTRESS FORD: No, certainly.
NARRATOR: Aside to her
MISTRESS FORD: Speak louder.
MISTRESS PAGE: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.
MISTRESS FORD: Why?
MISTRESS PAGE: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again:
MISTRESS PAGE: he so takes on yonder with my husband, so rails
MISTRESS PAGE: against all married mankind, so curses all Eve's
MISTRESS PAGE: daughters, of what complexion soever, and so buffets
MISTRESS PAGE: himself on the forehead, crying, 'Peer out, peer
MISTRESS PAGE: out!' that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but
MISTRESS PAGE: tameness, civility and patience, to this his
MISTRESS PAGE: distemper he is in now: I am glad the fat knight is not here.
MISTRESS FORD: Why, does he talk of him?
MISTRESS PAGE: Of none but him, and swears he was carried out, the
MISTRESS PAGE: last time he searched for him, in a basket, protests
MISTRESS PAGE: to my husband he is now here, and hath drawn him and
MISTRESS PAGE: the rest of their company from their sport, to make
MISTRESS PAGE: another experiment of his suspicion: but I am glad
MISTRESS PAGE: the knight is not here, now he shall see his own foolery.
MISTRESS FORD: How near is he, Mistress Page?
MISTRESS PAGE: Hard by, at street end, he will be here anon.
MISTRESS FORD: I am undone! The knight is here.
MISTRESS PAGE: Why then you are utterly shamed, and he's but a dead
MISTRESS PAGE: man. What a woman are you!--Away with him, away
MISTRESS PAGE: with him! better shame than murder.
FORD: Which way should be go? how should I bestow him?
FORD: Shall I put him into the basket again?
NARRATOR: Re-enter FALSTAFF
FALSTAFF: No, I'll come no more i' the basket. May I not go
FALSTAFF: out ere he come?
MISTRESS PAGE: Alas, three of Master Ford's brothers watch the door
MISTRESS PAGE: with pistols, that none shall issue out, otherwise
MISTRESS PAGE: you might slip away ere he came. But what make you here?
FALSTAFF: What shall I do? I'll creep up into the chimney.
MISTRESS FORD: There they always use to discharge their
MISTRESS FORD: birding-pieces. Creep into the kiln-hole.
FALSTAFF: Where is it?
MISTRESS FORD: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press,
MISTRESS FORD: coffer, chest, trunk, well, vault, but he hath an
MISTRESS FORD: abstract for the remembrance of such places, and
MISTRESS FORD: goes to them by his note: there is no hiding you in the house.
FALSTAFF: I'll go out then.
MISTRESS PAGE: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir
MISTRESS PAGE: John. Unless you go out disguised--
MISTRESS FORD: How might we disguise him?
MISTRESS PAGE: Alas the day, I know not! There is no woman's gown
MISTRESS PAGE: big enough for him otherwise he might put on a hat,
MISTRESS PAGE: a muffler and a kerchief, and so escape.
FALSTAFF: Good hearts, devise something: any extremity rather
FALSTAFF: than a mischief.
MISTRESS FORD: My maid's aunt, the fat woman of Brentford, has a
MISTRESS FORD: gown above.
MISTRESS PAGE: On my word, it will serve him, she's as big as he
MISTRESS PAGE: is: and there's her thrummed hat and her muffler
MISTRESS PAGE: too. Run up, Sir John.
MISTRESS FORD: Go, go, sweet Sir John: Mistress Page and I will
MISTRESS FORD: look some linen for your head.
MISTRESS PAGE: Quick, quick! we'll come dress you straight: put
MISTRESS PAGE: on the gown the while.
NARRATOR: Exit FALSTAFF
MISTRESS FORD: I would my husband would meet him in this shape: he
MISTRESS FORD: cannot abide the old woman of Brentford, he swears
MISTRESS FORD: she's a witch, forbade her my house and hath
MISTRESS FORD: threatened to beat her.
MISTRESS PAGE: Heaven guide him to thy husband's cudgel, and the
MISTRESS PAGE: devil guide his cudgel afterwards!
MISTRESS FORD: But is my husband coming?
MISTRESS PAGE: Ah, in good sadness, is he, and talks of the basket
MISTRESS PAGE: too, howsoever he hath had intelligence.
MISTRESS FORD: We'll try that, for I'll appoint my men to carry the
MISTRESS FORD: basket again, to meet him at the door with it, as
MISTRESS FORD: they did last time.
MISTRESS PAGE: Nay, but he'll be here presently: let's go dress him
MISTRESS PAGE: like the witch of Brentford.
MISTRESS FORD: I'll first direct my men what they shall do with the
MISTRESS FORD: basket. Go up, I'll bring linen for him straight.
NARRATOR: Exit
MISTRESS PAGE: Hang him, dishonest varlet! we cannot misuse him enough.
MISTRESS PAGE: We'll leave a proof, by that which we will do,
MISTRESS PAGE: Wives may be merry, and yet honest too:
MISTRESS PAGE: We do not act that often jest and laugh,
MISTRESS PAGE: 'Tis old, but true, Still swine eat all the draff.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: Re-enter MISTRESS FORD with two Servants
MISTRESS FORD: Go, sirs, take the basket again on your shoulders:
MISTRESS FORD: your master is hard at door, if he bid you set it
MISTRESS FORD: down, obey him: quickly, dispatch.
NARRATOR: Exit
First Servant: Come, come, take it up.
Second Servant: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again.
First Servant: I hope not, I had as lief bear so much lead.
NARRATOR: Enter FORD, PAGE, SHALLOW, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS
FORD: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any
FORD: way then to unfool me again? Set down the basket,

NARRATOR: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn.

NARRATOR: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn.

NARRATOR: ACT V
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A room in the Garter Inn.
NARRATOR: Enter FALSTAFF and MISTRESS QUICKLY
FALSTAFF: Prithee, no more prattling, go. I'll hold. This is
FALSTAFF: the third time, I hope good luck lies in odd
FALSTAFF: numbers. Away I go. They say there is divinity in
FALSTAFF: odd numbers, either in nativity, chance, or death. Away!
MISTRESS QUICKLY: I'll provide you a chain, and I'll do what I can to
MISTRESS QUICKLY: get you a pair of horns.
FALSTAFF: Away, I say, time wears: hold up your head, and mince.
NARRATOR: Exit MISTRESS QUICKLY
NARRATOR: Enter FORD
FALSTAFF: How now, Master Brook! Master Brook, the matter
FALSTAFF: will be known to-night, or never. Be you in the
FALSTAFF: Park about midnight, at Herne's oak, and you shall
FALSTAFF: see wonders.
FORD: Went you not to her yesterday, sir, as you told me
FORD: you had appointed?
FALSTAFF: I went to her, Master Brook, as you see, like a poor
FALSTAFF: old man: but I came from her, Master Brook, like a
FALSTAFF: poor old woman. That same knave Ford, her husband,
FALSTAFF: hath the finest mad devil of jealousy in him,
FALSTAFF: Master Brook, that ever governed frenzy. I will tell
FALSTAFF: you: he beat me grievously, in the shape of a
FALSTAFF: woman, for in the shape of man, Master Brook, I fear
FALSTAFF: not Goliath with a weaver's beam, because I know
FALSTAFF: also life is a shuttle. I am in haste, go along
FALSTAFF: with me: I'll tell you all, Master Brook. Since I
FALSTAFF: plucked geese, played truant and whipped top, I knew
FALSTAFF: not what 'twas to be beaten till lately. Follow
FALSTAFF: me: I'll tell you strange things of this knave
FALSTAFF: Ford, on whom to-night I will be revenged, and I
FALSTAFF: will deliver his wife into your hand. Follow.
FALSTAFF: Strange things in hand, Master Brook! Follow.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Windsor Park.
NARRATOR: Enter PAGE, SHALLOW, and SLENDER
PAGE: Come, come, we'll couch i' the castle-ditch till we
PAGE: see the light of our fairies. Remember, son Slender,
PAGE: my daughter.
SLENDER: Ay, forsooth, I have spoke with her and we have a
SLENDER: nay-word how to know one another: I come to her in
SLENDER: white, and cry 'mum,' she cries 'budget,' and by
SLENDER: that we know one another.
SHALLOW: That's good too: but what needs either your 'mum'
SHALLOW: or her 'budget?' the white will decipher her well
SHALLOW: enough. It hath struck ten o'clock.
PAGE: The night is dark, light and spirits will become it
PAGE: well. Heaven prosper our sport! No man means evil
PAGE: but the devil, and we shall know him by his horns.
PAGE: Let's away, follow me.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A street leading to the Park.
NARRATOR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and DOCTOR CAIUS

MISTRESS PAGE: see your time, take her by the band, away with her

MISTRESS PAGE: into the Park: we two must go together.
DOCTOR CAIUS: I know vat I have to do. Adieu.

MISTRESS PAGE: My husband will not rejoice so much at the abuse of
MISTRESS PAGE: Falstaff as he will chafe at the doctor's marrying

MISTRESS PAGE: chiding than a great deal of heart-break.

MISTRESS PAGE: They are all couched in a pit hard by Herne's oak,
MISTRESS PAGE: with obscured lights, which, at the very instant of
MISTRESS PAGE: Falstaff's and our meeting, they will at once
MISTRESS PAGE: display to the night.
MISTRESS FORD: That cannot choose but amaze him.
MISTRESS PAGE: If he be not amazed, he will be mocked, if he be
MISTRESS PAGE: amazed, he will every way be mocked.
MISTRESS FORD: We'll betray him finely.
MISTRESS PAGE: Against such lewdsters and their lechery
MISTRESS PAGE: Those that betray them do no treachery.
