NARRATOR: ACT I
NARRATOR: PROLOGUE
NARRATOR: Enter GOWER
NARRATOR: Before the palace of Antioch
LODOVICO: To sing a song that old was sung,
LODOVICO: From ashes ancient Gower is come,
LODOVICO: Assuming man's infirmities,
LODOVICO: To glad your ear, and please your eyes.
LODOVICO: It hath been sung at festivals,
LODOVICO: On ember-eves and holy-ales,
LODOVICO: And lords and ladies in their lives
LODOVICO: Have read it for restoratives:
LODOVICO: The purchase is to make men glorious,
LODOVICO: Et bonum quo antiquius, eo melius.
LODOVICO: If you, born in these latter times,
LODOVICO: When wit's more ripe, accept my rhymes.
LODOVICO: And that to hear an old man sing
LODOVICO: May to your wishes pleasure bring
LODOVICO: I life would wish, and that I might
LODOVICO: Waste it for you, like taper-light.
LODOVICO: This Antioch, then, Antiochus the Great
LODOVICO: Built up, this city, for his chiefest seat:
LODOVICO: The fairest in all Syria,
LODOVICO: I tell you what mine authors say:
LODOVICO: This king unto him took a fere,
LODOVICO: Who died and left a female heir,
LODOVICO: So buxom, blithe, and full of face,
LODOVICO: As heaven had lent her all his grace,
LODOVICO: With whom the father liking took,
LODOVICO: And her to incest did provoke:
LODOVICO: Bad child, worse father! to entice his own
LODOVICO: To evil should be done by none:
LODOVICO: But custom what they did begin
LODOVICO: Was with long use account no sin.
LODOVICO: The beauty of this sinful dame
LODOVICO: Made many princes thither frame,
LODOVICO: To seek her as a bed-fellow,
LODOVICO: In marriage-pleasures play-fellow:
LODOVICO: Which to prevent he made a law,
LODOVICO: To keep her still, and men in awe,
LODOVICO: That whoso ask'd her for his wife,
LODOVICO: His riddle told not, lost his life:
LODOVICO: So for her many a wight did die,
LODOVICO: As yon grim looks do testify.
LODOVICO: What now ensues, to the judgment of your eye
LODOVICO: I give, my cause who best can justify.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Antioch. A room in the palace.
NARRATOR: Enter ANTIOCHUS, Prince PERICLES, and followers
ANTIOCHUS: Young prince of Tyre, you have at large received
ANTIOCHUS: The danger of the task you undertake.
PERICLES: I have, Antiochus, and, with a soul
PERICLES: Embolden'd with the glory of her praise,
PERICLES: Think death no hazard in this enterprise.
ANTIOCHUS: Bring in our daughter, clothed like a bride,
ANTIOCHUS: For the embracements even of Jove himself,
ANTIOCHUS: At whose conception, till Lucina reign'd,
ANTIOCHUS: Nature this dowry gave, to glad her presence,
ANTIOCHUS: The senate-house of planets all did sit,
ANTIOCHUS: To knit in her their best perfections.
NARRATOR: Music. Enter the Daughter of ANTIOCHUS
PERICLES: See where she comes, apparell'd like the spring,
PERICLES: Graces her subjects, and her thoughts the king
PERICLES: Of every virtue gives renown to men!
PERICLES: Her face the book of praises, where is read
PERICLES: Nothing but curious pleasures, as from thence
PERICLES: Sorrow were ever razed and testy wrath
PERICLES: Could never be her mild companion.
PERICLES: You gods that made me man, and sway in love,
PERICLES: That have inflamed desire in my breast
PERICLES: To taste the fruit of yon celestial tree,
PERICLES: Or die in the adventure, be my helps,
PERICLES: As I am son and servant to your will,
PERICLES: To compass such a boundless happiness!
ANTIOCHUS: Prince Pericles,--
PERICLES: That would be son to great Antiochus.
ANTIOCHUS: Before thee stands this fair Hesperides,
ANTIOCHUS: With golden fruit, but dangerous to be touch'd,
ANTIOCHUS: For death-like dragons here affright thee hard:
ANTIOCHUS: Her face, like heaven, enticeth thee to view
ANTIOCHUS: Her countless glory, which desert must gain,
ANTIOCHUS: And which, without desert, because thine eye
ANTIOCHUS: Presumes to reach, all thy whole heap must die.
ANTIOCHUS: Yon sometimes famous princes, like thyself,
ANTIOCHUS: Drawn by report, adventurous by desire,
ANTIOCHUS: Tell thee, with speechless tongues and semblance pale,
ANTIOCHUS: That without covering, save yon field of stars,
ANTIOCHUS: Here they stand martyrs, slain in Cupid's wars,
ANTIOCHUS: And with dead cheeks advise thee to desist
ANTIOCHUS: For going on death's net, whom none resist.
PERICLES: Antiochus, I thank thee, who hath taught
PERICLES: My frail mortality to know itself,
PERICLES: And by those fearful objects to prepare
PERICLES: This body, like to them, to what I must,
PERICLES: For death remember'd should be like a mirror,
PERICLES: Who tells us life's but breath, to trust it error.
PERICLES: I'll make my will then, and, as sick men do
PERICLES: Who know the world, see heaven, but, feeling woe,
PERICLES: Gripe not at earthly joys as erst they did,
PERICLES: So I bequeath a happy peace to you
PERICLES: And all good men, as every prince should do,
PERICLES: My riches to the earth from whence they came,
PERICLES: But my unspotted fire of love to you.
NARRATOR: To the Daughter of ANTIOCHUS
PERICLES: Thus ready for the way of life or death,
PERICLES: I wait the sharpest blow, Antiochus.
ANTIOCHUS: Scorning advice, read the conclusion then:
ANTIOCHUS: Which read and not expounded, 'tis decreed,
ANTIOCHUS: As these before thee thou thyself shalt bleed.
Daughter: Of all say'd yet, mayst thou prove prosperous!
Daughter: Of all say'd yet, I wish thee happiness!
PERICLES: Like a bold champion, I assume the lists,
PERICLES: Nor ask advice of any other thought
PERICLES: But faithfulness and courage.
NARRATOR: He reads the riddle
PERICLES: I am no viper, yet I feed
PERICLES: On mother's flesh which did me breed.
PERICLES: I sought a husband, in which labour
PERICLES: I found that kindness in a father:
PERICLES: He's father, son, and husband mild,
PERICLES: I mother, wife, and yet his child.
PERICLES: How they may be, and yet in two,
PERICLES: As you will live, resolve it you.
PERICLES: Sharp physic is the last: but, O you powers
PERICLES: That give heaven countless eyes to view men's acts,
PERICLES: Why cloud they not their sights perpetually,
PERICLES: If this be true, which makes me pale to read it?
PERICLES: Fair glass of light, I loved you, and could still,
NARRATOR: Takes hold of the hand of the Daughter of ANTIOCHUS
PERICLES: Were not this glorious casket stored with ill:
PERICLES: But I must tell you, now my thoughts revolt
PERICLES: For he's no man on whom perfections wait
PERICLES: That, knowing sin within, will touch the gate.
PERICLES: You are a fair viol, and your sense the strings,
PERICLES: Who, finger'd to make man his lawful music,
PERICLES: Would draw heaven down, and all the gods, to hearken:
PERICLES: But being play'd upon before your time,
PERICLES: Hell only danceth at so harsh a chime.
PERICLES: Good sooth, I care not for you.
ANTIOCHUS: Prince Pericles, touch not, upon thy life.
ANTIOCHUS: For that's an article within our law,
ANTIOCHUS: As dangerous as the rest. Your time's expired:
ANTIOCHUS: Either expound now, or receive your sentence.
PERICLES: Great king,
PERICLES: Few love to hear the sins they love to act,
PERICLES: 'Twould braid yourself too near for me to tell it.
PERICLES: Who has a book of all that monarchs do,
PERICLES: He's more secure to keep it shut than shown:
PERICLES: For vice repeated is like the wandering wind.
PERICLES: Blows dust in other's eyes, to spread itself,
PERICLES: And yet the end of all is bought thus dear,
PERICLES: The breath is gone, and the sore eyes see clear:
PERICLES: To stop the air would hurt them. The blind mole casts
PERICLES: Copp'd hills towards heaven, to tell the earth is throng'd
PERICLES: By man's oppression, and the poor worm doth die for't.
PERICLES: Kings are earth's gods, in vice their law's
PERICLES: their will,
PERICLES: And if Jove stray, who dares say Jove doth ill?
PERICLES: It is enough you know, and it is fit,
PERICLES: What being more known grows worse, to smother it.
PERICLES: All love the womb that their first being bred,
PERICLES: Then give my tongue like leave to love my head.
ANTIOCHUS: [Aside]  Heaven, that I had thy head! he has found
ANTIOCHUS: the meaning:
ANTIOCHUS: But I will gloze with him.--Young prince of Tyre,
ANTIOCHUS: Though by the tenor of our strict edict,
ANTIOCHUS: Your exposition misinterpreting,
ANTIOCHUS: We might proceed to cancel of your days,
ANTIOCHUS: Yet hope, succeeding from so fair a tree
ANTIOCHUS: As your fair self, doth tune us otherwise:
ANTIOCHUS: Forty days longer we do respite you,
ANTIOCHUS: If by which time our secret be undone,
ANTIOCHUS: This mercy shows we'll joy in such a son:
ANTIOCHUS: And until then your entertain shall be
ANTIOCHUS: As doth befit our honour and your worth.
NARRATOR: Exeunt all but PERICLES
PERICLES: How courtesy would seem to cover sin,
PERICLES: When what is done is like an hypocrite,
PERICLES: The which is good in nothing but in sight!
PERICLES: If it be true that I interpret false,
PERICLES: Then were it certain you were not so bad
PERICLES: As with foul incest to abuse your soul,
PERICLES: Where now you're both a father and a son,
PERICLES: By your untimely claspings with your child,
PERICLES: Which pleasure fits an husband, not a father,
PERICLES: And she an eater of her mother's flesh,
PERICLES: By the defiling of her parent's bed,
PERICLES: And both like serpents are, who though they feed
PERICLES: On sweetest flowers, yet they poison breed.
PERICLES: Antioch, farewell! for wisdom sees, those men
PERICLES: Blush not in actions blacker than the night,
PERICLES: Will shun no course to keep them from the light.
PERICLES: One sin, I know, another doth provoke,
PERICLES: Murder's as near to lust as flame to smoke:
PERICLES: Poison and treason are the hands of sin,
PERICLES: Ay, and the targets, to put off the shame:
PERICLES: Then, lest my lie be cropp'd to keep you clear,
PERICLES: By flight I'll shun the danger which I fear.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: Re-enter ANTIOCHUS
ANTIOCHUS: He hath found the meaning, for which we mean
ANTIOCHUS: To have his head.
ANTIOCHUS: He must not live to trumpet forth my infamy,
ANTIOCHUS: Nor tell the world Antiochus doth sin
ANTIOCHUS: In such a loathed manner,
ANTIOCHUS: And therefore instantly this prince must die:
ANTIOCHUS: For by his fall my honour must keep high.
ANTIOCHUS: Who attends us there?
NARRATOR: Enter THALIARD
THALIARD: Doth your highness call?
ANTIOCHUS: Thaliard,
ANTIOCHUS: You are of our chamber, and our mind partakes
ANTIOCHUS: Her private actions to your secrecy,
ANTIOCHUS: And for your faithfulness we will advance you.
ANTIOCHUS: Thaliard, behold, here's poison, and here's gold,
ANTIOCHUS: We hate the prince of Tyre, and thou must kill him:
ANTIOCHUS: It fits thee not to ask the reason why,
ANTIOCHUS: Because we bid it. Say, is it done?
THALIARD: My lord,
THALIARD: 'Tis done.
ANTIOCHUS: Enough.
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
ANTIOCHUS: Let your breath cool yourself, telling your haste.
Messenger: My lord, prince Pericles is fled.
NARRATOR: Exit
ANTIOCHUS: As thou
ANTIOCHUS: Wilt live, fly after: and like an arrow shot
ANTIOCHUS: From a well-experienced archer hits the mark
ANTIOCHUS: His eye doth level at, so thou ne'er return
ANTIOCHUS: Unless thou say 'Prince Pericles is dead.'
THALIARD: My lord,
THALIARD: If I can get him within my pistol's length,
THALIARD: I'll make him sure enough: so, farewell to your highness.
ANTIOCHUS: Thaliard, adieu!
NARRATOR: Exit THALIARD
ANTIOCHUS: Till Pericles be dead,
ANTIOCHUS: My heart can lend no succor to my head.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Tyre. A room in the palace.
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES
PERICLES: [To Lords without]  Let none disturb us.--Why should
PERICLES: this change of thoughts,
PERICLES: The sad companion, dull-eyed melancholy,
PERICLES: Be my so used a guest as not an hour,
PERICLES: In the day's glorious walk, or peaceful night,
PERICLES: The tomb where grief should sleep, can breed me quiet?
PERICLES: Here pleasures court mine eyes, and mine eyes shun them,
PERICLES: And danger, which I fear'd, is at Antioch,
PERICLES: Whose aim seems far too short to hit me here:
PERICLES: Yet neither pleasure's art can joy my spirits,
PERICLES: Nor yet the other's distance comfort me.
PERICLES: Then it is thus: the passions of the mind,
PERICLES: That have their first conception by mis-dread,
PERICLES: Have after-nourishment and life by care,
PERICLES: And what was first but fear what might be done,
PERICLES: Grows elder now and cares it be not done.
PERICLES: And so with me: the great Antiochus,
PERICLES: 'Gainst whom I am too little to contend,
PERICLES: Since he's so great can make his will his act,
PERICLES: Will think me speaking, though I swear to silence,
PERICLES: Nor boots it me to say I honour him.
PERICLES: If he suspect I may dishonour him:
PERICLES: And what may make him blush in being known,
PERICLES: He'll stop the course by which it might be known,
PERICLES: With hostile forces he'll o'erspread the land,
PERICLES: And with the ostent of war will look so huge,
PERICLES: Amazement shall drive courage from the state,
PERICLES: Our men be vanquish'd ere they do resist,
PERICLES: And subjects punish'd that ne'er thought offence:
PERICLES: Which care of them, not pity of myself,
PERICLES: Who am no more but as the tops of trees,
PERICLES: Which fence the roots they grow by and defend them,
PERICLES: Makes both my body pine and soul to languish,
PERICLES: And punish that before that he would punish.
NARRATOR: Enter HELICANUS, with other Lords
First Lord: Joy and all comfort in your sacred breast!
Second Lord: And keep your mind, till you return to us,
Second Lord: Peaceful and comfortable!
HELICANUS: Peace, peace, and give experience tongue.
HELICANUS: They do abuse the king that flatter him:
HELICANUS: For flattery is the bellows blows up sin,
HELICANUS: The thing which is flatter'd, but a spark,
HELICANUS: To which that blast gives heat and stronger glowing,
HELICANUS: Whereas reproof, obedient and in order,
HELICANUS: Fits kings, as they are men, for they may err.
HELICANUS: When Signior Sooth here does proclaim a peace,
HELICANUS: He flatters you, makes war upon your life.
HELICANUS: Prince, pardon me, or strike me, if you please,
HELICANUS: I cannot be much lower than my knees.
PERICLES: All leave us else, but let your cares o'erlook
PERICLES: What shipping and what lading's in our haven,
PERICLES: And then return to us.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Lords
PERICLES: Helicanus, thou
PERICLES: Hast moved us: what seest thou in our looks?
HELICANUS: An angry brow, dread lord.
PERICLES: If there be such a dart in princes' frowns,
PERICLES: How durst thy tongue move anger to our face?
HELICANUS: How dare the plants look up to heaven, from whence
HELICANUS: They have their nourishment?
PERICLES: Thou know'st I have power
PERICLES: To take thy life from thee.
HELICANUS: [Kneeling]
HELICANUS: I have ground the axe myself,
HELICANUS: Do you but strike the blow.
PERICLES: Rise, prithee, rise.
PERICLES: Sit down: thou art no flatterer:
PERICLES: I thank thee for it, and heaven forbid
PERICLES: That kings should let their ears hear their
PERICLES: faults hid!
PERICLES: Fit counsellor and servant for a prince,
PERICLES: Who by thy wisdom makest a prince thy servant,
PERICLES: What wouldst thou have me do?
HELICANUS: To bear with patience
HELICANUS: Such griefs as you yourself do lay upon yourself.
PERICLES: Thou speak'st like a physician, Helicanus,
PERICLES: That minister'st a potion unto me
PERICLES: That thou wouldst tremble to receive thyself.
PERICLES: Attend me, then: I went to Antioch,
PERICLES: Where as thou know'st, against the face of death,
PERICLES: I sought the purchase of a glorious beauty.
PERICLES: From whence an issue I might propagate,
PERICLES: Are arms to princes, and bring joys to subjects.
PERICLES: Her face was to mine eye beyond all wonder,
PERICLES: The rest--hark in thine ear--as black as incest:
PERICLES: Which by my knowledge found, the sinful father
PERICLES: Seem'd not to strike, but smooth: but thou
PERICLES: know'st this,
PERICLES: 'Tis time to fear when tyrants seem to kiss.
PERICLES: Such fear so grew in me, I hither fled,
PERICLES: Under the covering of a careful night,
PERICLES: Who seem'd my good protector, and, being here,
PERICLES: Bethought me what was past, what might succeed.
PERICLES: I knew him tyrannous, and tyrants' fears
PERICLES: Decrease not, but grow faster than the years:
PERICLES: And should he doubt it, as no doubt he doth,
PERICLES: That I should open to the listening air
PERICLES: How many worthy princes' bloods were shed,
PERICLES: To keep his bed of blackness unlaid ope,
PERICLES: To lop that doubt, he'll fill this land with arms,
PERICLES: And make pretence of wrong that I have done him:
PERICLES: When all, for mine, if I may call offence,
PERICLES: Must feel war's blow, who spares not innocence:
PERICLES: Which love to all, of which thyself art one,
PERICLES: Who now reprovest me for it,--
HELICANUS: Alas, sir!
PERICLES: Drew sleep out of mine eyes, blood from my cheeks,
PERICLES: Musings into my mind, with thousand doubts
PERICLES: How I might stop this tempest ere it came,
PERICLES: And finding little comfort to relieve them,
PERICLES: I thought it princely charity to grieve them.
HELICANUS: Well, my lord, since you have given me leave to speak.
HELICANUS: Freely will I speak. Antiochus you fear,
HELICANUS: And justly too, I think, you fear the tyrant,
HELICANUS: Who either by public war or private treason
HELICANUS: Will take away your life.
HELICANUS: Therefore, my lord, go travel for a while,
HELICANUS: Till that his rage and anger be forgot,
HELICANUS: Or till the Destinies do cut his thread of life.
HELICANUS: Your rule direct to any, if to me.
HELICANUS: Day serves not light more faithful than I'll be.
PERICLES: I do not doubt thy faith,
PERICLES: But should he wrong my liberties in my absence?
HELICANUS: We'll mingle our bloods together in the earth,
HELICANUS: From whence we had our being and our birth.
PERICLES: Tyre, I now look from thee then, and to Tarsus
PERICLES: Intend my travel, where I'll hear from thee,
PERICLES: And by whose letters I'll dispose myself.
PERICLES: The care I had and have of subjects' good
PERICLES: On thee I lay whose wisdom's strength can bear it.
PERICLES: I'll take thy word for faith, not ask thine oath:
PERICLES: Who shuns not to break one will sure crack both:
PERICLES: But in our orbs we'll live so round and safe,
PERICLES: That time of both this truth shall ne'er convince,
PERICLES: Thou show'dst a subject's shine, I a true prince.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Tyre. An ante-chamber in the palace.
NARRATOR: Enter THALIARD
THALIARD: So, this is Tyre, and this the court. Here must I
THALIARD: kill King Pericles, and if I do it not, I am sure to
THALIARD: be hanged at home: 'tis dangerous. Well, I perceive
THALIARD: he was a wise fellow, and had good discretion, that,
THALIARD: being bid to ask what he would of the king, desired
THALIARD: he might know none of his secrets: now do I see he
THALIARD: had some reason for't, for if a king bid a man be a
THALIARD: villain, he's bound by the indenture of his oath to
THALIARD: be one! Hush! here come the lords of Tyre.
NARRATOR: Enter HELICANUS and ESCANES, with other Lords of Tyre
HELICANUS: You shall not need, my fellow peers of Tyre,
HELICANUS: Further to question me of your king's departure:
HELICANUS: His seal'd commission, left in trust with me,
HELICANUS: Doth speak sufficiently he's gone to travel.
THALIARD: [Aside]  How! the king gone!
HELICANUS: If further yet you will be satisfied,
HELICANUS: Why, as it were unlicensed of your loves,
HELICANUS: He would depart, I'll give some light unto you.
HELICANUS: Being at Antioch--
THALIARD: [Aside]          What from Antioch?
HELICANUS: Royal Antiochus--on what cause I know not--
HELICANUS: Took some displeasure at him, at least he judged so:
HELICANUS: And doubting lest that he had err'd or sinn'd,
HELICANUS: To show his sorrow, he'ld correct himself,
HELICANUS: So puts himself unto the shipman's toil,
HELICANUS: With whom each minute threatens life or death.
THALIARD: [Aside]  Well, I perceive
THALIARD: I shall not be hang'd now, although I would,
THALIARD: But since he's gone, the king's seas must please:
THALIARD: He 'scaped the land, to perish at the sea.
THALIARD: I'll present myself. Peace to the lords of Tyre!
HELICANUS: Lord Thaliard from Antiochus is welcome.
THALIARD: From him I come
THALIARD: With message unto princely Pericles,
THALIARD: But since my landing I have understood
THALIARD: Your lord has betook himself to unknown travels,
THALIARD: My message must return from whence it came.
HELICANUS: We have no reason to desire it,
HELICANUS: Commended to our master, not to us:
HELICANUS: Yet, ere you shall depart, this we desire,
HELICANUS: As friends to Antioch, we may feast in Tyre.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Tarsus. A room in the Governor's house.
NARRATOR: Enter CLEON, the governor of Tarsus, with DIONYZA, and others
CLEON: My Dionyza, shall we rest us here,
CLEON: And by relating tales of others' griefs,
CLEON: See if 'twill teach us to forget our own?
DIONYZA: That were to blow at fire in hope to quench it,
DIONYZA: For who digs hills because they do aspire
DIONYZA: Throws down one mountain to cast up a higher.
DIONYZA: O my distressed lord, even such our griefs are,
DIONYZA: Here they're but felt, and seen with mischief's eyes,
DIONYZA: But like to groves, being topp'd, they higher rise.
CLEON: O Dionyza,
CLEON: Who wanteth food, and will not say he wants it,
CLEON: Or can conceal his hunger till he famish?
CLEON: Our tongues and sorrows do sound deep
CLEON: Our woes into the air, our eyes do weep,
CLEON: Till tongues fetch breath that may proclaim them louder,
CLEON: That, if heaven slumber while their creatures want,
CLEON: They may awake their helps to comfort them.
CLEON: I'll then discourse our woes, felt several years,
CLEON: And wanting breath to speak help me with tears.
DIONYZA: I'll do my best, sir.
CLEON: This Tarsus, o'er which I have the government,
CLEON: A city on whom plenty held full hand,
CLEON: For riches strew'd herself even in the streets,
CLEON: Whose towers bore heads so high they kiss'd the clouds,
CLEON: And strangers ne'er beheld but wondered at,
CLEON: Whose men and dames so jetted and adorn'd,
CLEON: Like one another's glass to trim them by:
CLEON: Their tables were stored full, to glad the sight,
CLEON: And not so much to feed on as delight,
CLEON: All poverty was scorn'd, and pride so great,
CLEON: The name of help grew odious to repeat.
DIONYZA: O, 'tis too true.
CLEON: But see what heaven can do! By this our change,
CLEON: These mouths, who but of late, earth, sea, and air,
CLEON: Were all too little to content and please,
CLEON: Although they gave their creatures in abundance,
CLEON: As houses are defiled for want of use,
CLEON: They are now starved for want of exercise:
CLEON: Those palates who, not yet two summers younger,
CLEON: Must have inventions to delight the taste,
CLEON: Would now be glad of bread, and beg for it:
CLEON: Those mothers who, to nousle up their babes,
CLEON: Thought nought too curious, are ready now
CLEON: To eat those little darlings whom they loved.
CLEON: So sharp are hunger's teeth, that man and wife
CLEON: Draw lots who first shall die to lengthen life:
CLEON: Here stands a lord, and there a lady weeping,
CLEON: Here many sink, yet those which see them fall
CLEON: Have scarce strength left to give them burial.
CLEON: Is not this true?
DIONYZA: Our cheeks and hollow eyes do witness it.
CLEON: O, let those cities that of plenty's cup
CLEON: And her prosperities so largely taste,
CLEON: With their superfluous riots, hear these tears!
CLEON: The misery of Tarsus may be theirs.
NARRATOR: Enter a Lord
Lord: Where's the lord governor?
CLEON: Here.
CLEON: Speak out thy sorrows which thou bring'st in haste,
CLEON: For comfort is too far for us to expect.
Lord: We have descried, upon our neighbouring shore,
Lord: A portly sail of ships make hitherward.
CLEON: I thought as much.
CLEON: One sorrow never comes but brings an heir,
CLEON: That may succeed as his inheritor,
CLEON: And so in ours: some neighbouring nation,
CLEON: Taking advantage of our misery,
CLEON: Hath stuff'd these hollow vessels with their power,
CLEON: To beat us down, the which are down already,
CLEON: And make a conquest of unhappy me,
CLEON: Whereas no glory's got to overcome.
Lord: That's the least fear, for, by the semblance
Lord: Of their white flags display'd, they bring us peace,
Lord: And come to us as favourers, not as foes.
CLEON: Thou speak'st like him's untutor'd to repeat:
CLEON: Who makes the fairest show means most deceit.
CLEON: But bring they what they will and what they can,
CLEON: What need we fear?
CLEON: The ground's the lowest, and we are half way there.
CLEON: Go tell their general we attend him here,
CLEON: To know for what he comes, and whence he comes,
CLEON: And what he craves.
Lord: I go, my lord.
NARRATOR: Exit
CLEON: Welcome is peace, if he on peace consist,
CLEON: If wars, we are unable to resist.
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES with Attendants
PERICLES: Lord governor, for so we hear you are,
PERICLES: Let not our ships and number of our men
PERICLES: Be like a beacon fired to amaze your eyes.
PERICLES: We have heard your miseries as far as Tyre,
PERICLES: And seen the desolation of your streets:
PERICLES: Nor come we to add sorrow to your tears,
PERICLES: But to relieve them of their heavy load,
PERICLES: And these our ships, you happily may think
PERICLES: Are like the Trojan horse was stuff'd within
PERICLES: With bloody veins, expecting overthrow,
PERICLES: Are stored with corn to make your needy bread,
PERICLES: And give them life whom hunger starved half dead.
All: The gods of Greece protect you!
All: And we'll pray for you.
PERICLES: Arise, I pray you, rise:
PERICLES: We do not look for reverence, but to love,
PERICLES: And harbourage for ourself, our ships, and men.
CLEON: The which when any shall not gratify,
CLEON: Or pay you with unthankfulness in thought,
CLEON: Be it our wives, our children, or ourselves,
CLEON: The curse of heaven and men succeed their evils!
CLEON: Till when,--the which I hope shall ne'er be seen,--
CLEON: Your grace is welcome to our town and us.
PERICLES: Which welcome we'll accept, feast here awhile,
PERICLES: Until our stars that frown lend us a smile.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT II
NARRATOR: Enter GOWER
GOWER: Here have you seen a mighty king
GOWER: His child, I wis, to incest bring,
GOWER: A better prince and benign lord,
GOWER: That will prove awful both in deed and word.
GOWER: Be quiet then as men should be,
GOWER: Till he hath pass'd necessity.
GOWER: I'll show you those in troubles reign,
GOWER: Losing a mite, a mountain gain.
GOWER: The good in conversation,
GOWER: To whom I give my benison,
GOWER: Is still at Tarsus, where each man
GOWER: Thinks all is writ he speken can,
GOWER: And, to remember what he does,
GOWER: Build his statue to make him glorious:
GOWER: But tidings to the contrary
GOWER: Are brought your eyes, what need speak I?
GOWER: DUMB SHOW.
GOWER: Enter at one door PERICLES talking with CLEON, all  the train with them. Enter at another door a  Gentleman, with a letter to PERICLES, PERICLES  shows the letter to CLEON, gives the Messenger a  reward, and knights him. Exit PERICLES at one door, and CLEON at another
GOWER: Good Helicane, that stay'd at home,
GOWER: Not to eat honey like a drone
GOWER: From others' labours, for though he strive
GOWER: To killen bad, keep good alive,
GOWER: And to fulfil his prince' desire,
GOWER: Sends word of all that haps in Tyre:
GOWER: How Thaliard came full bent with sin
GOWER: And had intent to murder him,
GOWER: And that in Tarsus was not best
GOWER: Longer for him to make his rest.
GOWER: He, doing so, put forth to seas,
GOWER: Where when men been, there's seldom ease,
GOWER: For now the wind begins to blow,
GOWER: Thunder above and deeps below
GOWER: Make such unquiet, that the ship
GOWER: Should house him safe is wreck'd and split,
GOWER: And he, good prince, having all lost,
GOWER: By waves from coast to coast is tost:
GOWER: All perishen of man, of pelf,
GOWER: Ne aught escapen but himself,
GOWER: Till fortune, tired with doing bad,
GOWER: Threw him ashore, to give him glad:
GOWER: And here he comes. What shall be next,
GOWER: Pardon old Gower,--this longs the text.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Pentapolis. An open place by the sea-side.
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES, wet
PERICLES: Yet cease your ire, you angry stars of heaven!
PERICLES: Wind, rain, and thunder, remember, earthly man
PERICLES: Is but a substance that must yield to you,
PERICLES: And I, as fits my nature, do obey you:
PERICLES: Alas, the sea hath cast me on the rocks,
PERICLES: Wash'd me from shore to shore, and left me breath
PERICLES: Nothing to think on but ensuing death:
PERICLES: Let it suffice the greatness of your powers
PERICLES: To have bereft a prince of all his fortunes,
PERICLES: And having thrown him from your watery grave,
PERICLES: Here to have death in peace is all he'll crave.
NARRATOR: Enter three FISHERMEN
First Fisherman: What, ho, Pilch!
Second Fisherman: Ha, come and bring away the nets!
First Fisherman: What, Patch-breech, I say!
Third Fisherman: What say you, master?
First Fisherman: Look how thou stirrest now! come away, or I'll
First Fisherman: fetch thee with a wanion.
Third Fisherman: Faith, master, I am thinking of the poor men that
Third Fisherman: were cast away before us even now.
First Fisherman: Alas, poor souls, it grieved my heart to hear what
First Fisherman: pitiful cries they made to us to help them, when,
First Fisherman: well-a-day, we could scarce help ourselves.
Third Fisherman: Nay, master, said not I as much when I saw the
Third Fisherman: porpus how he bounced and tumbled? they say
Third Fisherman: they're half fish, half flesh: a plague on them,
Third Fisherman: they ne'er come but I look to be washed. Master, I
Third Fisherman: marvel how the fishes live in the sea.
First Fisherman: Why, as men do a-land, the great ones eat up the
First Fisherman: little ones: I can compare our rich misers to
First Fisherman: nothing so fitly as to a whale, a' plays and
First Fisherman: tumbles, driving the poor fry before him, and at
First Fisherman: last devours them all at a mouthful: such whales
First Fisherman: have I heard on o' the land, who never leave gaping
First Fisherman: till they've swallowed the whole parish, church,
First Fisherman: steeple, bells, and all.
PERICLES: [Aside]  A pretty moral.
Third Fisherman: But, master, if I had been the sexton, I would have
Third Fisherman: been that day in the belfry.
Second Fisherman: Why, man?
Third Fisherman: Because he should have swallowed me too: and when I
Third Fisherman: had been in his belly, I would have kept such a
Third Fisherman: jangling of the bells, that he should never have
Third Fisherman: left, till he cast bells, steeple, church, and
Third Fisherman: parish up again. But if the good King Simonides
Third Fisherman: were of my mind,--
PERICLES: [Aside]  Simonides!
Third Fisherman: We would purge the land of these drones, that rob
Third Fisherman: the bee of her honey.
PERICLES: [Aside]  How from the finny subject of the sea
PERICLES: These fishers tell the infirmities of men,
PERICLES: And from their watery empire recollect
PERICLES: All that may men approve or men detect!
PERICLES: Peace be at your labour, honest fishermen.
Second Fisherman: Honest! good fellow, what's that? If it be a day
Second Fisherman: fits you, search out of the calendar, and nobody
Second Fisherman: look after it.
PERICLES: May see the sea hath cast upon your coast.
Second Fisherman: What a drunken knave was the sea to cast thee in our
Second Fisherman: way!
PERICLES: A man whom both the waters and the wind,
PERICLES: In that vast tennis-court, have made the ball
PERICLES: For them to play upon, entreats you pity him:
PERICLES: He asks of you, that never used to beg.
First Fisherman: No, friend, cannot you beg? Here's them in our
First Fisherman: country Greece gets more with begging than we can do
First Fisherman: with working.
Second Fisherman: Canst thou catch any fishes, then?
PERICLES: I never practised it.
Second Fisherman: Nay, then thou wilt starve, sure, for here's nothing
Second Fisherman: to be got now-a-days, unless thou canst fish for't.
PERICLES: What I have been I have forgot to know,
PERICLES: But what I am, want teaches me to think on:
PERICLES: A man throng'd up with cold: my veins are chill,
PERICLES: And have no more of life than may suffice
PERICLES: To give my tongue that heat to ask your help,
PERICLES: Which if you shall refuse, when I am dead,
PERICLES: For that I am a man, pray see me buried.
First Fisherman: Die quoth-a? Now gods forbid! I have a gown here,
First Fisherman: come, put it on, keep thee warm. Now, afore me, a
First Fisherman: handsome fellow! Come, thou shalt go home, and
First Fisherman: we'll have flesh for holidays, fish for
First Fisherman: fasting-days, and moreo'er puddings and flap-jacks,
First Fisherman: and thou shalt be welcome.
PERICLES: I thank you, sir.
Second Fisherman: Hark you, my friend, you said you could not beg.
PERICLES: I did but crave.
Second Fisherman: But crave! Then I'll turn craver too, and so I
Second Fisherman: shall 'scape whipping.
PERICLES: Why, are all your beggars whipped, then?
Second Fisherman: O, not all, my friend, not all, for if all your
Second Fisherman: beggars were whipped, I would wish no better office
Second Fisherman: than to be beadle. But, master, I'll go draw up the
Second Fisherman: net.
NARRATOR: Exit with Third Fisherman
PERICLES: [Aside]  How well this honest mirth becomes their labour!
First Fisherman: Hark you, sir, do you know where ye are?
PERICLES: Not well.
First Fisherman: Why, I'll tell you: this is called Pentapolis, and
First Fisherman: our king the good Simonides.
PERICLES: The good King Simonides, do you call him.
First Fisherman: Ay, sir, and he deserves so to be called for his
First Fisherman: peaceable reign and good government.
PERICLES: He is a happy king, since he gains from his subjects
PERICLES: the name of good by his government. How far is his
PERICLES: court distant from this shore?
First Fisherman: Marry, sir, half a day's journey: and I'll tell
First Fisherman: you, he hath a fair daughter, and to-morrow is her
First Fisherman: birth-day, and there are princes and knights come
First Fisherman: from all parts of the world to just and tourney for her love.
PERICLES: Were my fortunes equal to my desires, I could wish
PERICLES: to make one there.
First Fisherman: O, sir, things must be as they may, and what a man
First Fisherman: cannot get, he may lawfully deal for--his wife's soul.
NARRATOR: Re-enter Second and Third Fishermen, drawing up a net
Second Fisherman: Help, master, help! here's a fish hangs in the net,
Second Fisherman: like a poor man's right in the law, 'twill hardly
Second Fisherman: come out. Ha! bots on't, 'tis come at last, and
Second Fisherman: 'tis turned to a rusty armour.
PERICLES: An armour, friends! I pray you, let me see it.
PERICLES: Thanks, fortune, yet, that, after all my crosses,
PERICLES: Thou givest me somewhat to repair myself,
PERICLES: And though it was mine own, part of my heritage,
PERICLES: Which my dead father did bequeath to me.
PERICLES: With this strict charge, even as he left his life,
PERICLES: 'Keep it, my Pericles, it hath been a shield
PERICLES: Twixt me and death,'--and pointed to this brace,--
PERICLES: 'For that it saved me, keep it, in like necessity--
PERICLES: The which the gods protect thee from!--may
PERICLES: defend thee.'
PERICLES: It kept where I kept, I so dearly loved it,
PERICLES: Till the rough seas, that spare not any man,
PERICLES: Took it in rage, though calm'd have given't again:
PERICLES: I thank thee for't: my shipwreck now's no ill,
PERICLES: Since I have here my father's gift in's will.
First Fisherman: What mean you, sir?
PERICLES: To beg of you, kind friends, this coat of worth,
PERICLES: For it was sometime target to a king,
PERICLES: I know it by this mark. He loved me dearly,
PERICLES: And for his sake I wish the having of it,
PERICLES: And that you'ld guide me to your sovereign's court,
PERICLES: Where with it I may appear a gentleman,
PERICLES: And if that ever my low fortune's better,
PERICLES: I'll pay your bounties, till then rest your debtor.
First Fisherman: Why, wilt thou tourney for the lady?
PERICLES: I'll show the virtue I have borne in arms.
First Fisherman: Why, do 'e take it, and the gods give thee good on't!
Second Fisherman: Ay, but hark you, my friend, 'twas we that made up
Second Fisherman: this garment through the rough seams of the waters:
Second Fisherman: there are certain condolements, certain vails. I
Second Fisherman: hope, sir, if you thrive, you'll remember from
Second Fisherman: whence you had it.
PERICLES: Believe 't, I will.
PERICLES: By your furtherance I am clothed in steel,
PERICLES: And, spite of all the rapture of the sea,
PERICLES: This jewel holds his building on my arm:
PERICLES: Unto thy value I will mount myself
PERICLES: Upon a courser, whose delightful steps
PERICLES: Shall make the gazer joy to see him tread.
PERICLES: Only, my friend, I yet am unprovided
PERICLES: Of a pair of bases.
Second Fisherman: We'll sure provide: thou shalt have my best gown to
Second Fisherman: make thee a pair, and I'll bring thee to the court myself.
PERICLES: Then honour be but a goal to my will,
PERICLES: This day I'll rise, or else add ill to ill.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The same. A public way or platform leading to the
PERICLES: lists. A pavilion by the side of it for the
PERICLES: reception of King, Princess, Lords,  and c.
NARRATOR: Enter SIMONIDES, THAISA, Lords, and Attendants
SIMONIDES: Are the knights ready to begin the triumph?
First Lord: They are, my liege,
First Lord: And stay your coming to present themselves.
SIMONIDES: Return them, we are ready, and our daughter,
SIMONIDES: In honour of whose birth these triumphs are,
SIMONIDES: Sits here, like beauty's child, whom nature gat
SIMONIDES: For men to see, and seeing wonder at.
NARRATOR: Exit a Lord
THAISA: It pleaseth you, my royal father, to express
THAISA: My commendations great, whose merit's less.
SIMONIDES: It's fit it should be so, for princes are
SIMONIDES: A model which heaven makes like to itself:
SIMONIDES: As jewels lose their glory if neglected,
SIMONIDES: So princes their renowns if not respected.
SIMONIDES: 'Tis now your honour, daughter, to explain
SIMONIDES: The labour of each knight in his device.
THAISA: Which, to preserve mine honour, I'll perform.
THAISA: Enter a Knight, he passes over, and his Squire presents his shield to the Princess
SIMONIDES: Who is the first that doth prefer himself?
THAISA: A knight of Sparta, my renowned father,
THAISA: And the device he bears upon his shield
THAISA: Is a black Ethiope reaching at the sun
THAISA: The word, 'Lux tua vita mihi.'
SIMONIDES: He loves you well that holds his life of you.
NARRATOR: The Second Knight passes over
SIMONIDES: Who is the second that presents himself?
THAISA: A prince of Macedon, my royal father,
THAISA: And the device he bears upon his shield
THAISA: Is an arm'd knight that's conquer'd by a lady,
THAISA: The motto thus, in Spanish, 'Piu por dulzura que por fuerza.'
NARRATOR: The Third Knight passes over
SIMONIDES: And what's the third?
THAISA: The third of Antioch,
THAISA: And his device, a wreath of chivalry,
THAISA: The word, 'Me pompae provexit apex.'
NARRATOR: The Fourth Knight passes over
SIMONIDES: What is the fourth?
THAISA: A burning torch that's turned upside down,
THAISA: The word, 'Quod me alit, me extinguit.'
SIMONIDES: Which shows that beauty hath his power and will,
SIMONIDES: Which can as well inflame as it can kill.
NARRATOR: The Fifth Knight passes over
THAISA: The fifth, an hand environed with clouds,
THAISA: Holding out gold that's by the touchstone tried,
THAISA: The motto thus, 'Sic spectanda fides.'
NARRATOR: The Sixth Knight, PERICLES, passes over
SIMONIDES: And what's
SIMONIDES: The sixth and last, the which the knight himself
SIMONIDES: With such a graceful courtesy deliver'd?
THAISA: He seems to be a stranger, but his present is
THAISA: A wither'd branch, that's only green at top,
THAISA: The motto, 'In hac spe vivo.'
SIMONIDES: A pretty moral,
SIMONIDES: From the dejected state wherein he is,
SIMONIDES: He hopes by you his fortunes yet may flourish.
First Lord: He had need mean better than his outward show
First Lord: Can any way speak in his just commend,
First Lord: For by his rusty outside he appears
First Lord: To have practised more the whipstock than the lance.
Second Lord: He well may be a stranger, for he comes
Second Lord: To an honour'd triumph strangely furnished.
Third Lord: And on set purpose let his armour rust
Third Lord: Until this day, to scour it in the dust.
SIMONIDES: Opinion's but a fool, that makes us scan
SIMONIDES: The outward habit by the inward man.
SIMONIDES: But stay, the knights are coming: we will withdraw
SIMONIDES: Into the gallery.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: Great shouts within and all cry 'The mean knight!'
NARRATOR: SCENE III. The same. A hall of state: a banquet prepared.
NARRATOR: Enter SIMONIDES, THAISA, Lords, Attendants, and Knights, from tilting
SIMONIDES: Knights,
SIMONIDES: To say you're welcome were superfluous.
SIMONIDES: To place upon the volume of your deeds,
SIMONIDES: As in a title-page, your worth in arms,
SIMONIDES: Were more than you expect, or more than's fit,
SIMONIDES: Since every worth in show commends itself.
SIMONIDES: Prepare for mirth, for mirth becomes a feast:
SIMONIDES: You are princes and my guests.
THAISA: But you, my knight and guest,
THAISA: To whom this wreath of victory I give,
THAISA: And crown you king of this day's happiness.
PERICLES: 'Tis more by fortune, lady, than by merit.
SIMONIDES: Call it by what you will, the day is yours,
SIMONIDES: And here, I hope, is none that envies it.
SIMONIDES: In framing an artist, art hath thus decreed,
SIMONIDES: To make some good, but others to exceed,
SIMONIDES: And you are her labour'd scholar. Come, queen o'
SIMONIDES: the feast,--
SIMONIDES: For, daughter, so you are,--here take your place:
SIMONIDES: Marshal the rest, as they deserve their grace.
KNIGHTS: We are honour'd much by good Simonides.
SIMONIDES: Your presence glads our days: honour we love,
SIMONIDES: For who hates honour hates the gods above.

PERICLES: Some other is more fit.
First Knight: Contend not, sir, for we are gentlemen
First Knight: That neither in our hearts nor outward eyes
First Knight: Envy the great nor do the low despise.
PERICLES: You are right courteous knights.
SIMONIDES: Sit, sir, sit.
PERICLES: By Jove, I wonder, that is king of thoughts,
PERICLES: These cates resist me, she but thought upon.
THAISA: By Juno, that is queen of marriage,
THAISA: All viands that I eat do seem unsavoury.
THAISA: Wishing him my meat. Sure, he's a gallant gentleman.
SIMONIDES: He's but a country gentleman,
SIMONIDES: Has done no more than other knights have done,
SIMONIDES: Has broken a staff or so, so let it pass.
THAISA: To me he seems like diamond to glass.
PERICLES: Yon king's to me like to my father's picture,
PERICLES: Which tells me in that glory once he was,
PERICLES: Had princes sit, like stars, about his throne,
PERICLES: And he the sun, for them to reverence,
PERICLES: None that beheld him, but, like lesser lights,
PERICLES: Did vail their crowns to his supremacy:
PERICLES: Where now his son's like a glow-worm in the night,
PERICLES: The which hath fire in darkness, none in light:
PERICLES: Whereby I see that Time's the king of men,
PERICLES: He's both their parent, and he is their grave,
PERICLES: And gives them what he will, not what they crave.
SIMONIDES: What, are you merry, knights?
Knights: Who can be other in this royal presence?
SIMONIDES: Here, with a cup that's stored unto the brim,--
SIMONIDES: As you do love, fill to your mistress' lips,--
SIMONIDES: We drink this health to you.
KNIGHTS: We thank your grace.
SIMONIDES: Yet pause awhile:
SIMONIDES: Yon knight doth sit too melancholy,
SIMONIDES: As if the entertainment in our court
SIMONIDES: Had not a show might countervail his worth.
SIMONIDES: Note it not you, Thaisa?
THAISA: What is it
THAISA: To me, my father?
SIMONIDES: O, attend, my daughter:
SIMONIDES: Princes in this should live like gods above,
SIMONIDES: Who freely give to every one that comes
SIMONIDES: To honour them:
SIMONIDES: And princes not doin g so are like to gnats,
SIMONIDES: Which make a sound, but kill'd are wonder'd at.
SIMONIDES: Therefore to make his entrance more sweet,
SIMONIDES: Here, say we drink this standing-bowl of wine to him.
THAISA: Alas, my father, it befits not me
THAISA: Unto a stranger knight to be so bold:
THAISA: He may my proffer take for an offence,
THAISA: Since men take women's gifts for impudence.
SIMONIDES: How!
SIMONIDES: Do as I bid you, or you'll move me else.
THAISA: [Aside]  Now, by the gods, he could not please me better.
SIMONIDES: And furthermore tell him, we desire to know of him,
SIMONIDES: Of whence he is, his name and parentage.
THAISA: The king my father, sir, has drunk to you.
PERICLES: I thank him.
THAISA: Wishing it so much blood unto your life.
PERICLES: I thank both him and you, and pledge him freely.
THAISA: And further he desires to know of you,
THAISA: Of whence you are, your name and parentage.
PERICLES: A gentleman of Tyre, my name, Pericles,
PERICLES: My education been in arts and arms,
PERICLES: Who, looking for adventures in the world,
PERICLES: Was by the rough seas reft of ships and men,
PERICLES: And after shipwreck driven upon this shore.
THAISA: He thanks your grace, names himself Pericles,
THAISA: A gentleman of Tyre,
THAISA: Who only by misfortune of the seas
THAISA: Bereft of ships and men, cast on this shore.
SIMONIDES: Now, by the gods, I pity his misfortune,
SIMONIDES: And will awake him from his melancholy.
SIMONIDES: Come, gentlemen, we sit too long on trifles,
SIMONIDES: And waste the time, which looks for other revels.
SIMONIDES: Even in your armours, as you are address'd,
SIMONIDES: Will very well become a soldier's dance.
SIMONIDES: I will not have excuse, with saying this
SIMONIDES: Loud music is too harsh for ladies' heads,
SIMONIDES: Since they love men in arms as well as beds.
NARRATOR: The Knights dance
SIMONIDES: So, this was well ask'd,'twas so well perform'd.
SIMONIDES: Come, sir,
SIMONIDES: Here is a lady that wants breathing too:
SIMONIDES: And I have heard, you knights of Tyre
SIMONIDES: Are excellent in making ladies trip,
SIMONIDES: And that their measures are as excellent.
PERICLES: In those that practise them they are, my lord.
SIMONIDES: O, that's as much as you would be denied
SIMONIDES: Of your fair courtesy.
NARRATOR: The Knights and Ladies dance
SIMONIDES: Unclasp, unclasp:
SIMONIDES: Thanks, gentlemen, to all, all have done well.
NARRATOR: To PERICLES
SIMONIDES: But you the best. Pages and lights, to conduct
SIMONIDES: These knights unto their several lodgings!
NARRATOR: To PERICLES
SIMONIDES: Yours, sir,
SIMONIDES: We have given order to be next our own.
PERICLES: I am at your grace's pleasure.
SIMONIDES: Princes, it is too late to talk of love,
SIMONIDES: And that's the mark I know you level at:
SIMONIDES: Therefore each one betake him to his rest,
SIMONIDES: To-morrow all for speeding do their best.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Tyre. A room in the Governor's house.
NARRATOR: Enter HELICANUS and ESCANES
HELICANUS: No, Escanes, know this of me,
HELICANUS: Antiochus from incest lived not free:
HELICANUS: For which, the most high gods not minding longer
HELICANUS: To withhold the vengeance that they had in store,
HELICANUS: Due to this heinous capital offence,
HELICANUS: Even in the height and pride of all his glory,
HELICANUS: When he was seated in a chariot
HELICANUS: Of an inestimable value, and his daughter with him,
HELICANUS: A fire from heaven came and shrivell'd up
HELICANUS: Their bodies, even to loathing, for they so stunk,
HELICANUS: That all those eyes adored them ere their fall
HELICANUS: Scorn now their hand should give them burial.
ESCANES: 'Twas very strange.
HELICANUS: And yet but justice, for though
HELICANUS: This king were great, his greatness was no guard
HELICANUS: To bar heaven's shaft, but sin had his reward.
ESCANES: 'Tis very true.
NARRATOR: Enter two or three Lords
First Lord: See, not a man in private conference
First Lord: Or council has respect with him but he.
Second Lord: It shall no longer grieve without reproof.
Third Lord: And cursed be he that will not second it.
First Lord: Follow me, then. Lord Helicane, a word.
HELICANUS: With me? and welcome: happy day, my lords.
First Lord: Know that our griefs are risen to the top,
First Lord: And now at length they overflow their banks.
HELICANUS: Your griefs! for what? wrong not your prince you love.
First Lord: Wrong not yourself, then, noble Helicane,
First Lord: But if the prince do live, let us salute him,
First Lord: Or know what ground's made happy by his breath.
First Lord: If in the world he live, we'll seek him out,
First Lord: If in his grave he rest, we'll find him there,
First Lord: And be resolved he lives to govern us,
First Lord: Or dead, give's cause to mourn his funeral,
First Lord: And leave us to our free election.
Second Lord: Whose death indeed's the strongest in our censure:
Second Lord: And knowing this kingdom is without a head,--
Second Lord: Like goodly buildings left without a roof
Second Lord: Soon fall to ruin,--your noble self,
Second Lord: That best know how to rule and how to reign,
Second Lord: We thus submit unto,--our sovereign.
All: Live, noble Helicane!
HELICANUS: For honour's cause, forbear your suffrages:
HELICANUS: If that you love Prince Pericles, forbear.
HELICANUS: Take I your wish, I leap into the seas,
HELICANUS: Where's hourly trouble for a minute's ease.
HELICANUS: A twelvemonth longer, let me entreat you to
HELICANUS: Forbear the absence of your king:
HELICANUS: If in which time expired, he not return,
HELICANUS: I shall with aged patience bear your yoke.
HELICANUS: But if I cannot win you to this love,
HELICANUS: Go search like nobles, like noble subjects,
HELICANUS: And in your search spend your adventurous worth,
HELICANUS: Whom if you find, and win unto return,
HELICANUS: You shall like diamonds sit about his crown.
First Lord: To wisdom he's a fool that will not yield,
First Lord: And since Lord Helicane enjoineth us,
First Lord: We with our travels will endeavour us.
HELICANUS: Then you love us, we you, and we'll clasp hands:
HELICANUS: When peers thus knit, a kingdom ever stands.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE V. Pentapolis. A room in the palace.
NARRATOR: Enter SIMONIDES, reading a letter, at one door: the Knights meet him
First Knight: Good morrow to the good Simonides.
SIMONIDES: Knights, from my daughter this I let you know,
SIMONIDES: That for this twelvemonth she'll not undertake
SIMONIDES: A married life.
SIMONIDES: Her reason to herself is only known,
SIMONIDES: Which yet from her by no means can I get.
Second Knight: May we not get access to her, my lord?
SIMONIDES: 'Faith, by no means, she has so strictly tied
SIMONIDES: Her to her chamber, that 'tis impossible.
SIMONIDES: One twelve moons more she'll wear Diana's livery,
SIMONIDES: This by the eye of Cynthia hath she vow'd
SIMONIDES: And on her virgin honour will not break it.
Third Knight: Loath to bid farewell, we take our leaves.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Knights
SIMONIDES: So,
SIMONIDES: They are well dispatch'd, now to my daughter's letter:
SIMONIDES: She tells me here, she'd wed the stranger knight,
SIMONIDES: Or never more to view nor day nor light.
SIMONIDES: 'Tis well, mistress, your choice agrees with mine,
SIMONIDES: I like that well: nay, how absolute she's in't,
SIMONIDES: Not minding whether I dislike or no!
SIMONIDES: Well, I do commend her choice,
SIMONIDES: And will no longer have it be delay'd.
SIMONIDES: Soft! here he comes: I must dissemble it.
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES
PERICLES: All fortune to the good Simonides!
SIMONIDES: To you as much, sir! I am beholding to you
SIMONIDES: For your sweet music this last night: I do
SIMONIDES: Protest my ears were never better fed
SIMONIDES: With such delightful pleasing harmony.
PERICLES: It is your grace's pleasure to commend,
PERICLES: Not my desert.
SIMONIDES: Sir, you are music's master.
PERICLES: The worst of all her scholars, my good lord.
SIMONIDES: Let me ask you one thing:
SIMONIDES: What do you think of my daughter, sir?
PERICLES: A most virtuous princess.
SIMONIDES: And she is fair too, is she not?
PERICLES: As a fair day in summer, wondrous fair.
SIMONIDES: Sir, my daughter thinks very well of you,
SIMONIDES: Ay, so well, that you must be her master,
SIMONIDES: And she will be your scholar: therefore look to it.
PERICLES: I am unworthy for her schoolmaster.
SIMONIDES: She thinks not so, peruse this writing else.
PERICLES: [Aside]  What's here?
PERICLES: A letter, that she loves the knight of Tyre!
PERICLES: 'Tis the king's subtlety to have my life.
PERICLES: O, seek not to entrap me, gracious lord,
PERICLES: A stranger and distressed gentleman,
PERICLES: That never aim'd so high to love your daughter,
PERICLES: But bent all offices to honour her.
SIMONIDES: Thou hast bewitch'd my daughter, and thou art
SIMONIDES: A villain.
PERICLES: By the gods, I have not:
PERICLES: Never did thought of mine levy offence,
PERICLES: Nor never did my actions yet commence
PERICLES: A deed might gain her love or your displeasure.
SIMONIDES: Traitor, thou liest.
PERICLES: Traitor!
SIMONIDES: Ay, traitor.
PERICLES: Even in his throat--unless it be the king--
PERICLES: That calls me traitor, I return the lie.
SIMONIDES: [Aside]  Now, by the gods, I do applaud his courage.
PERICLES: My actions are as noble as my thoughts,
PERICLES: That never relish'd of a base descent.
PERICLES: I came unto your court for honour's cause,
PERICLES: And not to be a rebel to her state,
PERICLES: And he that otherwise accounts of me,
PERICLES: This sword shall prove he's honour's enemy.
SIMONIDES: No?
SIMONIDES: Here comes my daughter, she can witness it.
NARRATOR: Enter THAISA
PERICLES: Then, as you are as virtuous as fair,
PERICLES: Resolve your angry father, if my tongue
PERICLES: Did ere solicit, or my hand subscribe
PERICLES: To any syllable that made love to you.
THAISA: Why, sir, say if you had,
THAISA: Who takes offence at that would make me glad?
SIMONIDES: Yea, mistress, are you so peremptory?
NARRATOR: Aside
SIMONIDES: I am glad on't with all my heart.--
SIMONIDES: I'll tame you, I'll bring you in subjection.
SIMONIDES: Will you, not having my consent,
SIMONIDES: Bestow your love and your affections
SIMONIDES: Upon a stranger?
NARRATOR: Aside
SIMONIDES: who, for aught I know,
SIMONIDES: May be, nor can I think the contrary,
SIMONIDES: As great in blood as I myself.--
SIMONIDES: Therefore hear you, mistress, either frame
SIMONIDES: Your will to mine,--and you, sir, hear you,
SIMONIDES: Either be ruled by me, or I will make you--
SIMONIDES: Man and wife:
SIMONIDES: Nay, come, your hands and lips must seal it too:
SIMONIDES: And being join'd, I'll thus your hopes destroy,
SIMONIDES: And for a further grief,--God give you joy!--
SIMONIDES: What, are you both pleased?
THAISA: Yes, if you love me, sir.
PERICLES: Even as my life, or blood that fosters it.
SIMONIDES: What, are you both agreed?
BOTH: Yes, if it please your majesty.
SIMONIDES: It pleaseth me so well, that I will see you wed,
SIMONIDES: And then with what haste you can get you to bed.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: Enter GOWER
GOWER: Now sleep y-slaked hath the rout,
GOWER: No din but snores the house about,
GOWER: Made louder by the o'er-fed breast
GOWER: Of this most pompous marriage-feast.
GOWER: The cat, with eyne of burning coal,
GOWER: Now crouches fore the mouse's hole,
GOWER: And crickets sing at the oven's mouth,
GOWER: E'er the blither for their drouth.
GOWER: Hymen hath brought the bride to bed.
GOWER: Where, by the loss of maidenhead,
GOWER: A babe is moulded. Be attent,
GOWER: And time that is so briefly spent
GOWER: With your fine fancies quaintly eche:
GOWER: What's dumb in show I'll plain with speech.
GOWER: DUMB SHOW.
GOWER: Enter, PERICLES and SIMONIDES at one door, with  Attendants, a Messenger meets them, kneels, and  gives PERICLES a letter: PERICLES shows it  SIMONIDES, the Lords kneel to him. Then enter  THAISA with child, with LYCHORIDA a nurse. The  KING shows her the letter, she rejoices: she and  PERICLES takes leave of her father, and depart with  LYCHORIDA and their Attendants. Then exeunt SIMONIDES and the rest
GOWER: By many a dern and painful perch
GOWER: Of Pericles the careful search,
GOWER: By the four opposing coigns
GOWER: Which the world together joins,
GOWER: Is made with all due diligence
GOWER: That horse and sail and high expense
GOWER: Can stead the quest. At last from Tyre,
GOWER: Fame answering the most strange inquire,
GOWER: To the court of King Simonides
GOWER: Are letters brought, the tenor these:
GOWER: Antiochus and his daughter dead,
GOWER: The men of Tyrus on the head
GOWER: Of Helicanus would set on
GOWER: The crown of Tyre, but he will none:
GOWER: The mutiny he there hastes t' oppress,
GOWER: Says to 'em, if King Pericles
GOWER: Come not home in twice six moons,
GOWER: He, obedient to their dooms,
GOWER: Will take the crown. The sum of this,
GOWER: Brought hither to Pentapolis,
GOWER: Y-ravished the regions round,
GOWER: And every one with claps can sound,
GOWER: 'Our heir-apparent is a king!
GOWER: Who dream'd, who thought of such a thing?'
GOWER: Brief, he must hence depart to Tyre:
GOWER: His queen with child makes her desire--
GOWER: Which who shall cross?--along to go:
GOWER: Omit we all their dole and woe:
GOWER: Lychorida, her nurse, she takes,
GOWER: And so to sea. Their vessel shakes
GOWER: On Neptune's billow, half the flood
GOWER: Hath their keel cut: but fortune's mood
GOWER: Varies again, the grisly north
GOWER: Disgorges such a tempest forth,
GOWER: That, as a duck for life that dives,
GOWER: So up and down the poor ship drives:
GOWER: The lady shrieks, and well-a-near
GOWER: Does fall in travail with her fear:
GOWER: And what ensues in this fell storm
GOWER: Shall for itself itself perform.
GOWER: I nill relate, action may
GOWER: Conveniently the rest convey,
GOWER: Which might not what by me is told.
GOWER: In your imagination hold
GOWER: This stage the ship, upon whose deck
GOWER: The sea-tost Pericles appears to speak.
NARRATOR: Exit
GOWER: SCENE I:
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES, on shipboard
PERICLES: Thou god of this great vast, rebuke these surges,
PERICLES: Which wash both heaven and hell, and thou, that hast
PERICLES: Upon the winds command, bind them in brass,
PERICLES: Having call'd them from the deep! O, still
PERICLES: Thy deafening, dreadful thunders, gently quench
PERICLES: Thy nimble, sulphurous flashes! O, how, Lychorida,
PERICLES: How does my queen? Thou stormest venomously,
PERICLES: Wilt thou spit all thyself? The seaman's whistle
PERICLES: Is as a whisper in the ears of death,
PERICLES: Unheard. Lychorida!--Lucina, O
PERICLES: Divinest patroness, and midwife gentle
PERICLES: To those that cry by night, convey thy deity
PERICLES: Aboard our dancing boat, make swift the pangs
PERICLES: Of my queen's travails!
NARRATOR: Enter LYCHORIDA, with an Infant
PERICLES: Now, Lychorida!
LYCHORIDA: Here is a thing too young for such a place,
LYCHORIDA: Who, if it had conceit, would die, as I
LYCHORIDA: Am like to do: take in your arms this piece
LYCHORIDA: Of your dead queen.
PERICLES: How, how, Lychorida!
LYCHORIDA: Patience, good sir, do not assist the storm.
LYCHORIDA: Here's all that is left living of your queen,
LYCHORIDA: A little daughter: for the sake of it,
LYCHORIDA: Be manly, and take comfort.
PERICLES: O you gods!
PERICLES: Why do you make us love your goodly gifts,
PERICLES: And snatch them straight away? We here below
PERICLES: Recall not what we give, and therein may
PERICLES: Use honour with you.
LYCHORIDA: Patience, good sir,
LYCHORIDA: Even for this charge.
PERICLES: Now, mild may be thy life!
PERICLES: For a more blustrous birth had never babe:
PERICLES: Quiet and gentle thy conditions! for
PERICLES: Thou art the rudeliest welcome to this world
PERICLES: That ever was prince's child. Happy what follows!
PERICLES: Thou hast as chiding a nativity
PERICLES: As fire, air, water, earth, and heaven can make,
PERICLES: To herald thee from the womb: even at the first
PERICLES: Thy loss is more than can thy portage quit,
PERICLES: With all thou canst find here. Now, the good gods
PERICLES: Throw their best eyes upon't!
NARRATOR: Enter two Sailors
First Sailor: What courage, sir? God save you!
PERICLES: Courage enough: I do not fear the flaw,
PERICLES: It hath done to me the worst. Yet, for the love
PERICLES: Of this poor infant, this fresh-new sea-farer,
PERICLES: I would it would be quiet.
First Sailor: Slack the bolins there! Thou wilt not, wilt thou?
First Sailor: Blow, and split thyself.
Second Sailor: But sea-room, an the brine and cloudy billow kiss
Second Sailor: the moon, I care not.
First Sailor: Sir, your queen must overboard: the sea works high,
First Sailor: the wind is loud, and will not lie till the ship be
First Sailor: cleared of the dead.
PERICLES: That's your superstition.
First Sailor: Pardon us, sir, with us at sea it hath been still
First Sailor: observed: and we are strong in custom. Therefore
First Sailor: briefly yield her, for she must overboard straight.
PERICLES: As you think meet. Most wretched queen!
LYCHORIDA: Here she lies, sir.
PERICLES: A terrible childbed hast thou had, my dear,
PERICLES: No light, no fire: the unfriendly elements
PERICLES: Forgot thee utterly: nor have I time
PERICLES: To give thee hallow'd to thy grave, but straight
PERICLES: Must cast thee, scarcely coffin'd, in the ooze,
PERICLES: Where, for a monument upon thy bones,
PERICLES: And e'er-remaining lamps, the belching whale
PERICLES: And humming water must o'erwhelm thy corpse,
PERICLES: Lying with simple shells. O Lychorida,
PERICLES: Bid Nestor bring me spices, ink and paper,
PERICLES: My casket and my jewels, and bid Nicander
PERICLES: Bring me the satin coffer: lay the babe
PERICLES: Upon the pillow: hie thee, whiles I say
PERICLES: A priestly farewell to her: suddenly, woman.
NARRATOR: Exit LYCHORIDA
Second Sailor: Sir, we have a chest beneath the hatches, caulked
Second Sailor: and bitumed ready.
PERICLES: I thank thee. Mariner, say what coast is this?
Second Sailor: We are near Tarsus.
PERICLES: Thither, gentle mariner.
PERICLES: Alter thy course for Tyre. When canst thou reach it?
Second Sailor: By break of day, if the wind cease.
PERICLES: O, make for Tarsus!
PERICLES: There will I visit Cleon, for the babe
PERICLES: Cannot hold out to Tyrus: there I'll leave it
PERICLES: At careful nursing. Go thy ways, good mariner:
PERICLES: I'll bring the body presently.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Ephesus. A room in CERIMON's house.
NARRATOR: Enter CERIMON, with a Servant, and some Persons who have been shipwrecked
CERIMON: Philemon, ho!
NARRATOR: Enter PHILEMON
PHILEMON: Doth my lord call?
CERIMON: Get fire and meat for these poor men:
CERIMON: 'T has been a turbulent and stormy night.
Servant: I have been in many, but such a night as this,
Servant: Till now, I ne'er endured.
CERIMON: Your master will be dead ere you return,
CERIMON: There's nothing can be minister'd to nature
CERIMON: That can recover him.
NARRATOR: To PHILEMON
CERIMON: Give this to the 'pothecary,
CERIMON: And tell me how it works.
NARRATOR: Exeunt all but CERIMON
NARRATOR: Enter two Gentlemen
First Gentleman: Good morrow.
Second Gentleman: Good morrow to your lordship.
CERIMON: Gentlemen,
CERIMON: Why do you stir so early?
First Gentleman: Sir,
First Gentleman: Our lodgings, standing bleak upon the sea,
First Gentleman: Shook as the earth did quake,
First Gentleman: The very principals did seem to rend,
First Gentleman: And all-to topple: pure surprise and fear
First Gentleman: Made me to quit the house.
Second Gentleman: That is the cause we trouble you so early,
Second Gentleman: 'Tis not our husbandry.
CERIMON: O, you say well.
First Gentleman: But I much marvel that your lordship, having
First Gentleman: Rich tire about you, should at these early hours
First Gentleman: Shake off the golden slumber of repose.
First Gentleman: 'Tis most strange,
First Gentleman: Nature should be so conversant with pain,
First Gentleman: Being thereto not compell'd.
CERIMON: I hold it ever,
CERIMON: Virtue and cunning were endowments greater
CERIMON: Than nobleness and riches: careless heirs
CERIMON: May the two latter darken and expend,
CERIMON: But immortality attends the former.
CERIMON: Making a man a god. 'Tis known, I ever
CERIMON: Have studied physic, through which secret art,
CERIMON: By turning o'er authorities, I have,
CERIMON: Together with my practise, made familiar
CERIMON: To me and to my aid the blest infusions
CERIMON: That dwell in vegetives, in metals, stones,
CERIMON: And I can speak of the disturbances
CERIMON: That nature works, and of her cures, which doth give me
CERIMON: A more content in course of true delight
CERIMON: Than to be thirsty after tottering honour,
CERIMON: Or tie my treasure up in silken bags,
CERIMON: To please the fool and death.
Second Gentleman: Your honour has through Ephesus pour'd forth
Second Gentleman: Your charity, and hundreds call themselves
Second Gentleman: Your creatures, who by you have been restored:
Second Gentleman: And not your knowledge, your personal pain, but even
Second Gentleman: Your purse, still open, hath built Lord Cerimon
Second Gentleman: Such strong renown as time shall ne'er decay.
NARRATOR: Enter two or three Servants with a chest
First Servant: So, lift there.
CERIMON: What is that?
First Servant: Sir, even now
First Servant: Did the sea toss upon our shore this chest:
First Servant: 'Tis of some wreck.
CERIMON: Set 't down, let's look upon't.
Second Gentleman: 'Tis like a coffin, sir.
CERIMON: Whate'er it be,
CERIMON: 'Tis wondrous heavy. Wrench it open straight:
CERIMON: If the sea's stomach be o'ercharged with gold,
CERIMON: 'Tis a good constraint of fortune it belches upon us.
Second Gentleman: 'Tis so, my lord.
CERIMON: How close 'tis caulk'd and bitumed!
CERIMON: Did the sea cast it up?
First Servant: I never saw so huge a billow, sir,
First Servant: As toss'd it upon shore.
CERIMON: Wrench it open,
CERIMON: Soft! it smells most sweetly in my sense.
Second Gentleman: A delicate odour.
CERIMON: As ever hit my nostril. So, up with it.
CERIMON: O you most potent gods! what's here? a corse!
First Gentleman: Most strange!
CERIMON: Shrouded in cloth of state, balm'd and entreasured
CERIMON: With full bags of spices! A passport too!
CERIMON: Apollo, perfect me in the characters!
NARRATOR: Reads from a scroll
CERIMON: 'Here I give to understand,
CERIMON: If e'er this coffin drive a-land,
CERIMON: I, King Pericles, have lost
CERIMON: This queen, worth all our mundane cost.
CERIMON: Who finds her, give her burying,
CERIMON: She was the daughter of a king:
CERIMON: Besides this treasure for a fee,
CERIMON: The gods requite his charity!'
CERIMON: If thou livest, Pericles, thou hast a heart
CERIMON: That even cracks for woe! This chanced tonight.
Second Gentleman: Most likely, sir.
CERIMON: Nay, certainly to-night,
CERIMON: For look how fresh she looks! They were too rough
CERIMON: That threw her in the sea. Make a fire within:
CERIMON: Fetch hither all my boxes in my closet.
NARRATOR: Exit a Servant
CERIMON: Death may usurp on nature many hours,
CERIMON: And yet the fire of life kindle again
CERIMON: The o'erpress'd spirits. I heard of an Egyptian
CERIMON: That had nine hours lien dead,
CERIMON: Who was by good appliance recovered.
NARRATOR: Re-enter a Servant, with boxes, napkins, and fire
CERIMON: Well said, well said, the fire and cloths.
CERIMON: The rough and woeful music that we have,
CERIMON: Cause it to sound, beseech you.
CERIMON: The viol once more: how thou stirr'st, thou block!
CERIMON: The music there!--I pray you, give her air.
CERIMON: Gentlemen.
CERIMON: This queen will live: nature awakes, a warmth
CERIMON: Breathes out of her: she hath not been entranced
CERIMON: Above five hours: see how she gins to blow
CERIMON: Into life's flower again!
First Gentleman: The heavens,
First Gentleman: Through you, increase our wonder and set up
First Gentleman: Your fame forever.
CERIMON: She is alive, behold,
CERIMON: Her eyelids, cases to those heavenly jewels
CERIMON: Which Pericles hath lost,
CERIMON: Begin to part their fringes of bright gold,
CERIMON: The diamonds of a most praised water
CERIMON: Do appear, to make the world twice rich. Live,
CERIMON: And make us weep to hear your fate, fair creature,
CERIMON: Rare as you seem to be.
NARRATOR: She moves
THAISA: O dear Diana,
THAISA: Where am I? Where's my lord? What world is this?
Second Gentleman: Is not this strange?
First Gentleman: Most rare.
CERIMON: Hush, my gentle neighbours!
CERIMON: Lend me your hands, to the next chamber bear her.
CERIMON: Get linen: now this matter must be look'd to,
CERIMON: For her relapse is mortal. Come, come,
CERIMON: And AEsculapius guide us!
NARRATOR: Exeunt, carrying her away
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Tarsus. A room in CLEON's house.
NARRATOR: Enter PERICLES, CLEON, DIONYZA, and LYCHORIDA with MARINA in her arms
PERICLES: Most honour'd Cleon, I must needs be gone,
PERICLES: My twelve months are expired, and Tyrus stands
PERICLES: In a litigious peace. You, and your lady,
PERICLES: Take from my heart all thankfulness! The gods
PERICLES: Make up the rest upon you!
CLEON: Your shafts of fortune, though they hurt you mortally,
CLEON: Yet glance full wanderingly on us.
DIONYZA: O your sweet queen!
DIONYZA: That the strict fates had pleased you had brought her hither,
DIONYZA: To have bless'd mine eyes with her!
PERICLES: We cannot but obey
PERICLES: The powers above us. Could I rage and roar
PERICLES: As doth the sea she lies in, yet the end
PERICLES: Must be as 'tis. My gentle babe Marina, whom,
PERICLES: For she was born at sea, I have named so, here
PERICLES: I charge your charity withal, leaving her
PERICLES: The infant of your care, beseeching you
PERICLES: To give her princely training, that she may be
PERICLES: Manner'd as she is born.
CLEON: Fear not, my lord, but think
CLEON: Your grace, that fed my country with your corn,
CLEON: For which the people's prayers still fall upon you,
CLEON: Must in your child be thought on. If neglection
CLEON: Should therein make me vile, the common body,
CLEON: By you relieved, would force me to my duty:
CLEON: But if to that my nature need a spur,
CLEON: The gods revenge it upon me and mine,
CLEON: To the end of generation!
PERICLES: I believe you,
PERICLES: Your honour and your goodness teach me to't,
PERICLES: Without your vows. Till she be married, madam,
PERICLES: By bright Diana, whom we honour, all
PERICLES: Unscissor'd shall this hair of mine remain,
PERICLES: Though I show ill in't. So I take my leave.
PERICLES: Good madam, make me blessed in your care
PERICLES: In bringing up my child.
DIONYZA: I have one myself,
DIONYZA: Who shall not be more dear to my respect
DIONYZA: Than yours, my lord.
PERICLES: Madam, my thanks and prayers.
CLEON: We'll bring your grace e'en to the edge o' the shore,
CLEON: Then give you up to the mask'd Neptune and
CLEON: The gentlest winds of heaven.
PERICLES: I will embrace
PERICLES: Your offer. Come, dearest madam. O, no tears,
PERICLES: Lychorida, no tears:
PERICLES: Look to your little mistress, on whose grace
PERICLES: You may depend hereafter. Come, my lord.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Ephesus. A room in CERIMON's house.
NARRATOR: Enter CERIMON and THAISA
CERIMON: Madam, this letter, and some certain jewels,
CERIMON: Lay with you in your coffer: which are now
CERIMON: At your command. Know you the character?
THAISA: It is my lord's.
THAISA: That I was shipp'd at sea, I well remember,
THAISA: Even on my eaning time, but whether there
THAISA: Deliver'd, by the holy gods,
THAISA: I cannot rightly say. But since King Pericles,
THAISA: My wedded lord, I ne'er shall see again,
THAISA: A vestal livery will I take me to,
THAISA: And never more have joy.
CERIMON: Madam, if this you purpose as ye speak,
CERIMON: Diana's temple is not distant far,
CERIMON: Where you may abide till your date expire.
CERIMON: Moreover, if you please, a niece of mine
CERIMON: Shall there attend you.
THAISA: My recompense is thanks, that's all,
THAISA: Yet my good will is great, though the gift small.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT IV
NARRATOR: Enter GOWER
GOWER: Imagine Pericles arrived at Tyre,
GOWER: Welcomed and settled to his own desire.
GOWER: His woeful queen we leave at Ephesus,
GOWER: Unto Diana there a votaress.
GOWER: Now to Marina bend your mind,
GOWER: Whom our fast-growing scene must find
GOWER: At Tarsus, and by Cleon train'd
GOWER: In music, letters, who hath gain'd
GOWER: Of education all the grace,
GOWER: Which makes her both the heart and place
GOWER: Of general wonder. But, alack,
GOWER: That monster envy, oft the wrack
GOWER: Of earned praise, Marina's life
GOWER: Seeks to take off by treason's knife.
GOWER: And in this kind hath our Cleon
GOWER: One daughter, and a wench full grown,
GOWER: Even ripe for marriage-rite, this maid
GOWER: Hight Philoten: and it is said
GOWER: For certain in our story, she
GOWER: Would ever with Marina be:
GOWER: Be't when she weaved the sleided silk
GOWER: With fingers long, small, white as milk,
GOWER: Or when she would with sharp needle wound
GOWER: The cambric, which she made more sound
GOWER: By hurting it, or when to the lute
GOWER: She sung, and made the night-bird mute,
GOWER: That still records with moan, or when
GOWER: She would with rich and constant pen
GOWER: Vail to her mistress Dian, still
GOWER: This Philoten contends in skill
GOWER: With absolute Marina: so
GOWER: With the dove of Paphos might the crow
GOWER: Vie feathers white. Marina gets
GOWER: All praises, which are paid as debts,
GOWER: And not as given. This so darks
GOWER: In Philoten all graceful marks,
GOWER: That Cleon's wife, with envy rare,
GOWER: A present murderer does prepare
GOWER: For good Marina, that her daughter
GOWER: Might stand peerless by this slaughter.
GOWER: The sooner her vile thoughts to stead,
GOWER: Lychorida, our nurse, is dead:
GOWER: And cursed Dionyza hath
GOWER: The pregnant instrument of wrath
GOWER: Prest for this blow. The unborn event
GOWER: I do commend to your content:
GOWER: Only I carry winged time
GOWER: Post on the lame feet of my rhyme,
GOWER: Which never could I so convey,
GOWER: Unless your thoughts went on my way.
GOWER: Dionyza does appear,
GOWER: With Leonine, a murderer.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Tarsus. An open place near the sea-shore.
NARRATOR: Enter DIONYZA and LEONINE
DIONYZA: Thy oath remember, thou hast sworn to do't:
DIONYZA: 'Tis but a blow, which never shall be known.
DIONYZA: Thou canst not do a thing in the world so soon,
DIONYZA: To yield thee so much profit. Let not conscience,
DIONYZA: Which is but cold, inflaming love i' thy bosom,
DIONYZA: Inflame too nicely, nor let pity, which
DIONYZA: Even women have cast off, melt thee, but be
DIONYZA: A soldier to thy purpose.
LEONINE: I will do't, but yet she is a goodly creature.
DIONYZA: The fitter, then, the gods should have her. Here
DIONYZA: she comes weeping for her only mistress' death.
DIONYZA: Thou art resolved?
LEONINE: I am resolved.
NARRATOR: Enter MARINA, with a basket of flowers
MARINA: No, I will rob Tellus of her weed,
MARINA: To strew thy green with flowers: the yellows, blues,
MARINA: The purple violets, and marigolds,
MARINA: Shall as a carpet hang upon thy grave,
MARINA: While summer-days do last. Ay me! poor maid,
MARINA: Born in a tempest, when my mother died,
MARINA: This world to me is like a lasting storm,
MARINA: Whirring me from my friends.
DIONYZA: How now, Marina! why do you keep alone?
DIONYZA: How chance my daughter is not with you? Do not
DIONYZA: Consume your blood with sorrowing: you have
DIONYZA: A nurse of me. Lord, how your favour's changed
DIONYZA: With this unprofitable woe!
DIONYZA: Come, give me your flowers, ere the sea mar it.
DIONYZA: Walk with Leonine, the air is quick there,
DIONYZA: And it pierces and sharpens the stomach. Come,
DIONYZA: Leonine, take her by the arm, walk with her.
MARINA: No, I pray you,
MARINA: I'll not bereave you of your servant.
DIONYZA: Come, come,
DIONYZA: I love the king your father, and yourself,
DIONYZA: With more than foreign heart. We every day
DIONYZA: Expect him here: when he shall come and find
DIONYZA: Our paragon to all reports thus blasted,
DIONYZA: He will repent the breadth of his great voyage,
DIONYZA: Blame both my lord and me, that we have taken
DIONYZA: No care to your best courses. Go, I pray you,
DIONYZA: Walk, and be cheerful once again, reserve
DIONYZA: That excellent complexion, which did steal
DIONYZA: The eyes of young and old. Care not for me
DIONYZA: I can go home alone.
MARINA: Well, I will go,
MARINA: But yet I have no desire to it.
DIONYZA: Come, come, I know 'tis good for you.
DIONYZA: Walk half an hour, Leonine, at the least:
DIONYZA: Remember what I have said.
LEONINE: I warrant you, madam.
DIONYZA: I'll leave you, my sweet lady, for a while:
DIONYZA: Pray, walk softly, do not heat your blood:
DIONYZA: What! I must have a care of you.
MARINA: My thanks, sweet madam.
NARRATOR: Exit DIONYZA
MARINA: Is this wind westerly that blows?
LEONINE: South-west.
MARINA: When I was born, the wind was north.
LEONINE: Was't so?
MARINA: My father, as nurse said, did never fear,
MARINA: But cried 'Good seaman!' to the sailors, galling
MARINA: His kingly hands, haling ropes,
MARINA: And, clasping to the mast, endured a sea
MARINA: That almost burst the deck.

MARINA: When I was born:
MARINA: Never was waves nor wind more violent,
MARINA: And from the ladder-tackle washes off
MARINA: A canvas-climber. 'Ha!' says one, 'wilt out?'
MARINA: And with a dropping industry they skip
MARINA: From stem to stern: the boatswain whistles, and
MARINA: The master calls, and trebles their confusion.
LEONINE: Come, say your prayers.
MARINA: What mean you?
LEONINE: If you require a little space for prayer,
LEONINE: I grant it: pray, but be not tedious,
LEONINE: For the gods are quick of ear, and I am sworn
LEONINE: To do my work with haste.
MARINA: Why will you kill me?
LEONINE: To satisfy my lady.
MARINA: Why would she have me kill'd?
MARINA: Now, as I can remember, by my troth,
MARINA: I never did her hurt in all my life:
MARINA: I never spake bad word, nor did ill turn
MARINA: To any living creature: believe me, la,
MARINA: I never kill'd a mouse, nor hurt a fly:
MARINA: I trod upon a worm against my will,
MARINA: But I wept for it. How have I offended,
MARINA: Wherein my death might yield her any profit,
MARINA: Or my life imply her any danger?
LEONINE: My commission
LEONINE: Is not to reason of the deed, but do it.
MARINA: You will not do't for all the world, I hope.
MARINA: You are well favour'd, and your looks foreshow
MARINA: You have a gentle heart. I saw you lately,
MARINA: When you caught hurt in parting two that fought:
MARINA: Good sooth, it show'd well in you: do so now:
MARINA: Your lady seeks my life, come you between,
MARINA: And save poor me, the weaker.
LEONINE: I am sworn,
LEONINE: And will dispatch.
NARRATOR: He seizes her

NARRATOR: LEONINE runs away

Third Pirate: Half-part, mates, half-part.
Third Pirate: Come, let's have her aboard suddenly.

LEONINE: Perhaps they will but please themselves upon her,
