NARRATOR: Exit GRUMIO
HORTENSIO: I know her answer.
PETRUCHIO: What?
HORTENSIO: She will not.
PETRUCHIO: The fouler fortune mine, and there an end.
BAPTISTA: Now, by my holidame, here comes Katharina!
NARRATOR: Re-enter KATARINA
KATHARINA: What is your will, sir, that you send for me?
PETRUCHIO: Where is your sister, and Hortensio's wife?
KATHARINA: They sit conferring by the parlor fire.
PETRUCHIO: Go fetch them hither: if they deny to come.
PETRUCHIO: Swinge me them soundly forth unto their husbands:
PETRUCHIO: Away, I say, and bring them hither straight.
NARRATOR: Exit KATHARINA
LUCENTIO: Here is a wonder, if you talk of a wonder.
HORTENSIO: And so it is: I wonder what it bodes.
PETRUCHIO: Marry, peace it bodes, and love and quiet life,
PETRUCHIO: And awful rule and right supremacy,
PETRUCHIO: And, to be short, what not, that's sweet and happy?
BAPTISTA: Now, fair befal thee, good Petruchio!
BAPTISTA: The wager thou hast won, and I will add
BAPTISTA: Unto their losses twenty thousand crowns,
BAPTISTA: Another dowry to another daughter,
BAPTISTA: For she is changed, as she had never been.
PETRUCHIO: Nay, I will win my wager better yet
PETRUCHIO: And show more sign of her obedience,
PETRUCHIO: Her new-built virtue and obedience.
PETRUCHIO: See where she comes and brings your froward wives
PETRUCHIO: As prisoners to her womanly persuasion.
NARRATOR: Re-enter KATHARINA, with BIANCA and Widow
PETRUCHIO: Katharina, that cap of yours becomes you not:
PETRUCHIO: Off with that bauble, throw it under-foot.
Widow: Lord, let me never have a cause to sigh,
Widow: Till I be brought to such a silly pass!
BIANCA: Fie! what a foolish duty call you this?
LUCENTIO: I would your duty were as foolish too:
LUCENTIO: The wisdom of your duty, fair Bianca,
LUCENTIO: Hath cost me an hundred crowns since supper-time.
BIANCA: The more fool you, for laying on my duty.
PETRUCHIO: Katharina, I charge thee, tell these headstrong women
PETRUCHIO: What duty they do owe their lords and husbands.
Widow: Come, come, you're mocking: we will have no telling.
PETRUCHIO: Come on, I say, and first begin with her.
Widow: She shall not.
PETRUCHIO: I say she shall: and first begin with her.
KATHARINA: Fie, fie! unknit that threatening unkind brow,
KATHARINA: And dart not scornful glances from those eyes,
KATHARINA: To wound thy lord, thy king, thy governor:
KATHARINA: It blots thy beauty as frosts do bite the meads,
KATHARINA: Confounds thy fame as whirlwinds shake fair buds,
KATHARINA: And in no sense is meet or amiable.
KATHARINA: A woman moved is like a fountain troubled,
KATHARINA: Muddy, ill-seeming, thick, bereft of beauty,
KATHARINA: And while it is so, none so dry or thirsty
KATHARINA: Will deign to sip or touch one drop of it.
KATHARINA: Thy husband is thy lord, thy life, thy keeper,
KATHARINA: Thy head, thy sovereign, one that cares for thee,
KATHARINA: And for thy maintenance commits his body
KATHARINA: To painful labour both by sea and land,
KATHARINA: To watch the night in storms, the day in cold,
KATHARINA: Whilst thou liest warm at home, secure and safe,
KATHARINA: And craves no other tribute at thy hands
KATHARINA: But love, fair looks and true obedience,
KATHARINA: Too little payment for so great a debt.
KATHARINA: Such duty as the subject owes the prince
KATHARINA: Even such a woman oweth to her husband,
KATHARINA: And when she is froward, peevish, sullen, sour,
KATHARINA: And not obedient to his honest will,
KATHARINA: What is she but a foul contending rebel
KATHARINA: And graceless traitor to her loving lord?
KATHARINA: I am ashamed that women are so simple
KATHARINA: To offer war where they should kneel for peace,
KATHARINA: Or seek for rule, supremacy and sway,
KATHARINA: When they are bound to serve, love and obey.
KATHARINA: Why are our bodies soft and weak and smooth,
KATHARINA: Unapt to toil and trouble in the world,
KATHARINA: But that our soft conditions and our hearts
KATHARINA: Should well agree with our external parts?
KATHARINA: Come, come, you froward and unable worms!
KATHARINA: My mind hath been as big as one of yours,
KATHARINA: My heart as great, my reason haply more,
KATHARINA: To bandy word for word and frown for frown,
KATHARINA: But now I see our lances are but straws,
KATHARINA: Our strength as weak, our weakness past compare,
KATHARINA: That seeming to be most which we indeed least are.
KATHARINA: Then vail your stomachs, for it is no boot,
KATHARINA: And place your hands below your husband's foot:
KATHARINA: In token of which duty, if he please,
KATHARINA: My hand is ready, may it do him ease.
PETRUCHIO: Why, there's a wench! Come on, and kiss me, Kate.
LUCENTIO: Well, go thy ways, old lad, for thou shalt ha't.
VINCENTIO: 'Tis a good hearing when children are toward.
LUCENTIO: But a harsh hearing when women are froward.
PETRUCHIO: Come, Kate, we'll to bed.
PETRUCHIO: We three are married, but you two are sped.
NARRATOR: To LUCENTIO
PETRUCHIO: 'Twas I won the wager, though you hit the white,
PETRUCHIO: And, being a winner, God give you good night!
NARRATOR: Exeunt PETRUCHIO and KATHARINA
HORTENSIO: Now, go thy ways, thou hast tamed a curst shrew.
LUCENTIO: 'Tis a wonder, by your leave, she will be tamed so.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
''' PLAY: The Tempest '''
NARRATOR: ACT I
NARRATOR: SCENE I. On a ship at sea: a tempestuous noise
LUCENTIO: of thunder and lightning heard.
NARRATOR: Enter a Master and a Boatswain
Master: Boatswain!
Boatswain: Here, master: what cheer?
Master: Good, speak to the mariners: fall to't, yarely,
Master: or we run ourselves aground: bestir, bestir.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: Enter Mariners
Boatswain: Heigh, my hearts! cheerly, cheerly, my hearts!
Boatswain: yare, yare! Take in the topsail. Tend to the
Boatswain: master's whistle. Blow, till thou burst thy wind,
Boatswain: if room enough!
NARRATOR: Enter ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, ANTONIO, FERDINAND, GONZALO, and others
ALONSO: Good boatswain, have care. Where's the master?
ALONSO: Play the men.
Boatswain: I pray now, keep below.
ANTONIO: Where is the master, boatswain?
Boatswain: Do you not hear him? You mar our labour: keep your
Boatswain: cabins: you do assist the storm.
GONZALO: Nay, good, be patient.
Boatswain: When the sea is. Hence! What cares these roarers
Boatswain: for the name of king? To cabin: silence! trouble us not.
GONZALO: Good, yet remember whom thou hast aboard.
Boatswain: None that I more love than myself. You are a
Boatswain: counsellor, if you can command these elements to
Boatswain: silence, and work the peace of the present, we will
Boatswain: not hand a rope more, use your authority: if you
Boatswain: cannot, give thanks you have lived so long, and make
Boatswain: yourself ready in your cabin for the mischance of
Boatswain: the hour, if it so hap. Cheerly, good hearts! Out
Boatswain: of our way, I say.
NARRATOR: Exit
GONZALO: I have great comfort from this fellow: methinks he
GONZALO: hath no drowning mark upon him, his complexion is
GONZALO: perfect gallows. Stand fast, good Fate, to his
GONZALO: hanging: make the rope of his destiny our cable,
GONZALO: for our own doth little advantage. If he be not
GONZALO: born to be hanged, our case is miserable.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: Re-enter Boatswain
Boatswain: Down with the topmast! yare! lower, lower! Bring
Boatswain: her to try with main-course.
NARRATOR: A cry within
Boatswain: A plague upon this howling! they are louder than
Boatswain: the weather or our office.
NARRATOR: Re-enter SEBASTIAN, ANTONIO, and GONZALO
Boatswain: Yet again! what do you here? Shall we give o'er
Boatswain: and drown? Have you a mind to sink?
SEBASTIAN: A pox o' your throat, you bawling, blasphemous,
SEBASTIAN: incharitable dog!
Boatswain: Work you then.
ANTONIO: Hang, cur! hang, you whoreson, insolent noisemaker!
ANTONIO: We are less afraid to be drowned than thou art.
GONZALO: I'll warrant him for drowning, though the ship were
GONZALO: no stronger than a nutshell and as leaky as an
GONZALO: unstanched wench.
Boatswain: Lay her a-hold, a-hold! set her two courses off to
Boatswain: sea again, lay her off.
NARRATOR: Enter Mariners wet
Mariners: All lost! to prayers, to prayers! all lost!
Boatswain: What, must our mouths be cold?
GONZALO: The king and prince at prayers! let's assist them,
GONZALO: For our case is as theirs.
SEBASTIAN: I'm out of patience.
ANTONIO: We are merely cheated of our lives by drunkards:
ANTONIO: This wide-chapp'd rascal--would thou mightst lie drowning
ANTONIO: The washing of ten tides!
GONZALO: He'll be hang'd yet,
GONZALO: Though every drop of water swear against it
GONZALO: And gape at widest to glut him.
GONZALO: A confused noise within:   'Mercy on us!'--  'We split, we split!'--'Farewell, my wife and  children!'-- 'Farewell, brother!'--'We split, we split, we split!'
ANTONIO: Let's all sink with the king.
SEBASTIAN: Let's take leave of him.
NARRATOR: Exeunt ANTONIO and SEBASTIAN
GONZALO: Now would I give a thousand furlongs of sea for an
GONZALO: acre of barren ground, long heath, brown furze, any
GONZALO: thing. The wills above be done! but I would fain
GONZALO: die a dry death.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The island. Before PROSPERO'S cell.
NARRATOR: Enter PROSPERO and MIRANDA
MIRANDA: If by your art, my dearest father, you have
MIRANDA: Put the wild waters in this roar, allay them.
MIRANDA: The sky, it seems, would pour down stinking pitch,
MIRANDA: But that the sea, mounting to the welkin's cheek,
MIRANDA: Dashes the fire out. O, I have suffered
MIRANDA: With those that I saw suffer: a brave vessel,
MIRANDA: Who had, no doubt, some noble creature in her,
MIRANDA: Dash'd all to pieces. O, the cry did knock
MIRANDA: Against my very heart. Poor souls, they perish'd.
MIRANDA: Had I been any god of power, I would
MIRANDA: Have sunk the sea within the earth or ere
MIRANDA: It should the good ship so have swallow'd and
MIRANDA: The fraughting souls within her.
PROSPERO: Be collected:
PROSPERO: No more amazement: tell your piteous heart
PROSPERO: There's no harm done.
MIRANDA: O, woe the day!
PROSPERO: No harm.
PROSPERO: I have done nothing but in care of thee,
PROSPERO: Of thee, my dear one, thee, my daughter, who
PROSPERO: Art ignorant of what thou art, nought knowing
PROSPERO: Of whence I am, nor that I am more better
PROSPERO: Than Prospero, master of a full poor cell,
PROSPERO: And thy no greater father.
MIRANDA: More to know
MIRANDA: Did never meddle with my thoughts.
PROSPERO: 'Tis time
PROSPERO: I should inform thee farther. Lend thy hand,
PROSPERO: And pluck my magic garment from me. So:
NARRATOR: Lays down his mantle
PROSPERO: Lie there, my art. Wipe thou thine eyes, have comfort.
PROSPERO: The direful spectacle of the wreck, which touch'd
PROSPERO: The very virtue of compassion in thee,
PROSPERO: I have with such provision in mine art
PROSPERO: So safely ordered that there is no soul--
PROSPERO: No, not so much perdition as an hair
PROSPERO: Betid to any creature in the vessel
PROSPERO: Which thou heard'st cry, which thou saw'st sink. Sit down,
PROSPERO: For thou must now know farther.
MIRANDA: You have often
MIRANDA: Begun to tell me what I am, but stopp'd
MIRANDA: And left me to a bootless inquisition,
MIRANDA: Concluding 'Stay: not yet.'
PROSPERO: The hour's now come,
PROSPERO: The very minute bids thee ope thine ear,
PROSPERO: Obey and be attentive. Canst thou remember
PROSPERO: A time before we came unto this cell?
PROSPERO: I do not think thou canst, for then thou wast not
PROSPERO: Out three years old.
MIRANDA: Certainly, sir, I can.
PROSPERO: By what? by any other house or person?
PROSPERO: Of any thing the image tell me that
PROSPERO: Hath kept with thy remembrance.
MIRANDA: 'Tis far off
MIRANDA: And rather like a dream than an assurance
MIRANDA: That my remembrance warrants. Had I not
MIRANDA: Four or five women once that tended me?
PROSPERO: Thou hadst, and more, Miranda. But how is it
PROSPERO: That this lives in thy mind? What seest thou else
PROSPERO: In the dark backward and abysm of time?
PROSPERO: If thou remember'st aught ere thou camest here,
PROSPERO: How thou camest here thou mayst.
MIRANDA: But that I do not.
PROSPERO: Twelve year since, Miranda, twelve year since,
PROSPERO: Thy father was the Duke of Milan and
PROSPERO: A prince of power.
MIRANDA: Sir, are not you my father?
PROSPERO: Thy mother was a piece of virtue, and
PROSPERO: She said thou wast my daughter, and thy father
PROSPERO: Was Duke of Milan, and thou his only heir
PROSPERO: And princess no worse issued.
MIRANDA: O the heavens!
MIRANDA: What foul play had we, that we came from thence?
MIRANDA: Or blessed was't we did?
PROSPERO: Both, both, my girl:
PROSPERO: By foul play, as thou say'st, were we heaved thence,
PROSPERO: But blessedly holp hither.
MIRANDA: O, my heart bleeds
MIRANDA: To think o' the teen that I have turn'd you to,
MIRANDA: Which is from my remembrance! Please you, farther.
PROSPERO: My brother and thy uncle, call'd Antonio--
PROSPERO: I pray thee, mark me--that a brother should
PROSPERO: Be so perfidious!--he whom next thyself
PROSPERO: Of all the world I loved and to him put
PROSPERO: The manage of my state, as at that time
PROSPERO: Through all the signories it was the first
PROSPERO: And Prospero the prime duke, being so reputed
PROSPERO: In dignity, and for the liberal arts
PROSPERO: Without a parallel, those being all my study,
PROSPERO: The government I cast upon my brother
PROSPERO: And to my state grew stranger, being transported
PROSPERO: And rapt in secret studies. Thy false uncle--
PROSPERO: Dost thou attend me?
MIRANDA: Sir, most heedfully.
PROSPERO: Being once perfected how to grant suits,
PROSPERO: How to deny them, who to advance and who
PROSPERO: To trash for over-topping, new created
PROSPERO: The creatures that were mine, I say, or changed 'em,
PROSPERO: Or else new form'd 'em, having both the key
PROSPERO: Of officer and office, set all hearts i' the state
PROSPERO: To what tune pleased his ear, that now he was
PROSPERO: The ivy which had hid my princely trunk,
PROSPERO: And suck'd my verdure out on't. Thou attend'st not.
MIRANDA: O, good sir, I do.
PROSPERO: I pray thee, mark me.
PROSPERO: I, thus neglecting worldly ends, all dedicated
PROSPERO: To closeness and the bettering of my mind
PROSPERO: With that which, but by being so retired,
PROSPERO: O'er-prized all popular rate, in my false brother
PROSPERO: Awaked an evil nature, and my trust,
PROSPERO: Like a good parent, did beget of him
PROSPERO: A falsehood in its contrary as great
PROSPERO: As my trust was, which had indeed no limit,
PROSPERO: A confidence sans bound. He being thus lorded,
PROSPERO: Not only with what my revenue yielded,
PROSPERO: But what my power might else exact, like one
PROSPERO: Who having into truth, by telling of it,
PROSPERO: Made such a sinner of his memory,
PROSPERO: To credit his own lie, he did believe
PROSPERO: He was indeed the duke, out o' the substitution
PROSPERO: And executing the outward face of royalty,
PROSPERO: With all prerogative: hence his ambition growing--
PROSPERO: Dost thou hear?
MIRANDA: Your tale, sir, would cure deafness.
PROSPERO: To have no screen between this part he play'd
PROSPERO: And him he play'd it for, he needs will be
PROSPERO: Absolute Milan. Me, poor man, my library
PROSPERO: Was dukedom large enough: of temporal royalties
PROSPERO: He thinks me now incapable, confederates--
PROSPERO: So dry he was for sway--wi' the King of Naples
PROSPERO: To give him annual tribute, do him homage,
PROSPERO: Subject his coronet to his crown and bend
PROSPERO: The dukedom yet unbow'd--alas, poor Milan!--
PROSPERO: To most ignoble stooping.
MIRANDA: O the heavens!
PROSPERO: Mark his condition and the event, then tell me
PROSPERO: If this might be a brother.
MIRANDA: I should sin
MIRANDA: To think but nobly of my grandmother:
MIRANDA: Good wombs have borne bad sons.
PROSPERO: Now the condition.
PROSPERO: The King of Naples, being an enemy
PROSPERO: To me inveterate, hearkens my brother's suit,
PROSPERO: Which was, that he, in lieu o' the premises
PROSPERO: Of homage and I know not how much tribute,
PROSPERO: Should presently extirpate me and mine
PROSPERO: Out of the dukedom and confer fair Milan
PROSPERO: With all the honours on my brother: whereon,
PROSPERO: A treacherous army levied, one midnight
PROSPERO: Fated to the purpose did Antonio open
PROSPERO: The gates of Milan, and, i' the dead of darkness,
PROSPERO: The ministers for the purpose hurried thence
PROSPERO: Me and thy crying self.
MIRANDA: Alack, for pity!
MIRANDA: I, not remembering how I cried out then,
MIRANDA: Will cry it o'er again: it is a hint
MIRANDA: That wrings mine eyes to't.
PROSPERO: Hear a little further
PROSPERO: And then I'll bring thee to the present business
PROSPERO: Which now's upon's, without the which this story
PROSPERO: Were most impertinent.
MIRANDA: Wherefore did they not
MIRANDA: That hour destroy us?
PROSPERO: Well demanded, wench:
PROSPERO: My tale provokes that question. Dear, they durst not,
PROSPERO: So dear the love my people bore me, nor set
PROSPERO: A mark so bloody on the business, but
PROSPERO: With colours fairer painted their foul ends.
PROSPERO: In few, they hurried us aboard a bark,
PROSPERO: Bore us some leagues to sea, where they prepared
PROSPERO: A rotten carcass of a boat, not rigg'd,
PROSPERO: Nor tackle, sail, nor mast, the very rats
PROSPERO: Instinctively had quit it: there they hoist us,
PROSPERO: To cry to the sea that roar'd to us, to sigh
PROSPERO: To the winds whose pity, sighing back again,
PROSPERO: Did us but loving wrong.
MIRANDA: Alack, what trouble
MIRANDA: Was I then to you!
PROSPERO: O, a cherubim
PROSPERO: Thou wast that did preserve me. Thou didst smile.
PROSPERO: Infused with a fortitude from heaven,
PROSPERO: When I have deck'd the sea with drops full salt,
PROSPERO: Under my burthen groan'd, which raised in me
PROSPERO: An undergoing stomach, to bear up
PROSPERO: Against what should ensue.
MIRANDA: How came we ashore?
PROSPERO: By Providence divine.
PROSPERO: Some food we had and some fresh water that
PROSPERO: A noble Neapolitan, Gonzalo,
PROSPERO: Out of his charity, being then appointed
PROSPERO: Master of this design, did give us, with
PROSPERO: Rich garments, linens, stuffs and necessaries,
PROSPERO: Which since have steaded much, so, of his gentleness,
PROSPERO: Knowing I loved my books, he furnish'd me
PROSPERO: From mine own library with volumes that
PROSPERO: I prize above my dukedom.
MIRANDA: Would I might
MIRANDA: But ever see that man!
PROSPERO: Now I arise:
NARRATOR: Resumes his mantle
PROSPERO: Sit still, and hear the last of our sea-sorrow.
PROSPERO: Here in this island we arrived, and here
PROSPERO: Have I, thy schoolmaster, made thee more profit
PROSPERO: Than other princesses can that have more time
PROSPERO: For vainer hours and tutors not so careful.
MIRANDA: Heavens thank you for't! And now, I pray you, sir,
MIRANDA: For still 'tis beating in my mind, your reason
MIRANDA: For raising this sea-storm?
PROSPERO: Know thus far forth.
PROSPERO: By accident most strange, bountiful Fortune,
PROSPERO: Now my dear lady, hath mine enemies
PROSPERO: Brought to this shore, and by my prescience
PROSPERO: I find my zenith doth depend upon
PROSPERO: A most auspicious star, whose influence
PROSPERO: If now I court not but omit, my fortunes
PROSPERO: Will ever after droop. Here cease more questions:
PROSPERO: Thou art inclined to sleep, 'tis a good dulness,
PROSPERO: And give it way: I know thou canst not choose.
NARRATOR: MIRANDA sleeps
PROSPERO: Come away, servant, come. I am ready now.
PROSPERO: Approach, my Ariel, come.
NARRATOR: Enter ARIEL
ARIEL: All hail, great master! grave sir, hail! I come
ARIEL: To answer thy best pleasure, be't to fly,
ARIEL: To swim, to dive into the fire, to ride
ARIEL: On the curl'd clouds, to thy strong bidding task
ARIEL: Ariel and all his quality.
PROSPERO: Hast thou, spirit,
PROSPERO: Perform'd to point the tempest that I bade thee?
ARIEL: To every article.
ARIEL: I boarded the king's ship, now on the beak,
ARIEL: Now in the waist, the deck, in every cabin,
ARIEL: I flamed amazement: sometime I'ld divide,
ARIEL: And burn in many places, on the topmast,
ARIEL: The yards and bowsprit, would I flame distinctly,
ARIEL: Then meet and join. Jove's lightnings, the precursors
ARIEL: O' the dreadful thunder-claps, more momentary
ARIEL: And sight-outrunning were not, the fire and cracks
ARIEL: Of sulphurous roaring the most mighty Neptune
ARIEL: Seem to besiege and make his bold waves tremble,
ARIEL: Yea, his dread trident shake.
PROSPERO: My brave spirit!
PROSPERO: Who was so firm, so constant, that this coil
PROSPERO: Would not infect his reason?
ARIEL: Not a soul
ARIEL: But felt a fever of the mad and play'd
ARIEL: Some tricks of desperation. All but mariners
ARIEL: Plunged in the foaming brine and quit the vessel,
ARIEL: Then all afire with me: the king's son, Ferdinand,
ARIEL: With hair up-staring,--then like reeds, not hair,--
ARIEL: Was the first man that leap'd, cried, 'Hell is empty
ARIEL: And all the devils are here.'
PROSPERO: Why that's my spirit!
PROSPERO: But was not this nigh shore?
ARIEL: Close by, my master.
PROSPERO: But are they, Ariel, safe?
ARIEL: Not a hair perish'd,
ARIEL: On their sustaining garments not a blemish,
ARIEL: But fresher than before: and, as thou badest me,
ARIEL: In troops I have dispersed them 'bout the isle.
ARIEL: The king's son have I landed by himself,
ARIEL: Whom I left cooling of the air with sighs
ARIEL: In an odd angle of the isle and sitting,
ARIEL: His arms in this sad knot.
PROSPERO: Of the king's ship
PROSPERO: The mariners say how thou hast disposed
PROSPERO: And all the rest o' the fleet.
ARIEL: Safely in harbour
ARIEL: Is the king's ship, in the deep nook, where once
ARIEL: Thou call'dst me up at midnight to fetch dew
ARIEL: From the still-vex'd Bermoothes, there she's hid:
ARIEL: The mariners all under hatches stow'd,
ARIEL: Who, with a charm join'd to their suffer'd labour,
ARIEL: I have left asleep, and for the rest o' the fleet
ARIEL: Which I dispersed, they all have met again
ARIEL: And are upon the Mediterranean flote,
ARIEL: Bound sadly home for Naples,
ARIEL: Supposing that they saw the king's ship wreck'd
ARIEL: And his great person perish.
PROSPERO: Ariel, thy charge
PROSPERO: Exactly is perform'd: but there's more work.
PROSPERO: What is the time o' the day?
ARIEL: Past the mid season.
PROSPERO: At least two glasses. The time 'twixt six and now
PROSPERO: Must by us both be spent most preciously.
ARIEL: Is there more toil? Since thou dost give me pains,
ARIEL: Let me remember thee what thou hast promised,
ARIEL: Which is not yet perform'd me.
PROSPERO: How now? moody?
PROSPERO: What is't thou canst demand?
ARIEL: My liberty.
PROSPERO: Before the time be out? no more!
ARIEL: I prithee,
ARIEL: Remember I have done thee worthy service,
ARIEL: Told thee no lies, made thee no mistakings, served
ARIEL: Without or grudge or grumblings: thou didst promise
ARIEL: To bate me a full year.
PROSPERO: Dost thou forget
PROSPERO: From what a torment I did free thee?
ARIEL: No.
PROSPERO: Thou dost, and think'st it much to tread the ooze
PROSPERO: Of the salt deep,
PROSPERO: To run upon the sharp wind of the north,
PROSPERO: To do me business in the veins o' the earth
PROSPERO: When it is baked with frost.
ARIEL: I do not, sir.
PROSPERO: Thou liest, malignant thing! Hast thou forgot
PROSPERO: The foul witch Sycorax, who with age and envy
PROSPERO: Was grown into a hoop? hast thou forgot her?
ARIEL: No, sir.
PROSPERO: Thou hast. Where was she born? speak, tell me.
ARIEL: Sir, in Argier.
PROSPERO: O, was she so? I must
PROSPERO: Once in a month recount what thou hast been,
PROSPERO: Which thou forget'st. This damn'd witch Sycorax,
PROSPERO: For mischiefs manifold and sorceries terrible
PROSPERO: To enter human hearing, from Argier,
PROSPERO: Thou know'st, was banish'd: for one thing she did
PROSPERO: They would not take her life. Is not this true?
ARIEL: Ay, sir.
PROSPERO: This blue-eyed hag was hither brought with child
PROSPERO: And here was left by the sailors. Thou, my slave,
PROSPERO: As thou report'st thyself, wast then her servant,
PROSPERO: And, for thou wast a spirit too delicate
PROSPERO: To act her earthy and abhorr'd commands,
PROSPERO: Refusing her grand hests, she did confine thee,
PROSPERO: By help of her more potent ministers
PROSPERO: And in her most unmitigable rage,
PROSPERO: Into a cloven pine, within which rift
PROSPERO: Imprison'd thou didst painfully remain
PROSPERO: A dozen years, within which space she died
PROSPERO: And left thee there, where thou didst vent thy groans
PROSPERO: As fast as mill-wheels strike. Then was this island--
PROSPERO: Save for the son that she did litter here,
PROSPERO: A freckled whelp hag-born--not honour'd with
PROSPERO: A human shape.
ARIEL: Yes, Caliban her son.
PROSPERO: Dull thing, I say so, he, that Caliban
PROSPERO: Whom now I keep in service. Thou best know'st
PROSPERO: What torment I did find thee in, thy groans
PROSPERO: Did make wolves howl and penetrate the breasts
PROSPERO: Of ever angry bears: it was a torment
PROSPERO: To lay upon the damn'd, which Sycorax
PROSPERO: Could not again undo: it was mine art,
PROSPERO: When I arrived and heard thee, that made gape
PROSPERO: The pine and let thee out.
ARIEL: I thank thee, master.
PROSPERO: If thou more murmur'st, I will rend an oak
PROSPERO: And peg thee in his knotty entrails till
PROSPERO: Thou hast howl'd away twelve winters.
ARIEL: Pardon, master,
ARIEL: I will be correspondent to command
ARIEL: And do my spiriting gently.
PROSPERO: Do so, and after two days
PROSPERO: I will discharge thee.
ARIEL: That's my noble master!
ARIEL: What shall I do? say what, what shall I do?
PROSPERO: Go make thyself like a nymph o' the sea: be subject
PROSPERO: To no sight but thine and mine, invisible
PROSPERO: To every eyeball else. Go take this shape
PROSPERO: And hither come in't: go, hence with diligence!
NARRATOR: Exit ARIEL
PROSPERO: Awake, dear heart, awake! thou hast slept well, Awake!
MIRANDA: The strangeness of your story put
MIRANDA: Heaviness in me.
PROSPERO: Shake it off. Come on,
PROSPERO: We'll visit Caliban my slave, who never
PROSPERO: Yields us kind answer.
MIRANDA: 'Tis a villain, sir,
MIRANDA: I do not love to look on.
PROSPERO: But, as 'tis,
PROSPERO: We cannot miss him: he does make our fire,
PROSPERO: Fetch in our wood and serves in offices
PROSPERO: That profit us. What, ho! slave! Caliban!
PROSPERO: Thou earth, thou! speak.
CALIBAN: [Within]  There's wood enough within.
PROSPERO: Come forth, I say! there's other business for thee:
PROSPERO: Come, thou tortoise! when?
NARRATOR: Re-enter ARIEL like a water-nymph
PROSPERO: Fine apparition! My quaint Ariel,
PROSPERO: Hark in thine ear.
ARIEL: My lord it shall be done.
NARRATOR: Exit
PROSPERO: Thou poisonous slave, got by the devil himself
PROSPERO: Upon thy wicked dam, come forth!
NARRATOR: Enter CALIBAN
CALIBAN: As wicked dew as e'er my mother brush'd
CALIBAN: With raven's feather from unwholesome fen
CALIBAN: Drop on you both! a south-west blow on ye
CALIBAN: And blister you all o'er!
PROSPERO: For this, be sure, to-night thou shalt have cramps,
PROSPERO: Side-stitches that shall pen thy breath up, urchins
PROSPERO: Shall, for that vast of night that they may work,
PROSPERO: All exercise on thee, thou shalt be pinch'd
PROSPERO: As thick as honeycomb, each pinch more stinging
PROSPERO: Than bees that made 'em.
CALIBAN: I must eat my dinner.
CALIBAN: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother,
CALIBAN: Which thou takest from me. When thou camest first,
CALIBAN: Thou strokedst me and madest much of me, wouldst give me
CALIBAN: Water with berries in't, and teach me how
CALIBAN: To name the bigger light, and how the less,
CALIBAN: That burn by day and night: and then I loved thee
CALIBAN: And show'd thee all the qualities o' the isle,
CALIBAN: The fresh springs, brine-pits, barren place and fertile:
CALIBAN: Cursed be I that did so! All the charms
CALIBAN: Of Sycorax, toads, beetles, bats, light on you!
CALIBAN: For I am all the subjects that you have,
CALIBAN: Which first was mine own king: and here you sty me
CALIBAN: In this hard rock, whiles you do keep from me
CALIBAN: The rest o' the island.
PROSPERO: Thou most lying slave,
PROSPERO: Whom stripes may move, not kindness! I have used thee,
PROSPERO: Filth as thou art, with human care, and lodged thee
PROSPERO: In mine own cell, till thou didst seek to violate
PROSPERO: The honour of my child.
CALIBAN: O ho, O ho! would't had been done!
CALIBAN: Thou didst prevent me, I had peopled else
CALIBAN: This isle with Calibans.
PROSPERO: Abhorred slave,
PROSPERO: Which any print of goodness wilt not take,
PROSPERO: Being capable of all ill! I pitied thee,
PROSPERO: Took pains to make thee speak, taught thee each hour
PROSPERO: One thing or other: when thou didst not, savage,
PROSPERO: Know thine own meaning, but wouldst gabble like
PROSPERO: A thing most brutish, I endow'd thy purposes
PROSPERO: With words that made them known. But thy vile race,
PROSPERO: Though thou didst learn, had that in't which
PROSPERO: good natures
PROSPERO: Could not abide to be with, therefore wast thou
PROSPERO: Deservedly confined into this rock,
PROSPERO: Who hadst deserved more than a prison.
CALIBAN: You taught me language, and my profit on't
CALIBAN: Is, I know how to curse. The red plague rid you
CALIBAN: For learning me your language!
PROSPERO: Hag-seed, hence!
PROSPERO: Fetch us in fuel, and be quick, thou'rt best,
PROSPERO: To answer other business. Shrug'st thou, malice?
PROSPERO: If thou neglect'st or dost unwillingly
PROSPERO: What I command, I'll rack thee with old cramps,
PROSPERO: Fill all thy bones with aches, make thee roar
PROSPERO: That beasts shall tremble at thy din.
CALIBAN: No, pray thee.
NARRATOR: Aside
CALIBAN: I must obey: his art is of such power,
CALIBAN: It would control my dam's god, Setebos,
CALIBAN: and make a vassal of him.
PROSPERO: So, slave, hence!
NARRATOR: Exit CALIBAN
NARRATOR: Re-enter ARIEL, invisible, playing and singing, FERDINAND following
PROSPERO: ARIEL'S song.
PROSPERO: Come unto these yellow sands,
PROSPERO: And then take hands:
PROSPERO: Courtsied when you have and kiss'd
PROSPERO: The wild waves whist,
PROSPERO: Foot it featly here and there,
PROSPERO: And, sweet sprites, the burthen bear.
PROSPERO: Hark, hark!
PROSPERO: Burthen [dispersedly, within
PROSPERO: The watch-dogs bark!
NARRATOR: Burthen Bow-wow
PROSPERO: Hark, hark! I hear
PROSPERO: The strain of strutting chanticleer
PROSPERO: Cry, Cock-a-diddle-dow.
FERDINAND: Where should this music be? i' the air or the earth?
FERDINAND: It sounds no more: and sure, it waits upon
FERDINAND: Some god o' the island. Sitting on a bank,
FERDINAND: Weeping again the king my father's wreck,
FERDINAND: This music crept by me upon the waters,
FERDINAND: Allaying both their fury and my passion
FERDINAND: With its sweet air: thence I have follow'd it,
FERDINAND: Or it hath drawn me rather. But 'tis gone.
FERDINAND: No, it begins again.
NARRATOR: ARIEL sings
FERDINAND: Full fathom five thy father lies,
FERDINAND: Of his bones are coral made,
FERDINAND: Those are pearls that were his eyes:
FERDINAND: Nothing of him that doth fade
FERDINAND: But doth suffer a sea-change
FERDINAND: Into something rich and strange.
FERDINAND: Sea-nymphs hourly ring his knell
NARRATOR: Burthen Ding-dong
FERDINAND: Hark! now I hear them,--Ding-dong, bell.
FERDINAND: The ditty does remember my drown'd father.
FERDINAND: This is no mortal business, nor no sound
FERDINAND: That the earth owes. I hear it now above me.
PROSPERO: The fringed curtains of thine eye advance
PROSPERO: And say what thou seest yond.
MIRANDA: What is't? a spirit?
MIRANDA: Lord, how it looks about! Believe me, sir,
MIRANDA: It carries a brave form. But 'tis a spirit.
PROSPERO: No, wench, it eats and sleeps and hath such senses
PROSPERO: As we have, such. This gallant which thou seest
PROSPERO: Was in the wreck, and, but he's something stain'd
PROSPERO: With grief that's beauty's canker, thou mightst call him
PROSPERO: A goodly person: he hath lost his fellows
PROSPERO: And strays about to find 'em.
MIRANDA: I might call him
MIRANDA: A thing divine, for nothing natural
MIRANDA: I ever saw so noble.
PROSPERO: [Aside] It goes on, I see,
PROSPERO: As my soul prompts it. Spirit, fine spirit! I'll free thee
PROSPERO: Within two days for this.
FERDINAND: Most sure, the goddess
FERDINAND: On whom these airs attend! Vouchsafe my prayer
FERDINAND: May know if you remain upon this island,
FERDINAND: And that you will some good instruction give
FERDINAND: How I may bear me here: my prime request,
FERDINAND: Which I do last pronounce, is, O you wonder!
FERDINAND: If you be maid or no?
MIRANDA: No wonder, sir,
MIRANDA: But certainly a maid.
FERDINAND: My language! heavens!
FERDINAND: I am the best of them that speak this speech,
FERDINAND: Were I but where 'tis spoken.
PROSPERO: How? the best?
PROSPERO: What wert thou, if the King of Naples heard thee?
FERDINAND: A single thing, as I am now, that wonders
FERDINAND: To hear thee speak of Naples. He does hear me,
FERDINAND: And that he does I weep: myself am Naples,
FERDINAND: Who with mine eyes, never since at ebb, beheld
FERDINAND: The king my father wreck'd.
MIRANDA: Alack, for mercy!
FERDINAND: Yes, faith, and all his lords, the Duke of Milan
FERDINAND: And his brave son being twain.
PROSPERO: [Aside]	The Duke of Milan
PROSPERO: And his more braver daughter could control thee,
PROSPERO: If now 'twere fit to do't. At the first sight
PROSPERO: They have changed eyes. Delicate Ariel,
PROSPERO: I'll set thee free for this.
NARRATOR: To FERDINAND
PROSPERO: A word, good sir,
PROSPERO: I fear you have done yourself some wrong: a word.
MIRANDA: Why speaks my father so ungently? This
MIRANDA: Is the third man that e'er I saw, the first
MIRANDA: That e'er I sigh'd for: pity move my father
MIRANDA: To be inclined my way!
FERDINAND: O, if a virgin,
FERDINAND: And your affection not gone forth, I'll make you
FERDINAND: The queen of Naples.
PROSPERO: Soft, sir! one word more.
NARRATOR: Aside
PROSPERO: They are both in either's powers, but this swift business
PROSPERO: I must uneasy make, lest too light winning
PROSPERO: Make the prize light.
NARRATOR: To FERDINAND
PROSPERO: One word more, I charge thee
PROSPERO: That thou attend me: thou dost here usurp
PROSPERO: The name thou owest not, and hast put thyself
PROSPERO: Upon this island as a spy, to win it
PROSPERO: From me, the lord on't.
FERDINAND: No, as I am a man.
MIRANDA: There's nothing ill can dwell in such a temple:
MIRANDA: If the ill spirit have so fair a house,
MIRANDA: Good things will strive to dwell with't.
PROSPERO: Follow me.
PROSPERO: Speak not you for him, he's a traitor. Come,
PROSPERO: I'll manacle thy neck and feet together:
PROSPERO: Sea-water shalt thou drink, thy food shall be
PROSPERO: The fresh-brook muscles, wither'd roots and husks
PROSPERO: Wherein the acorn cradled. Follow.
FERDINAND: No,
FERDINAND: I will resist such entertainment till
FERDINAND: Mine enemy has more power.
NARRATOR: Draws, and is charmed from moving
MIRANDA: O dear father,
MIRANDA: Make not too rash a trial of him, for
MIRANDA: He's gentle and not fearful.
PROSPERO: What? I say,
PROSPERO: My foot my tutor? Put thy sword up, traitor,
PROSPERO: Who makest a show but darest not strike, thy conscience
PROSPERO: Is so possess'd with guilt: come from thy ward,
PROSPERO: For I can here disarm thee with this stick
PROSPERO: And make thy weapon drop.
MIRANDA: Beseech you, father.
PROSPERO: Hence! hang not on my garments.
MIRANDA: Sir, have pity,
MIRANDA: I'll be his surety.
PROSPERO: Silence! one word more
PROSPERO: Shall make me chide thee, if not hate thee. What!
PROSPERO: An advocate for an imposter! hush!
PROSPERO: Thou think'st there is no more such shapes as he,
PROSPERO: Having seen but him and Caliban: foolish wench!
PROSPERO: To the most of men this is a Caliban
PROSPERO: And they to him are angels.
MIRANDA: My affections
MIRANDA: Are then most humble, I have no ambition
MIRANDA: To see a goodlier man.
PROSPERO: Come on, obey:
PROSPERO: Thy nerves are in their infancy again
PROSPERO: And have no vigour in them.
FERDINAND: So they are,
FERDINAND: My spirits, as in a dream, are all bound up.
FERDINAND: My father's loss, the weakness which I feel,
FERDINAND: The wreck of all my friends, nor this man's threats,
FERDINAND: To whom I am subdued, are but light to me,
FERDINAND: Might I but through my prison once a day
FERDINAND: Behold this maid: all corners else o' the earth
FERDINAND: Let liberty make use of, space enough
FERDINAND: Have I in such a prison.
PROSPERO: [Aside]                It works.
NARRATOR: To FERDINAND
PROSPERO: Come on.
PROSPERO: Thou hast done well, fine Ariel!
NARRATOR: To FERDINAND
PROSPERO: Follow me.
NARRATOR: To ARIEL
PROSPERO: Hark what thou else shalt do me.
MIRANDA: Be of comfort,
MIRANDA: My father's of a better nature, sir,
MIRANDA: Than he appears by speech: this is unwonted
MIRANDA: Which now came from him.
PROSPERO: Thou shalt be free
PROSPERO: As mountain winds: but then exactly do
PROSPERO: All points of my command.
ARIEL: To the syllable.
PROSPERO: Come, follow. Speak not for him.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT II
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Another part of the island.
NARRATOR: Enter ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, ANTONIO, GONZALO, ADRIAN, FRANCISCO, and others
GONZALO: Beseech you, sir, be merry, you have cause,
GONZALO: So have we all, of joy, for our escape
GONZALO: Is much beyond our loss. Our hint of woe
GONZALO: Is common, every day some sailor's wife,
GONZALO: The masters of some merchant and the merchant
GONZALO: Have just our theme of woe, but for the miracle,
GONZALO: I mean our preservation, few in millions
GONZALO: Can speak like us: then wisely, good sir, weigh
GONZALO: Our sorrow with our comfort.
ALONSO: Prithee, peace.
SEBASTIAN: He receives comfort like cold porridge.
ANTONIO: The visitor will not give him o'er so.
SEBASTIAN: Look he's winding up the watch of his wit,
SEBASTIAN: by and by it will strike.
GONZALO: Sir,--
SEBASTIAN: One: tell.
GONZALO: When every grief is entertain'd that's offer'd,
GONZALO: Comes to the entertainer--
SEBASTIAN: A dollar.
GONZALO: Dolour comes to him, indeed: you
GONZALO: have spoken truer than you purposed.
SEBASTIAN: You have taken it wiselier than I meant you should.
GONZALO: Therefore, my lord,--
ANTONIO: Fie, what a spendthrift is he of his tongue!
ALONSO: I prithee, spare.
GONZALO: Well, I have done: but yet,--
SEBASTIAN: He will be talking.
ANTONIO: Which, of he or Adrian, for a good
ANTONIO: wager, first begins to crow?
SEBASTIAN: The old cock.
ANTONIO: The cockerel.
SEBASTIAN: Done. The wager?
ANTONIO: A laughter.
SEBASTIAN: A match!
ADRIAN: Though this island seem to be desert,--
SEBASTIAN: Ha, ha, ha! So, you're paid.
ADRIAN: Uninhabitable and almost inaccessible,--
SEBASTIAN: Yet,--
ADRIAN: Yet,--
ANTONIO: He could not miss't.
ADRIAN: It must needs be of subtle, tender and delicate
ADRIAN: temperance.
ANTONIO: Temperance was a delicate wench.
SEBASTIAN: Ay, and a subtle, as he most learnedly delivered.
ADRIAN: The air breathes upon us here most sweetly.
SEBASTIAN: As if it had lungs and rotten ones.
ANTONIO: Or as 'twere perfumed by a fen.
GONZALO: Here is everything advantageous to life.
ANTONIO: True, save means to live.
SEBASTIAN: Of that there's none, or little.
GONZALO: How lush and lusty the grass looks! how green!
ANTONIO: The ground indeed is tawny.
SEBASTIAN: With an eye of green in't.
ANTONIO: He misses not much.
SEBASTIAN: No, he doth but mistake the truth totally.
GONZALO: But the rarity of it is,--which is indeed almost
GONZALO: beyond credit,--
SEBASTIAN: As many vouched rarities are.
GONZALO: That our garments, being, as they were, drenched in
GONZALO: the sea, hold notwithstanding their freshness and
GONZALO: glosses, being rather new-dyed than stained with
GONZALO: salt water.
ANTONIO: If but one of his pockets could speak, would it not
ANTONIO: say he lies?
SEBASTIAN: Ay, or very falsely pocket up his report
GONZALO: Methinks our garments are now as fresh as when we
GONZALO: put them on first in Afric, at the marriage of
GONZALO: the king's fair daughter Claribel to the King of Tunis.
SEBASTIAN: 'Twas a sweet marriage, and we prosper well in our return.
ADRIAN: Tunis was never graced before with such a paragon to
ADRIAN: their queen.
GONZALO: Not since widow Dido's time.
ANTONIO: Widow! a pox o' that! How came that widow in?
ANTONIO: widow Dido!
SEBASTIAN: What if he had said 'widower AEneas' too? Good Lord,
SEBASTIAN: how you take it!
ADRIAN: 'Widow Dido' said you? you make me study of that:
ADRIAN: she was of Carthage, not of Tunis.
GONZALO: This Tunis, sir, was Carthage.
ADRIAN: Carthage?
GONZALO: I assure you, Carthage.
SEBASTIAN: His word is more than the miraculous harp, he hath
SEBASTIAN: raised the wall and houses too.
ANTONIO: What impossible matter will he make easy next?
SEBASTIAN: I think he will carry this island home in his pocket
SEBASTIAN: and give it his son for an apple.
ANTONIO: And, sowing the kernels of it in the sea, bring
ANTONIO: forth more islands.
GONZALO: Ay.
ANTONIO: Why, in good time.
GONZALO: Sir, we were talking that our garments seem now
GONZALO: as fresh as when we were at Tunis at the marriage
GONZALO: of your daughter, who is now queen.
ANTONIO: And the rarest that e'er came there.
SEBASTIAN: Bate, I beseech you, widow Dido.
ANTONIO: O, widow Dido! ay, widow Dido.
GONZALO: Is not, sir, my doublet as fresh as the first day I
GONZALO: wore it? I mean, in a sort.
ANTONIO: That sort was well fished for.
GONZALO: When I wore it at your daughter's marriage?
ALONSO: You cram these words into mine ears against
ALONSO: The stomach of my sense. Would I had never
ALONSO: Married my daughter there! for, coming thence,
ALONSO: My son is lost and, in my rate, she too,
ALONSO: Who is so far from Italy removed
ALONSO: I ne'er again shall see her. O thou mine heir
ALONSO: Of Naples and of Milan, what strange fish
ALONSO: Hath made his meal on thee?
FRANCISCO: Sir, he may live:
FRANCISCO: I saw him beat the surges under him,
FRANCISCO: And ride upon their backs, he trod the water,
FRANCISCO: Whose enmity he flung aside, and breasted
FRANCISCO: The surge most swoln that met him, his bold head
FRANCISCO: 'Bove the contentious waves he kept, and oar'd
FRANCISCO: Himself with his good arms in lusty stroke
FRANCISCO: To the shore, that o'er his wave-worn basis bow'd,
FRANCISCO: As stooping to relieve him: I not doubt
FRANCISCO: He came alive to land.
ALONSO: No, no, he's gone.
SEBASTIAN: Sir, you may thank yourself for this great loss,
SEBASTIAN: That would not bless our Europe with your daughter,
SEBASTIAN: But rather lose her to an African,
SEBASTIAN: Where she at least is banish'd from your eye,
SEBASTIAN: Who hath cause to wet the grief on't.
ALONSO: Prithee, peace.
SEBASTIAN: You were kneel'd to and importuned otherwise
SEBASTIAN: By all of us, and the fair soul herself
SEBASTIAN: Weigh'd between loathness and obedience, at
SEBASTIAN: Which end o' the beam should bow. We have lost your
SEBASTIAN: son,
SEBASTIAN: I fear, for ever: Milan and Naples have
SEBASTIAN: More widows in them of this business' making
SEBASTIAN: Than we bring men to comfort them:
SEBASTIAN: The fault's your own.
ALONSO: So is the dear'st o' the loss.
GONZALO: My lord Sebastian,
GONZALO: The truth you speak doth lack some gentleness
GONZALO: And time to speak it in: you rub the sore,
GONZALO: When you should bring the plaster.
SEBASTIAN: Very well.
ANTONIO: And most chirurgeonly.
GONZALO: It is foul weather in us all, good sir,
GONZALO: When you are cloudy.
SEBASTIAN: Foul weather?
ANTONIO: Very foul.
GONZALO: Had I plantation of this isle, my lord,--
ANTONIO: He'ld sow't with nettle-seed.
SEBASTIAN: Or docks, or mallows.
GONZALO: And were the king on't, what would I do?
SEBASTIAN: 'Scape being drunk for want of wine.
GONZALO: I' the commonwealth I would by contraries
GONZALO: Execute all things, for no kind of traffic
GONZALO: Would I admit, no name of magistrate,
GONZALO: Letters should not be known, riches, poverty,
GONZALO: And use of service, none, contract, succession,
GONZALO: Bourn, bound of land, tilth, vineyard, none,
GONZALO: No use of metal, corn, or wine, or oil,
GONZALO: No occupation, all men idle, all,
GONZALO: And women too, but innocent and pure,
GONZALO: No sovereignty,--
SEBASTIAN: Yet he would be king on't.
ANTONIO: The latter end of his commonwealth forgets the
ANTONIO: beginning.
GONZALO: All things in common nature should produce
GONZALO: Without sweat or endeavour: treason, felony,
GONZALO: Sword, pike, knife, gun, or need of any engine,
GONZALO: Would I not have, but nature should bring forth,
GONZALO: Of its own kind, all foison, all abundance,
GONZALO: To feed my innocent people.
SEBASTIAN: No marrying 'mong his subjects?
ANTONIO: None, man, all idle: whores and knaves.
GONZALO: I would with such perfection govern, sir,
GONZALO: To excel the golden age.
SEBASTIAN: God save his majesty!
ANTONIO: Long live Gonzalo!
GONZALO: And,--do you mark me, sir?
ALONSO: Prithee, no more: thou dost talk nothing to me.
GONZALO: I do well believe your highness, and
GONZALO: did it to minister occasion to these gentlemen,
GONZALO: who are of such sensible and nimble lungs that
GONZALO: they always use to laugh at nothing.
ANTONIO: 'Twas you we laughed at.
GONZALO: Who in this kind of merry fooling am nothing
GONZALO: to you: so you may continue and laugh at
GONZALO: nothing still.
ANTONIO: What a blow was there given!
SEBASTIAN: An it had not fallen flat-long.
GONZALO: You are gentlemen of brave metal, you would lift
GONZALO: the moon out of her sphere, if she would continue
GONZALO: in it five weeks without changing.
NARRATOR: Enter ARIEL, invisible, playing solemn music
SEBASTIAN: We would so, and then go a bat-fowling.
ANTONIO: Nay, good my lord, be not angry.
GONZALO: No, I warrant you, I will not adventure
GONZALO: my discretion so weakly. Will you laugh
GONZALO: me asleep, for I am very heavy?
ANTONIO: Go sleep, and hear us.
NARRATOR: All sleep except ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, and ANTONIO
ALONSO: What, all so soon asleep! I wish mine eyes
ALONSO: Would, with themselves, shut up my thoughts: I find
ALONSO: They are inclined to do so.
SEBASTIAN: Please you, sir,
SEBASTIAN: Do not omit the heavy offer of it:
SEBASTIAN: It seldom visits sorrow, when it doth,
SEBASTIAN: It is a comforter.
ANTONIO: We two, my lord,
ANTONIO: Will guard your person while you take your rest,
ANTONIO: And watch your safety.
ALONSO: Thank you. Wondrous heavy.
NARRATOR: ALONSO sleeps. Exit ARIEL
SEBASTIAN: What a strange drowsiness possesses them!
ANTONIO: It is the quality o' the climate.
SEBASTIAN: Why
SEBASTIAN: Doth it not then our eyelids sink? I find not
SEBASTIAN: Myself disposed to sleep.
ANTONIO: Nor I, my spirits are nimble.
ANTONIO: They fell together all, as by consent,
ANTONIO: They dropp'd, as by a thunder-stroke. What might,
ANTONIO: Worthy Sebastian? O, what might?--No more:--
ANTONIO: And yet me thinks I see it in thy face,

ANTONIO: My strong imagination sees a crown
ANTONIO: Dropping upon thy head.

ANTONIO: Do you not hear me speak?
SEBASTIAN: I do, and surely
SEBASTIAN: It is a sleepy language and thou speak'st
SEBASTIAN: Out of thy sleep. What is it thou didst say?
SEBASTIAN: This is a strange repose, to be asleep

SEBASTIAN: And yet so fast asleep.
ANTONIO: Noble Sebastian,
ANTONIO: Thou let'st thy fortune sleep--die, rather, wink'st

SEBASTIAN: Thou dost snore distinctly,
SEBASTIAN: There's meaning in thy snores.
ANTONIO: I am more serious than my custom: you
ANTONIO: Must be so too, if heed me, which to do
ANTONIO: Trebles thee o'er.
SEBASTIAN: Well, I am standing water.
ANTONIO: I'll teach you how to flow.
SEBASTIAN: Do so: to ebb
SEBASTIAN: Hereditary sloth instructs me.
ANTONIO: O,
ANTONIO: If you but knew how you the purpose cherish
ANTONIO: Whiles thus you mock it! how, in stripping it,
ANTONIO: You more invest it! Ebbing men, indeed,
ANTONIO: Most often do so near the bottom run
ANTONIO: By their own fear or sloth.
SEBASTIAN: Prithee, say on:
SEBASTIAN: The setting of thine eye and cheek proclaim
SEBASTIAN: A matter from thee, and a birth indeed
SEBASTIAN: Which throes thee much to yield.
ANTONIO: Thus, sir:
ANTONIO: Although this lord of weak remembrance, this,
ANTONIO: Who shall be of as little memory

ANTONIO: For he's a spirit of persuasion, only
ANTONIO: Professes to persuade,--the king his son's alive,
ANTONIO: 'Tis as impossible that he's undrown'd
ANTONIO: And he that sleeps here swims.
SEBASTIAN: I have no hope
SEBASTIAN: That he's undrown'd.
ANTONIO: O, out of that 'no hope'
ANTONIO: What great hope have you! no hope that way is
ANTONIO: Another way so high a hope that even
ANTONIO: Ambition cannot pierce a wink beyond,
ANTONIO: But doubt discovery there. Will you grant with me
ANTONIO: That Ferdinand is drown'd?
SEBASTIAN: He's gone.
ANTONIO: Then, tell me,
ANTONIO: Who's the next heir of Naples?
SEBASTIAN: Claribel.
ANTONIO: She that is queen of Tunis, she that dwells

SEBASTIAN: What stuff is this! how say you?
SEBASTIAN: 'Tis true, my brother's daughter's queen of Tunis,
SEBASTIAN: So is she heir of Naples, 'twixt which regions
SEBASTIAN: There is some space.
ANTONIO: A space whose every cubit
ANTONIO: Seems to cry out, 'How shall that Claribel

ANTONIO: And let Sebastian wake.' Say, this were death

ANTONIO: As this Gonzalo, I myself could make

ANTONIO: The mind that I do! what a sleep were this
ANTONIO: For your advancement! Do you understand me?
SEBASTIAN: Methinks I do.
ANTONIO: And how does your content
ANTONIO: Tender your own good fortune?
SEBASTIAN: I remember
SEBASTIAN: You did supplant your brother Prospero.
ANTONIO: True:
ANTONIO: And look how well my garments sit upon me,
ANTONIO: Much feater than before: my brother's servants
ANTONIO: Were then my fellows, now they are my men.
SEBASTIAN: But, for your conscience?
ANTONIO: Ay, sir, where lies that? if 'twere a kibe,
ANTONIO: 'Twould put me to my slipper: but I feel not

ANTONIO: That stand 'twixt me and Milan, candied be they

ANTONIO: No better than the earth he lies upon,

ANTONIO: Should not upbraid our course. For all the rest,
ANTONIO: They'll take suggestion as a cat laps milk,
ANTONIO: They'll tell the clock to any business that
ANTONIO: We say befits the hour.
SEBASTIAN: Thy case, dear friend,
SEBASTIAN: Shall be my precedent, as thou got'st Milan,
SEBASTIAN: I'll come by Naples. Draw thy sword: one stroke

SEBASTIAN: And I the king shall love thee.
ANTONIO: Draw together,
ANTONIO: And when I rear my hand, do you the like,
ANTONIO: To fall it on Gonzalo.
SEBASTIAN: O, but one word.
NARRATOR: They talk apart
NARRATOR: Re-enter ARIEL, invisible
ARIEL: My master through his art foresees the danger
ARIEL: That you, his friend, are in, and sends me forth--
ARIEL: For else his project dies--to keep them living.
NARRATOR: Sings in GONZALO's ear
ARIEL: While you here do snoring lie,
ARIEL: Open-eyed conspiracy
ARIEL: His time doth take.
ARIEL: If of life you keep a care,
ARIEL: Shake off slumber, and beware:
ARIEL: Awake, awake!
ANTONIO: Then let us both be sudden.
GONZALO: Now, good angels
GONZALO: Preserve the king.
NARRATOR: They wake
ALONSO: Why, how now? ho, awake! Why are you drawn?
ALONSO: Wherefore this ghastly looking?
GONZALO: What's the matter?
SEBASTIAN: Whiles we stood here securing your repose,
SEBASTIAN: Even now, we heard a hollow burst of bellowing

SEBASTIAN: It struck mine ear most terribly.
ALONSO: I heard nothing.
ANTONIO: O, 'twas a din to fright a monster's ear,
ANTONIO: To make an earthquake! sure, it was the roar
ANTONIO: Of a whole herd of lions.
ALONSO: Heard you this, Gonzalo?
GONZALO: Upon mine honour, sir, I heard a humming,
GONZALO: And that a strange one too, which did awake me:
GONZALO: I shaked you, sir, and cried: as mine eyes open'd,
GONZALO: I saw their weapons drawn: there was a noise,
GONZALO: That's verily. 'Tis best we stand upon our guard,
GONZALO: Or that we quit this place, let's draw our weapons.
ALONSO: Lead off this ground, and let's make further search
ALONSO: For my poor son.
GONZALO: Heavens keep him from these beasts!
GONZALO: For he is, sure, i' the island.
ALONSO: Lead away.
ARIEL: Prospero my lord shall know what I have done:
ARIEL: So, king, go safely on to seek thy son.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Another part of the island.
NARRATOR: Enter CALIBAN with a burden of wood. A noise of thunder heard
CALIBAN: All the infections that the sun sucks up
CALIBAN: From bogs, fens, flats, on Prosper fall and make him
CALIBAN: By inch-meal a disease! His spirits hear me
CALIBAN: And yet I needs must curse. But they'll nor pinch,
CALIBAN: Fright me with urchin--shows, pitch me i' the mire,

NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Before PROSPERO'S Cell.
NARRATOR: Enter FERDINAND, bearing a log
FERDINAND: There be some sports are painful, and their labour
FERDINAND: Delight in them sets off: some kinds of baseness
FERDINAND: Are nobly undergone and most poor matters
FERDINAND: Point to rich ends. This my mean task
FERDINAND: Would be as heavy to me as odious, but
FERDINAND: The mistress which I serve quickens what's dead
FERDINAND: And makes my labours pleasures: O, she is
FERDINAND: Ten times more gentle than her father's crabbed,
FERDINAND: And he's composed of harshness. I must remove
FERDINAND: Some thousands of these logs and pile them up,
FERDINAND: Upon a sore injunction: my sweet mistress
FERDINAND: Weeps when she sees me work, and says, such baseness
FERDINAND: Had never like executor. I forget:
FERDINAND: But these sweet thoughts do even refresh my labours,
FERDINAND: Most busy lest, when I do it.
FERDINAND: Enter MIRANDA, and PROSPERO at a distance, unseen
MIRANDA: Alas, now, pray you,
MIRANDA: Work not so hard: I would the lightning had
MIRANDA: Burnt up those logs that you are enjoin'd to pile!
MIRANDA: Pray, set it down and rest you: when this burns,
MIRANDA: 'Twill weep for having wearied you. My father
MIRANDA: Is hard at study, pray now, rest yourself,
MIRANDA: He's safe for these three hours.
FERDINAND: O most dear mistress,
FERDINAND: The sun will set before I shall discharge
FERDINAND: What I must strive to do.
MIRANDA: If you'll sit down,
MIRANDA: I'll bear your logs the while: pray, give me that,
MIRANDA: I'll carry it to the pile.
FERDINAND: No, precious creature,
FERDINAND: I had rather crack my sinews, break my back,
FERDINAND: Than you should such dishonour undergo,
FERDINAND: While I sit lazy by.
MIRANDA: It would become me
MIRANDA: As well as it does you: and I should do it
MIRANDA: With much more ease, for my good will is to it,
MIRANDA: And yours it is against.
PROSPERO: Poor worm, thou art infected!
PROSPERO: This visitation shows it.
MIRANDA: You look wearily.
FERDINAND: No, noble mistress,'tis fresh morning with me
FERDINAND: When you are by at night. I do beseech you--
FERDINAND: Chiefly that I might set it in my prayers--
FERDINAND: What is your name?
MIRANDA: Miranda.--O my father,
MIRANDA: I have broke your hest to say so!
FERDINAND: Admired Miranda!
FERDINAND: Indeed the top of admiration! worth
FERDINAND: What's dearest to the world! Full many a lady
FERDINAND: I have eyed with best regard and many a time
FERDINAND: The harmony of their tongues hath into bondage
FERDINAND: Brought my too diligent ear: for several virtues
FERDINAND: Have I liked several women, never any
FERDINAND: With so fun soul, but some defect in her
FERDINAND: Did quarrel with the noblest grace she owed
FERDINAND: And put it to the foil: but you, O you,
FERDINAND: So perfect and so peerless, are created
FERDINAND: Of every creature's best!
MIRANDA: I do not know
MIRANDA: One of my sex, no woman's face remember,
MIRANDA: Save, from my glass, mine own, nor have I seen
MIRANDA: More that I may call men than you, good friend,
MIRANDA: And my dear father: how features are abroad,
MIRANDA: I am skilless of, but, by my modesty,
MIRANDA: The jewel in my dower, I would not wish
MIRANDA: Any companion in the world but you,
MIRANDA: Nor can imagination form a shape,
MIRANDA: Besides yourself, to like of. But I prattle
MIRANDA: Something too wildly and my father's precepts
MIRANDA: I therein do forget.
FERDINAND: I am in my condition
FERDINAND: A prince, Miranda, I do think, a king,
FERDINAND: I would, not so!--and would no more endure
FERDINAND: This wooden slavery than to suffer
FERDINAND: The flesh-fly blow my mouth. Hear my soul speak:
FERDINAND: The very instant that I saw you, did
FERDINAND: My heart fly to your service, there resides,
FERDINAND: To make me slave to it, and for your sake
FERDINAND: Am I this patient log--man.
MIRANDA: Do you love me?
FERDINAND: O heaven, O earth, bear witness to this sound
FERDINAND: And crown what I profess with kind event
FERDINAND: If I speak true! if hollowly, invert
FERDINAND: What best is boded me to mischief! I
FERDINAND: Beyond all limit of what else i' the world
FERDINAND: Do love, prize, honour you.
MIRANDA: I am a fool
MIRANDA: To weep at what I am glad of.
PROSPERO: Fair encounter
PROSPERO: Of two most rare affections! Heavens rain grace
PROSPERO: On that which breeds between 'em!
FERDINAND: Wherefore weep you?
MIRANDA: At mine unworthiness that dare not offer
MIRANDA: What I desire to give, and much less take
MIRANDA: What I shall die to want. But this is trifling,
MIRANDA: And all the more it seeks to hide itself,
MIRANDA: The bigger bulk it shows. Hence, bashful cunning!
MIRANDA: And prompt me, plain and holy innocence!
MIRANDA: I am your wife, if you will marry me,
MIRANDA: If not, I'll die your maid: to be your fellow
MIRANDA: You may deny me, but I'll be your servant,
MIRANDA: Whether you will or no.
FERDINAND: My mistress, dearest,
FERDINAND: And I thus humble ever.
MIRANDA: My husband, then?
FERDINAND: Ay, with a heart as willing
FERDINAND: As bondage e'er of freedom: here's my hand.
MIRANDA: And mine, with my heart in't, and now farewell
MIRANDA: Till half an hour hence.
FERDINAND: A thousand thousand!
NARRATOR: Exeunt FERDINAND and MIRANDA severally
PROSPERO: So glad of this as they I cannot be,
PROSPERO: Who are surprised withal, but my rejoicing
PROSPERO: At nothing can be more. I'll to my book,
PROSPERO: For yet ere supper-time must I perform
PROSPERO: Much business appertaining.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE II. Another part of the island.
NARRATOR: Enter CALIBAN, STEPHANO, and TRINCULO
STEPHANO: Tell not me, when the butt is out, we will drink

STEPHANO: board 'em. Servant-monster, drink to me.

TRINCULO: say there's but five upon this isle: we are three
TRINCULO: of them, if th' other two be brained like us, the
TRINCULO: state totters.
STEPHANO: Drink, servant-monster, when I bid thee: thy eyes
STEPHANO: are almost set in thy head.
TRINCULO: Where should they be set else? he were a brave
TRINCULO: monster indeed, if they were set in his tail.
STEPHANO: My man-monster hath drown'd his tongue in sack:
STEPHANO: for my part, the sea cannot drown me, I swam, ere I
STEPHANO: could recover the shore, five and thirty leagues off

STEPHANO: monster, or my standard.
TRINCULO: Your lieutenant, if you list, he's no standard.

TRINCULO: Nor go neither, but you'll lie like dogs and yet say
TRINCULO: nothing neither.
STEPHANO: Moon-calf, speak once in thy life, if thou beest a
STEPHANO: good moon-calf.
CALIBAN: How does thy honour? Let me lick thy shoe.
CALIBAN: I'll not serve him, he's not valiant.
TRINCULO: Thou liest, most ignorant monster: I am in case to

TRINCULO: 'Lord' quoth he! That a monster should be such a natural!

STEPHANO: Marry, will I	kneel and repeat it, I will stand,
STEPHANO: and so shall Trinculo.
NARRATOR: Enter ARIEL, invisible
CALIBAN: As I told thee before, I am subject to a tyrant, a
CALIBAN: sorcerer, that by his cunning hath cheated me of the island.

STEPHANO: That's most certain.

ARIEL: Thou liest, thou canst not.

TRINCULO: off.
STEPHANO: Didst thou not say he lied?

STEPHANO: Do I so? take thou that.
NARRATOR: Beats TRINCULO
STEPHANO: As you like this, give me the lie another time.
TRINCULO: I did not give the lie. Out o' your
TRINCULO: wits and bearing too? A pox o' your bottle!
TRINCULO: this can sack and drinking do. A murrain on
TRINCULO: your monster, and the devil take your fingers!
CALIBAN: Ha, ha, ha!
STEPHANO: Now, forward with your tale. Prithee, stand farther
STEPHANO: off.
CALIBAN: Beat him enough: after a little time
CALIBAN: I'll beat him too.

CALIBAN: Why, as I told thee, 'tis a custom with him,

CALIBAN: Which when he has a house, he'll deck withal

STEPHANO: Is it so brave a lass?
CALIBAN: Ay, lord, she will become thy bed, I warrant.
CALIBAN: And bring thee forth brave brood.
STEPHANO: Monster, I will kill this man: his daughter and I

STEPHANO: like the plot, Trinculo?
TRINCULO: Excellent.
STEPHANO: Give me thy hand: I am sorry I beat thee, but,
STEPHANO: while thou livest, keep a good tongue in thy head.
CALIBAN: Within this half hour will he be asleep:
CALIBAN: Wilt thou destroy him then?
STEPHANO: Ay, on mine honour.
ARIEL: This will I tell my master.
CALIBAN: Thou makest me merry, I am full of pleasure:
CALIBAN: Let us be jocund: will you troll the catch
CALIBAN: You taught me but while-ere?
STEPHANO: At thy request, monster, I will do reason, any
STEPHANO: reason. Come on, Trinculo, let us sing.
NARRATOR: Sings
STEPHANO: Flout 'em and scout 'em
STEPHANO: And scout 'em and flout 'em
STEPHANO: Thought is free.
CALIBAN: That's not the tune.
NARRATOR: Ariel plays the tune on a tabour and pipe
STEPHANO: What is this same?
TRINCULO: This is the tune of our catch, played by the picture
TRINCULO: of Nobody.
STEPHANO: If thou beest a man, show thyself in thy likeness:
STEPHANO: if thou beest a devil, take't as thou list.
TRINCULO: O, forgive me my sins!
STEPHANO: He that dies pays all debts: I defy thee. Mercy upon us!
CALIBAN: Art thou afeard?
STEPHANO: No, monster, not I.
CALIBAN: Be not afeard, the isle is full of noises,
CALIBAN: Sounds and sweet airs, that give delight and hurt not.
CALIBAN: Sometimes a thousand twangling instruments
CALIBAN: Will hum about mine ears, and sometime voices
CALIBAN: That, if I then had waked after long sleep,
CALIBAN: Will make me sleep again: and then, in dreaming,
CALIBAN: The clouds methought would open and show riches
CALIBAN: Ready to drop upon me that, when I waked,
CALIBAN: I cried to dream again.
STEPHANO: This will prove a brave kingdom to me, where I shall
STEPHANO: have my music for nothing.
CALIBAN: When Prospero is destroyed.
STEPHANO: That shall be by and by: I remember the story.
TRINCULO: The sound is going away, let's follow it, and
TRINCULO: after do our work.
STEPHANO: Lead, monster, we'll follow. I would I could see
STEPHANO: this tabourer, he lays it on.
TRINCULO: Wilt come? I'll follow, Stephano.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. Another part of the island.
NARRATOR: Enter ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, ANTONIO, GONZALO, ADRIAN, FRANCISCO, and others
GONZALO: By'r lakin, I can go no further, sir,
GONZALO: My old bones ache: here's a maze trod indeed
GONZALO: Through forth-rights and meanders! By your patience,
GONZALO: I needs must rest me.
ALONSO: Old lord, I cannot blame thee,
ALONSO: Who am myself attach'd with weariness,
ALONSO: To the dulling of my spirits: sit down, and rest.
ALONSO: Even here I will put off my hope and keep it
ALONSO: No longer for my flatterer: he is drown'd
ALONSO: Whom thus we stray to find, and the sea mocks
ALONSO: Our frustrate search on land. Well, let him go.
ANTONIO: [Aside to SEBASTIAN]  I am right glad that he's so
ANTONIO: out of hope.
ANTONIO: Do not, for one repulse, forego the purpose
ANTONIO: That you resolved to effect.
SEBASTIAN: [Aside to ANTONIO]  The next advantage
SEBASTIAN: Will we take throughly.
ANTONIO: [Aside to SEBASTIAN]  Let it be to-night,
ANTONIO: For, now they are oppress'd with travel, they
ANTONIO: Will not, nor cannot, use such vigilance
ANTONIO: As when they are fresh.
SEBASTIAN: [Aside to ANTONIO]  I say, to-night: no more.
NARRATOR: Solemn and strange music
ALONSO: What harmony is this? My good friends, hark!
GONZALO: Marvellous sweet music!
GONZALO: Enter PROSPERO above, invisible. Enter several  strange Shapes, bringing in a banquet,  they dance about it with gentle actions of  salutation, and, inviting the King,  and c. to eat, they depart
ALONSO: Give us kind keepers, heavens! What were these?
SEBASTIAN: A living drollery. Now I will believe
SEBASTIAN: That there are unicorns, that in Arabia
SEBASTIAN: There is one tree, the phoenix' throne, one phoenix
SEBASTIAN: At this hour reigning there.

ANTONIO: And I'll be sworn 'tis true: travellers ne'er did
ANTONIO: lie,
ANTONIO: Though fools at home condemn 'em.
GONZALO: If in Naples

GONZALO: For, certes, these are people of the island--

GONZALO: Our human generation you shall find

PROSPERO: [Aside]	Praise in departing.
FRANCISCO: They vanish'd strangely.
SEBASTIAN: No matter, since
SEBASTIAN: They have left their viands behind, for we have stomachs.
SEBASTIAN: Will't please you taste of what is here?

GONZALO: Faith, sir, you need not fear. When we were boys,
GONZALO: Who would believe that there were mountaineers

GONZALO: Wallets of flesh? or that there were such men

GONZALO: Each putter-out of five for one will bring us
GONZALO: Good warrant of.
ALONSO: I will stand to and feed,
ALONSO: Although my last: no matter, since I feel
ALONSO: The best is past. Brother, my lord the duke,
ALONSO: Stand to and do as we.
ALONSO: Thunder and lightning. Enter ARIEL, like a  harpy, claps his wings upon the table, and, with a quaint device, the banquet vanishes
ARIEL: You are three men of sin, whom Destiny,
ARIEL: That hath to instrument this lower world
ARIEL: And what is in't, the never-surfeited sea
ARIEL: Hath caused to belch up you, and on this island
ARIEL: Where man doth not inhabit, you 'mongst men
ARIEL: Being most unfit to live. I have made you mad,
ARIEL: And even with such-like valour men hang and drown
ARIEL: Their proper selves.
ARIEL: ALONSO, SEBASTIAN  and c. draw their swords
ARIEL: You fools! I and my fellows
ARIEL: Are ministers of Fate: the elements,
ARIEL: Of whom your swords are temper'd, may as well
ARIEL: Wound the loud winds, or with bemock'd-at stabs
ARIEL: Kill the still-closing waters, as diminish
ARIEL: One dowle that's in my plume: my fellow-ministers
ARIEL: Are like invulnerable. If you could hurt,
ARIEL: Your swords are now too massy for your strengths
ARIEL: And will not be uplifted. But remember--
ARIEL: For that's my business to you--that you three
ARIEL: From Milan did supplant good Prospero,
ARIEL: Exposed unto the sea, which hath requit it,
ARIEL: Him and his innocent child: for which foul deed
ARIEL: The powers, delaying, not forgetting, have
ARIEL: Incensed the seas and shores, yea, all the creatures,
ARIEL: Against your peace. Thee of thy son, Alonso,
ARIEL: They have bereft, and do pronounce by me:
ARIEL: Lingering perdition, worse than any death
ARIEL: Can be at once, shall step by step attend
ARIEL: You and your ways, whose wraths to guard you from--
ARIEL: Which here, in this most desolate isle, else falls
ARIEL: Upon your heads--is nothing but heart-sorrow
ARIEL: And a clear life ensuing.
ARIEL: He vanishes in thunder, then, to soft music  enter the Shapes again, and dance, with mocks and mows, and carrying out the table
PROSPERO: Bravely the figure of this harpy hast thou
PROSPERO: Perform'd, my Ariel, a grace it had, devouring:
PROSPERO: Of my instruction hast thou nothing bated
PROSPERO: In what thou hadst to say: so, with good life
PROSPERO: And observation strange, my meaner ministers
PROSPERO: Their several kinds have done. My high charms work
PROSPERO: And these mine enemies are all knit up
PROSPERO: In their distractions, they now are in my power,
PROSPERO: And in these fits I leave them, while I visit
PROSPERO: Young Ferdinand, whom they suppose is drown'd,
PROSPERO: And his and mine loved darling.
NARRATOR: Exit above
GONZALO: I' the name of something holy, sir, why stand you
GONZALO: In this strange stare?
ALONSO: O, it is monstrous, monstrous:
ALONSO: Methought the billows spoke and told me of it,
ALONSO: The winds did sing it to me, and the thunder,
ALONSO: That deep and dreadful organ-pipe, pronounced
ALONSO: The name of Prosper: it did bass my trespass.
ALONSO: Therefore my son i' the ooze is bedded, and
ALONSO: I'll seek him deeper than e'er plummet sounded

NARRATOR: Exit
SEBASTIAN: But one fiend at a time,
SEBASTIAN: I'll fight their legions o'er.
ANTONIO: I'll be thy second.
NARRATOR: Exeunt SEBASTIAN, and ANTONIO
GONZALO: All three of them are desperate: their great guilt,
GONZALO: Like poison given to work a great time after,
GONZALO: Now 'gins to bite the spirits. I do beseech you
GONZALO: That are of suppler joints, follow them swiftly

GONZALO: May now provoke them to.

NARRATOR: ACT IV
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Before PROSPERO'S cell.
NARRATOR: Enter PROSPERO, FERDINAND, and MIRANDA
PROSPERO: If I have too austerely punish'd you,
PROSPERO: Your compensation makes amends, for I
PROSPERO: Have given you here a third of mine own life,
PROSPERO: Or that for which I live, who once again
PROSPERO: I tender to thy hand: all thy vexations
PROSPERO: Were but my trials of thy love and thou
PROSPERO: Hast strangely stood the test here, afore Heaven,
PROSPERO: I ratify this my rich gift. O Ferdinand,
PROSPERO: Do not smile at me that I boast her off,
PROSPERO: For thou shalt find she will outstrip all praise
PROSPERO: And make it halt behind her.
FERDINAND: I do believe it
FERDINAND: Against an oracle.
PROSPERO: Then, as my gift and thine own acquisition
PROSPERO: Worthily purchased take my daughter: but
PROSPERO: If thou dost break her virgin-knot before
PROSPERO: All sanctimonious ceremonies may
PROSPERO: With full and holy rite be minister'd,
PROSPERO: No sweet aspersion shall the heavens let fall
PROSPERO: To make this contract grow: but barren hate,
PROSPERO: Sour-eyed disdain and discord shall bestrew
PROSPERO: The union of your bed with weeds so loathly
PROSPERO: That you shall hate it both: therefore take heed,
PROSPERO: As Hymen's lamps shall light you.
FERDINAND: As I hope
FERDINAND: For quiet days, fair issue and long life,
FERDINAND: With such love as 'tis now, the murkiest den,
FERDINAND: The most opportune place, the strong'st suggestion.
FERDINAND: Our worser genius can, shall never melt
FERDINAND: Mine honour into lust, to take away
FERDINAND: The edge of that day's celebration
FERDINAND: When I shall think: or Phoebus' steeds are founder'd,
FERDINAND: Or Night kept chain'd below.
PROSPERO: Fairly spoke.
PROSPERO: Sit then and talk with her, she is thine own.
PROSPERO: What, Ariel! my industrious servant, Ariel!
NARRATOR: Enter ARIEL
ARIEL: What would my potent master? here I am.
PROSPERO: Thou and thy meaner fellows your last service
PROSPERO: Did worthily perform, and I must use you
PROSPERO: In such another trick. Go bring the rabble,
PROSPERO: O'er whom I give thee power, here to this place:
PROSPERO: Incite them to quick motion, for I must
PROSPERO: Bestow upon the eyes of this young couple
PROSPERO: Some vanity of mine art: it is my promise,
PROSPERO: And they expect it from me.
ARIEL: Presently?
PROSPERO: Ay, with a twink.
ARIEL: Before you can say 'come' and 'go,'
ARIEL: And breathe twice and cry 'so, so,'
ARIEL: Each one, tripping on his toe,
ARIEL: Will be here with mop and mow.
ARIEL: Do you love me, master? no?
PROSPERO: Dearly my delicate Ariel. Do not approach
PROSPERO: Till thou dost hear me call.
ARIEL: Well, I conceive.
NARRATOR: Exit
PROSPERO: Look thou be true, do not give dalliance
PROSPERO: Too much the rein: the strongest oaths are straw
PROSPERO: To the fire i' the blood: be more abstemious,
PROSPERO: Or else, good night your vow!
FERDINAND: I warrant you sir,
FERDINAND: The white cold virgin snow upon my heart
FERDINAND: Abates the ardour of my liver.
PROSPERO: Well.
PROSPERO: Now come, my Ariel! bring a corollary,
PROSPERO: Rather than want a spirit: appear and pertly!
PROSPERO: No tongue! all eyes! be silent.
NARRATOR: Soft music
NARRATOR: Enter IRIS
IRIS: Ceres, most bounteous lady, thy rich leas
IRIS: Of wheat, rye, barley, vetches, oats and pease,
IRIS: Thy turfy mountains, where live nibbling sheep,
IRIS: And flat meads thatch'd with stover, them to keep,
IRIS: Thy banks with pioned and twilled brims,
IRIS: Which spongy April at thy hest betrims,
IRIS: To make cold nymphs chaste crowns, and thy broom -groves,
IRIS: Whose shadow the dismissed bachelor loves,
IRIS: Being lass-lorn: thy pole-clipt vineyard,
IRIS: And thy sea-marge, sterile and rocky-hard,
IRIS: Where thou thyself dost air,--the queen o' the sky,
IRIS: Whose watery arch and messenger am I,
IRIS: Bids thee leave these, and with her sovereign grace,
IRIS: Here on this grass-plot, in this very place,
IRIS: To come and sport: her peacocks fly amain:
IRIS: Approach, rich Ceres, her to entertain.
NARRATOR: Enter CERES
CERES: Hail, many-colour'd messenger, that ne'er
CERES: Dost disobey the wife of Jupiter,
CERES: Who with thy saffron wings upon my flowers
CERES: Diffusest honey-drops, refreshing showers,
CERES: And with each end of thy blue bow dost crown
CERES: My bosky acres and my unshrubb'd down,
CERES: Rich scarf to my proud earth, why hath thy queen
CERES: Summon'd me hither, to this short-grass'd green?
IRIS: A contract of true love to celebrate,
IRIS: And some donation freely to estate
IRIS: On the blest lovers.
CERES: Tell me, heavenly bow,
CERES: If Venus or her son, as thou dost know,
CERES: Do now attend the queen? Since they did plot
CERES: The means that dusky Dis my daughter got,
CERES: Her and her blind boy's scandal'd company
CERES: I have forsworn.
IRIS: Of her society
IRIS: Be not afraid: I met her deity
IRIS: Cutting the clouds towards Paphos and her son
IRIS: Dove-drawn with her. Here thought they to have done
IRIS: Some wanton charm upon this man and maid,
IRIS: Whose vows are, that no bed-right shall be paid
IRIS: Till Hymen's torch be lighted: but vain,
IRIS: Mars's hot minion is returned again,
IRIS: Her waspish-headed son has broke his arrows,
IRIS: Swears he will shoot no more but play with sparrows
IRIS: And be a boy right out.
CERES: High'st queen of state,
CERES: Great Juno, comes, I know her by her gait.
NARRATOR: Enter JUNO
JUNO: How does my bounteous sister? Go with me
JUNO: To bless this twain, that they may prosperous be
JUNO: And honour'd in their issue.
JUNO: They sing:
JUNO: Honour, riches, marriage-blessing,
JUNO: Long continuance, and increasing,
JUNO: Hourly joys be still upon you!
JUNO: Juno sings her blessings upon you.
CERES: Earth's increase, foison plenty,
CERES: Barns and garners never empty,
CERES: Vines and clustering bunches growing,
CERES: Plants with goodly burthen bowing,
CERES: Spring come to you at the farthest
CERES: In the very end of harvest!
CERES: Scarcity and want shall shun you,
CERES: Ceres' blessing so is on you.
FERDINAND: This is a most majestic vision, and
FERDINAND: Harmoniously charmingly. May I be bold
FERDINAND: To think these spirits?
PROSPERO: Spirits, which by mine art
PROSPERO: I have from their confines call'd to enact
PROSPERO: My present fancies.
FERDINAND: Let me live here ever,
FERDINAND: So rare a wonder'd father and a wife
FERDINAND: Makes this place Paradise.
NARRATOR: Juno and Ceres whisper, and send Iris on employment
PROSPERO: Sweet, now, silence!
PROSPERO: Juno and Ceres whisper seriously,
PROSPERO: There's something else to do: hush, and be mute,
PROSPERO: Or else our spell is marr'd.
IRIS: You nymphs, call'd Naiads, of the windring brooks,
IRIS: With your sedged crowns and ever-harmless looks,
IRIS: Leave your crisp channels and on this green land
IRIS: Answer your summons, Juno does command:
IRIS: Come, temperate nymphs, and help to celebrate
IRIS: A contract of true love, be not too late.
NARRATOR: Enter certain Nymphs
IRIS: You sunburnt sicklemen, of August weary,
IRIS: Come hither from the furrow and be merry:
IRIS: Make holiday, your rye-straw hats put on
IRIS: And these fresh nymphs encounter every one
IRIS: In country footing.
IRIS: Enter certain Reapers, properly habited: they  join with the Nymphs in a graceful dance,  towards the end whereof PROSPERO starts  suddenly, and speaks, after which, to a  strange, hollow, and confused noise, they heavily vanish
PROSPERO: [Aside]  I had forgot that foul conspiracy
PROSPERO: Of the beast Caliban and his confederates
PROSPERO: Against my life: the minute of their plot
PROSPERO: Is almost come.
NARRATOR: To the Spirits
PROSPERO: Well done! avoid, no more!
FERDINAND: This is strange: your father's in some passion
FERDINAND: That works him strongly.
MIRANDA: Never till this day
MIRANDA: Saw I him touch'd with anger so distemper'd.
PROSPERO: You do look, my son, in a moved sort,
PROSPERO: As if you were dismay'd: be cheerful, sir.
PROSPERO: Our revels now are ended. These our actors,
PROSPERO: As I foretold you, were all spirits and
PROSPERO: Are melted into air, into thin air:
PROSPERO: And, like the baseless fabric of this vision,
PROSPERO: The cloud-capp'd towers, the gorgeous palaces,
PROSPERO: The solemn temples, the great globe itself,
PROSPERO: Ye all which it inherit, shall dissolve
PROSPERO: And, like this insubstantial pageant faded,

PROSPERO: As dreams are made on, and our little life
PROSPERO: Is rounded with a sleep. Sir, I am vex'd,

PROSPERO: Be not disturb'd with my infirmity:
PROSPERO: If you be pleased, retire into my cell
PROSPERO: And there repose: a turn or two I'll walk,
PROSPERO: To still my beating mind.
MIRANDA: We wish your peace.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
PROSPERO: Come with a thought I thank thee, Ariel: come.
NARRATOR: Enter ARIEL
ARIEL: Thy thoughts I cleave to. What's thy pleasure?
PROSPERO: Spirit,
PROSPERO: We must prepare to meet with Caliban.

ARIEL: their ears,
ARIEL: Advanced their eyelids, lifted up their noses

ARIEL: There dancing up to the chins, that the foul lake
ARIEL: O'erstunk their feet.
PROSPERO: This was well done, my bird.
PROSPERO: Thy shape invisible retain thou still:
PROSPERO: The trumpery in my house, go bring it hither,
PROSPERO: For stale to catch these thieves.
ARIEL: I go, I go.

PROSPERO: A devil, a born devil, on whose nature

NARRATOR: ACT V
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Before PROSPERO'S cell.
NARRATOR: Enter PROSPERO in his magic robes, and ARIEL

PROSPERO: My charms crack not, my spirits obey, and time

ARIEL: You said our work should cease.
PROSPERO: I did say so,
PROSPERO: When first I raised the tempest. Say, my spirit,

ARIEL: Would become tender.
PROSPERO: Dost thou think so, spirit?
ARIEL: Mine would, sir, were I human.
PROSPERO: And mine shall.
PROSPERO: Hast thou, which art but air, a touch, a feeling
PROSPERO: Of their afflictions, and shall not myself,
PROSPERO: One of their kind, that relish all as sharply,
PROSPERO: Passion as they, be kindlier moved than thou art?
PROSPERO: Though with their high wrongs I am struck to the quick,
PROSPERO: Yet with my nobler reason 'gaitist my fury
PROSPERO: Do I take part: the rarer action is
PROSPERO: In virtue than in vengeance: they being penitent,
PROSPERO: The sole drift of my purpose doth extend
PROSPERO: Not a frown further. Go release them, Ariel:
PROSPERO: My charms I'll break, their senses I'll restore,
PROSPERO: And they shall be themselves.
ARIEL: I'll fetch them, sir.

PROSPERO: Ye elves of hills, brooks, standing lakes and groves,

PROSPERO: The noontide sun, call'd forth the mutinous winds,
