EGLAMOUR: If we recover that, we are sure enough.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The same. The DUKE's palace.
NARRATOR: Enter THURIO, PROTEUS, and JULIA
THURIO: Sir Proteus, what says Silvia to my suit?
PROTEUS: O, sir, I find her milder than she was,
PROTEUS: And yet she takes exceptions at your person.
THURIO: What, that my leg is too long?
PROTEUS: No, that it is too little.
THURIO: I'll wear a boot, to make it somewhat rounder.
JULIA: [Aside]  But love will not be spurr'd to what
JULIA: it loathes.
THURIO: What says she to my face?
PROTEUS: She says it is a fair one.
THURIO: Nay then, the wanton lies, my face is black.
PROTEUS: But pearls are fair, and the old saying is,
PROTEUS: Black men are pearls in beauteous ladies' eyes.
JULIA: [Aside]  'Tis true, such pearls as put out
JULIA: ladies' eyes,
JULIA: For I had rather wink than look on them.
THURIO: How likes she my discourse?
PROTEUS: Ill, when you talk of war.
THURIO: But well, when I discourse of love and peace?
JULIA: [Aside]  But better, indeed, when you hold your peace.
THURIO: What says she to my valour?
PROTEUS: O, sir, she makes no doubt of that.
JULIA: [Aside]  She needs not, when she knows it cowardice.
THURIO: What says she to my birth?
PROTEUS: That you are well derived.
JULIA: [Aside]  True, from a gentleman to a fool.
THURIO: Considers she my possessions?
PROTEUS: O, ay, and pities them.
THURIO: Wherefore?
JULIA: [Aside]  That such an ass should owe them.
PROTEUS: That they are out by lease.
JULIA: Here comes the duke.
NARRATOR: Enter DUKE
DUKE: How now, Sir Proteus! how now, Thurio!
DUKE: Which of you saw Sir Eglamour of late?
THURIO: Not I.
PROTEUS: Nor I.
DUKE: Saw you my daughter?
PROTEUS: Neither.
DUKE: Why then,
DUKE: She's fled unto that peasant Valentine,
DUKE: And Eglamour is in her company.
DUKE: 'Tis true, for Friar Laurence met them both,
DUKE: As he in penance wander'd through the forest,
DUKE: Him he knew well, and guess'd that it was she,
DUKE: But, being mask'd, he was not sure of it,
DUKE: Besides, she did intend confession
DUKE: At Patrick's cell this even, and there she was not,
DUKE: These likelihoods confirm her flight from hence.
DUKE: Therefore, I pray you, stand not to discourse,
DUKE: But mount you presently and meet with me
DUKE: Upon the rising of the mountain-foot
DUKE: That leads towards Mantua, whither they are fled:
DUKE: Dispatch, sweet gentlemen, and follow me.
NARRATOR: Exit
THURIO: Why, this it is to be a peevish girl,
THURIO: That flies her fortune when it follows her.
THURIO: I'll after, more to be revenged on Eglamour
THURIO: Than for the love of reckless Silvia.
NARRATOR: Exit
PROTEUS: And I will follow, more for Silvia's love
PROTEUS: Than hate of Eglamour that goes with her.
NARRATOR: Exit
JULIA: And I will follow, more to cross that love
JULIA: Than hate for Silvia that is gone for love.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE III. The frontiers of Mantua. The forest.
NARRATOR: Enter Outlaws with SILVIA
First Outlaw: Come, come,
First Outlaw: Be patient, we must bring you to our captain.
SILVIA: A thousand more mischances than this one
SILVIA: Have learn'd me how to brook this patiently.
Second Outlaw: Come, bring her away.
First Outlaw: Where is the gentleman that was with her?
Third Outlaw: Being nimble-footed, he hath outrun us,
Third Outlaw: But Moyses and Valerius follow him.
Third Outlaw: Go thou with her to the west end of the wood,
Third Outlaw: There is our captain: we'll follow him that's fled,
Third Outlaw: The thicket is beset, he cannot 'scape.
First Outlaw: Come, I must bring you to our captain's cave:
First Outlaw: Fear not, he bears an honourable mind,
First Outlaw: And will not use a woman lawlessly.
SILVIA: O Valentine, this I endure for thee!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Another part of the forest.
NARRATOR: Enter VALENTINE
VALENTINE: How use doth breed a habit in a man!
VALENTINE: This shadowy desert, unfrequented woods,
VALENTINE: I better brook than flourishing peopled towns:
VALENTINE: Here can I sit alone, unseen of any,
VALENTINE: And to the nightingale's complaining notes
VALENTINE: Tune my distresses and record my woes.
VALENTINE: O thou that dost inhabit in my breast,
VALENTINE: Leave not the mansion so long tenantless,
VALENTINE: Lest, growing ruinous, the building fall
VALENTINE: And leave no memory of what it was!
VALENTINE: Repair me with thy presence, Silvia,
VALENTINE: Thou gentle nymph, cherish thy forlorn swain!
VALENTINE: What halloing and what stir is this to-day?
VALENTINE: These are my mates, that make their wills their law,
VALENTINE: Have some unhappy passenger in chase.
VALENTINE: They love me well, yet I have much to do
VALENTINE: To keep them from uncivil outrages.
VALENTINE: Withdraw thee, Valentine: who's this comes here?
NARRATOR: Enter PROTEUS, SILVIA, and JULIA
PROTEUS: Madam, this service I have done for you,
PROTEUS: Though you respect not aught your servant doth,
PROTEUS: To hazard life and rescue you from him
PROTEUS: That would have forced your honour and your love,
PROTEUS: Vouchsafe me, for my meed, but one fair look,
PROTEUS: A smaller boon than this I cannot beg
PROTEUS: And less than this, I am sure, you cannot give.
VALENTINE: [Aside]  How like a dream is this I see and hear!
VALENTINE: Love, lend me patience to forbear awhile.
SILVIA: O miserable, unhappy that I am!
PROTEUS: Unhappy were you, madam, ere I came,
PROTEUS: But by my coming I have made you happy.
SILVIA: By thy approach thou makest me most unhappy.
JULIA: [Aside]  And me, when he approacheth to your presence.
SILVIA: Had I been seized by a hungry lion,
SILVIA: I would have been a breakfast to the beast,
SILVIA: Rather than have false Proteus rescue me.
SILVIA: O, Heaven be judge how I love Valentine,
SILVIA: Whose life's as tender to me as my soul!
SILVIA: And full as much, for more there cannot be,
SILVIA: I do detest false perjured Proteus.
SILVIA: Therefore be gone, solicit me no more.
PROTEUS: What dangerous action, stood it next to death,
PROTEUS: Would I not undergo for one calm look!
PROTEUS: O, 'tis the curse in love, and still approved,
PROTEUS: When women cannot love where they're beloved!
SILVIA: When Proteus cannot love where he's beloved.
SILVIA: Read over Julia's heart, thy first best love,
SILVIA: For whose dear sake thou didst then rend thy faith
SILVIA: Into a thousand oaths, and all those oaths
SILVIA: Descended into perjury, to love me.
SILVIA: Thou hast no faith left now, unless thou'dst two,
SILVIA: And that's far worse than none, better have none
SILVIA: Than plural faith which is too much by one:
SILVIA: Thou counterfeit to thy true friend!
PROTEUS: In love
PROTEUS: Who respects friend?
SILVIA: All men but Proteus.
PROTEUS: Nay, if the gentle spirit of moving words
PROTEUS: Can no way change you to a milder form,
PROTEUS: I'll woo you like a soldier, at arms' end,
PROTEUS: And love you 'gainst the nature of love,--force ye.
SILVIA: O heaven!
PROTEUS: I'll force thee yield to my desire.
VALENTINE: Ruffian, let go that rude uncivil touch,
VALENTINE: Thou friend of an ill fashion!
PROTEUS: Valentine!
VALENTINE: Thou common friend, that's without faith or love,
VALENTINE: For such is a friend now, treacherous man!
VALENTINE: Thou hast beguiled my hopes, nought but mine eye
VALENTINE: Could have persuaded me: now I dare not say
VALENTINE: I have one friend alive, thou wouldst disprove me.
VALENTINE: Who should be trusted, when one's own right hand
VALENTINE: Is perjured to the bosom? Proteus,
VALENTINE: I am sorry I must never trust thee more,
VALENTINE: But count the world a stranger for thy sake.
VALENTINE: The private wound is deepest: O time most accurst,
VALENTINE: 'Mongst all foes that a friend should be the worst!
PROTEUS: My shame and guilt confounds me.
PROTEUS: Forgive me, Valentine: if hearty sorrow
PROTEUS: Be a sufficient ransom for offence,
PROTEUS: I tender 't here, I do as truly suffer
PROTEUS: As e'er I did commit.
VALENTINE: Then I am paid,
VALENTINE: And once again I do receive thee honest.
VALENTINE: Who by repentance is not satisfied
VALENTINE: Is nor of heaven nor earth, for these are pleased.
VALENTINE: By penitence the Eternal's wrath's appeased:
VALENTINE: And, that my love may appear plain and free,
VALENTINE: All that was mine in Silvia I give thee.
JULIA: O me unhappy!
NARRATOR: Swoons
PROTEUS: Look to the boy.
VALENTINE: Why, boy! why, wag! how now! what's the matter?
VALENTINE: Look up, speak.
JULIA: O good sir, my master charged me to deliver a ring
JULIA: to Madam Silvia, which, out of my neglect, was never done.
PROTEUS: Where is that ring, boy?
JULIA: Here 'tis, this is it.
PROTEUS: How! let me see:
PROTEUS: Why, this is the ring I gave to Julia.
JULIA: O, cry you mercy, sir, I have mistook:
JULIA: This is the ring you sent to Silvia.
PROTEUS: But how camest thou by this ring? At my depart
PROTEUS: I gave this unto Julia.
JULIA: And Julia herself did give it me,
JULIA: And Julia herself hath brought it hither.
PROTEUS: How! Julia!
JULIA: Behold her that gave aim to all thy oaths,
JULIA: And entertain'd 'em deeply in her heart.
JULIA: How oft hast thou with perjury cleft the root!
JULIA: O Proteus, let this habit make thee blush!
JULIA: Be thou ashamed that I have took upon me
JULIA: Such an immodest raiment, if shame live
JULIA: In a disguise of love:
JULIA: It is the lesser blot, modesty finds,
JULIA: Women to change their shapes than men their minds.
PROTEUS: Than men their minds! 'tis true.
PROTEUS: O heaven! were man
PROTEUS: But constant, he were perfect. That one error
PROTEUS: Fills him with faults, makes him run through all the sins:
PROTEUS: Inconstancy falls off ere it begins.
PROTEUS: What is in Silvia's face, but I may spy
PROTEUS: More fresh in Julia's with a constant eye?
VALENTINE: Come, come, a hand from either:
VALENTINE: Let me be blest to make this happy close,
VALENTINE: 'Twere pity two such friends should be long foes.
PROTEUS: Bear witness, Heaven, I have my wish for ever.
JULIA: And I mine.
NARRATOR: Enter Outlaws, with DUKE and THURIO
Outlaws: A prize, a prize, a prize!
VALENTINE: Forbear, forbear, I say! it is my lord the duke.
VALENTINE: Your grace is welcome to a man disgraced,
VALENTINE: Banished Valentine.
DUKE: Sir Valentine!
THURIO: Yonder is Silvia, and Silvia's mine.
VALENTINE: Thurio, give back, or else embrace thy death,
VALENTINE: Come not within the measure of my wrath,
VALENTINE: Do not name Silvia thine, if once again,
VALENTINE: Verona shall not hold thee. Here she stands,
VALENTINE: Take but possession of her with a touch:
VALENTINE: I dare thee but to breathe upon my love.
THURIO: Sir Valentine, I care not for her, I,
THURIO: I hold him but a fool that will endanger
THURIO: His body for a girl that loves him not:
THURIO: I claim her not, and therefore she is thine.
DUKE: The more degenerate and base art thou,
DUKE: To make such means for her as thou hast done
DUKE: And leave her on such slight conditions.
DUKE: Now, by the honour of my ancestry,
DUKE: I do applaud thy spirit, Valentine,
DUKE: And think thee worthy of an empress' love:
DUKE: Know then, I here forget all former griefs,
DUKE: Cancel all grudge, repeal thee home again,
DUKE: Plead a new state in thy unrivall'd merit,
DUKE: To which I thus subscribe: Sir Valentine,
DUKE: Thou art a gentleman and well derived,
DUKE: Take thou thy Silvia, for thou hast deserved her.
VALENTINE: I thank your grace, the gift hath made me happy.
VALENTINE: I now beseech you, for your daughter's sake,
VALENTINE: To grant one boom that I shall ask of you.
DUKE: I grant it, for thine own, whate'er it be.
VALENTINE: These banish'd men that I have kept withal
VALENTINE: Are men endued with worthy qualities:
VALENTINE: Forgive them what they have committed here
VALENTINE: And let them be recall'd from their exile:
VALENTINE: They are reformed, civil, full of good
VALENTINE: And fit for great employment, worthy lord.
DUKE: Thou hast prevail'd, I pardon them and thee:
DUKE: Dispose of them as thou know'st their deserts.
DUKE: Come, let us go: we will include all jars
DUKE: With triumphs, mirth and rare solemnity.
VALENTINE: And, as we walk along, I dare be bold
VALENTINE: With our discourse to make your grace to smile.
VALENTINE: What think you of this page, my lord?
DUKE: I think the boy hath grace in him, he blushes.
VALENTINE: I warrant you, my lord, more grace than boy.
DUKE: What mean you by that saying?
VALENTINE: Please you, I'll tell you as we pass along,
VALENTINE: That you will wonder what hath fortuned.
VALENTINE: Come, Proteus, 'tis your penance but to hear
VALENTINE: The story of your loves discovered:
VALENTINE: That done, our day of marriage shall be yours,
VALENTINE: One feast, one house, one mutual happiness.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
''' PLAY: macbeth '''
NARRATOR: ACT I
NARRATOR: SCENE I. A desert place.
NARRATOR: Thunder and lightning. Enter three Witches
First Witch: When shall we three meet again
First Witch: In thunder, lightning, or in rain?
Second Witch: When the hurlyburly's done,
Second Witch: When the battle's lost and won.
Third Witch: That will be ere the set of sun.
First Witch: Where the place?
Second Witch: Upon the heath.
Third Witch: There to meet with Macbeth.
First Witch: I come, Graymalkin!
Second Witch: Paddock calls.
Third Witch: Anon.
ALL: Fair is foul, and foul is fair:
ALL: Hover through the fog and filthy air.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE II. A camp near Forres.
NARRATOR: Alarum within. Enter DUNCAN, MALCOLM, DONALBAIN, LENNOX, with Attendants, meeting a bleeding Sergeant
DUNCAN: What bloody man is that? He can report,
DUNCAN: As seemeth by his plight, of the revolt
DUNCAN: The newest state.
MALCOLM: This is the sergeant
MALCOLM: Who like a good and hardy soldier fought
MALCOLM: 'Gainst my captivity. Hail, brave friend!
MALCOLM: Say to the king the knowledge of the broil
MALCOLM: As thou didst leave it.
Sergeant: Doubtful it stood,
Sergeant: As two spent swimmers, that do cling together
Sergeant: And choke their art. The merciless Macdonwald--
Sergeant: Worthy to be a rebel, for to that
Sergeant: The multiplying villanies of nature
Sergeant: Do swarm upon him--from the western isles
Sergeant: Of kerns and gallowglasses is supplied,
Sergeant: And fortune, on his damned quarrel smiling,
Sergeant: Show'd like a rebel's whore: but all's too weak:
Sergeant: For brave Macbeth--well he deserves that name--
Sergeant: Disdaining fortune, with his brandish'd steel,
Sergeant: Which smoked with bloody execution,
Sergeant: Like valour's minion carved out his passage
Sergeant: Till he faced the slave,
Sergeant: Which ne'er shook hands, nor bade farewell to him,
Sergeant: Till he unseam'd him from the nave to the chaps,
Sergeant: And fix'd his head upon our battlements.
DUNCAN: O valiant cousin! worthy gentleman!
Sergeant: As whence the sun 'gins his reflection
Sergeant: Shipwrecking storms and direful thunders break,
Sergeant: So from that spring whence comfort seem'd to come
Sergeant: Discomfort swells. Mark, king of Scotland, mark:
Sergeant: No sooner justice had with valour arm'd
Sergeant: Compell'd these skipping kerns to trust their heels,
Sergeant: But the Norweyan lord surveying vantage,
Sergeant: With furbish'd arms and new supplies of men
Sergeant: Began a fresh assault.
DUNCAN: Dismay'd not this
DUNCAN: Our captains, Macbeth and Banquo?
Sergeant: Yes,
Sergeant: As sparrows eagles, or the hare the lion.
Sergeant: If I say sooth, I must report they were
Sergeant: As cannons overcharged with double cracks, so they
Sergeant: Doubly redoubled strokes upon the foe:
Sergeant: Except they meant to bathe in reeking wounds,
Sergeant: Or memorise another Golgotha,
Sergeant: I cannot tell.
Sergeant: But I am faint, my gashes cry for help.
DUNCAN: So well thy words become thee as thy wounds,
DUNCAN: They smack of honour both. Go get him surgeons.
NARRATOR: Exit Sergeant, attended
DUNCAN: Who comes here?
NARRATOR: Enter ROSS
MALCOLM: The worthy thane of Ross.
LENNOX: What a haste looks through his eyes! So should he look
LENNOX: That seems to speak things strange.
ROSS: God save the king!
DUNCAN: Whence camest thou, worthy thane?
ROSS: From Fife, great king,
ROSS: Where the Norweyan banners flout the sky
ROSS: And fan our people cold. Norway himself,
ROSS: With terrible numbers,
ROSS: Assisted by that most disloyal traitor
ROSS: The thane of Cawdor, began a dismal conflict,
ROSS: Till that Bellona's bridegroom, lapp'd in proof,
ROSS: Confronted him with self-comparisons,
ROSS: Point against point rebellious, arm 'gainst arm.
ROSS: Curbing his lavish spirit: and, to conclude,
ROSS: The victory fell on us.
DUNCAN: Great happiness!
ROSS: That now
ROSS: Sweno, the Norways' king, craves composition:
ROSS: Nor would we deign him burial of his men
ROSS: Till he disbursed at Saint Colme's inch
ROSS: Ten thousand dollars to our general use.
DUNCAN: No more that thane of Cawdor shall deceive
DUNCAN: Our bosom interest: go pronounce his present death,
DUNCAN: And with his former title greet Macbeth.
ROSS: I'll see it done.
DUNCAN: What he hath lost noble Macbeth hath won.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A heath near Forres.
NARRATOR: Thunder. Enter the three Witches
First Witch: Where hast thou been, sister?
Second Witch: Killing swine.
Third Witch: Sister, where thou?
First Witch: A sailor's wife had chestnuts in her lap,
First Witch: And munch'd, and munch'd, and munch'd:--
First Witch: 'Give me,' quoth I:
First Witch: 'Aroint thee, witch!' the rump-fed ronyon cries.
First Witch: Her husband's to Aleppo gone, master o' the Tiger:
First Witch: But in a sieve I'll thither sail,
First Witch: And, like a rat without a tail,
First Witch: I'll do, I'll do, and I'll do.
Second Witch: I'll give thee a wind.
First Witch: Thou'rt kind.
Third Witch: And I another.
First Witch: I myself have all the other,
First Witch: And the very ports they blow,
First Witch: All the quarters that they know
First Witch: I' the shipman's card.
First Witch: I will drain him dry as hay:
First Witch: Sleep shall neither night nor day
First Witch: Hang upon his pent-house lid,
First Witch: He shall live a man forbid:
First Witch: Weary se'nnights nine times nine
First Witch: Shall he dwindle, peak and pine:
First Witch: Though his bark cannot be lost,
First Witch: Yet it shall be tempest-tost.
First Witch: Look what I have.
Second Witch: Show me, show me.
First Witch: Here I have a pilot's thumb,
First Witch: Wreck'd as homeward he did come.
NARRATOR: Drum within
Third Witch: A drum, a drum!
Third Witch: Macbeth doth come.
ALL: The weird sisters, hand in hand,
ALL: Posters of the sea and land,
ALL: Thus do go about, about:
ALL: Thrice to thine and thrice to mine
ALL: And thrice again, to make up nine.
ALL: Peace! the charm's wound up.
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH and BANQUO
MACBETH: So foul and fair a day I have not seen.
BANQUO: How far is't call'd to Forres? What are these
BANQUO: So wither'd and so wild in their attire,
BANQUO: That look not like the inhabitants o' the earth,
BANQUO: And yet are on't? Live you? or are you aught
BANQUO: That man may question? You seem to understand me,
BANQUO: By each at once her chappy finger laying
BANQUO: Upon her skinny lips: you should be women,
BANQUO: And yet your beards forbid me to interpret
BANQUO: That you are so.
MACBETH: Speak, if you can: what are you?
First Witch: All hail, Macbeth! hail to thee, thane of Glamis!
Second Witch: All hail, Macbeth, hail to thee, thane of Cawdor!
Third Witch: All hail, Macbeth, thou shalt be king hereafter!
BANQUO: Good sir, why do you start, and seem to fear
BANQUO: Things that do sound so fair? I' the name of truth,
BANQUO: Are ye fantastical, or that indeed
BANQUO: Which outwardly ye show? My noble partner
BANQUO: You greet with present grace and great prediction
BANQUO: Of noble having and of royal hope,
BANQUO: That he seems rapt withal: to me you speak not.
BANQUO: If you can look into the seeds of time,
BANQUO: And say which grain will grow and which will not,
BANQUO: Speak then to me, who neither beg nor fear
BANQUO: Your favours nor your hate.
First Witch: Hail!
Second Witch: Hail!
Third Witch: Hail!
First Witch: Lesser than Macbeth, and greater.
Second Witch: Not so happy, yet much happier.
Third Witch: Thou shalt get kings, though thou be none:
Third Witch: So all hail, Macbeth and Banquo!
First Witch: Banquo and Macbeth, all hail!
MACBETH: Stay, you imperfect speakers, tell me more:
MACBETH: By Sinel's death I know I am thane of Glamis,
MACBETH: But how of Cawdor? the thane of Cawdor lives,
MACBETH: A prosperous gentleman, and to be king
MACBETH: Stands not within the prospect of belief,
MACBETH: No more than to be Cawdor. Say from whence
MACBETH: You owe this strange intelligence? or why
MACBETH: Upon this blasted heath you stop our way
MACBETH: With such prophetic greeting? Speak, I charge you.
NARRATOR: Witches vanish
BANQUO: The earth hath bubbles, as the water has,
BANQUO: And these are of them. Whither are they vanish'd?
MACBETH: Into the air, and what seem'd corporal melted
MACBETH: As breath into the wind. Would they had stay'd!
BANQUO: Were such things here as we do speak about?
BANQUO: Or have we eaten on the insane root
BANQUO: That takes the reason prisoner?
MACBETH: Your children shall be kings.
BANQUO: You shall be king.
MACBETH: And thane of Cawdor too: went it not so?
BANQUO: To the selfsame tune and words. Who's here?
NARRATOR: Enter ROSS and ANGUS
ROSS: The king hath happily received, Macbeth,
ROSS: The news of thy success, and when he reads
ROSS: Thy personal venture in the rebels' fight,
ROSS: His wonders and his praises do contend
ROSS: Which should be thine or his: silenced with that,
ROSS: In viewing o'er the rest o' the selfsame day,
ROSS: He finds thee in the stout Norweyan ranks,
ROSS: Nothing afeard of what thyself didst make,
ROSS: Strange images of death. As thick as hail
ROSS: Came post with post, and every one did bear
ROSS: Thy praises in his kingdom's great defence,
ROSS: And pour'd them down before him.
ANGUS: We are sent
ANGUS: To give thee from our royal master thanks,
ANGUS: Only to herald thee into his sight,
ANGUS: Not pay thee.
ROSS: And, for an earnest of a greater honour,
ROSS: He bade me, from him, call thee thane of Cawdor:
ROSS: In which addition, hail, most worthy thane!
ROSS: For it is thine.
BANQUO: What, can the devil speak true?
MACBETH: The thane of Cawdor lives: why do you dress me
MACBETH: In borrow'd robes?
ANGUS: Who was the thane lives yet,
ANGUS: But under heavy judgment bears that life
ANGUS: Which he deserves to lose. Whether he was combined
ANGUS: With those of Norway, or did line the rebel
ANGUS: With hidden help and vantage, or that with both
ANGUS: He labour'd in his country's wreck, I know not,
ANGUS: But treasons capital, confess'd and proved,
ANGUS: Have overthrown him.
MACBETH: [Aside]  Glamis, and thane of Cawdor!
MACBETH: The greatest is behind.
NARRATOR: To ROSS and ANGUS
MACBETH: Thanks for your pains.
NARRATOR: To BANQUO
MACBETH: Do you not hope your children shall be kings,
MACBETH: When those that gave the thane of Cawdor to me
MACBETH: Promised no less to them?
BANQUO: That trusted home
BANQUO: Might yet enkindle you unto the crown,
BANQUO: Besides the thane of Cawdor. But 'tis strange:
BANQUO: And oftentimes, to win us to our harm,
BANQUO: The instruments of darkness tell us truths,
BANQUO: Win us with honest trifles, to betray's
BANQUO: In deepest consequence.
BANQUO: Cousins, a word, I pray you.
MACBETH: [Aside]	Two truths are told,
MACBETH: As happy prologues to the swelling act
MACBETH: Of the imperial theme.--I thank you, gentlemen.
NARRATOR: Aside
MACBETH: Cannot be ill, cannot be good: if ill,
MACBETH: Why hath it given me earnest of success,
MACBETH: Commencing in a truth? I am thane of Cawdor:
MACBETH: If good, why do I yield to that suggestion
MACBETH: Whose horrid image doth unfix my hair
MACBETH: And make my seated heart knock at my ribs,
MACBETH: Against the use of nature? Present fears
MACBETH: Are less than horrible imaginings:
MACBETH: My thought, whose murder yet is but fantastical,
MACBETH: Shakes so my single state of man that function
MACBETH: Is smother'd in surmise, and nothing is
MACBETH: But what is not.
BANQUO: Look, how our partner's rapt.
MACBETH: [Aside]  If chance will have me king, why, chance may crown me,
MACBETH: Without my stir.
BANQUO: New horrors come upon him,
BANQUO: Like our strange garments, cleave not to their mould
BANQUO: But with the aid of use.
MACBETH: [Aside]                Come what come may,
MACBETH: Time and the hour runs through the roughest day.
BANQUO: Worthy Macbeth, we stay upon your leisure.
MACBETH: Give me your favour: my dull brain was wrought
MACBETH: With things forgotten. Kind gentlemen, your pains
MACBETH: Are register'd where every day I turn
MACBETH: The leaf to read them. Let us toward the king.
MACBETH: Think upon what hath chanced, and, at more time,
MACBETH: The interim having weigh'd it, let us speak
MACBETH: Our free hearts each to other.
BANQUO: Very gladly.
MACBETH: Till then, enough. Come, friends.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Forres. The palace.
NARRATOR: Flourish. Enter DUNCAN, MALCOLM, DONALBAIN, LENNOX, and Attendants
DUNCAN: Is execution done on Cawdor? Are not
DUNCAN: Those in commission yet return'd?
MALCOLM: My liege,
MALCOLM: They are not yet come back. But I have spoke
MALCOLM: With one that saw him die: who did report
MALCOLM: That very frankly he confess'd his treasons,
MALCOLM: Implored your highness' pardon and set forth
MALCOLM: A deep repentance: nothing in his life
MALCOLM: Became him like the leaving it, he died
MALCOLM: As one that had been studied in his death
MALCOLM: To throw away the dearest thing he owed,
MALCOLM: As 'twere a careless trifle.
DUNCAN: There's no art
DUNCAN: To find the mind's construction in the face:
DUNCAN: He was a gentleman on whom I built
DUNCAN: An absolute trust.
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH, BANQUO, ROSS, and ANGUS
DUNCAN: O worthiest cousin!
DUNCAN: The sin of my ingratitude even now
DUNCAN: Was heavy on me: thou art so far before
DUNCAN: That swiftest wing of recompense is slow
DUNCAN: To overtake thee. Would thou hadst less deserved,
DUNCAN: That the proportion both of thanks and payment
DUNCAN: Might have been mine! only I have left to say,
DUNCAN: More is thy due than more than all can pay.
MACBETH: The service and the loyalty I owe,
MACBETH: In doing it, pays itself. Your highness' part
MACBETH: Is to receive our duties, and our duties
MACBETH: Are to your throne and state children and servants,
MACBETH: Which do but what they should, by doing every thing
MACBETH: Safe toward your love and honour.
DUNCAN: Welcome hither:
DUNCAN: I have begun to plant thee, and will labour
DUNCAN: To make thee full of growing. Noble Banquo,
DUNCAN: That hast no less deserved, nor must be known
DUNCAN: No less to have done so, let me enfold thee
DUNCAN: And hold thee to my heart.
BANQUO: There if I grow,
BANQUO: The harvest is your own.
DUNCAN: My plenteous joys,
DUNCAN: Wanton in fulness, seek to hide themselves
DUNCAN: In drops of sorrow. Sons, kinsmen, thanes,
DUNCAN: And you whose places are the nearest, know
DUNCAN: We will establish our estate upon
DUNCAN: Our eldest, Malcolm, whom we name hereafter
DUNCAN: The Prince of Cumberland, which honour must
DUNCAN: Not unaccompanied invest him only,
DUNCAN: But signs of nobleness, like stars, shall shine
DUNCAN: On all deservers. From hence to Inverness,
DUNCAN: And bind us further to you.
MACBETH: The rest is labour, which is not used for you:
MACBETH: I'll be myself the harbinger and make joyful
MACBETH: The hearing of my wife with your approach,
MACBETH: So humbly take my leave.
DUNCAN: My worthy Cawdor!
MACBETH: [Aside]  The Prince of Cumberland! that is a step
MACBETH: On which I must fall down, or else o'erleap,
MACBETH: For in my way it lies. Stars, hide your fires,
MACBETH: Let not light see my black and deep desires:
MACBETH: The eye wink at the hand, yet let that be,
MACBETH: Which the eye fears, when it is done, to see.
NARRATOR: Exit
DUNCAN: True, worthy Banquo, he is full so valiant,
DUNCAN: And in his commendations I am fed,
DUNCAN: It is a banquet to me. Let's after him,
DUNCAN: Whose care is gone before to bid us welcome:
DUNCAN: It is a peerless kinsman.
NARRATOR: Flourish. Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE V. Inverness. Macbeth's castle.
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH, reading a letter
LADY MACBETH: 'They met me in the day of success: and I have
LADY MACBETH: learned by the perfectest report, they have more in
LADY MACBETH: them than mortal knowledge. When I burned in desire
LADY MACBETH: to question them further, they made themselves air,
LADY MACBETH: into which they vanished. Whiles I stood rapt in
LADY MACBETH: the wonder of it, came missives from the king, who
LADY MACBETH: all-hailed me 'Thane of Cawdor,' by which title,
LADY MACBETH: before, these weird sisters saluted me, and referred
LADY MACBETH: me to the coming on of time, with 'Hail, king that
LADY MACBETH: shalt be!' This have I thought good to deliver
LADY MACBETH: thee, my dearest partner of greatness, that thou
LADY MACBETH: mightst not lose the dues of rejoicing, by being
LADY MACBETH: ignorant of what greatness is promised thee. Lay it
LADY MACBETH: to thy heart, and farewell.'
LADY MACBETH: Glamis thou art, and Cawdor, and shalt be
LADY MACBETH: What thou art promised: yet do I fear thy nature,
LADY MACBETH: It is too full o' the milk of human kindness
LADY MACBETH: To catch the nearest way: thou wouldst be great,
LADY MACBETH: Art not without ambition, but without
LADY MACBETH: The illness should attend it: what thou wouldst highly,
LADY MACBETH: That wouldst thou holily, wouldst not play false,
LADY MACBETH: And yet wouldst wrongly win: thou'ldst have, great Glamis,
LADY MACBETH: That which cries 'Thus thou must do, if thou have it,
LADY MACBETH: And that which rather thou dost fear to do
LADY MACBETH: Than wishest should be undone.' Hie thee hither,
LADY MACBETH: That I may pour my spirits in thine ear,
LADY MACBETH: And chastise with the valour of my tongue
LADY MACBETH: All that impedes thee from the golden round,
LADY MACBETH: Which fate and metaphysical aid doth seem
LADY MACBETH: To have thee crown'd withal.
NARRATOR: Enter a Messenger
LADY MACBETH: What is your tidings?
Messenger: The king comes here to-night.
LADY MACBETH: Thou'rt mad to say it:
LADY MACBETH: Is not thy master with him? who, were't so,
LADY MACBETH: Would have inform'd for preparation.
Messenger: So please you, it is true: our thane is coming:
Messenger: One of my fellows had the speed of him,
Messenger: Who, almost dead for breath, had scarcely more
Messenger: Than would make up his message.
LADY MACBETH: Give him tending,
LADY MACBETH: He brings great news.
NARRATOR: Exit Messenger
LADY MACBETH: The raven himself is hoarse
LADY MACBETH: That croaks the fatal entrance of Duncan
LADY MACBETH: Under my battlements. Come, you spirits
LADY MACBETH: That tend on mortal thoughts, unsex me here,
LADY MACBETH: And fill me from the crown to the toe top-full
LADY MACBETH: Of direst cruelty! make thick my blood,
LADY MACBETH: Stop up the access and passage to remorse,
LADY MACBETH: That no compunctious visitings of nature
LADY MACBETH: Shake my fell purpose, nor keep peace between
LADY MACBETH: The effect and it! Come to my woman's breasts,
LADY MACBETH: And take my milk for gall, you murdering ministers,
LADY MACBETH: Wherever in your sightless substances
LADY MACBETH: You wait on nature's mischief! Come, thick night,
LADY MACBETH: And pall thee in the dunnest smoke of hell,
LADY MACBETH: That my keen knife see not the wound it makes,
LADY MACBETH: Nor heaven peep through the blanket of the dark,
LADY MACBETH: To cry 'Hold, hold!'
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: Great Glamis! worthy Cawdor!
LADY MACBETH: Greater than both, by the all-hail hereafter!
LADY MACBETH: Thy letters have transported me beyond
LADY MACBETH: This ignorant present, and I feel now
LADY MACBETH: The future in the instant.
MACBETH: My dearest love,
MACBETH: Duncan comes here to-night.
LADY MACBETH: And when goes hence?
MACBETH: To-morrow, as he purposes.
LADY MACBETH: O, never
LADY MACBETH: Shall sun that morrow see!
LADY MACBETH: Your face, my thane, is as a book where men
LADY MACBETH: May read strange matters. To beguile the time,
LADY MACBETH: Look like the time, bear welcome in your eye,
LADY MACBETH: Your hand, your tongue: look like the innocent flower,
LADY MACBETH: But be the serpent under't. He that's coming
LADY MACBETH: Must be provided for: and you shall put
LADY MACBETH: This night's great business into my dispatch,
LADY MACBETH: Which shall to all our nights and days to come
LADY MACBETH: Give solely sovereign sway and masterdom.
MACBETH: We will speak further.
LADY MACBETH: Only look up clear,
LADY MACBETH: To alter favour ever is to fear:
LADY MACBETH: Leave all the rest to me.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE VI. Before Macbeth's castle.
NARRATOR: Hautboys and torches. Enter DUNCAN, MALCOLM,  DONALBAIN, BANQUO, LENNOX, MACDUFF, ROSS, ANGUS, and Attendants
DUNCAN: This castle hath a pleasant seat, the air
DUNCAN: Nimbly and sweetly recommends itself
DUNCAN: Unto our gentle senses.
BANQUO: This guest of summer,
BANQUO: The temple-haunting martlet, does approve,
BANQUO: By his loved mansionry, that the heaven's breath
BANQUO: Smells wooingly here: no jutty, frieze,
BANQUO: Buttress, nor coign of vantage, but this bird
BANQUO: Hath made his pendent bed and procreant cradle:
BANQUO: Where they most breed and haunt, I have observed,
BANQUO: The air is delicate.
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH
DUNCAN: See, see, our honour'd hostess!
DUNCAN: The love that follows us sometime is our trouble,
DUNCAN: Which still we thank as love. Herein I teach you
DUNCAN: How you shall bid God 'ild us for your pains,
DUNCAN: And thank us for your trouble.
LADY MACBETH: All our service
LADY MACBETH: In every point twice done and then done double
LADY MACBETH: Were poor and single business to contend
LADY MACBETH: Against those honours deep and broad wherewith
LADY MACBETH: Your majesty loads our house: for those of old,
LADY MACBETH: And the late dignities heap'd up to them,
LADY MACBETH: We rest your hermits.
DUNCAN: Where's the thane of Cawdor?
DUNCAN: We coursed him at the heels, and had a purpose
DUNCAN: To be his purveyor: but he rides well,
DUNCAN: And his great love, sharp as his spur, hath holp him
DUNCAN: To his home before us. Fair and noble hostess,
DUNCAN: We are your guest to-night.
LADY MACBETH: Your servants ever
LADY MACBETH: Have theirs, themselves and what is theirs, in compt,
LADY MACBETH: To make their audit at your highness' pleasure,
LADY MACBETH: Still to return your own.
DUNCAN: Give me your hand,
DUNCAN: Conduct me to mine host: we love him highly,
DUNCAN: And shall continue our graces towards him.
DUNCAN: By your leave, hostess.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE VII. Macbeth's castle.
NARRATOR: Hautboys and torches. Enter a Sewer, and divers  Servants with dishes and service, and pass over the stage. Then enter MACBETH
MACBETH: If it were done when 'tis done, then 'twere well
MACBETH: It were done quickly: if the assassination
MACBETH: Could trammel up the consequence, and catch
MACBETH: With his surcease success, that but this blow
MACBETH: Might be the be-all and the end-all here,
MACBETH: But here, upon this bank and shoal of time,
MACBETH: We'ld jump the life to come. But in these cases
MACBETH: We still have judgment here, that we but teach
MACBETH: Bloody instructions, which, being taught, return
MACBETH: To plague the inventor: this even-handed justice
MACBETH: Commends the ingredients of our poison'd chalice
MACBETH: To our own lips. He's here in double trust,
MACBETH: First, as I am his kinsman and his subject,
MACBETH: Strong both against the deed, then, as his host,
MACBETH: Who should against his murderer shut the door,
MACBETH: Not bear the knife myself. Besides, this Duncan
MACBETH: Hath borne his faculties so meek, hath been
MACBETH: So clear in his great office, that his virtues
MACBETH: Will plead like angels, trumpet-tongued, against
MACBETH: The deep damnation of his taking-off,
MACBETH: And pity, like a naked new-born babe,
MACBETH: Striding the blast, or heaven's cherubim, horsed
MACBETH: Upon the sightless couriers of the air,
MACBETH: Shall blow the horrid deed in every eye,
MACBETH: That tears shall drown the wind. I have no spur
MACBETH: To prick the sides of my intent, but only
MACBETH: Vaulting ambition, which o'erleaps itself
MACBETH: And falls on the other.
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH
MACBETH: How now! what news?
LADY MACBETH: He has almost supp'd: why have you left the chamber?
MACBETH: Hath he ask'd for me?
LADY MACBETH: Know you not he has?
MACBETH: We will proceed no further in this business:
MACBETH: He hath honour'd me of late, and I have bought
MACBETH: Golden opinions from all sorts of people,
MACBETH: Which would be worn now in their newest gloss,
MACBETH: Not cast aside so soon.
LADY MACBETH: Was the hope drunk
LADY MACBETH: Wherein you dress'd yourself? hath it slept since?
LADY MACBETH: And wakes it now, to look so green and pale
LADY MACBETH: At what it did so freely? From this time
LADY MACBETH: Such I account thy love. Art thou afeard
LADY MACBETH: To be the same in thine own act and valour
LADY MACBETH: As thou art in desire? Wouldst thou have that
LADY MACBETH: Which thou esteem'st the ornament of life,
LADY MACBETH: And live a coward in thine own esteem,
LADY MACBETH: Letting 'I dare not' wait upon 'I would,'
LADY MACBETH: Like the poor cat i' the adage?
MACBETH: Prithee, peace:
MACBETH: I dare do all that may become a man,
MACBETH: Who dares do more is none.
LADY MACBETH: What beast was't, then,
LADY MACBETH: That made you break this enterprise to me?
LADY MACBETH: When you durst do it, then you were a man,
LADY MACBETH: And, to be more than what you were, you would
LADY MACBETH: Be so much more the man. Nor time nor place
LADY MACBETH: Did then adhere, and yet you would make both:
LADY MACBETH: They have made themselves, and that their fitness now
LADY MACBETH: Does unmake you. I have given suck, and know
LADY MACBETH: How tender 'tis to love the babe that milks me:
LADY MACBETH: I would, while it was smiling in my face,
LADY MACBETH: Have pluck'd my nipple from his boneless gums,
LADY MACBETH: And dash'd the brains out, had I so sworn as you
LADY MACBETH: Have done to this.
MACBETH: If we should fail?
LADY MACBETH: We fail!
LADY MACBETH: But screw your courage to the sticking-place,
LADY MACBETH: And we'll not fail. When Duncan is asleep--
LADY MACBETH: Whereto the rather shall his day's hard journey
LADY MACBETH: Soundly invite him--his two chamberlains
LADY MACBETH: Will I with wine and wassail so convince
LADY MACBETH: That memory, the warder of the brain,
LADY MACBETH: Shall be a fume, and the receipt of reason
LADY MACBETH: A limbeck only: when in swinish sleep
LADY MACBETH: Their drenched natures lie as in a death,
LADY MACBETH: What cannot you and I perform upon
LADY MACBETH: The unguarded Duncan? what not put upon
LADY MACBETH: His spongy officers, who shall bear the guilt
LADY MACBETH: Of our great quell?
MACBETH: Bring forth men-children only,
MACBETH: For thy undaunted mettle should compose
MACBETH: Nothing but males. Will it not be received,
MACBETH: When we have mark'd with blood those sleepy two
MACBETH: Of his own chamber and used their very daggers,
MACBETH: That they have done't?
LADY MACBETH: Who dares receive it other,
LADY MACBETH: As we shall make our griefs and clamour roar
LADY MACBETH: Upon his death?
MACBETH: I am settled, and bend up
MACBETH: Each corporal agent to this terrible feat.
MACBETH: Away, and mock the time with fairest show:
MACBETH: False face must hide what the false heart doth know.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT II
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Court of Macbeth's castle.
NARRATOR: Enter BANQUO, and FLEANCE bearing a torch before him
BANQUO: How goes the night, boy?
FLEANCE: The moon is down, I have not heard the clock.
BANQUO: And she goes down at twelve.
FLEANCE: I take't, 'tis later, sir.
BANQUO: Hold, take my sword. There's husbandry in heaven,
BANQUO: Their candles are all out. Take thee that too.
BANQUO: A heavy summons lies like lead upon me,
BANQUO: And yet I would not sleep: merciful powers,
BANQUO: Restrain in me the cursed thoughts that nature
BANQUO: Gives way to in repose!
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH, and a Servant with a torch
BANQUO: Give me my sword.
BANQUO: Who's there?
MACBETH: A friend.
BANQUO: What, sir, not yet at rest? The king's a-bed:
BANQUO: He hath been in unusual pleasure, and
BANQUO: Sent forth great largess to your offices.
BANQUO: This diamond he greets your wife withal,
BANQUO: By the name of most kind hostess, and shut up
BANQUO: In measureless content.
MACBETH: Being unprepared,
MACBETH: Our will became the servant to defect,
MACBETH: Which else should free have wrought.
BANQUO: All's well.
BANQUO: I dreamt last night of the three weird sisters:
BANQUO: To you they have show'd some truth.
MACBETH: I think not of them:
MACBETH: Yet, when we can entreat an hour to serve,
MACBETH: We would spend it in some words upon that business,
MACBETH: If you would grant the time.
BANQUO: At your kind'st leisure.
MACBETH: If you shall cleave to my consent, when 'tis,
MACBETH: It shall make honour for you.
BANQUO: So I lose none
BANQUO: In seeking to augment it, but still keep
BANQUO: My bosom franchised and allegiance clear,
BANQUO: I shall be counsell'd.
MACBETH: Good repose the while!
BANQUO: Thanks, sir: the like to you!
NARRATOR: Exeunt BANQUO and FLEANCE
MACBETH: Go bid thy mistress, when my drink is ready,
MACBETH: She strike upon the bell. Get thee to bed.
NARRATOR: Exit Servant
MACBETH: Is this a dagger which I see before me,
MACBETH: The handle toward my hand? Come, let me clutch thee.
MACBETH: I have thee not, and yet I see thee still.
MACBETH: Art thou not, fatal vision, sensible
MACBETH: To feeling as to sight? or art thou but
MACBETH: A dagger of the mind, a false creation,
MACBETH: Proceeding from the heat-oppressed brain?
MACBETH: I see thee yet, in form as palpable
MACBETH: As this which now I draw.
MACBETH: Thou marshall'st me the way that I was going,
MACBETH: And such an instrument I was to use.
MACBETH: Mine eyes are made the fools o' the other senses,
MACBETH: Or else worth all the rest, I see thee still,
MACBETH: And on thy blade and dudgeon gouts of blood,
MACBETH: Which was not so before. There's no such thing:
MACBETH: It is the bloody business which informs
MACBETH: Thus to mine eyes. Now o'er the one halfworld
MACBETH: Nature seems dead, and wicked dreams abuse
MACBETH: The curtain'd sleep, witchcraft celebrates
MACBETH: Pale Hecate's offerings, and wither'd murder,
MACBETH: Alarum'd by his sentinel, the wolf,
MACBETH: Whose howl's his watch, thus with his stealthy pace.
MACBETH: With Tarquin's ravishing strides, towards his design
MACBETH: Moves like a ghost. Thou sure and firm-set earth,
MACBETH: Hear not my steps, which way they walk, for fear
MACBETH: Thy very stones prate of my whereabout,
MACBETH: And take the present horror from the time,
MACBETH: Which now suits with it. Whiles I threat, he lives:
MACBETH: Words to the heat of deeds too cold breath gives.
NARRATOR: A bell rings
MACBETH: I go, and it is done, the bell invites me.
MACBETH: Hear it not, Duncan, for it is a knell
MACBETH: That summons thee to heaven or to hell.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The same.
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: That which hath made them drunk hath made me bold,
LADY MACBETH: What hath quench'd them hath given me fire.
LADY MACBETH: Hark! Peace!
LADY MACBETH: It was the owl that shriek'd, the fatal bellman,
LADY MACBETH: Which gives the stern'st good-night. He is about it:
LADY MACBETH: The doors are open, and the surfeited grooms
LADY MACBETH: Do mock their charge with snores: I have drugg'd
LADY MACBETH: their possets,
LADY MACBETH: That death and nature do contend about them,
LADY MACBETH: Whether they live or die.
MACBETH: [Within]  Who's there? what, ho!
LADY MACBETH: Alack, I am afraid they have awaked,
LADY MACBETH: And 'tis not done. The attempt and not the deed
LADY MACBETH: Confounds us. Hark! I laid their daggers ready,
LADY MACBETH: He could not miss 'em. Had he not resembled
LADY MACBETH: My father as he slept, I had done't.
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: My husband!
MACBETH: I have done the deed. Didst thou not hear a noise?
LADY MACBETH: I heard the owl scream and the crickets cry.
LADY MACBETH: Did not you speak?
MACBETH: When?
LADY MACBETH: Now.
MACBETH: As I descended?
LADY MACBETH: Ay.
MACBETH: Hark!
MACBETH: Who lies i' the second chamber?
LADY MACBETH: Donalbain.
MACBETH: This is a sorry sight.
NARRATOR: Looking on his hands
LADY MACBETH: A foolish thought, to say a sorry sight.
MACBETH: There's one did laugh in's sleep, and one cried
MACBETH: 'Murder!'
MACBETH: That they did wake each other: I stood and heard them:
MACBETH: But they did say their prayers, and address'd them
MACBETH: Again to sleep.
LADY MACBETH: There are two lodged together.
MACBETH: One cried 'God bless us!' and 'Amen' the other,
MACBETH: As they had seen me with these hangman's hands.
MACBETH: Listening their fear, I could not say 'Amen,'
MACBETH: When they did say 'God bless us!'
LADY MACBETH: Consider it not so deeply.
MACBETH: But wherefore could not I pronounce 'Amen'?
MACBETH: I had most need of blessing, and 'Amen'
MACBETH: Stuck in my throat.
LADY MACBETH: These deeds must not be thought
LADY MACBETH: After these ways, so, it will make us mad.
MACBETH: Methought I heard a voice cry 'Sleep no more!
MACBETH: Macbeth does murder sleep', the innocent sleep,
MACBETH: Sleep that knits up the ravell'd sleeve of care,
MACBETH: The death of each day's life, sore labour's bath,
MACBETH: Balm of hurt minds, great nature's second course,
MACBETH: Chief nourisher in life's feast,--
LADY MACBETH: What do you mean?
MACBETH: Still it cried 'Sleep no more!' to all the house:
MACBETH: 'Glamis hath murder'd sleep, and therefore Cawdor
MACBETH: Shall sleep no more, Macbeth shall sleep no more.'
LADY MACBETH: Who was it that thus cried? Why, worthy thane,
LADY MACBETH: You do unbend your noble strength, to think
LADY MACBETH: So brainsickly of things. Go get some water,
LADY MACBETH: And wash this filthy witness from your hand.
LADY MACBETH: Why did you bring these daggers from the place?
LADY MACBETH: They must lie there: go carry them, and smear
LADY MACBETH: The sleepy grooms with blood.
MACBETH: I'll go no more:
MACBETH: I am afraid to think what I have done,
MACBETH: Look on't again I dare not.
LADY MACBETH: Infirm of purpose!
LADY MACBETH: Give me the daggers: the sleeping and the dead
LADY MACBETH: Are but as pictures: 'tis the eye of childhood
LADY MACBETH: That fears a painted devil. If he do bleed,
LADY MACBETH: I'll gild the faces of the grooms withal,
LADY MACBETH: For it must seem their guilt.
NARRATOR: Exit. Knocking within
MACBETH: Whence is that knocking?
MACBETH: How is't with me, when every noise appals me?
MACBETH: What hands are here? ha! they pluck out mine eyes.
MACBETH: Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood
MACBETH: Clean from my hand? No, this my hand will rather
MACBETH: The multitudinous seas in incarnadine,
MACBETH: Making the green one red.
NARRATOR: Re-enter LADY MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: My hands are of your colour, but I shame
LADY MACBETH: To wear a heart so white.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
LADY MACBETH: I hear a knocking
LADY MACBETH: At the south entry: retire we to our chamber,
LADY MACBETH: A little water clears us of this deed:
LADY MACBETH: How easy is it, then! Your constancy
LADY MACBETH: Hath left you unattended.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
LADY MACBETH: Hark! more knocking.
LADY MACBETH: Get on your nightgown, lest occasion call us,
LADY MACBETH: And show us to be watchers. Be not lost
LADY MACBETH: So poorly in your thoughts.
MACBETH: To know my deed, 'twere best not know myself.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
MACBETH: Wake Duncan with thy knocking! I would thou couldst!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. The same.
NARRATOR: Knocking within. Enter a Porter
Porter: Here's a knocking indeed! If a
Porter: man were porter of hell-gate, he should have
Porter: old turning the key.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Porter: Knock,
Porter: knock, knock! Who's there, i' the name of
Porter: Beelzebub? Here's a farmer, that hanged
Porter: himself on the expectation of plenty: come in
Porter: time, have napkins enow about you, here
Porter: you'll sweat for't.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Porter: Knock,
Porter: knock! Who's there, in the other devil's
Porter: name? Faith, here's an equivocator, that could
Porter: swear in both the scales against either scale,
Porter: who committed treason enough for God's sake,
Porter: yet could not equivocate to heaven: O, come
Porter: in, equivocator.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Porter: Knock,
Porter: knock, knock! Who's there? Faith, here's an
Porter: English tailor come hither, for stealing out of
Porter: a French hose: come in, tailor, here you may
Porter: roast your goose.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Porter: Knock,
Porter: knock, never at quiet! What are you? But
Porter: this place is too cold for hell. I'll devil-porter
Porter: it no further: I had thought to have let in
Porter: some of all professions that go the primrose
Porter: way to the everlasting bonfire.
NARRATOR: Knocking within
Porter: Anon, anon! I pray you, remember the porter.
NARRATOR: Opens the gate
NARRATOR: Enter MACDUFF and LENNOX
MACDUFF: Was it so late, friend, ere you went to bed,
MACDUFF: That you do lie so late?
Porter: 'Faith sir, we were carousing till the
Porter: second cock: and drink, sir, is a great
Porter: provoker of three things.
MACDUFF: What three things does drink especially provoke?
Porter: Marry, sir, nose-painting, sleep, and
Porter: urine. Lechery, sir, it provokes, and unprovokes,
Porter: it provokes the desire, but it takes
Porter: away the performance: therefore, much drink
Porter: may be said to be an equivocator with lechery:
Porter: it makes him, and it mars him, it sets
Porter: him on, and it takes him off, it persuades him,
Porter: and disheartens him, makes him stand to, and
Porter: not stand to, in conclusion, equivocates him
Porter: in a sleep, and, giving him the lie, leaves him.
MACDUFF: I believe drink gave thee the lie last night.
Porter: That it did, sir, i' the very throat on
Porter: me: but I requited him for his lie, and, I
Porter: think, being too strong for him, though he took
Porter: up my legs sometime, yet I made a shift to cast
Porter: him.
MACDUFF: Is thy master stirring?
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH
MACDUFF: Our knocking has awaked him, here he comes.
LENNOX: Good morrow, noble sir.
MACBETH: Good morrow, both.
MACDUFF: Is the king stirring, worthy thane?
MACBETH: Not yet.
MACDUFF: He did command me to call timely on him:
MACDUFF: I have almost slipp'd the hour.
MACBETH: I'll bring you to him.
MACDUFF: I know this is a joyful trouble to you,
MACDUFF: But yet 'tis one.
MACBETH: The labour we delight in physics pain.
MACBETH: This is the door.
MACDUFF: I'll make so bold to call,
MACDUFF: For 'tis my limited service.
NARRATOR: Exit
LENNOX: Goes the king hence to-day?
MACBETH: He does: he did appoint so.
LENNOX: The night has been unruly: where we lay,
LENNOX: Our chimneys were blown down, and, as they say,
LENNOX: Lamentings heard i' the air, strange screams of death,
LENNOX: And prophesying with accents terrible
LENNOX: Of dire combustion and confused events
LENNOX: New hatch'd to the woeful time: the obscure bird
LENNOX: Clamour'd the livelong night: some say, the earth
LENNOX: Was feverous and did shake.
MACBETH: 'Twas a rough night.
LENNOX: My young remembrance cannot parallel
LENNOX: A fellow to it.
NARRATOR: Re-enter MACDUFF
MACDUFF: O horror, horror, horror! Tongue nor heart
MACDUFF: Cannot conceive nor name thee!
LENNOX: What's the matter.
MACDUFF: Confusion now hath made his masterpiece!
MACDUFF: Most sacrilegious murder hath broke ope
MACDUFF: The Lord's anointed temple, and stole thence
MACDUFF: The life o' the building!
MACBETH: What is 't you say? the life?
LENNOX: Mean you his majesty?
MACDUFF: Approach the chamber, and destroy your sight
MACDUFF: With a new Gorgon: do not bid me speak,
MACDUFF: See, and then speak yourselves.
NARRATOR: Exeunt MACBETH and LENNOX
MACDUFF: Awake, awake!
MACDUFF: Ring the alarum-bell. Murder and treason!
MACDUFF: Banquo and Donalbain! Malcolm! awake!
MACDUFF: Shake off this downy sleep, death's counterfeit,
MACDUFF: And look on death itself! up, up, and see
MACDUFF: The great doom's image! Malcolm! Banquo!
MACDUFF: As from your graves rise up, and walk like sprites,
MACDUFF: To countenance this horror! Ring the bell.
NARRATOR: Bell rings
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: What's the business,
LADY MACBETH: That such a hideous trumpet calls to parley
LADY MACBETH: The sleepers of the house? speak, speak!
MACDUFF: O gentle lady,
MACDUFF: 'Tis not for you to hear what I can speak:
MACDUFF: The repetition, in a woman's ear,
MACDUFF: Would murder as it fell.
NARRATOR: Enter BANQUO
MACDUFF: O Banquo, Banquo,
MACDUFF: Our royal master 's murder'd!
LADY MACBETH: Woe, alas!
LADY MACBETH: What, in our house?
BANQUO: Too cruel any where.
BANQUO: Dear Duff, I prithee, contradict thyself,
BANQUO: And say it is not so.
NARRATOR: Re-enter MACBETH and LENNOX, with ROSS
MACBETH: Had I but died an hour before this chance,
MACBETH: I had lived a blessed time, for, from this instant,
MACBETH: There 's nothing serious in mortality:
MACBETH: All is but toys: renown and grace is dead,
MACBETH: The wine of life is drawn, and the mere lees
MACBETH: Is left this vault to brag of.
NARRATOR: Enter MALCOLM and DONALBAIN
DONALBAIN: What is amiss?
MACBETH: You are, and do not know't:
MACBETH: The spring, the head, the fountain of your blood
MACBETH: Is stopp'd, the very source of it is stopp'd.
MACDUFF: Your royal father 's murder'd.
MALCOLM: O, by whom?
LENNOX: Those of his chamber, as it seem'd, had done 't:
LENNOX: Their hands and faces were an badged with blood,
LENNOX: So were their daggers, which unwiped we found
LENNOX: Upon their pillows:
LENNOX: They stared, and were distracted, no man's life
LENNOX: Was to be trusted with them.
MACBETH: O, yet I do repent me of my fury,
MACBETH: That I did kill them.
MACDUFF: Wherefore did you so?
MACBETH: Who can be wise, amazed, temperate and furious,
MACBETH: Loyal and neutral, in a moment? No man:
MACBETH: The expedition my violent love
MACBETH: Outrun the pauser, reason. Here lay Duncan,
MACBETH: His silver skin laced with his golden blood,
MACBETH: And his gash'd stabs look'd like a breach in nature
MACBETH: For ruin's wasteful entrance: there, the murderers,
MACBETH: Steep'd in the colours of their trade, their daggers
MACBETH: Unmannerly breech'd with gore: who could refrain,
MACBETH: That had a heart to love, and in that heart
MACBETH: Courage to make 's love kno wn?
LADY MACBETH: Help me hence, ho!
MACDUFF: Look to the lady.
MALCOLM: [Aside to DONALBAIN]  Why do we hold our tongues,
MALCOLM: That most may claim this argument for ours?
DONALBAIN: [Aside to MALCOLM]  What should be spoken here,
DONALBAIN: where our fate,
DONALBAIN: Hid in an auger-hole, may rush, and seize us?
DONALBAIN: Let 's away,
DONALBAIN: Our tears are not yet brew'd.
MALCOLM: [Aside to DONALBAIN]        Nor our strong sorrow
MALCOLM: Upon the foot of motion.
BANQUO: Look to the lady:
NARRATOR: LADY MACBETH is carried out
BANQUO: And when we have our naked frailties hid,
BANQUO: That suffer in exposure, let us meet,
BANQUO: And question this most bloody piece of work,
BANQUO: To know it further. Fears and scruples shake us:
BANQUO: In the great hand of God I stand, and thence
BANQUO: Against the undivulged pretence I fight
BANQUO: Of treasonous malice.
MACDUFF: And so do I.
ALL: So all.
MACBETH: Let's briefly put on manly readiness,
MACBETH: And meet i' the hall together.
ALL: Well contented.
NARRATOR: Exeunt all but Malcolm and Donalbain.
MALCOLM: What will you do? Let's not consort with them:
MALCOLM: To show an unfelt sorrow is an office
MALCOLM: Which the false man does easy. I'll to England.
DONALBAIN: To Ireland, I, our separated fortune
DONALBAIN: Shall keep us both the safer: where we are,
DONALBAIN: There's daggers in men's smiles: the near in blood,
DONALBAIN: The nearer bloody.
MALCOLM: This murderous shaft that's shot
MALCOLM: Hath not yet lighted, and our safest way
MALCOLM: Is to avoid the aim. Therefore, to horse,
MALCOLM: And let us not be dainty of leave-taking,
MALCOLM: But shift away: there's warrant in that theft
MALCOLM: Which steals itself, when there's no mercy left.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. Outside Macbeth's castle.
NARRATOR: Enter ROSS and an old Man
Old Man: Threescore and ten I can remember well:
Old Man: Within the volume of which time I have seen
Old Man: Hours dreadful and things strange, but this sore night
Old Man: Hath trifled former knowings.
ROSS: Ah, good father,
ROSS: Thou seest, the heavens, as troubled with man's act,
ROSS: Threaten his bloody stage: by the clock, 'tis day,
ROSS: And yet dark night strangles the travelling lamp:
ROSS: Is't night's predominance, or the day's shame,
ROSS: That darkness does the face of earth entomb,
ROSS: When living light should kiss it?
Old Man: 'Tis unnatural,
Old Man: Even like the deed that's done. On Tuesday last,
Old Man: A falcon, towering in her pride of place,
Old Man: Was by a mousing owl hawk'd at and kill'd.
ROSS: And Duncan's horses--a thing most strange and certain--
ROSS: Beauteous and swift, the minions of their race,
ROSS: Turn'd wild in nature, broke their stalls, flung out,
ROSS: Contending 'gainst obedience, as they would make
ROSS: War with mankind.
Old Man: 'Tis said they eat each other.
ROSS: They did so, to the amazement of mine eyes
ROSS: That look'd upon't. Here comes the good Macduff.
NARRATOR: Enter MACDUFF
ROSS: How goes the world, sir, now?
MACDUFF: Why, see you not?
ROSS: Is't known who did this more than bloody deed?
MACDUFF: Those that Macbeth hath slain.
ROSS: Alas, the day!
ROSS: What good could they pretend?
MACDUFF: They were suborn'd:
MACDUFF: Malcolm and Donalbain, the king's two sons,
MACDUFF: Are stol'n away and fled, which puts upon them
MACDUFF: Suspicion of the deed.
ROSS: 'Gainst nature still!
ROSS: Thriftless ambition, that wilt ravin up
ROSS: Thine own life's means! Then 'tis most like
ROSS: The sovereignty will fall upon Macbeth.
MACDUFF: He is already named, and gone to Scone
MACDUFF: To be invested.
ROSS: Where is Duncan's body?
MACDUFF: Carried to Colmekill,
MACDUFF: The sacred storehouse of his predecessors,
MACDUFF: And guardian of their bones.
ROSS: Will you to Scone?
MACDUFF: No, cousin, I'll to Fife.
ROSS: Well, I will thither.
MACDUFF: Well, may you see things well done there: adieu!
MACDUFF: Lest our old robes sit easier than our new!
ROSS: Farewell, father.
Old Man: God's benison go with you, and with those
Old Man: That would make good of bad, and friends of foes!
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: ACT III
NARRATOR: SCENE I. Forres. The palace.
NARRATOR: Enter BANQUO
BANQUO: Thou hast it now: king, Cawdor, Glamis, all,
BANQUO: As the weird women promised, and, I fear,
BANQUO: Thou play'dst most foully for't: yet it was said
BANQUO: It should not stand in thy posterity,
BANQUO: But that myself should be the root and father
BANQUO: Of many kings. If there come truth from them--
BANQUO: As upon thee, Macbeth, their speeches shine--
BANQUO: Why, by the verities on thee made good,
BANQUO: May they not be my oracles as well,
BANQUO: And set me up in hope? But hush! no more.
NARRATOR: Sennet sounded. Enter MACBETH, as king, LADY  MACBETH, as queen, LENNOX, ROSS, Lords, Ladies, and Attendants
MACBETH: Here's our chief guest.
LADY MACBETH: If he had been forgotten,
LADY MACBETH: It had been as a gap in our great feast,
LADY MACBETH: And all-thing unbecoming.
MACBETH: To-night we hold a solemn supper sir,
MACBETH: And I'll request your presence.
BANQUO: Let your highness
BANQUO: Command upon me, to the which my duties
BANQUO: Are with a most indissoluble tie
BANQUO: For ever knit.
MACBETH: Ride you this afternoon?
BANQUO: Ay, my good lord.
MACBETH: We should have else desired your good advice,
MACBETH: Which still hath been both grave and prosperous,
MACBETH: In this day's council, but we'll take to-morrow.
MACBETH: Is't far you ride?
BANQUO: As far, my lord, as will fill up the time
BANQUO: 'Twixt this and supper: go not my horse the better,
BANQUO: I must become a borrower of the night
BANQUO: For a dark hour or twain.
MACBETH: Fail not our feast.
BANQUO: My lord, I will not.
MACBETH: We hear, our bloody cousins are bestow'd
MACBETH: In England and in Ireland, not confessing
MACBETH: Their cruel parricide, filling their hearers
MACBETH: With strange invention: but of that to-morrow,
MACBETH: When therewithal we shall have cause of state
MACBETH: Craving us jointly. Hie you to horse: adieu,
MACBETH: Till you return at night. Goes Fleance with you?
BANQUO: Ay, my good lord: our time does call upon 's.
MACBETH: I wish your horses swift and sure of foot,
MACBETH: And so I do commend you to their backs. Farewell.
NARRATOR: Exit BANQUO
MACBETH: Let every man be master of his time
MACBETH: Till seven at night: to make society
MACBETH: The sweeter welcome, we will keep ourself
MACBETH: Till supper-time alone: while then, God be with you!
NARRATOR: Exeunt all but MACBETH, and an attendant
MACBETH: Sirrah, a word with you: attend those men
MACBETH: Our pleasure?
ATTENDANT: They are, my lord, without the palace gate.
MACBETH: Bring them before us.
NARRATOR: Exit Attendant
MACBETH: To be thus is nothing,
MACBETH: But to be safely thus.--Our fears in Banquo
MACBETH: Stick deep, and in his royalty of nature
MACBETH: Reigns that which would be fear'd: 'tis much he dares,
MACBETH: And, to that dauntless temper of his mind,
MACBETH: He hath a wisdom that doth guide his valour
MACBETH: To act in safety. There is none but he
MACBETH: Whose being I do fear: and, under him,
MACBETH: My Genius is rebuked, as, it is said,
MACBETH: Mark Antony's was by Caesar. He chid the sisters
MACBETH: When first they put the name of king upon me,
MACBETH: And bade them speak to him: then prophet-like
MACBETH: They hail'd him father to a line of kings:
MACBETH: Upon my head they placed a fruitless crown,
MACBETH: And put a barren sceptre in my gripe,
MACBETH: Thence to be wrench'd with an unlineal hand,
MACBETH: No son of mine succeeding. If 't be so,
MACBETH: For Banquo's issue have I filed my mind,
MACBETH: For them the gracious Duncan have I murder'd,
MACBETH: Put rancours in the vessel of my peace
MACBETH: Only for them, and mine eternal jewel
MACBETH: Given to the common enemy of man,
MACBETH: To make them kings, the seed of Banquo kings!
MACBETH: Rather than so, come fate into the list.
MACBETH: And champion me to the utterance! Who's there!
NARRATOR: Re-enter Attendant, with two Murderers
MACBETH: Now go to the door, and stay there till we call.
NARRATOR: Exit Attendant
MACBETH: Was it not yesterday we spoke together?
First Murderer: It was, so please your highness.
MACBETH: Well then, now
MACBETH: Have you consider'd of my speeches? Know
MACBETH: That it was he in the times past which held you
MACBETH: So under fortune, which you thought had been
MACBETH: Our innocent self: this I made good to you
MACBETH: In our last conference, pass'd in probation with you,
MACBETH: How you were borne in hand, how cross'd,
MACBETH: the instruments,
MACBETH: Who wrought with them, and all things else that might
MACBETH: To half a soul and to a notion crazed
MACBETH: Say 'Thus did Banquo.'
First Murderer: You made it known to us.
MACBETH: I did so, and went further, which is now
MACBETH: Our point of second meeting. Do you find
MACBETH: Your patience so predominant in your nature
MACBETH: That you can let this go? Are you so gospell'd
MACBETH: To pray for this good man and for his issue,
MACBETH: Whose heavy hand hath bow'd you to the grave
MACBETH: And beggar'd yours for ever?
First Murderer: We are men, my liege.
MACBETH: Ay, in the catalogue ye go for men,
MACBETH: As hounds and greyhounds, mongrels, spaniels, curs,
MACBETH: Shoughs, water-rugs and demi-wolves, are clept
MACBETH: All by the name of dogs: the valued file
MACBETH: Distinguishes the swift, the slow, the subtle,
MACBETH: The housekeeper, the hunter, every one
MACBETH: According to the gift which bounteous nature
MACBETH: Hath in him closed, whereby he does receive
MACBETH: Particular addition. from the bill
MACBETH: That writes them all alike: and so of men.
MACBETH: Now, if you have a station in the file,
MACBETH: Not i' the worst rank of manhood, say 't,
MACBETH: And I will put that business in your bosoms,
MACBETH: Whose execution takes your enemy off,
MACBETH: Grapples you to the heart and love of us,
MACBETH: Who wear our health but sickly in his life,
MACBETH: Which in his death were perfect.
Second Murderer: I am one, my liege,
Second Murderer: Whom the vile blows and buffets of the world
Second Murderer: Have so incensed that I am reckless what
Second Murderer: I do to spite the world.
First Murderer: And I another
First Murderer: So weary with disasters, tugg'd with fortune,
First Murderer: That I would set my lie on any chance,
First Murderer: To mend it, or be rid on't.
MACBETH: Both of you
MACBETH: Know Banquo was your enemy.
Both Murderers: True, my lord.
MACBETH: So is he mine, and in such bloody distance,
MACBETH: That every minute of his being thrusts
MACBETH: Against my near'st of life: and though I could
MACBETH: With barefaced power sweep him from my sight
MACBETH: And bid my will avouch it, yet I must not,
MACBETH: For certain friends that are both his and mine,
MACBETH: Whose loves I may not drop, but wail his fall
MACBETH: Who I myself struck down, and thence it is,
MACBETH: That I to your assistance do make love,
MACBETH: Masking the business from the common eye
MACBETH: For sundry weighty reasons.
Second Murderer: We shall, my lord,
Second Murderer: Perform what you command us.
First Murderer: Though our lives--
MACBETH: Your spirits shine through you. Within this hour at most
MACBETH: I will advise you where to plant yourselves,
MACBETH: Acquaint you with the perfect spy o' the time,
MACBETH: The moment on't, for't must be done to-night,
MACBETH: And something from the palace, always thought
MACBETH: That I require a clearness: and with him--
MACBETH: To leave no rubs nor botches in the work--
MACBETH: Fleance his son, that keeps him company,
MACBETH: Whose absence is no less material to me
MACBETH: Than is his father's, must embrace the fate
MACBETH: Of that dark hour. Resolve yourselves apart:
MACBETH: I'll come to you anon.
Both Murderers: We are resolved, my lord.
MACBETH: I'll call upon you straight: abide within.
NARRATOR: Exeunt Murderers
MACBETH: It is concluded. Banquo, thy soul's flight,
MACBETH: If it find heaven, must find it out to-night.
NARRATOR: Exit
NARRATOR: SCENE II. The palace.
NARRATOR: Enter LADY MACBETH and a Servant
LADY MACBETH: Is Banquo gone from court?
Servant: Ay, madam, but returns again to-night.
LADY MACBETH: Say to the king, I would attend his leisure
LADY MACBETH: For a few words.
Servant: Madam, I will.
NARRATOR: Exit
LADY MACBETH: Nought's had, all's spent,
LADY MACBETH: Where our desire is got without content:
LADY MACBETH: 'Tis safer to be that which we destroy
LADY MACBETH: Than by destruction dwell in doubtful joy.
NARRATOR: Enter MACBETH
LADY MACBETH: How now, my lord! why do you keep alone,
LADY MACBETH: Of sorriest fancies your companions making,
LADY MACBETH: Using those thoughts which should indeed have died
LADY MACBETH: With them they think on? Things without all remedy
LADY MACBETH: Should be without regard: what's done is done.
MACBETH: We have scotch'd the snake, not kill'd it:
MACBETH: She'll close and be herself, whilst our poor malice
MACBETH: Remains in danger of her former tooth.
MACBETH: But let the frame of things disjoint, both the
MACBETH: worlds suffer,
MACBETH: Ere we will eat our meal in fear and sleep
MACBETH: In the affliction of these terrible dreams
MACBETH: That shake us nightly: better be with the dead,
MACBETH: Whom we, to gain our peace, have sent to peace,
MACBETH: Than on the torture of the mind to lie
MACBETH: In restless ecstasy. Duncan is in his grave,
MACBETH: After life's fitful fever he sleeps well,
MACBETH: Treason has done his worst: nor steel, nor poison,
MACBETH: Malice domestic, foreign levy, nothing,
MACBETH: Can touch him further.
LADY MACBETH: Come on,
LADY MACBETH: Gentle my lord, sleek o'er your rugged looks,
LADY MACBETH: Be bright and jovial among your guests to-night.
MACBETH: So shall I, love, and so, I pray, be you:
MACBETH: Let your remembrance apply to Banquo,
MACBETH: Present him eminence, both with eye and tongue:
MACBETH: Unsafe the while, that we
MACBETH: Must lave our honours in these flattering streams,
MACBETH: And make our faces vizards to our hearts,
MACBETH: Disguising what they are.
LADY MACBETH: You must leave this.
MACBETH: O, full of scorpions is my mind, dear wife!
MACBETH: Thou know'st that Banquo, and his Fleance, lives.
LADY MACBETH: But in them nature's copy's not eterne.
MACBETH: There's comfort yet, they are assailable,
MACBETH: Then be thou jocund: ere the bat hath flown
MACBETH: His cloister'd flight, ere to black Hecate's summons
MACBETH: The shard-borne beetle with his drowsy hums
MACBETH: Hath rung night's yawning peal, there shall be done
MACBETH: A deed of dreadful note.
LADY MACBETH: What's to be done?
MACBETH: Be innocent of the knowledge, dearest chuck,
MACBETH: Till thou applaud the deed. Come, seeling night,
MACBETH: Scarf up the tender eye of pitiful day,
MACBETH: And with thy bloody and invisible hand
MACBETH: Cancel and tear to pieces that great bond
MACBETH: Which keeps me pale! Light thickens, and the crow
MACBETH: Makes wing to the rooky wood:
MACBETH: Good things of day begin to droop and drowse,
MACBETH: While night's black agents to their preys do rouse.
MACBETH: Thou marvell'st at my words: but hold thee still,
MACBETH: Things bad begun make strong themselves by ill.
MACBETH: So, prithee, go with me.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE III. A park near the palace.
NARRATOR: Enter three Murderers
First Murderer: But who did bid thee join with us?
Third Murderer: Macbeth.
Second Murderer: He needs not our mistrust, since he delivers
Second Murderer: Our offices and what we have to do
Second Murderer: To the direction just.
First Murderer: Then stand with us.
First Murderer: The west yet glimmers with some streaks of day:
First Murderer: Now spurs the lated traveller apace
First Murderer: To gain the timely inn, and near approaches
First Murderer: The subject of our watch.
Third Murderer: Hark! I hear horses.
BANQUO: [Within]  Give us a light there, ho!
Second Murderer: Then 'tis he: the rest
Second Murderer: That are within the note of expectation
Second Murderer: Already are i' the court.
First Murderer: His horses go about.
Third Murderer: Almost a mile: but he does usually,
Third Murderer: So all men do, from hence to the palace gate
Third Murderer: Make it their walk.
Second Murderer: A light, a light!
NARRATOR: Enter BANQUO, and FLEANCE with a torch
Third Murderer: 'Tis he.
First Murderer: Stand to't.
BANQUO: It will be rain to-night.
First Murderer: Let it come down.
NARRATOR: They set upon BANQUO
BANQUO: O, treachery! Fly, good Fleance, fly, fly, fly!
BANQUO: Thou mayst revenge. O slave!
NARRATOR: Dies. FLEANCE escapes
Third Murderer: Who did strike out the light?
First Murderer: Wast not the way?
Third Murderer: There's but one down, the son is fled.
Second Murderer: We have lost
Second Murderer: Best half of our affair.
First Murderer: Well, let's away, and say how much is done.
NARRATOR: Exeunt
NARRATOR: SCENE IV. The same. Hall in the palace.
NARRATOR: A banquet prepared. Enter MACBETH, LADY MACBETH, ROSS, LENNOX, Lords, and Attendants
MACBETH: You know your own degrees, sit down: at first
MACBETH: And last the hearty welcome.
Lords: Thanks to your majesty.
MACBETH: Ourself will mingle with society,
MACBETH: And play the humble host.
MACBETH: Our hostess keeps her state, but in best time
MACBETH: We will require her welcome.
LADY MACBETH: Pronounce it for me, sir, to all our friends,
LADY MACBETH: For my heart speaks they are welcome.
NARRATOR: First Murderer appears at the door
MACBETH: See, they encounter thee with their hearts' thanks.
MACBETH: Both sides are even: here I'll sit i' the midst:
MACBETH: Be large in mirth, anon we'll drink a measure
MACBETH: The table round.
NARRATOR: Approaching the door
MACBETH: There's blood on thy face.
First Murderer: 'Tis Banquo's then.
MACBETH: 'Tis better thee without than he within.
MACBETH: Is he dispatch'd?
First Murderer: My lord, his throat is cut, that I did for him.
MACBETH: Thou art the best o' the cut-throats: yet he's good
MACBETH: That did the like for Fleance: if thou didst it,
MACBETH: Thou art the nonpareil.
First Murderer: Most royal sir,
First Murderer: Fleance is 'scaped.
MACBETH: Then comes my fit again: I had else been perfect,
MACBETH: Whole as the marble, founded as the rock,
MACBETH: As broad and general as the casing air:
MACBETH: But now I am cabin'd, cribb'd, confined, bound in
MACBETH: To saucy doubts and fears. But Banquo's safe?
First Murderer: Ay, my good lord: safe in a ditch he bides,
First Murderer: With twenty trenched gashes on his head,
First Murderer: The least a death to nature.
MACBETH: Thanks for that:
MACBETH: There the grown serpent lies, the worm that's fled
MACBETH: Hath nature that in time will venom breed,
MACBETH: No teeth for the present. Get thee gone: to-morrow
MACBETH: We'll hear, ourselves, again.
NARRATOR: Exit Murderer
LADY MACBETH: My royal lord,
LADY MACBETH: You do not give the cheer: the feast is sold
LADY MACBETH: That is not often vouch'd, while 'tis a-making,
LADY MACBETH: 'Tis given with welcome: to feed were best at home,
LADY MACBETH: From thence the sauce to meat is ceremony,
LADY MACBETH: Meeting were bare without it.
MACBETH: Sweet remembrancer!
MACBETH: Now, good digestion wait on appetite,
MACBETH: And health on both!
LENNOX: May't please your highness sit.
NARRATOR: The GHOST OF BANQUO enters, and sits in MACBETH's place
MACBETH: Here had we now our country's honour roof'd,
MACBETH: Were the graced person of our Banquo present,
MACBETH: Who may I rather challenge for unkindness
MACBETH: Than pity for mischance!
ROSS: His absence, sir,
ROSS: Lays blame upon his promise. Please't your highness
ROSS: To grace us with your royal company.
MACBETH: The table's full.
LENNOX: Here is a place reserved, sir.
MACBETH: Where?
LENNOX: Here, my good lord. What is't that moves your highness?
MACBETH: Which of you have done this?
Lords: What, my good lord?
MACBETH: Thou canst not say I did it: never shake
MACBETH: Thy gory locks at me.
ROSS: Gentlemen, rise: his highness is not well.
LADY MACBETH: Sit, worthy friends: my lord is often thus,
LADY MACBETH: And hath been from his youth: pray you, keep seat,
LADY MACBETH: The fit is momentary, upon a thought
LADY MACBETH: He will again be well: if much you note him,
LADY MACBETH: You shall offend him and extend his passion:
LADY MACBETH: Feed, and regard him not. Are you a man?
MACBETH: Ay, and a bold one, that dare look on that
MACBETH: Which might appal the devil.
LADY MACBETH: O proper stuff!
LADY MACBETH: This is the very painting of your fear:
LADY MACBETH: This is the air-drawn dagger which, you said,
LADY MACBETH: Led you to Duncan. O, these flaws and starts,
LADY MACBETH: Impostors to true fear, would well become
LADY MACBETH: A woman's story at a winter's fire,
LADY MACBETH: Authorized by her grandam. Shame itself!
LADY MACBETH: Why do you make such faces? When all's done,
LADY MACBETH: You look but on a stool.
MACBETH: Prithee, see there! behold! look! lo!
MACBETH: how say you?
MACBETH: Why, what care I? If thou canst nod, speak too.
MACBETH: If charnel-houses and our graves must send
MACBETH: Those that we bury back, our monuments
MACBETH: Shall be the maws of kites.
NARRATOR: GHOST OF BANQUO vanishes
LADY MACBETH: What, quite unmann'd in folly?
MACBETH: If I stand here, I saw him.
LADY MACBETH: Fie, for shame!
MACBETH: Blood hath been shed ere now, i' the olden time,
MACBETH: Ere human statute purged the gentle weal,
MACBETH: Ay, and since too, murders have been perform'd
MACBETH: Too terrible for the ear: the times have been,
MACBETH: That, when the brains were out, the man would die,
MACBETH: And there an end, but now they rise again,
MACBETH: With twenty mortal murders on their crowns,
MACBETH: And push us from our stools: this is more strange
MACBETH: Than such a murder is.
LADY MACBETH: My worthy lord,
LADY MACBETH: Your noble friends do lack you.
MACBETH: I do forget.
MACBETH: Do not muse at me, my most worthy friends,
MACBETH: I have a strange infirmity, which is nothing
MACBETH: To those that know me. Come, love and health to all,
MACBETH: Then I'll sit down. Give me some wine, fill full.
MACBETH: I drink to the general joy o' the whole table,
MACBETH: And to our dear friend Banquo, whom we miss,
MACBETH: Would he were here! to all, and him, we thirst,
MACBETH: And all to all.
Lords: Our duties, and the pledge.
NARRATOR: Re-enter GHOST OF BANQUO
MACBETH: Avaunt! and quit my sight! let the earth hide thee!
MACBETH: Thy bones are marrowless, thy blood is cold,
MACBETH: Thou hast no speculation in those eyes
MACBETH: Which thou dost glare with!
LADY MACBETH: Think of this, good peers,
LADY MACBETH: But as a thing of custom: 'tis no other,
LADY MACBETH: Only it spoils the pleasure of the time.
MACBETH: What man dare, I dare:
MACBETH: Approach thou like the rugged Russian bear,
MACBETH: The arm'd rhinoceros, or the Hyrcan tiger,
MACBETH: Take any shape but that, and my firm nerves
MACBETH: Shall never tremble: or be alive again,
MACBETH: And dare me to the desert with thy sword,
MACBETH: If trembling I inhabit then, protest me
MACBETH: The baby of a girl. Hence, horrible shadow!
MACBETH: Unreal mockery, hence!
NARRATOR: GHOST OF BANQUO vanishes
MACBETH: Why, so: being gone,
MACBETH: I am a man again. Pray you, sit still.
LADY MACBETH: You have displaced the mirth, broke the good meeting,
LADY MACBETH: With most admired disorder.
MACBETH: Can such things be,
MACBETH: And overcome us like a summer's cloud,
MACBETH: Without our special wonder? You make me strange
MACBETH: Even to the disposition that I owe,
MACBETH: When now I think you can behold such sights,
MACBETH: And keep the natural ruby of your cheeks,
MACBETH: When mine is blanched with fear.
ROSS: What sights, my lord?
LADY MACBETH: I pray you, speak not, he grows worse and worse,
LADY MACBETH: Question enrages him. At once, good night:
LADY MACBETH: Stand not upon the order of your going,
LADY MACBETH: But go at once.
LENNOX: Good night, and better health
LENNOX: Attend his majesty!
LADY MACBETH: A kind good night to all!
NARRATOR: Exeunt all but MACBETH and LADY MACBETH
MACBETH: It will have blood, they say, blood will have blood:
MACBETH: Stones have been known to move and trees to speak,
MACBETH: Augurs and understood relations have
MACBETH: By magot-pies and choughs and rooks brought forth
MACBETH: The secret'st man of blood. What is the night?
LADY MACBETH: Almost at odds with morning, which is which.
MACBETH: How say'st thou, that Macduff denies his person
MACBETH: At our great bidding?
LADY MACBETH: Did you send to him, sir?
MACBETH: I hear it by the way, but I will send:
MACBETH: There's not a one of them but in his house
MACBETH: I keep a servant fee'd. I will to-morrow,
MACBETH: And betimes I will, to the weird sisters:
MACBETH: More shall they speak, for now I am bent to know,
